SECTION I-CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 
1. CONTRACT T
YPE AND CEILING
The purpose of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to establish a single-award contract for
the procurement of commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) tax preparation software and
associated support services. Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract Line-Item Numbers
(CLINs) will be used for the acquisition of software licenses and related services, as
required by volunteer sites.
This acquisition will be conducted in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 
(FAR) Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. 
This contract does not obligate any funds at the time of award. Funds will be obligated 
through the issuance of orders or modifications in accordance with applicable funding 
procedures. The Government does not guarantee that the total quantity of supplies or 
services ordered will equal the maximum contract ceiling. 
The contractor is guaranteed a minimum order of 8,500 software licenses during the 
base period and, if exercised, during each of the four (4) option periods. 
The maximum contract ceiling amount the Government may award under this contract 
is (To Be Completed at Time of Award). 
2. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE
The base ordering period is a 12-month base period, with four (4)
consecutive 12-month option ordering periods as stated below:
• Base Period: August 17, 2026 – August 16, 2027
• Option Period 1: August 17, 2027 – August 16, 2028
• Option Period 2: August 17, 2028 – August 16, 2029
• Option Period 3: August 17, 2029 – August 16, 2030
• Option Period 4: August 17, 2030 – August 16, 2031
Transition-in activities are required for the first (90) days of contract performance. 
During the initial contract period, transition activities such as knowledge 
transfer, system setup, data migration, help desk stand-up, training 
material development, live web-based training sessions, and system testing 
and acceptance, will be started in August 2026. 
In option years, training material development and live web-based training 
will be started in August and be completed before January each year. 
Software shall operate at its full capacity by the beginning of the 2027 
filing season (Tax Year 2026). 
Software licenses are valid one year of each contract period. 
DRAFT
2 of 124

3. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE
The place of performance will primarily be the Contractor’s site. Ta
sk orders may be
issued for performance to be at VITA sites, TCE site, Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
facilities, or Treasury facilities. The specific place of performance shall be identified in
the award.
4. ORDERING PROCEDURES
A Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) single-award contract will be awarded to the Contractor based
on the pricing submitted for each deliverable under the applicable Contract Line-Item
Numbers (CLINs). The Contractor shall provide software licenses and associated
support services in accordance with the requirements set forth in this contract.
Performance shall be authorized through the contract award and any subsequent 
contract modifications, as applicable. Work shall be performed upon direction of the 
Contracting Officer, based on requirements identified by the Contracting Officer’s 
Representative (COR) or Program Office and supported by a valid, fully funded 
requisition. 
5. SHIP TO LOCATIONS
Unless otherwise specified, all deliverables/ work products shall be provided to the IRS
COR and shipping to approximately 12,000 domestic and 70 international shipping
addresses which could include multiple deployments.
6. DELIVERABLES
Unless otherwise requested in writing by the COR, work products shall be produced
using Microsoft Office 2010 or later Professional products and delivered in accordance
with the deliverable schedule under Attachment 2. If it is required that deliverable(s) be
submitted in media storage form, all devices must be scanned and certified as virus
free.
7. RAMP-UP PERIOD
Work under this statement of work may require a ramp-up period at the initial start of
this contract. Under the Ramp-up Period the Contractor will recruit and hire personnel
specifically for this contract.
Note: Refer to 4.6 TASK 6 in the SOW: RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER-IN.
8. ORDER ADMINISTRATIVE DATA
8.1 Identification of Government Task Order Personnel 
The COR designation will be identified by the CO’s written designation memo. Similarly, 
the Alternate COR (ACOR) will be identified by the CO’s written designation memo. The 
CO will identify the (COR/ACOR) via e-mail to the Contractor 
8.2 Performance Required Beyond Standard Workday

If needed, performance may be required beyond the standard workday. Beginning with 
the delivery of software through April, help desk support shall be available as follows: 
Mon - Fri: 8 AM ET - 12 AM ET and Sat and Sun: 8 AM ET - 8 PM ET. Post filing 
season, normal help desk hours are required Mon-Fri: 8 AM ET – 5 PM ET. In the case 
of a problem the expectation is that the Contractor will have someone working on it until 
it is resolved or a work around is established. 
8.3 Personnel Removal and Replacement 
The applicable contractor employees are subject to investigation by the government. 
Applicable contractor employees who undergo contractor clearances that reveal, but are 
not limited to, the following may be unacceptable under this contract: conviction of a 
felony, a crime of violence or a serious misdemeanor, a record of arrests for continuing 
offenses, or failure to file or pay federal income tax. The government reserves the right 
to determine if a contractor employee assigned to a task shall continue with the task. 
The contractor shall agree to remove the person assigned within one day of official 
notification by the government and provide a replacement within five days. New hires or 
substitutions of personnel are subject to the contractor clearance requirement.  
8.4 Deliverables/ Work Products 
All contractor deliverables or work products shall remain categorized as "Official Use 
Only.” The release of any portion must be authorized in writing by the government. 
The contractor shall adhere to Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, which 
requires access to the Federal Government electronic and information technology. The 
law applies to all Federal agencies when they develop, procure, maintain, or use 
electronic and information technology. Federal agencies must ensure that this 
technology is accessible to employees and members of the public with disabilities. 
http://www.section508.gov/. 
Each Electronic and Information technology product or service furnished under this 
statement of work shall comply with the Electronic and Information Technology (EIT) 
Accessibility Standards (29 U.S.C. 87794(d)).  
For every EIT product or service accepted under this contract by the Government that 
does not comply with (29 U.S.C. 87794(d)), the contractor shall at the discretion of the 
Government, make every effort to replace or upgrade it with a compliant equivalent 
product or service, if commercially available and cost neutral, on either the planned 
refresh cycle of the product or service, or on the order renewal date, whichever shall 
occur first. 
The contractor will be working with sensitive taxpayer data under this contract and must 
demonstrate the ability to pass all IRS security reviews required to receive access to 
encrypted sensitive taxpayer data.

SECTION II-STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
1. Background:
The Stakeholder Partnerships, Education and Communication (SPEC) organization within
Customer Assistance, Relationships and Education (CARE), provides free elec
tronic tax
preparation for taxpayers who are generally low-income, elderly, disabled or have limited
English proficiency. This service is provided nationwide in approximately 12,000 volunteer
sites. Most of the return preparation is performed by certified volunteers.
Over each of the last three years, approximately 3.6 million Federal returns and 2.7 million state 
returns were processed at these sites by over 96,000 volunteers, partners and employees. 
Generally, sites operate from January (beginning of e-file) through April 15. Some sites remain 
open year around. 
1.1 Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA): 
SPEC partners with Community Based Coalitions, Non-profit Organizations, and local City and 
State Governmental Agencies to provide free tax preparation services. These agencies support 
the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) program. VITA partners and volunteers prepare 
basic tax returns for low-income taxpayers, who are U.S. citizens, residents and non-resident 
aliens. All tax preparation is performed by a certified volunteer with the taxpayer present or by a 
taxpayer with the assistance of a certified volunteer. These returns generally include income 
from wages. 
VITA sites are located at neighborhood community centers, libraries, churches, shopping malls 
and other locations that are convenient to the taxpayer, including a supplemental program for 
taxpayers living abroad or near U.S. embassies overseas. Internet accessibility is to be 
determined by location. 
SPEC also partners with the Armed Forces Tax Council to provide free return preparation for 
active and retired military personnel at military bases and ships across the nation and 
internationally. These returns can be more complex and include a wide- variety of forms and 
schedules. These sites have Internet access but operate in a secure environment which tends to 
impede communication speeds. 
1.2 Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE): 
Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE) offers tax assistance services similar to those provided 
by VITA, as well as free tax counseling for elderly taxpayers, who are restricted to retirement 
homes, neighborhood sites, or private care homes. These returns are generally more complex 
than those prepared through VITA and may include income from pensions, annuities, and 
social security benefits. 
2. Objectives:
The objectives of this single award contract are the following:
• provide secure, commercial off the shelf (COTS) Tax Preparation Software supporting
VITA/TCE operations

• enable accurate preparation and transmission of federal and state taxes returns
• provide reliable user support and training to ensure successful filing season operations
• deliver timely and accurate reporting to support IRS program oversight
3. Scope:
The Contractor shall provide COTS tax preparation software, support services, training,
reporting, and system capabilities necessary to support IRS VITA and TCE programs across
approximately 12,000 sites globally.

CARE’s requirements include contractor support and facilitation of the following tasks:
Task 1 - Orientation Briefing 
Task 2 - Software Production Environment: Software 
Task 3 - Reporting Capabilities: User Generated, Recurring Contractor Generated Management 
Reporting and Ad Hoc Contractor Generated Reporting 
Task 4 - Help desk assistance and technical problem resolution support  
Task 5 - Regulatory, Security and Privacy Standards 
Task 6 - Ramp-Up Knowledge Transfer-In  
Task 7 - Ramp-Up Knowledge Transfer-Out  
Task 8 - Period of Performance Summary Report 
Task 9 - Transition to Support 
Task 10 - Site File Upload to the Tax Software 
Task 11 - Direct Client Portal

Within two (2) weeks of award, the contractor shall conduct an orientation briefing for the

expect the contractor to expend significant resources in preparation for this briefing. Rather, the 
intent of the briefing is to initiate the communication process between the Government and 
Contractor by introducing key participants, explaining their roles, reviewing communication 
ground rules, and assuring a common understanding of the requirements and objectives. 
The orientation briefing shall be held at an IRS facility

RFI Virtualization Enterprise Software Solutions 

For: Virtualization Enterprise Software Solutions for the Department of War (DoW)
RFI Number: 842674441
Issuing Agency: Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA)
Date of Issuance: 4/24/26
Response Due Date: 15 Days Post-Release

1.0 INTRODUCTION & PURPOSE

The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA), on behalf of the Department of War (DoW), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to conduct market research. The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified sources capable of providing a standardized, enterprise-scalable virtualization software solution, to include all associated software sustainment, upgrades, and technical support services under an enterprise-wide agreement within the next 12 months. The objective is to establish a centralized, efficient, and cost-effective procurement vehicle.

The Government intends to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a five-year ordering period (one-year base period and four one-year options) to procure products and services for the DoW, including 4th Estate Agencies, Combatant Commands (COCOMs), and Military Departments (MILDEPs), against the GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Information Technology category.

This is an RFI only. This is not a solicitation or Request for Quote (RFQ) and does not commit the Government to award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI are solely at the interested party's expense.

2.0 BACKGROUND AND CURRENT VIRTUALIZATION ENVIRONMENT

The Department of War (DoW) is committed to leveraging advanced technologies to enhance the security and effectiveness of its IT operations. DISA is collaborating with DoW components to create an enterprise-wide solution for procuring commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) virtualization software. This initiative aims to consolidate numerous existing contracts and streamline vendor management for critical Virtualization products supporting server virtualization, cybersecurity, endpoint protection, and network management across the DoW's IT infrastructure.

The DoW’s virtualization environment is a critical component of its global IT infrastructure, providing enterprise compute capabilities supporting approximately 700,000 cores. This environment is characterized by its significant scale, geographic diversity, and complex security requirements, with resources deployed across CONUS and OCONUS locations. These include DoW data centers, enterprise computing facilities, and tactical/forward-deployed environments, spanning multiple security domains and classification levels. All solutions must align with DoW enterprise architecture, cybersecurity (e.g., STIGs, Impact Levels), and lifecycle sustainment requirements.

The platform primarily supports the following use cases:

Mission Application Hosting: Serving as the foundation for critical warfighting and business systems.

Development & Testing: Providing sandboxed environments for developing and testing new capabilities.

End-User Computing (EUC): Supporting Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) and other virtualized user-facing services.

3.0 SCOPE OF REQUIREMENTS

The Government requires a comprehensive virtualization portfolio to support an estimated 700,000 subscriptions. The proposed solution must be structured to accommodate diverse client needs through offerings like tiered bundles, individual licenses, and hybrid models.

A comprehensive migration plan with a detailed timeline is mandatory. This plan must detail the strategy for transitioning from the current VMware framework to the proposed solution with minimal disruption to mission-critical operations. The plan must also explicitly describe how Artificial Intelligence (AI) will be leveraged to drive automation, reduce administrative overhead, and simplify the deployment, management, and security of the platform.

Furthermore, all proposed capabilities must be designed to integrate with DoW regulations and frameworks, and must minimally address the following core areas:

3.1. Core Platform Capabilities

Virtualization: Provide a solution that supports both full virtualization and paravirtualization to consolidate applications and establish cloud or VDI environments. It must include live VM migration, storage migration, and seamless import/export functionality, including cross-migration, all managed from a unified administration plane.

Disaster Recovery & Backup: Deliver robust business continuity through VM-centric snapshots, clones, and replication. The solution must support enterprise-grade backup and recovery via modern APIs (e.g., VSS) and allow for granular recovery (file/folder, full VM, disk-level) across data centers.

Application & Data Virtualization: Provide capabilities to decouple applications from the underlying OS (application virtualization) and to abstract and integrate disparate data sources without requiring data movement (data virtualization).

Remote & Automated Management: Enable remote management and monitoring of all infrastructure, including direct remote console access. A comprehensive REST API for programmatic automation and third-party integration is mandatory.

3.2. Management, Analytics, and Security

Cybersecurity: Deliver advanced threat detection and incident response. This must include Secure Boot, shielded VMs, and native micro-segmentation for application-centric security policies. The system must use AI-driven insights for self-healing security configurations to maintain compliance.

Asset Management: Provide a centralized dashboard to discover, track, monitor, and manage all physical and virtual IT assets. Crucially, this tool must operate across the DoW's globally distributed and logically partitioned network boundaries, providing a unified view of asset utilization.

Network Management & Security: Offer solutions for network monitoring, management, and security, including capabilities for SD-WAN, web/email security, and virtual networking.

Logging, Analytics, and Reporting:

Log Management: Ingest syslog and custom logs from all platform components (hypervisors, hosts) and retain them for at least one year.

Analytics & Search: Provide real-time search and analytics to correlate events across all layers (hosts, clusters, VMs, applications, storage).

Performance & Capacity: Offer real-time and historical analytics (CPU, memory, storage, network) with one-year data retention. The platform must provide forecasting, capacity planning, and "what-if" modeling for workload placement.

Alerting & Notifications: Support threshold-based and dynamic anomaly detection alerts, with routing to multiple platforms via email, webhooks, and REST API integrations.

3.3. Security, Compliance, and Workforce Enablement

Security and Compliance

DoW Impact Level: Products must meet a minimum of DoW Impact Level 5 (IL5) certification, with a clearly defined roadmap to achieve IL6.

Authentication: The solution must support two-factor authentication via SAML 2.0 or OIDC to ensure integration with the DoW Enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (E-ICAM) solution.

Training and Continuous Learning

Foundational Awareness: Introductory training for all technical staff to build a baseline understanding of the new platform's architecture, terminology, and core concepts.

Deep Technical Training: An intensive, hands-on curriculum for senior engineers and the core migration team covering platform administration, advanced networking, security configuration, and migration-specific tooling.

Operational Enablement: Role-based training for day-to-day operations teams focused on new Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), common administrative tasks, and basic troubleshooting.

Continuous Learning: A strategy for ongoing education, including hands-on labs, to keep staff skills current on new features, performance optimization, and advanced security practices.

4.0 INFORMATION REQUESTED

Interested parties are requested to provide a response that addresses the following areas:

4.1. Company Information

Company Name, Address, and Website.

Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, and Phone Number).

CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI).

Business size and any applicable socioeconomic status.

4.2. Capability Statement

A detailed response addressing your company’s capabilities for all requirements outlined in Section 3.0. This should include specific responses to the following areas:

ROI and Value: Describe how your solution provides a clear return on investment (ROI) and long-term value, covering Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), quantifiable ROI metrics, cost effectiveness, enterprise scalability, and strategic modernization value.

Migration Strategy: Outline a phased migration framework (discovery, pilot, full-scale) from legacy virtualization, addressing DoW's scale and decentralized network. Include plans for risk mitigation, business continuity, and rollback.

Technology & Commercial Outlook: Provide a 3-5 year technology outlook for virtualization, detailing your product roadmap alignment with trends like sovereign clouds and AI/ML. Describe alternative and predictable consumption pricing models.

Security & Supply Chain: Detail your corporate security posture, compliance framework (e.g., IL5), and Secure Software Development Lifecycle (SSDLC) practices.

Global Technical Support: Present a detailed technical support framework for a globally distributed organization, including a sample SLA matrix. Confirm U.S. citizen support and the availability of cleared personnel.

Program Management: Describe your program management approach, account team structure, and governance model. Provide a sample Executive Dashboard or QBR template.

Training & Adoption: Outline your continuous adoption plan for establishing a Center of Excellence (CoE) and ensuring long-term user proficiency.

4.3. Contracting and Strategy

Provide a list of all GSA Schedules or other Government-wide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs) your company holds.

Provide confirmation of your status as an authorized reseller/distributor for the proposed products, including the OEM Letter of Authorization.

Provide substantive feedback on the Government's proposed acquisition strategy, commenting on the suitability of Enterprise License Agreements (ELAs) vs. consumption-based models.

Describe your license management methodology for an enterprise of DoW's scale, providing a case study from a comparable Federal agency.

4.4. Cost - Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM)

Submit a high-level, non-binding Cost ROM for all requirements, based on an estimated 700,000 subscriptions, detailing varied offerings (tiered, individual, hybrid).

The ROM should estimate total cost for a one-year base period and four one-year option periods. State your approach to price protection for option years and the pricing plan for integrating additional DoW agencies.

Submit a separate, non-binding Cost ROM detailing all one-time migration costs (e.g., professional services, training).

5.0 RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS

Submission POC: Responses shall be submitted electronically to adam.m.venhaus.civ@mail.mil & christinia.f.rhem.civ@mail.mil.

Email Subject Line: The subject line must read: “Response to RFI-DISA-VIRTUALIZATION-2026.”

Format: Responses should be submitted in Microsoft Word, Microsoft Excel, or Adobe PDF formats.

Page Limit: Responses are limited to 20 pages. The Title Page, Table of Contents, and OEM Letters of Authorization will not count against this limit.

Response Deadline: Responses are due no later than 10:00 AM CST 5/4/26. Late submissions may not be accepted.

Follow-On Engagement: After reviewing RFI responses, the Government may schedule follow-up activities. These could include industry days, one-on-one meetings, or requests for product demonstrations.

Sources Sought/Request For Information (RFI) 
Education Platform Requirements 
1.  Purpose and Scope  
This Sources Sought/ Request for Information is issued solely for market research and 
acquisition planning purposes.  This notice does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ), 
Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not obligate the Government to 
issue a solicitation or make an award. 
Responses are voluntary. No reimbursement will be provided for costs associated with 
responding to this notice.  
The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) seeks information to better understand 
current industry capabilities, architectural approaches, data strategies, and maturity related to a 
single, cohesive enterprise education platform that supports DoWEA’s global Pre-K – 12 
mission. 
2.  Background and Objective 
DoWEA operates a globally distributed education environment supporting instructional delivery, 
student services, and enterprise operations. As part of long-term modernization and consolidation 
planning, DoWEA is conducting market research to assess platforms that can: 
• Unify instructional and enterprise systems on a shared or tightly integrated data 
foundation. 
• Reduce system fragmentation and manual data movement. 
• Enable secure, near-real-time reporting, analytics, and AI-enabled insights at global scale. 
• Support interoperability with external analytics platforms and DoWEA-managed data 
environments. 
3. Teaching, Learning & Student Systems 
3.1 Integrated Platform Approach 
DoWEA is interested in platforms that support tightly integrated, natively developed or fully 
supported modules operating on a shared identity and data framework. Vendors may describe 
point to point or loosely coupled integrations; however, such approaches should be clearly 
identified and explained.  
3.2 Student Information System (SIS) 

2 
 
DoWEA seeks information on Student Information Systems (SIS) that can serve as the primary 
system of record for managing student data across the full student lifecycle.  Areas of interest 
include, but are not limited to: 
• Enrollment, registration, scheduling, attendance, grading, gradebook management, 
transcripts, discipline/behavior tracking, and program participation. 
• Secure student records management with rolebased access control, audit logging, 
alignment with the Privacy Act of 1974 and applicable DoW privacy regulations, and 
configurable data retention rules. 
• Support for DoWEA specific calendars, grading policies, credits, and reporting 
requirements. 
• Standards based, documented APIs that support data import and export for students, 
enrollment, roster, attendance, grades, transcripts, behavior, and program status data, 
including near real time exchange where available. 
3.3 Learning Management System (LMS) – Optional Module with Mandatory 
Integration 
DoWEA seeks information on education platforms that either include a native LMS module or 
provide strong, production ready integration with commonly used third party LMS solutions (for 
example, Schoology and Google Classroom) but not limited to those solutions.   Areas of interest 
include the platform’s ability to support: 
• Seamlessly integrate with external LMS platforms using standards-based mechanisms 
(e.g., LTI 1.3/Advantage, OneRoster, and secure APIs). 
• Support automated provisioning and synchronization of:  
o Courses, sections, teachers, students, and roles. 
o Assignments and grading workflows. 
o Enrollment changes, schedule updates, and staff reassignments. 
• Enable bidirectional grade pass back so that instructional grading performed in the LMS 
flows reliably to the SIS gradebook and transcript processes. 
• Maintain consistent user identity, authentication (SSO), and role-based access across the 
SIS and integrated LMS environments. 
• Provide visibility for instructional activity and learning signals (e.g., assignment 
completion, engagement indicators) for reporting and analytics, regardless of whether 
instruction occurs in a native or third-party LMS. 
• Ensure mobile support and parity of experience where supported by the external LMS. 
If a native LMS module is offered, vendors may describe capabilities related to: 
• Course and content management, assignments, rubrics, discussions, collaboration tools, 
and mobile applications. 
• Standards-based grading aligned with SIS grade calculation and transcript workflows. 

3 
 
• Learning analytics focused on engagement, progress, pacing, mastery, and course 
completion. 
3.4 Assessment 
DoWEA seeks information on assessment capabilities that support formative, benchmark, and 
summative use cases.  Areas of interest include: 
• Centralized, reusable item banks with tagging, version control, and alignment to 
standards. 
• Accommodation management aligned to IEP/504 requirements and multilingual learner 
needs. 
• Secure test administration with support for offline or low-bandwidth operation in global 
environments. 
• Proctoring and academic integrity safeguards, as applicable. 
• Import/export APIs supporting assessment results, accommodations, and item metadata. 
• Integration with LMS platforms (native or third-party) for assignment-based and 
classroom-embedded assessments. 
3.5 Special Education and Student Support Programs 
DoWEA seeks information on platforms that support special education and student services 
workflows.  Areas of interest include support for: 
• IEP/504, Multilingual Learner Programs (MLP), Advanced Academic Programs (AAP), 
and MTSS/RTI frameworks. 
• Intervention planning, service delivery logging, progress monitoring, and compliance 
reporting. 
• Strict role-based privacy controls to safeguard sensitive student data. 
• Standards-based APIs supporting exchange of accommodations, service records, progress 
data, and compliance indicators. 
4. Reporting, Analytics, and Data Interoperability 
DoWEA is interested in understanding how platforms support reporting and analytics across 
instructional and enterprise domains.  Areas of interest include: 
• Real-time or near real-time reporting across SIS, Assessment, Special Programs, and 
LMS platforms (native or third-party). 
• Role-appropriate dashboards for teachers, school leaders, district/regional leadership, and 
headquarters personnel. 
• Reporting shall not be degraded or functionally limited using an external LMS. 

4 
 
Vendors should describe how reporting data is structured and made available for analytical and 
AI use cases.  
5. Enterprise Operations & Business Services 
DoWEA seeks information on enterprise education platforms that provide or integrate with 
operational and business services to support a global education environment.  The following 
areas represent capabilities of interest for market research purposes. 
5.1 Finance / ERP 
Areas of interest include: 
• General Ledger, Accounts Payable/Receivable, multi-fund accounting, grants 
management, budgeting and forecasting. 
• Procurement and eProcurement workflows. 
• Inventory management and school activity funds. 
• Auditability and reporting are suitable for federal oversight. 
5.2 Human Resources /Human Capital Management (HCM) 
Areas of interest include: 
• Manpower management, including position control, Staff Deployment (by school, 
program, or funding source), Trend and Forecasting (enrollment driven staffing models), 
and Scenario Planning and Forecasting. 
• Recruiting, onboarding, licensure and credential tracking, staff evaluations, and substitute 
management. 
• Alignment of staff roles and credentials with instructional and system access. 
• Integration with enterprise identity and access management systems. 
5.3 Facilities /Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) 
Areas of interest include: 
• Work order management, preventive maintenance scheduling, asset lifecycle tracking, 
and space utilization. 
• Safety, security, and facilities related compliance workflows. 
5.4 Transportation 
Areas of interest include: 
• Route planning, ridership management, and parent notifications. 

5 
 
• Fleet management and vehicle maintenance tracking. 
5.5 IT Service Management (ITSM) & End-User Computing 
Areas of interest include: 
• Device, software, and asset management. 
• IT ticketing and service workflows. 
• Integration with Unified Endpoint Management (UEM/MDM) platforms. 
• Classroom device management and instructional visibility. 
6. Unified Data, Analytics & Interoperability 
6.1 Unified Data Architecture 
DoWEA seeks information on platform support unified or federated data approaches across 
instructional and enterprise domains.  Areas of interest include: 
• A shared or tightly federated data model across SIS, LMS, ERP, HR, facilities, 
transportation, and IT operations. 
• Near real-time data flows with minimal manual reconciliation. 
6.2 APIs & Interoperability Standards 
 Vendors may describe support for open APIs and industry standards, including: 
• Open REST APIs with pagination, filtering, and webhook/event support. 
• Support for current and future standards, including but not limited to:  
o IMS OneRoster 1.1+ 
o Ed-Fi Data Standard 4.0+ (native or certified adapter) 
o LTI 1.3/Advantage 
o QTI/APIP (as applicable) 
o SCORM (legacy) and xAPI 
o Identity standards: SAML 2.0, OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SCIM 2.0 
6.3 AI-Enabled Analytics & Business Intelligence 
DoWEA is interested in understanding how platforms support analytics and AI enabled insights 
across instructional and operational domains.  Areas of interest include: 
• Executive, instructional, and operational dashboards. 
• Early warning indicators for attendance, grades, behavior, and course completion with 
configurable thresholds. 

6 
 
• Machine learning explainability, including feature importance and counterfactual 
explanations. 
• Intervention tracking linked to analytic triggers. 
• Self-service analytics, including natural language queries where appropriate. 
• Export or integration with DoWEA managed data warehouse or lakehouse infrastructure. 
• Availability of Metadata catalogs with data lineage visualization. 
7. Data Quality & Master Data Management 
Areas of interest include: 
• Automated validation for completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and consistency. 
• Pre-configured quality checks for critical data (student demographics, attendance, grades, 
staff credentials). 
• Data quality dashboards, alerts, and trend analysis. 
• Support for DoWEA defined custom validation rules. 
• Master Data Management for students, staff, schools, and courses. 
• Data classification, PII tagging. and retention/minimization controls. 
8. Reporting Integration with External AI-Enabled Analytics Platforms (e.g., MS Fabric) 
DoWEA seeks information on how platform reporting and analytics capabilities interoperate 
seamlessly with external, AI enabled enterprise analytics platforms, including but not limited to 
MS Fabric, Power BI, and DoWEA managed data warehouse or lakehouse environments. The 
reporting architecture must support both native platform reporting and advanced external 
analytics without data duplication, vendor lock-in, or loss of data fidelity.  Vendors shall 
describe how their solutions enable secure, scalable, and transparent integration across 
instructional, operational, and enterprise analytics environments.  
9. Data Access & Export 
The platform shall provide secure, documented, and supported mechanisms to expose 
reporting data to external AI-enabled analytics platforms, including:  
o REST-based APIs. 
o Event- or change-based data feeds. 
o Bulk and incremental data export capabilities for historical and snapshot data. 
• Data access methods shall support near real-time and scheduled delivery patterns suitable 
for ingestion by AI-enabled analytics platforms. 
• Exported data shall be available in open, analytics-optimized formats, including but not 
limited to:  
o Parquet 
o Delta 

7 
 
o CSV 
o JSON 
• The solution shall not require proprietary or vendor-locked connectors to integrate with 
MS Fabric or comparable AI-enabled analytic platforms. 
10. Compatibility with AI-Enabled Analytics Architectures 
The reporting capability shall be compatible with modern analytics and AI architecture, 
including: 
• Lakehouse and warehouse ingestion models, enabling reporting data to land directly in 
DoWEA-managed analytic environments. 
• Semantic and analytical models that support downstream BI, AI, and machine learning 
workloads without reengineering. 
• Data pipelines, notebooks, and AI workflows, enabling DoWEA to apply advanced 
analytics, machine learning, and cross-domain insights beyond the platform’s native 
capabilities. 
Vendors shall clearly describe: 
• How reporting data is structured for analytical and AI consumption. 
• How data supports instructional, operational, and enterprise analytics use cases. 
• How platform data can be joined with non-platform data sources (e.g., finance, HR, 
logistics, cybersecurity, or operations data) in external analytics environments. 
11. Data Model Transparency & Metadata 
The vendor must provide full transparency of the reporting data model, including:  
o Tables, fields, relationships, and keys. 
o Business definitions for metrics, indicators, and calculated values. 
• A metadata catalog shall be available natively or exportable, supporting:  
o Schema discovery. 
o Data lineage from source systems through reporting outputs. 
o Field-level descriptions suitable for ingestion into enterprise metadata catalogs. 
• Any native semantic layers must be exportable, reproducible, or documentable for use in 
external AI-enabled analytic platforms. 
12. Security, Governance & Access Control 
Reporting interfaces shall comply with DoWEA security and data governance requirements, 
including:  

8 
 
o Role-based access controls aligned to SIS, HR, and enterprise roles. 
o Row-level and column-level security enforcement that is preserved or enforceable 
in external platforms. 
The solution shall support enterprise identity integration to enable:  
o Consistent authentication and authorization across the platform and external 
analytics environments. 
o Centralized logging and auditability. 
Data classification, PII tagging, retention, and minimization controls shall be preserved when 
reporting data is exposed to or consumed by AI-enabled analytic platforms. 
13. Incremental, Event-Driven & Near Real-Time Reporting 
The platform shall support incremental data extraction (e.g., change data capture or equivalent) 
to reduce latency and processing overhead.  Event driven updates via webhooks or event streams 
consumable by AI enabled platforms. 
• Examples include but are not limited to: 
o Enrollment changes,  
o Attendance updates,  
o Grade postings,  
o Intervention changes,  
o IEP status updates. 
Vendors shall identify which reporting domains support incremental delivery versus full refresh 
models.

Library of Congress

United States Copyright Office (USCO) Index Data

2026-COP-0018

OVERVIEW / BACKGROUND 

Index Data LLC custom built, developed and successfully implemented two software applications, eCO Receipts Public Interface and AD MetaSearch and a custom Z39.50 gateway to access the underlying Oracle Siebel database for the Library of Congress’ United States Copyright Office in 2009. These applications provide access and search functionality for Library patrons, Copyright staff and LC Recommending Officers to Copyright bibliographic data.  

The MasterKey platform, which is the underlying tool in the Metasearch software, was in production in Library Services as a federated search capability serving staff and meeting the needs of the general public searching Library databases.  

SCOPE

The contractor shall provide ongoing support for Copyright’s maintenance of its

customized software installation of two applications and one gateway: eCO Receipts Public Interface and Masterkey Metasearch Federated Search and the Z39.50 gateway.

REQUIREMENTS

The contractor shall provide maintenance that includes the following:

•	Review and analysis of defects reported, and changes required, scope and level of effort 	

•  Modify existing software to correct bug errors.

• Provide answers to specific technical how-to questions/concerns and bug fixes. 

Update the interface to add new database targets as needed

The core application was developed by Index Data for searching Library bibliographic and Copyright registration data through a customized materialized view Oracle database, The search user interface can be used for multiple search targets. The main searching is done by the Pazpar2 engine that was created and developed by Index Data. The following are tools and software that were used to develop and maintain these core applications: 

zSQLgate program 

Z39.50 SRU and SRW

Pazpar2 (Metasearch Engine)

YAZ Toolkit

C/C++

Perl

HTML/JavaScript

XML

SCHEDULE OF EVENTS/DELIVERABLES 

SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENTS

Support under this contract covers answers to specific technical how-to questions/concerns with bug fixes only. Note: It does not cover extended instruction beyond 15 minutes on how to use the software or perform various administrator functions, analytical help determining the best way to use the software, or enhancements or configuration changes that are considered new functionality.

Support hours are from 8:30 AM – 5:00 PM EST Monday – Friday (excluding Federal holidays)

Response Time – within 24 business hours

Resolve Time – Software maintenance as a product includes the publishing of bug/defect fixes that could be routine or emergency types via patches and updates/upgrades in function and technology to maintain the operability and usability of the software product. Furthermore, the contractor shall provide the greatest amount of lead time as reasonable to minimize the impact to usability and accessibility of the systems. 

The number of Library Technical Points of Contact (POC) shall not exceed three (3) LOC staff. 

 TESTING AND QUALITY ASSURANCE

Quality assurance will be achieved through establishing and agreeing upon scope for each bug deliverable, adhering to LOC SDLC complying with internal contractor review and stakeholder, USCCO, and COR review.     

KEY PERSONNEL

All technical staff assigned to this effort shall be considered key personnel.  In the event of key personnel reassignment, removal, or resignation, the Contractor shall provide written notification at least 30 calendar days in advance to the designated CO and COR.  This notification, at a minimum, shall include a justification statement (including proposed replacements/substitutions) in sufficient detail to permit evaluation of the impact of the proposed change on the program and its schedule.  The Contractor shall make no replacement of key personnel without prior written consent by the CO. The list of personnel (specified in an attachment to the Schedule of this contract) may, with the consent of both parties to this contract, be amended from time to time during the course of the contract to add or delete personnel, as appropriate.

	The Contractor shall identify individuals who will support the agreement. The contractor shall notify the COR one week prior to non-availability. Contractor’s away-time should not negatively impact the timely completion of a bug fix especially in the event of an emergency fix. 

	To simplify communication, all contact related to the Agreement between Index Data and the Customer must be facilitated by the COR.

Domain Name Service (DNS) directory development IAW Reference (l). 
 
b. Designates the Director, CIO and Information Technology Services (D/CIO-T), as 
the authority to manage the enterprise domain web property framework. 
 
2. D/CIO-T. 
 
a. Manages web properties residing on the enterprise domains. 
 
b. Assigns Director, Future Experience Office (D/TF), to develop NGA web property 
standards and guidelines for enterprise domains. 
 
3. D/TF. 
 
a. Establishes, assigns, and maintains DNS guidelines and standards. 
 
b. Maintains NGA web style guidance to ensure a consistent user experience across 
enterprise domains. 
 
c. Reviews, assumes control of, and removes NGA web properties that are not 
compliant with the standards and guidelines of this Instruction. 
 
d. Promotes usage of best practices to mitigate privacy risks and effectively protect 
personally identifiable information (PII) collected, stored, or transmitted on NGA web 
properties. (Reference (m)) 
 
e. Maintains the NGA Web Guidance and Resources website (hereinafter referred to 
as the Online Resources), located at https://www.intranet.nga.ic.gov/web/. 
 
4. Director, Office of Corporate Communications. 
 
a. Manages the review of all NGA products and information that are publicly 
released (where applicable), all external marketing (e.g., social media, correspondence 
with the press, and promotional products), and all writing for public release for 
adherence to NGA messaging standards on public-facing web properties available over 
the World Wide Web IAW Reference (n). 
 
b. Ensures that information released to the public is unclassified IAW Reference (n).

7

c. Coordinates and interacts with media and external sources regarding NGA web 
properties IAW Reference (n). 
 
5. Senior Component Official for Privacy collaborates with the D/CIO-T Chief 
Information Officer to ensure that protections and disclaimers are in place for web 
properties that collect, store, or transmit PII IAW Reference (m). 
 
6. Information Developers and Designers. 
 
a. Comply with web standards and guidance provided in the Online Resources when 
developing, modifying, and maintaining NGA web properties on enterprise domains. 
 
b. Comply with all header and footer guidance provided at the Online Resources, 
Content Delivery Network for all NGA web properties. 
 
c. Format and publish NGA web properties that enable all users to retrieve and use 
information, including Section 508 compliance, IAW References (d), (l), and (q). 
  

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
8 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
ENCLOSURE 3 
 
NGA WEB PROPERTIES GUIDANCE 
 
1. Workflow processes for requesting and developing NGA web properties are provided 
in the Web Governance Concept of Operations (CONOPS), the relevant Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs), and this Instruction.  
 
2. The CONOPS, SOPs, and links to style guides, design elements, and best practices 
are provided in the Online Resources. 
 
3. Web Design Style Guidance. 
 
a. NGA web properties meet and maintain high standards of effectiveness and 
usability to provide quality information that is readily discoverable and accessible to 
authorized users. (References (d) and (q)) 
 
b. The UXD Web Style Guide is a resource to help developers and software 
engineers overcome common design problems when creating a new web property. A 
core function of the Online Resources is to provide assistance in the creation of a more 
consistent “look and feel” across NGA web properties. The Online Resources UXD Web 
Style Guide is located on the following networks: 
 
NGANet/Joint Worldwide Intelligence 
Communications System (JWICS) 
https://www.intranet.nga.ic.gov/web/ 
http://design.nga.ic.gov 
Secret Internet Protocol Router 
Network (SIPRNet) https://design.nga.smil.mil 
Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU) https://designsystem.digital.gov/ 
http://design.nga.mil 
 
c. The efficient, effective, and consistent use of NGA web properties and web 
services standards promotes a more citizen-centered Government and user-friendly 
experience. 
 
4. Writing in Plain Language. 
 
a. Plain language and communication have many benefits. Avoiding vagueness and 
unnecessary complexity makes it easier for users to understand information and use 
services. Plain writing assists the user in complying with applicable requirements to 
better understand the NGA web property. (References (b) and (j)) 
 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
9 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must conform to the plain writing 
memorandums and referenced materials identified in the content guidance provided in 
the Online Resources. 
 
5. Copyright Protections. 
 
a. Copyright is a form of legal protection grounded in the US Constitution and 
granted by law for original works created in any medium. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must comply with the US Copyright 
laws and referenced materials IAW Reference (f). Copyright guidance is provided in the 
Online Resources. 
 
6. Accessibility Guidance. 
 
a. Accessibility is one of the most important aspects of web development. 
Accessibility allows the greatest number of users to view content more completely. 
Users have a better experience if accessibility is built into web properties from the 
beginning. 
 
b. US Code and Public Laws require Federal Agencies to ensure electronic and 
information technology (EIT) is accessible to people with disabilities. Section 508 of the 
Workforce Investment Act of 1998 applies to all Federal agencies when developing, 
procuring, maintaining, or using EIT. (References (a) and (q)) 
 
c. NGA web properties on enterprise domains comply with Section 508 
requirements. Accessibility guidance and tools are located on networks identified in 
paragraph 3.b. of this Enclosure. 
 
d. For overall questions regarding Section 508 compliance, contact the Section 508 
coordinator at NGASection508Coordinator@coe.ic.gov. (References (a) and (q)) 
 
7. Analytics, Performance Metrics, and Feedback Guidance. 
 
a. Web analytics are the collection, analysis, and communication of web data for 
purposes of understanding and optimizing web usage. Web analytics measure web 
traffic and assess the effectiveness of a web property. The resulting analysis helps the 
organization determine the value of its content or an application, and provides insight to 
improve its offerings and the user experience. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains should have a web analytics 
collection capability. (Reference (d)) Web analytic solutions are provided in the Online 
Resources. 
 
8. Security Guidance.

a. NGA web properties provide Government information and services to support the 
performance of NGA’s mission. Security and risk management are essential functions 
incorporated into the lifecycle of NGA web properties, including classification markings, 
public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates, and hypertext transfer protocol secure 
(HTTPS) IAW References (c), (k) and (p). 
 
b. Intelligence sources, methods, and activities are safeguarded IAW Reference (i). 
Additional information for classification marking requirements is provided in the Online 
Resources. 
 
c. Websites, services, and online resources available over the public internet that 
are maintained and operated in whole or in part by NGA are provided through HTTPS. 
(References (c) and (k)) Additional information for HTTPS implementation is provided in 
the Online Resources. 
 
9. Search and Discovery Guidance. 
 
a. Search functions are universal and an expected website feature commonly used 
to find information. Search engine optimization (SEO) is critical to reaching users who 
primarily rely on commercial search engines. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must provide search capabilities IAW 
References (d) and (h). D/TF provides search solutions, how to incorporate a search 
capability into an NGA web property, and how to maximize discovery of web assets via 
SEO and NGA search tools. Additional information is provided in the Online Resources. 
 
 
c. NGA web properties on enterprise domains are published to a registry to assist 
search and discovery of content and services. Search and Discovery Guides are 
available in the Online Resources. 
 
d. NGA web properties on enterprise domains contain metadata tags to assist 
search and discovery. Search and Discovery Guides are located on networks identified 
in paragraph 3.b. within this Enclosure provided in the Online Resources. 
 
10. NGA Dissemination on Domain Networks Guidance. 
 
a. IC computer domain networks disseminate intelligence information. NGA has 
multiple IC domain networks based on classification. Web properties are stored on 
servers that are connected to the domain networks and are reachable using DNS. 
When the DNS is translated into an Internet Protocol (IP) address, an information 
system (IS) can pinpoint the location of another IS/server where the web property is 
stored.

1.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), has a 
requirement for brand name Medicopia software licenses and Brand name Zebra 
Printers, and accessories. The Lattice Medicopia software application is used for 
positive patient identification (PPID) during specimen collecting. The Lattice Medicopia 
runs a Microsoft Windows Server 2019 operating system(s) and Microsoft SQL Server 
2019 database on the VA Enterprise network. Medicopia is a software solution provided 
by Lattice / DCS to allow positive patient identification (PPI) at the patient bedside with 
barcode scanning of the wristband before specimen collection. Medicopia is VA TRM 
approved, requires no modifications to VISTA or CPRS, and satisfies the Joint 
commission recommendation for PPID and printing labels at the bedside. A barcode 
scanner is used at the patients' bedside to scan their wristband, ensuring they are the 
correct patient. The mobile printer will only generate the specimen labels after positive 
patient identification. Medicopia can receive and display VISTA/CPRS lab orders and 
provides a method to print specimen labels in the presence of the patient with bar-
coded stickers. Medicopia tracks accurate data regarding collection date/time, collector, 
specimens, etc. Additional workflow assistance and data auditing services are also 
included, for supervisor and hospital informatics use. 
 
The proposed action will require the purchase of 40 Zebra printers, model ZQ610, 40-
each Zebra AC adapter, 40-each USB cables, one each Zebra wi-fi display android 
processor, one each communication cable, one each communication cable, one each 
USB power supply, 40-each ONECARE battery maintenance plan, 40-each POCC 
staging mobile ZQ61, 40-each combination mounting of ZQ610 customer supplied 
antenna bracket and monitor inset adapters. 
 
The Contractor shall provide installation services to perform the following; Zebra printer 
ZQ610 mounted on the Howard Medical Cart which connects to the VA computer via 
USB cable. Lattice Medicopia client software is installed on the VA computer to access 
Medicopia middleware to print specimen labels on the ZD610 Zebra printers.   
 
The Period of Performance shall be one 12-month base period plus four 12-month 
option periods for licenses and maintenance as described above. The delivery of 
hardware shall be within 45 days after receipt and processing of the delivery order.

1.1  SPECIFIC TASKS AND DELIVERABLES  
 
The Contractor shall provide the following: 
 
o HL7 ADT (Admit, Discharge, Transfer) messages. These messages 
are standardized, high-volume electronic messages used to communicate patient 
demographic and visit status changes between hospital information systems 
(HIS), Electronic Medical Records (EMR), and ancillary systems. They act as 
real-time updates ensuring all care systems share consistent data on patient 
movement, location, and registration. The server uses it to connect to VISTA and 
send/translate data back and forth from VISTA and the Zebra printers. If the 
interface goes down, the staff will implement their back-up plan, which they will 
devise, while HTM and OIT work with VISTA teams to bring the interface up. 
o LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) in Active Directory (AD) is the 
core, open-standard protocol used to query, read, and modify information stored 
within the Microsoft AD database. While Active Directory is the database itself, 
LDAP acts as the language applications use to authenticate users and locate 
network resources. 
o A Laboratory Information System (LIS) interface is a software connection that 
allows laboratory instruments and computer systems to exchange data 
automatically. It connects the LIS with Electronic Health Records (EHRs), 
Hospital Information Systems (HIS), and analytical instruments, eliminating 
manual data entry, accelerating reporting, and reducing errors. 
o The Contractor shall provide Implementation schedule and provide project 
management to ensure the project is on schedule and all software is functional 
and working, printers are installed and specimen labels are able to be printed in 
the various wards.  
o The Contractor shall hold weekly status meetings from project start through go-
live. 
 
1.2       TRAINING  
 
The contractor shall provide both classroom and on-site training for “super-users’ at the 
facility. Training sessions shall be for up to 16 trainees for one hour in duration. Training 
documentation will be provided electronically. The Contractor shall provide 
comprehensive training plan to include how to operate the equipment, what happens if 
equipment experiences work stoppages, how to print bar code labels and provide 
training materials which may include brochures, website information, manuals and any 
combination of these to ensure an immersive learning experience.

1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Information and Technology (OIT) 
Product Delivery Services (PDS) delivers integrated digital capabilities that support 
Veteran care nationwide.  Within PDS, the Health Services Portfolio’s Healthcare 
Environment and Logistics Management (HELM) Product Line (PL) implements, 
modernizes, sustains, standardizes, and streamlines software solutions for supply 
chain, logistics, expendables, assets, inventory, facilities, prosthetics, and 
environmental compliance HELM provides the enterprise capabilities needed to support 
a unified, efficient, and data driven supply chain and logistics environment across VA. 
VA does not currently operate with standardized, enterprise-wide supply chain business 
processes or technical systems. Numerous functional and capability gaps have been 
identified through Government Accountability Office (GAO) and Office of Inspector 
General (OIG) audits and internal assessments. VA requires accurate, reliable, and 
accessible supply chain data to improve ordering, fulfillment, and operational 
performance.  These needs align with VA’s Strategic Supply Chain (SC) Prioritization 
and Digital Modernization Strategy, which emphasize modernizing legacy systems, 
strengthening cybersecurity and resilience, improving data quality, enhancing user 
experience for logisticians, and establishing consistent, interoperable processes across 
VHA, VACO, VBA, and NCA. 
 
VA currently relies on approximately 63 disparate legacy systems across 174 sites, 
resulting in fragmented operations, limited enterprise visibility, and inefficiencies. 
Standardization and modernization are required to transform Supply Chain systems into 
integrated, enterprise-wide system of systems that supports responsive, efficient clinical 
and nonclinical supply operations. 
 
To meet mission needs, VA requires a full service, standardized, scalable healthcare 
logistics software solutions with modern supply chain management capabilities.  A 
unified digital environment shall enable lifecycle management efficiencies, data driven 
decision making, and seamless integration with major initiatives such as the Electronic 
Health Record Modernization (EHRM) and Financial Management Business 
Transformation (FMBT) programs.  HELM’s mission and modernization efforts directly 
support these enterprise requirements by advancing cloud-based logistics capabilities, 
modernizing legacy applications, and enabling consistent processes across VA’s supply 
chain functions.  In addition to modernization activities, several HELM products require 
ongoing Operation & Maintenance (O&M) support, enhancements, operation stability, 
security and Lifecyle support.  
 
HELM is organized into five subproduct lines (SPL): Environmental and Healthcare 
Management, Healthcare Technology and Asset Management, Expendable Inventory 
Management, Prosthetics, and Technical Services. Additional products scheduled such

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
21 April 2026 
 
AIRFIELD AUTOMATION SYSTEM (AFAS) SUPPORT 
AIR FORCE FLIGHT STANDARDS AGENCY 
TINKER AFB OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA 
 
 
1.0 SCOPE 
 
This task will require the contractor to provide the support necessary to perform support and 
engineering services to accomplish technical software support for the maintenance of the Airfield 
Automation System (AFAS) software system.  
 
1.1 GENERAL 
 
The Air Force Flight Standards Agency (AFFSA)/Airfield Automation Directorate requires Information 
Technology technical support with regards to Airfield Automation System (AFAS), a product of Systems 
Atlanta, Inc (SAI), software suite.   
The system is designed to meet the information needs of air traffic control (ATC) and airfield 
management (AM) personnel, both military and civilian. The AFAS resources in each Radar Approach 
Control (RAPCON) and/or Air Traffic Control Tower (ATCT) are a collection of Commercial Off The Shelf 
(COTS) general purpose systems that provide a centralized repository of information used to provide 
decision support tools, aid in planning purposes and maintain situational awareness for air traffic 
controllers. AFAS provides rapid access to a wide array of information from multiple sources, integrated 
for display and distribution via a single system.  
 
1.2 TASK EXECUTION PLAN 
 
1.2.1 Task 1:  Telephone Support 
 
The contractor shall provide telephone software support (both engineering and product technical 
support) direct to HQ AFFSA AFAS Program Manager and all AFAS customers.  
 
Contractor Help Desk personnel shall diagnose and resolve system and maintenance issues related to 
AFAS software configuration, SAI database building, AFAS network infrastructure, SAI software and 
associated AFAS support tools.   
 
Engineering support shall be provided by the contractor’s engineering staff to resolve AFAS software 
issues including those involving changes in operating system and security changes required for 
continued Air Force network operations. The contractor shall also provide reconfigurations of AFAS 
license files, as necessitated by changes in local network operations.  The contractor shall provide 
original and replacement configuration disks and software documentation, as needed.  
 
Product technical support shall be provided by the contractor’s training staff to resolve issues involving 
utilization of AFAS, using software features, creating and managing the database, configuring profiles, 
organizing data most efficiently for rapid access, and other product use knowledge areas. 

 
 
 
Contractor Help Desk personnel shall receive and log calls, fill out a Customer Service Request (CSR) 
form, and forward the CSR to the appropriate SAI resource for resolution.  Response time to each 
support request that is logged within the hours of support coverage shall be within two hours not to 
exceed twelve hours.  A monthly electronic CSR report identifying problems, date opened/closed and 
solution shall be provided to the AFAS Program Manager as well as notifying AFAS Program Manager by 
email each time a CSR is opened. Contractor format is acceptable.    
 
The contractor shall be available to provide telephone support for 8-continuous hours (eg., 0800-1600, 
0900-1700, Eastern Time), Monday through Friday, except contractor observed holidays. If support 
requires the direct involvement of Air Force personnel at overseas locations, telephone support shall be 
provided on a pre-scheduled basis to cover normal duty hours of the Air Force Location. 
 
1.2.2 Task 2:  Site Configuration/Reconfiguration  
 
AFAS location site configuration and reconfigurations generated as defined below: 
 
• What’s Up Gold (WUG) Remote Maintenance Monitor (RMM) reconfiguration(s) due to 
geographic moves of AFAS equipment 
• Global Naming Table (GNT) changes and updates 
• AFAS Workstation name changes 
• Proxy Server changes 
• DNS Server changes 
• IP Address changes 
 
Configuration changes will not be made until approved by AFAS Program Manager.  Configuration files 
to be delivered to applicable site and AFAS Program Manager.   
 
1.2.3 Task 3:  Engineering Services 
 
The contractor shall provide engineering services for AFAS as identified by AFAS Program Manager. 
These services may include activities such as: 
• Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs)  
• Catastrophic System Failure that exceed telephone support Technicians 
• IDS data page template designs 
• Remediation of system deficiencies of the core software 
• Software maintenance patching services 
• On-site technical support when needed 
 
Engineering services will not be provided until approved by AFAS Program Manager.   
 
1.2.4 Task 4: Image Creation 
 

 
 
One SDC/AFAS Image (Kiosk) based on Win 11 Operating System utilizing the current AF SDC that will 
include AFAS software and adaptations to make the AFAS workstation suitable for an operational air traffic 
environment and Win 11 patches available at the time of image creation.   
1.2.5 Continuation of Essential Department of Defense (DoD) Contractor Services During Crisis:  This 
requirement has been determined not to be essential and does not require continued support during a 
crisis as defined in DFARS 252.237-7023.  
 
1.3 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE/PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
 
The period of performance is twelve months beginning May 23, 2026 and ending May 22, 2027 plus 4 
option years.  Therefore, the total period of performance with options will run from May 23, 2026 
through May 22, 2031.       
 
1.4 GOVERNMENT FURNISHED EQUIPMENT/MATERIALS/FACILITIES 
 
N/A 
 
1.5 INSPECTION AND ACCEPTANCE 
 
Acceptance of invoice will be made by HQ AFFSA/AFAS COR (Contracting Officer Representative). 
 
2.0 APPLICABLE DOCUMENTS 
 
None 
 
3.0 REQUIREMENTS 
 
This task shall require the contractor to provide the support necessary to perform the following 
functions: 
• Provide first level support to all current AFAS systems and locations to include the following: 
• Resolve AFAS software issues including those involving issues caused by changes in 
operating system and security changes required for continued Air Force network operations. 
• Issues involving utilization of the AFAS, using software features, creating and managing the 
database, configuring profiles, organizing data most efficiently for rapid access in air traffic 
control environment, and other contractor product use knowledge areas. 
• Maintain current AFAS interfaces. 
• Generate new AFAS software configurations/license files approved by AFAS Program Manager 
and deliver to the applicable field unit and AFAS Program Manager. 
 
4.0 DELIVERABLE 
 
The contractor shall be aware that in the absence of any contract requirement from the Service 
Summary does not detract from its enforceability nor limit the rights or remedies of the Government 
under any other provision of the contract.  The contractor shall ensure the following service methods 
are achieved as follows:   
 
Service Summary (SS) Requirement 

 
 
The contractor shall ensure the performance objectives, performance thresholds, and support for 
surveillance methods are achieved as follows: 
 
Performance Objectives and Thresholds 
The contractor shall achieve performance thresholds identified in Table 2.1 of this PWS. 
 
NOTE 1:  The performance thresholds are designed to: 
 a. Align contractor performance objectives.  
 b. Focus on critical success factors in meeting performance objectives. 
 c. Reflect performance goals. 
 d. Promote continuous improvement in performance.  
NOTE 2:  The AFAS Program Manager will exercise surveillance over the performance thresholds. 
 
Surveillance Methods 
The contractor shall support the AFAS Program Manager’s surveillance methods as identified below: 
 a. Random sampling of recurring service outputs. 
 b. One hundred percent inspection of the output. 
 c. Periodic inspection of the process or output. 
 d. Customer complaints. 
 
NOTE:  The AFAS Program Manager may use a combination of surveillance methods, as defined above, 
to monitor contractor’s performance even though the specific surveillance method is not called out in 
Table 2.1.  
 
Contractor Performance Evaluation 
The contractor shall be aware that the evaluation of performance will occur when AFAS Program 
manager evaluates the service of the contractor to determine whether or not it meets the performance 
measures of the contract. 
 
NOTE:  In the event the performance measure is not met, the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) 
will issue written notification to the contractor.  In those cases, the PCO will take appropriate measures.

Contractor employees shall identify themselves as contractor personnel by introducing themselves or 
being introduced as contractor personnel and displaying distinguishing badges or other visible 
identification for meetings with Government personnel.  In addition, contractor personnel shall 
appropriately identify themselves as contractor employees in telephone conversations and in formal 
and informal written correspondence.   
 
5.1 Contractor 

 
 
 
The contractor shall prepare one combined invoice and receiving report through Wide Area Workflow 
(WAWF) online system.  The invoice shall be broken out according to contract service.  Registration 
information, invoicing procedures, software downloads and web based training are available at.  The 
contractor shall have an electronic business point of contact listed in their Central Registration (CCR) 
listed prior to using WAWF. 
 
5.1.2 Contractor Manpower Reporting (CMR):  The Contractor shall report ALL Contractor labor hours, to 
include sub-Contractor labor hours, required for the performance of the services provided under this 
contract via a secure data collection site.  The Contractor is required to completely fill in all required 
data fields at the website https://afcmra.dmdc.osd.mil.  
 
The Contractor shall report all labor hours executed during the Period of Performance (PoP) for each 
Government Fiscal Year (FY) which runs from 1 October through 30 September the following year.  
Although the labor hours executed may be completed any time during the FY, all data shall be 
completed no later than (NLT) 31 October of each calendar year.  Contractors may direct questions to 
the CMR help desk email listed at https://afcmra.dmdc.osd.mil. 
 
5.2 Government 
 
5.2.1 The contractor shall notify the designated government representative via e-mail when the invoice 
is input in the WAWF system.  They will either approve the invoice or coordinate with the contractor if it 
is not acceptable.   
 
5.2.2 The government representative is Ms. Leslie Westlund, HQ AFFSA/FM, 405-734-4891.
