# Questions Answers w/ SOO Para. Reference
1
Point of clarification for 1.5.1.2 - will installations without local IT support require the vendor provide 
any additional vulnerability scanning and management capabilities? We noted the previous response 
that the request is to provide the critical oversight, analysis, remediation guidance and hands-on 
technical support to manage the vulnerability lifecycle, not on operating the testing tools themselves.
No additional vulnerability scanning and management capabilities are required.  
While tool provision is out of scope (SOO 1.5.2), the contractor is responsible for 
the technical support for ongoing vulnerability management, including monitoring, 
lifecycle management and remediation guidance, and hands-on support as 
required by installations, both remote and onsite as needed (SOO 1.5.1.2, 
4.1.3.1.1).
2
Is AFSVC open to a fully vendor-managed model for remote security operations (SOC, SIEM)?
No. The SOO outlines a collaborative model to empower local staff, not a fully 
vendor-managed operation. Your role is to augment, not replace, local personnel 
(SOO 1.3.1, 2.2.3).
3
To what degree is in-person / hands-on support expected, and for what geographic areas? Would a 
proposed solution for quarterly travel be acceptable, or is the vendor expected to provide permanent 
local staff to support installations?
On-site and remote assistance is required (SOO 3.1). Expect hands-on support at 
~20-30 of 104 locations (SOO 1.4, 1.5.1.2). Travel is as-needed for physical audits 
and audit preparedness; permanent local staff are not required (SOO 6.4.2).
4
What level of security clearance is expected for vendor personnel? Will all vendor staff engaged in 
supporting AFSVC require a Tier 1? Will any vendor staff require a Tier 3?
Tier 1 is sufficient, most of the work is unclassified (SOO 6.6.1). Refer to SOO 
6.7.2.2, Contractor personnel shall not be assigned to perform duties within IAT-II 
or IAT-III, and or requiring “Limited Privileged Access” such as system or database 
administration rights, to any NAFI application or network.
5
Will vendor interact with any CUI / does the proposed solution require a CMMC certification?
Yes, the vendor will handle CUI and require training per SOO 6.6.3. Refer to SOO 
3.2 Contractor Qualifications.
6
Are all assets centrally managed (e.g., centralized patching tools, endpoint management, 
configuration management)?If not, identify unmanaged or partially managed assets.
The objective is to achieve a "proactive, centrally-governed security posture" (SOO 
1.3.1), which indicates assets are not currently all centrally managed. The SOO 
notes that "critical gaps in security tools and on-site technical support prevent a 
proactive, centrally managed defense" (SOO 1.2.1). 
7 Are legacy or end of life systems present? If yes, list known unsupported software or systems and 
any business constraints.
Any in-scope legacy or end of life systems will be upgraded by August 2026.  Many 
are scoped out using P2PE terminals.
8
Are externally facing assets included in scope?(Web servers, VPNs, firewalls, cloud services, etc.)
External assets are out of scope of this SOO, penetration testing is being 
conducted, per SOO 1.5.2.  The SOO requires expertise with firewalls, VPNs (SOO 
3.2.1.4), and cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, and GCP (SOO 3.2.1.9). 
9
Is there any preference for fee arrangements - per endpoint, hourly, fixed fee, etc.
The contract will be fixed fee, based on deliverables (SOO 3.1). See Contract 
Admin Data, Paragraph 4.
10 Will any cloud workloads be in-scope? Do you utilize any cloud service providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, 
GCP) for any part of your payment processing environment?
Yes, some Aloha Cloud is in CDE scope. Required expertise in AWS, Azure, and 
GCP, and the directive to prioritize cloud-based tools, confirm cloud workloads are 
in scope (SOO 3.2.1.9, 4.1.1.3).
11
 Many installations have successfully achieved PCI compliance using validated P2PE solutions, 
hosted payment pages, or centralized enterprise payment gateways. Has AFSVC evaluated whether 
standardizing one or more of these proven, lower-scope approaches—where 
appropriate—could enhance consistency across installations while reducing lifecycle costs and 
simplifying compliance sustainment, as an alternative to deploying and maintaining separate 
tool suites at each location?
Standardization is underway, as AFSVC has moved from a decentralized to 
centralized approach. An enterprise Tool suite solution, where applicable, is being 
requested in this SOO (4.1.1).
12 The SOO currently directs the contractor to recommend and implement a “complete enterprise tool 
suite” (SIEM, DLP, MFA, etc.) and to prioritize “modern, automated, and cloud-based tools.”  As a full-
service QSA with experience delivering thousands of services to similar environments outlined in both 
the original and current SOO we find that the scope in the first SOO to more cost effective and timely. 
Would AFSVC consider modifying the requirement to include, as part of Phase 1, a QSA-
performed assessment that delivers a validated scope-reduction roadmap and presents 
multiple compliant implementation approaches—including both tool-enabled and scope-
optimized models—along with a side-by-side 3–5 year total cost of ownership analysis to 
support AFSVC decision making?
The SOO requires the contractor to conduct a "Gap Analysis" and deliver a 
"Solution Implementation Strategy" for a "complete enterprise tool suite" (SOO 
4.1.1.1, 4.1.1.4). The contractor's role is to provide technical support, not to 
perform a QSA function, although collaboration with a QSA vendor is expected 
(SOO 4.1.3.2.2).
13
The SOO emphasizes on-site technical support, 24/7 monitoring, ongoing tool management, and 
sustainment across up to 30 installations. Has AFSVC conducted, or would it consider conducting, 
a comparative analysis of total lifecycle cost—including personnel, licensing, maintenance, 
training, and option years—across alternative compliant approaches, such as tool-intensive 
implementations versus scope reduction and process simplification, which for many federal 
and DoD organizations has historically reduced compliance effort by 70–90%, to ensure long-
term operational sustainability and resource alignment?
The SOO establishes the requirement to deploy and manage a standardized tool 
suite (SOO 1.5.1). A comparative cost analysis of alternative compliance 
approaches is not a specified deliverable within the SOO. The contractor is 
expected to provide a detailed cost analysis for the recommended tools as part of 
the implementation strategy (SOO 4.1.1.4.2). 
A P2PE based scope reduction strategy is in place, while certain components 
remain within full PCI scope.  Supporting data and documentation will be provided 
upon contract award.  
14
The SOO states that the AFSVC intends to award all phases to a single vendor but that Phases 2 and 4 
are at the AFSVC’s discretion based on Phase 1 results. Would AFSVC consider adding language to 
allow the Phase 1 contractor to recommend and potentially execute a QSA-led scope-reduction 
strategy, as well as evaluate multiple compliant execution paths, so the AFSVC can select the 
approach that best aligns with cost, risk tolerance, and sustainment objectives—potentially 
eliminating the need for Phases 2 and 4—prior to proceeding to subsequent phases?
The Government is currently engaged with a QSA firm; however, the expectation 
is that you will collabrate to develop and execute a forward-looking strategy. 
15
DoD cybersecurity guidance (e.g., Zero Trust principles, Cloud Security Playbook elements, and 
integration with existing DISN/DoDIN frameworks) emphasizes risk-based, least-privilege controls 
over broad tooling deployment. How does the SOO's focus on implementing and managing a full 
suite of security tools (SIEM, DLP, MFA across CDEs) align with these mandates, and would the 
AFSVC be open to requiring Phase 1 recommendations to demonstrate compatibility with DoD-
wide security architectures to avoid redundant or conflicting implementations?
Refer to SOO  1.2 Background and 1.3 Objective.  As part of the Phase 1: Gap 
Analysis and Remediation (SOO 4.1.1), AFSVC is requesting a strategy and 
recommendation for the required  security tools and services to comply with PCI 
DSS (SOO 4.1.1.3 and 4.1.1.4).  The solution must align with DoD standards, 
including NIST SP 800-53, CISA directives, and the DoD RMF (SOO 6.9.2) while 
closing PCI control gaps and avoiding redundancy. For further clarification, the DAF 
NAFIs process payment card transactions over locally managed commercial 
netwoks rather than the NIPRNet.
16
PCI DSS best practices for sustainment emphasize repeatable, low-effort processes over complex 
tooling. Has the AFSVC evaluated whether the proposed enterprise tool suite—including 
licensing, configuration, monitoring, and update requirements—aligns with sustainable 
compliance models observed in other federal environments, and would AFSVC consider 
incorporating long-term sustainment factors, such as operational complexity, maintenance 
demands, and staffing dependencies, into Phase 1 deliverables to support stable and durable 
compliance outcomes?”
A PCI DSS compliant recommendation is part of  SOO 4.1.1, Phase 1: Gap Analysis 
and Remediation
17
Should the Contractor plan for steady-state operations only, or include surge support for assessment
cycles, remediation efforts, or incident response events?
The contractor must plan for both. The SOO requires "Ongoing Technical Support" 
(SOO 4.1.3), including "24/7 Support Services" (SOO 4.1.3.1.3), "Tier 2/3 
Sustainment Support" for escalations (SOO 2.2.5), incident response assistance 
(SOO 4.1.3.4.2.4), and "PCI DSS Assessment Preparation Support" (SOO 4.1.3.2).
18 Are clearance requirements (e.g., Public Trust, Secret) required at contract start, and will the 
Government sponsor clearances if needed?
All clearances will be sponsored by the Govt once the Contract is awarded. See 
SOO Para 6.7. To ensure all Personnel needing background checks meet the 
requirements.
19 What are the expected incident response roles and responsibilities for the Contractor (e.g., triage, 
escalation, remediation support), and how will these integrate with Government teams?
The contractor is responsible for "hands-on technical support for 
ongoing...incident response" (SOO 1.5.1.2) and must have experience with 
"containment, eradication, and recovery" (SOO 3.2.1.3). Suspected incidents must 
             20 Are there minimum staffing levels, labor categories, or experience thresholds that the Government 
will use to determine technical acceptability?
AFSVC is seeking industry to provide this answer.
21 Is a Facility Clearance (FCL) required at time of proposal or award, and if so, will the Government 
sponsor the prime or subcontractor for FCL?
All clearances will be sponsored by the Govt once the Contract is awarded. See 
SOO Para 6.7. To ensure all Personnel needing background checks meet the 
requirements.
22 Through which channels do you accept payments (e.g., E-commerce, Card-Present/Retail, or Mail 
Order/Telephone Order)?
CDE scoping and inventory documentation will be provided upon contract award. 
Refer to SOO 4.1. 
23 Approximately how many credit/debit card transactions do you process annually across all 
channels?
Over 13 million annual payment card transactions (SOO 1.4).
24 Are you operating as a Merchant (taking payments for your own goods/services), a Service Provider 
(processing on behalf of others), or both?
AFSVC is a Merchant (SOO 1.1.1).
25 Does your organization store, process, or transmit Primary Account Numbers (PAN) in any electronic 
format?
Yes. The purpose of this SOO is to ensure full security of the CDE (SOO 1.1.1, 
1.3.1).
26
Do you store any Sensitive Authentication Data (SAD) after authorization (e.g., CVV, CID, or PIN data)?
No. Sensitive Authentication Data (SAD) is not stored.
27 For E-commerce, do you use a third-party redirect (like a hosted payment page), an iFrame, or do you 
capture the data directly on your own servers?
Hosted payment pages are used for individual activity ecommerce solutions; an 
enterprise eCommerce solution is in development. 
28 Is your Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) currently segmented from the rest of your corporate 
network, or is the entire network in scope?
The CDE is segmented.
29
Do any third-party vendors or partners have remote access to your internal network or the CDE?
Yes.
30 Do you use physical Point of Sale (POS) terminals or hardware security modules (HSM)? If so, are they 
PCI-validated?
Physical POS are in use and in the process of full PCI-validation.
31 If you take orders over the phone (MOTO), are calls recorded, and if so, is card data being captured in 
those recordings?
Calls are not recorded in the case of phone orders.
32 Can you provide a list of all third parties that could impact the security of your cardholder data (e.g., 
web hosting, data centers, managed firewall providers)?
Third party details can be delivered upon contract award.
33 Do you have an up-to-date network diagram and data flow diagram that specifically identifies all 
cardholder data flows?
We do have an up-to-date standardized network diagram.
34 Is your IT or security infrastructure managed in-house, or is it outsourced to a Managed Service 
Provider (MSP)?
The SOO implies a mixed environment. This contract is required due to a lack of 
specialized on-site IT support at many locations (SOO 2.0).
35 What was your most recent PCI DSS validation level (e.g., SAQ A, SAQ D, or Level 1 ROC), and when 
was it last completed?
AFSVC NAFI is a Level 1 Merchant and is currently undergoing a SAQ-D assessment 
with a QSA firm. Specific assessment results are considered sensitive and are not 
disclosed publicly.
36
What kind of service you are looking for? A GAP, Advisory, or a final assessment?
See SOO.
PCI DSS Compliance Technical Support & Sustainment (AF Installations) Questions and Answers 19 March 2026

37
For these 104 locations, what kind of locations do we have? Are these data centers, stores? Is 
required clearance to access these locations? If yes, which constrains are required?
The locations are DAF NAFI enterprise Services programs, including food, fitness, 
childcare, lodging, and recreation (SOO 1.1.1). Clearance requirements are

GENERAL INFORMATION

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

Jeron Nurse call support services 

Veterans Health Affairs, Network Contracting Office 5, is issuing this Notice of Intent to Sole Source in order to identify any potential sources that have the resources and capabilities to provide Help Desk Support Services for the Jeron Nurse Call System, including the Software Support and Assurance, Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center,1Medical Center Drive, Clarksburg, WV 26301.

The government is contemplating a Base +4 option period Firm Fixed Price contract to satisfy this requirement and meet the needs of the Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center.

INTERESTED & CAPABLE RESPONSES

NCO 5 is seeking responses from businesses that are interested in this procurement and consider themselves to have the resources, rights, and capabilities necessary to provide these services.  

Please respond with your:

•	Business name 

•	Business type 

•	Socio-economic status (e.g., Veteran-Owned, Woman-Owned, Disadvantaged Small Business, 8(a), etc.) 

•	Person of contact (including telephone number & email address)

•	GSA Contract number if applicable 

•	DUNS number and SAM UEI number

•	Capability statement

*	MUST PROVIDE Authorized Distributor Letter OR RESPONSE WILL BE DISCARDED 

Responses must be submitted by 8:00 AM (EST) Wednesday, April 29, 2026.  Responses to the information requested above may be submitted via email to jennifer.elkins2@va.gov No telephone calls will be accepted.

DISCLAIMERS

This Notice of Intent to Sole Source does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this notice that is marked proprietary will be handled accordingly in accordance with (IAW) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.201(e).  Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses incurred associated with responding to this RFI.

This Special Notice of Intent to Sole Source is for planning purposes ONLY.  The results of this notice will assist in the development of (1) the requirement, and (2) the acquisition strategy (e.g., small business set-aside, full and open competition, etc.).  VA assumes no responsibility for any costs incurred associated with the preparation of responses submitted as a result of this notice.

SCOPE OF WORK: Jeron Nurse Call Support Services

Louis A. Johnson VA Medical Center

1 Medical Center Dr.

Clarksburg, WV 26301

Contractor shall provide Help Desk Support Services for the Jeron Nurse Call System, including the Software Support and Assurance, located at the VAMC in Clarksburg, WV. All services shall be provided in accordance with the specifications, terms and conditions contained herein.

Period of Performance: The Period of Performance is for a base year plus four option years.

Base Year Period: 		May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2027

Option Year 1:			May 1, 2027 to April 30, 2028

Option Year 2:			May 1, 2028 to April 30, 2029

Option Year 3:			May 1, 2029 to April 30, 2030

Option Year 4:			May 1, 2030 to April 30, 2031

DESCRIPTION/SPECIFICATIONS/WORK STATEMENT

SERVICES: 

Contractor shall furnish the following:

Support and Help Desk Services for the Nurse call System, located at the VAMC in Clarksburg, WV.

24/7 Support hours

Software updates are provided.

2.  DEFINITIONS/ACRONYMS:

Biomedical Engineering - Supervisor or COR designee.

CO - Contracting Officer.

COR - Contracting Officer's Technical Representative.

PM - Preventive Maintenance Inspection.  Services which are periodic in nature and are required to maintain the equipment in such condition that it may be operated in accordance with its intended design and functional capacity with minimal incidence of malfunction or operative conditions.  Service shall consist of calibration and testing in accordance with the manufacturer’s latest established service procedures to ensure operation of equipment within manufacturer’s or VA’s performance specifications, whichever is the most rigorous.  PM includes cleaning, inspecting lubricating and testing all equipment.  All equipment shall be operated at least one complete operating cycle at the end of each PM

CM – Corrective Maintenance. Maintenance tasks that are undertaken to identify, isolate and repair a fault in order to restore equipment, a machine or a system to an operational condition so it can perform its intended function. Services may include troubleshooting, disassembly, adjustment, repair, part replacement, realignment, and operational verification to manufacturer’s or VA’s performance specifications, whichever is most rigorous.

FSE - Field Service Engineer.  A person who is authorized by the contractor to perform maintenance (corrective and/or preventive) services on the VA Outpatient Clinic premises.

ESR - Vendor Engineering Service Report.  A documentation of the services rendered for each incidence of work performance under the terms and conditions of the contract.

Acceptance Signature - VAMC employee who indicates FSE demonstrated service conclusion/status and user has accepted work as complete/pending as stated in ESR.

Authorization Signature - COR's signature; indicates COR accepts work status as stated in ESR.

NFPA - National Fire Protection Association.

CDRH - Center for Devices and Radiological Health.

VAMC - Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center.

OEM - Original Equipment Manufacturer

3.  CONFORMANCE STANDARDS:

Contractor shall provide services and material to ensure that the equipment functions in conformance with the latest requirements of NFPA-99, TJC, NEC, OSHA, HIPAA, Federal and VA security specifications and requirements as applicable. The equipment shall be maintained such that it meets or exceeds the performance specifications as established in the OEM’s technical specifications. Additional performance specifications that exceed the OEM specifications shall be specified in writing by the VA.

	4.  SUPPORT

Support for emergency issues is available 24x7x365. SCI will respond to Requests for Support based on the severity of the issue reported using the following priority order:

Critical Priority (system or production connection down): Critical Priority shall mean a software error that renders the software inoperable and causes a significant, time-dependent stoppage of business operations.

Critical Priority instances must be reported via telephone.

High Priority (significant business impact): High Priority shall mean a software error that causes the software to fail resulting in significant revenue or operational impact. Certain functions may remain operational. High Priority instances must be reported via telephone.

Medium Priority (low-impact failure): Medium Priority shall mean a software error causes a feature of the software to fail, resulting in a non-critical situation which allows business to remain in operation. A Medium Priority incident may include issues impacting a single user, or issues where the business impact under a Critical or High Priority is resolved, but ongoing research is needed to determine the root cause of the failure. Medium Priority instances may be reported via telephone, email or the Customer Web Portal (CWP).

Low Priority (assistance): Low Priority shall mean a software error that does not impact the day-to-day functionality of the software, or requests for general assistance/needs or questions. Low Priority instances may be reported via telephone, email or the Customer Web Portal (CWP).

Emergency Support is available 24x7x365 by calling (802) 658-1955

Email: northamerican-support@datainnovations.com

All software patches, updates, enhancements, upgrades and new product release versions of  Software.

All product and user documentation, training materials, tips & tricks and webinars.

	5. HOURS OF COVERAGE:

Support is provided 24x7x365

6.  SERVICE MANUALS:

The VAMC shall not provide service manuals or service diagnostic software to the contractor for use in providing services under this contract. The contractor shall obtain, have on file, and make available to its FSE's all operational and technical documentation, (such as:  operational and service manuals, schematics, and parts list), which are necessary to meet the performance requirements of this contract. The location and listing of the service data manuals, by name, and/or the manuals themselves shall be provided to the CO upon request.

7.  DOCUMENTATION/REPORTS:

The documentation will include equipment down time and detailed descriptions of the scheduled and unscheduled maintenance procedures performed, including replaced parts and prices (for outside normal working hour services) required to maintain the equipment in accordance with conformance standards. Such documentation shall meet the guidelines as set forth in the Conformance Standards. In addition, each ESR must at a minimum document the following data legibly and in complete detail:

Name of Contractor

Name of FSE who performed services.

Contractor Service ESR Number/Log Number.

Date, Time (starting and ending), Hours-On-Site for service call.

VA Purchase Order Number(s) (if any) covering the call, if outside normal working hours.

Description of Problem Reported by COR/User.

Identification of Equipment to be serviced to include the following:  Equipment ID # or EE# from the bar-code, Manufacturer's Name, Device Name, Model#, Serial #, and any other Manufacturer's identification numbers.

Itemized Description of Service(s) Performed (including Costs associated with after normal working hour services), including:  Labor and Travel, Parts (with part numbers) and Materials and Circuit Location of problem/corrective action.

Total Cost to be billed.

Signatures from the following:

FSE performing services described.

VA Employee who witnessed service described.

Equipment downtime calculated in accordance with Conformance Standards.

	

	NOTE: ANY ADDITIONAL CHARGES CLAIMED MUST BE APPROVED BY 	THE COR BEFORE SERVICE IS COMPLETED!

8.  REPORTING REQUIREMENTS:

The contractor shall report to Biomedical Engineering to "check-in" upon arrival and prior to performance of work under this contract.  This check-in is mandatory and can be accomplished in person or by phone contact.  When the service(s) is/are completed, the FSE shall document the services rendered on a legible ESR(s). The FSE shall be required to check out with the Biomedical Engineering Department (location to be specified at time of contract award) and submit the ESR(s) to the COR. All ESRs shall be submitted to the equipment user for an "acceptance signature" and to the COR for an "authorization signature."  If the COR is unavailable, a signed accepted copy of the ESR will be sent to the COR within 5 business days of work completion.  

Failure to comply, either in whole or in part, with either the notification or ESR requirements will be deemed significant non-compliance with the contract and may be justification for termination of the contract.

9.  ADDITIONAL CHARGES:

There will be no additional charge for time spent at the site during, or after the normal hours of coverage awaiting the arrival of additional FSE and/or delivery of parts.

10.  REPORTING REQUIRED SERVICES BEYOND THE CONTRACT SCOPE:

The Contractor shall immediately, but no later than 24 consecutive hours after discovery, notify the CO and COR, (in writing), of the existence or the development of any defects in, or repairs required to the scheduled equipment which the Contractor considers he/she is not responsible for under the terms of the contract.  The contractor shall furnish the CO and COR with a written estimate of the cost to make necessary repairs.

11.  CONDITION OF EQUIPMENT:

The contractor accepts responsibility for the equipment described in Covered Equipment and Systems Section, in "as is" condition.  Failure to inspect the equipment prior to contract award will not relieve the contractor from performance of the requirements of this contract.

12.  COMPETENCY OF PERSONNEL SERVICING EQUIPMENT:

Each respondent must have an established business, with an office and full-time staff.  The staff includes a "fully qualified" FSE and a "fully qualified" FSE who will serve as the backup.

"Fully Qualified" is based upon training and on experience in the field. For training, the FSE(s) shall have successfully completed a formalized training program, for the equipment identified in Covered Equipment and Systems Section.  For field experience, the FSE(s) shall have a minimum of two years of experience, with respect to scheduled and unscheduled preventive and remedial maintenance on equipment identified in Covered Equipment and Systems Section.

The FSE(s) shall be authorized by the contractor to perform the maintenance services as required.  All work shall be performed by "Fully Qualified" competent FSEs. PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
FOR 
 
 
 IDARNG CSMS COMPUTER NUMERICAL CONTROL (CNC) Services 
 
1.0 General: This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the requirement for 
one (1) Computer Numerical Control (CNC) a 3-axis machine with 3+2 positioning 
capability machine milling metal machining software package and one (1) CNC lathe 
metal machining software package to support the operation and programming of a 
vertical machining center located at the Idaho Army National Guard (IDARNG) 
Combined Support Maintenance Shop (CSMS) facility. 
 
The software shall provide Computer-Aided Design (CAD) capability. Proficiency in CAD 
software such as Mastercam, or a comparable program is required to generate CNC 
machine toolpaths and machine programs compatible with Government CNC milling 
equipment. The system shall support development, editing, simulation, and execution of 
CNC machining programs using industry-standard G-code. 
 
This PWS describes the license and software support requirements for One (1) Hass 
VF-4SS CNC Mill 3-axis machine with 3+2 positioning capability machine and One 
(1)Hass A-TL-2 CNC Lathe machine.  
 
1.1 Scope: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, 
supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as 
Government Furnished, to perform perpetual license granting and software support 
service requirements for One (1) Hass VF-4SS CNC Mill 3-axis machine with 3+2 
positioning capability machine and One (1) Hass A-TL-2 CNC Lathe machine, as 
defined in this PWS. Services shall include: 
 
• Delivery of CNC software licenses 
• Software installation and configuration 
• CNC machines post processor configuration 
• Operator training 
• Technical support and updates 
• Documentation 
 
1.2 Background: This performance work statement (PWS) describes a computer 
numerical control (CNC) multi-axis, single-spindle, vertical machining center intended 
for accurately and repeatedly shaping workpieces (i.e., raw blocks of materials) by the 
subtractive manufacturing material machining processes. CNC is in reference to a 
computer-controlled system able to programmatically command and control 
servomotors, facilitating various movements and functions of machine axes. Machining 

2 
 
process examples described herein are drilling, reaming, tapping, threading, 
counterboring, countersinking, pocketing, squaring, stepping, plain milling, angular 
milling, face milling, contouring, profiling, gear hobbling and boring.  
 
CNC milling is an automated machine process used to manufacture engineering parts 
by selectively and progressively removing material from a workpiece. Material removal 
(milling) occurs via use of a rotating multi-point cutting tool and computerized controls 
(i.e., CNC). Parts manufactured via CNC milling are most practical via use of Computer-
Aided Design (CAD) and Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) software. CAD enables 
development and design of a part. CAM programs are used to generate manufacturing 
tool paths and to automate the manufacturing processes; CAM converts the CAD model 
into an executable CNC program (.NC) for machine use.  
 
This results in CNC manufacturing (machine control), instructing (via “G-code”) the 
machine to execute the job to manufacture a physical part.  
 
G-code, per Electronic Industries Association (EIA) SAE RS-274, is required as the 
programming language; it describes geometric paths using a simple command structure 
of the letter “G” followed by a numeric value and includes M-codes as a fundamental 
part.   
 
Multi-axis, as identified herein, represents three through five axes as per the following:  
3 Axis: The cutting tool position is adjusted relative to the workpiece along the X (left to 
right movement), Y (front to back movement), and Z (up and down movement) axes to 
trim away material. The tool vector remains fixed relative to the workpiece.  
 
4 Axis: The workpiece is machined in the same manner as with a three-axis machine 
but has an added degree of freedom: 360-degree rotation around a single axis, i.e. the 
fourth axis. The axis can be either set to continually move/rotate and/or incrementally 
rotate/hold/lock into position during milling. For example, Y-axis rotation allows 360-
degree manipulation/adjustment of the tool vector within the workpiece X-Z plane. The 
machine can remove material from 360 degrees around the workpiece including the 
bottom side.  
 
3+2 Axis Machining: 5-sided or positional 5-axis machining, 3+2 axis machining is a 
process that uses a standard 3-axis (X, Y, and Z) milling machine with two additional 
rotary axes. These rotary axes (A and B) position the workpiece at a specific angle 
relative to the cutting tool. Once the workpiece is locked into position, the machine 
performs a normal 3-axis cutting operation. It is important to understand that in 3+2 
machining, the two rotary axes do not move simultaneously with the cutting tool during 
the machining process. Instead, they are used to orient the part for a series of 3-axis 
operations. 
 
Lathe: The lathe is a machine tool that rotates a workpiece on its axis to perform various 
operations such as cutting, sanding, knurling, drilling, or turning. The primary function of 

3 
 
a lathe is to shape materials like metal by bringing a cutting tool against a rotating 
workpiece. 
 
1.3 Period of Performance (PoP): The Period of Performance shall be one (1) Base 
Year of 12 months and four(4) 12 month option years. 
 
1.4 General Information:  
 
1.4.1 Place and Performance of Services: The contractor shall provide services 
between the hours of 0730-1600 on Tuesday through Friday, except on recognized 
US holidays or when the Government facility/installation is closed due to local or 
national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government-directed 
facility/installation closings. Performance shall be at (IDARNG) CSMS facility or virtually. 
The contractor shall at all times maintain an adequate work force for the uninterrupted

1.4.1.1 Telework: The Government will permit the contractor to telework in support of 
this requirement. In furtherance of Continuity of Operations Planning (COOP), a

operations stay operational during times of national emergency or incidents of national

1.4.1.2 Unscheduled gate closures by the Security Police may occur at any time 
causing all personnel entering or exiting a closed installation to experience a delay. This 
cannot be predicted or prevented. Contractors are not compensated for unexpected 
closures or delays. Vehicles operated by contractor personnel are subject to search 
pursuant to applicable regulations. Any moving violation of any applicable motor vehicle 
regulation may result in the termination of the contractor employee’s installation driving 
privileges.  
 
1.4.1.3 The contractor’s employees shall become familiar with and obey the regulations 
of the installation; including fire, traffic, safety and security regulations while on the 
installation. Contractor employees should only enter restricted areas when required to 
do so and only upon prior approval. All contractor employees shall carry proper 
identification with them at all times, and shall be subject to such checks as may be 
deemed necessary. The contractor shall ensure compliance with all regulations and 
orders of the installation, which may affect performance. The Government reserves the 
right to direct the removal of an employee from Government property or revoke access 
to Government systems for misconduct, security reasons, or any overt evidence of 
communicable disease. Removal of contractor employees for reasons stated above 
does not relieve the Contractor from responsibility for total performance of this contract.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
FOR 
 
 
 IDARNG MATES COMPUTER NUMERICAL CONTROL (CNC) Services 
 
1.0 General: This Performance Work Statement (PWS) describes the requirement for 
one (1) Computer Numerical Control (CNC) machining software package to support the 
operation and programming of a vertical machining center located at the Idaho Army 
National Guard (IDARNG) MATES facility. 
 
The software shall provide Computer-Aided Design (CAD) capability. Proficiency in CAD 
software such as Fusion 360, Solid Works, or a comparable program is required to 
generate CNC machine toolpaths and machine programs compatible with Government 
CNC milling equipment. The system shall support development, editing, simulation, and 
execution of CNC machining programs using industry-standard G-code. 
 
 
This PWS describes the license and software support requirements for One (1) Hass 
VF-4SS CNC Mill 4 Axis machine. 
 
1.1 Scope: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, 
supervision, and quality control necessary, except as specified in Paragraph 3.0 as 
Government Furnished, to perform perpetual license granting and software support 
requirements for One (1) Hass VF-4SS CNC Mill 4 Axis machine Services, as 
defined in this PWS. Services shall include: 
 
• Delivery of CNC software license 
• Software installation and configuration 
• CNC machine post processor configuration 
• Operator training 
• Technical support and updates 
• Documentation 
 
1.2 Background: This performance work statement (PWS) describes a computer 
numerical control (CNC) multi-axis, single-spindle, vertical machining center intended 
for accurately and repeatedly shaping workpieces (i.e., raw blocks of materials) by the 
subtractive manufacturing material machining processes. CNC is in reference to a 
computer-controlled system able to programmatically command and control 
servomotors, facilitating various movements and functions of machine axes. Machining 
process examples described herein are drilling, reaming, tapping, threading, 
counterboring, countersinking, pocketing, squaring, stepping, plain milling, angular 
milling, face milling, contouring, profiling, gear hobbling and boring.  

2 
 
 
CNC milling is an automated machine process used to manufacture engineering parts 
by selectively and progressively removing material from a workpiece. Material removal 
(milling) occurs via use of a rotating multi-point cutting tool and computerized controls 
(i.e., CNC). Parts manufactured via CNC milling are most practical via use of Computer-
Aided Design (CAD) and Computer-Aided Manufacturing (CAM) software. CAD enables 
development and design of a part. CAM programs are used to generate manufacturing 
tool paths and to automate the manufacturing processes; CAM converts the CAD model 
into an executable CNC program (.NC) for machine use.  
 
This results in CNC manufacturing (machine control), instructing (via “G-code”) the 
machine to execute the job to manufacture a physical part.  
 
G-code, per Electronic Industries Association (EIA) SAE RS-274, is required as the 
programming language; it describes geometric paths using a simple command structure 
of the letter “G” followed by a numeric value and includes M-codes as a fundamental 
part.   
 
Multi-axis, as identified herein, represents three through five axes as per the following:  
3 Axis: The cutting tool position is adjusted relative to the workpiece along the X (left to 
right movement), Y (front to back movement), and Z (up and down movement) axes to 
trim away material. The tool vector remains fixed relative to the workpiece.  
 
4 Axis: The workpiece is machined in the same manner as with a three-axis machine 
but has an added degree of freedom: 360-degree rotation around a single axis, i.e. the 
fourth axis. The axis can be either set to continually move/rotate and/or incrementally 
rotate/hold/lock into position during milling. For example, Y-axis rotation allows 360-
degree manipulation/adjustment of the tool vector within the workpiece X-Z plane. The 
machine can remove material from 360 degrees around the workpiece including the 
bottom side.  
  
 
1.3 Period of Performance (PoP): The Period of Performance shall be 1 Base Year of 
12 months. 
 
1.4 General Information:  
 
1.4.1 Place and Performance of Services: The contractor shall provide services 
between the hours of 0730-1630 on Tuesday through Friday, except on recognized 
US holidays or when the Government facility/installation is closed due to local or 
national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar Government-directed 
facility/installation closings. Performance shall be at (IDARNG) MATES facility or 
virtually. The contractor shall at all times maintain an adequate work force for the 
uninterrupted performance of all tasks defined within this PWS when the Government 
facility/installation is not closed for the above reasons. When hiring personnel, the 

3 
 
contractor shall keep in mind that the stability and continuity of the work force are 
essential.  
 
 
1.4.1.1 Telework: The Government will permit the contractor to telework in support of 
this requirement. In furtherance of Continuity of Operations Planning (COOP), a 
telework program may be enacted to ensure that the Government's mission-critical 
operations stay operational during times of national emergency or incidents of national 
significance. Telework shall be at no additional cost to the Government.  
 
1.4.1.2 Unscheduled gate closures by the Security Police may occur at any time 
causing all personnel entering or exiting a closed installation to experience a delay. This 
cannot be predicted or prevented. Contractors are not compensated for unexpected 
closures or delays. Vehicles operated by contractor personnel are subject to search 
pursuant to applicable regulations. Any moving violation of any applicable motor vehicle 
regulation may result in the termination of the contractor employee’s installation driving 
privileges.  
 
1.4.1.3 The contractor’s employees shall become familiar with and obey the regulations 
of the installation; including fire, traffic, safety and security regulations while on the 
installation. Contractor employees should only enter restricted areas when required to 
do so and only upon prior approval. All contractor employees shall carry proper 
identification with them at all times, and shall be subject to such checks as may be 
deemed necessary. The contractor shall ensure compliance with all regulations and 
orders of the installation, which may affect performance. The Government reserves the 
right to direct the removal of an employee from Government property or revoke access 
to Government systems for misconduct, security reasons, or any overt evidence of 
communicable disease. Removal of contractor employees for reasons stated above 
does not relieve the Contractor from responsibility for total performance of this contract. 
 
1.4.2 Recognized Holidays: The following are recognized United States (US) holidays. 
The contractor shall not perform services on these days:  
 
1.4.2.1 New Year’s Day: January 1st  
1.4.2.2 Martin Luther King, Jr.’s Birthday 
1.4.2.3 President’s Day 
1.4.2.4 Memorial Day 
1.4.2.5 Juneteenth National Independence Day: June 19th 
1.4.2.6 Independence Day: July 4th  
1.4.2.7 Labor Day 
1.4.2.8 Columbus Day 
1.4.2.9 Veteran’s Day: November 11th  
1.4.2.10 Thanksgiving Day 
1.4.2.11 Christmas Day: December 25th 
 

4 
 
1.4.3 Quality Control (QC):  The contractor shall develop and maintain an effective QC 
Plan (QCP) to ensure services are performed in accordance with this PWS. The 
contractor shall develop and implement procedures to identify, prevent, and ensure non-
recurrence of defective services. The contractor’s QCP is the means by which it assures 
itself that its work complies with the requirements of the contract.  As a minimum, the 
contractor shall develop QC procedures that address the areas identified in Technical 
Exhibit 1, Performance Requirements Summary (PRS). A final QCP shall be submitted 
to the Contracting Officer NLT 10 days after contract award. After acceptance of the 
QCP, the contractor shall obtain the Contracting Officer’s (KO’s) acceptance in writing 
of any proposed changes to its QCP.  
 
1.4.4 Quality Assurance (QA): The Government will evaluate the contractor’s 
performance under this contract in accordance with the Quality Assurance Surveillance 
Plan (QASP). This plan is primarily focused on what the Government will do to ensure 
that the contractor has performed in accordance with the performance standards. It 
defines how the performance standards will be applied, the frequency of surveillance, 
and acceptable quality level(s) or defect rate(s).  
 
 
1.4.5 Installation Access and Security Requirements. The contractor shall comply with 
all applicable installation/facility access and local security policies and procedures, 
which may be obtained from the COR. The contractor and all associated subcontractor 
employees shall provide all information required for background checks to meet 
installation access requirements to be accomplished by installation Provost Marshal 
Office, Director of Emergency Services, or Security Office. The contractor shall ensure 
compliance with all personal identity verification requirements as directed by 
Department of Defense (DoD), Headquarters Department of Army (HQDA) and/or local 
policy (see PWS 6.0).  Should the Force Protection Condition (FPCON) change, the 
Government may require changes in contractor security matters or processes.   
 
1.4.5.1 For contractors that do not require a CAC, but require access to a DoD facility or 
installation: Contractor and all associated sub-contractors employees shall comply with 
adjudication standards and procedures using the National Crime Information Center 
Interstate Identification (NCIC-III) and Terrorist Screening Database (TSDB) (Army 
Directive 2014-05), and applicable installation, facility and area commander 
installation/facility access, and local security policies and procedures (provided by a 
Government representative).   
 
1.4.5.3 Awareness Training (AT) Level 1: All contractor employees, including 
subcontractor employees, requiring access to Army installations, facilities, and 
controlled access areas shall complete AT Level 1 training within 30 calendar days after 
contract start date and within 30 calendar days of new employees commencing 
performance. The contractor shall submit certificates of completion for each affected 
contractor and subcontractor employee to the KO within 15 calendar days after 
completion of training by each employee or subcontractor personnel.  AT Level 1 
awareness training is available at the following website:
 
https://jkodirect.jten.mil/Atlas2/faces/page/login/Login.seam or http://jko.jten.mil. 

5 
 
 
1.4.5.5 Communications Security/Information Technology (COMSEC/IT) Security. All 
communications with DoD organizations are subject to COMSEC review.  All telephone 
communications networks are continually subject to intercept by unfriendly intelligence 
organizations.  DoD has authorized the military departments to conduct COMSEC 
monitoring and recording of telephone calls originating from, or terminating at, DoD 
organizations.  Therefore, the contractor is advised that any time contractor personnel 
place or receive a call they are subject to COMSEC procedures.  The contractor shall 
ensure wide and frequent dissemination of the above information to all employees 
dealing with DoD information.  The contractor shall abide by all Government regulations 
concerning the authorized use of the Government's computer network, including the 
restriction against using the network to recruit Government personnel or advertise job 
openings.   
 
1.4.5.6 Use of Government Information Systems (IS) and access to Government 
networks is a revocable privilege, not a right.  Users are the foundation of the DoD 
strategy and their actions affect the most vulnerable portion of the Army Enterprise 
Infostructure (AEI).  Contractor employees shall have a favorable background 
investigation or hold a security clearance and access approvals commensurate with the 
level of information processed or available on the system. Contractor employees shall: 
 
1.4.5.6.1 Comply with the command's Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) for Government 
owned IS and sign an AUP prior to or upon account activation. 
 
1.4.5.6.2 Complete initial and/or annual Information Assurance (IA) training as defined 
in the IA Best Business Practices (BBP) training 
(https://atc.us.army.mil/iastar/docs/Training_BBP.pdf). 
 
1.4.5.6.3 Mark and safeguard files, output products, and storage media per 
classification level and disseminate them only to individuals authorized to receive them 
with a valid need to know. 
 
1.4.5.6.4 Protect IS and IS peripherals located in their respective areas in accordance 
with physical security and data protection requirements. 
 
1.4.5.6.5 Practice safe network and Internet operating principles and take no actions 
that threaten the integrity of the system or network. 
 
1.4.5.7 Army Training Certification Tracking System (ATCTS): All contractor employees 
with access to a Government information system shall be registered in ATCTS 
(https://atc.us.army.mil/iastar/index.php) at commencement of services, and shall 
successfully complete the DoD Information Assurance awareness training prior to 
access to the IS and then annually thereafter. (https://iatraining.us.army.mil/).   
 

6 
 
1.4.5.8 Information Assurance (IA) Training. All contractor employees and associated 
subcontractor employees shall complete the DoD IA Awareness Training before 
issuance of network access and annually thereafter.  
 
1.4.5.9 Information Assurance (IA)/Information Technology (IT) certification. All 
contractor employees performing services involving IA/IT functions shall comply with 
DoD and Army workforce training requirements in DoDD 8140.01, DoD 8570.01-M and 
AR 25-2 within six months of the start of contract performance or appointment to IA/IT 
functions. In accordance with DoD 8570.01-M, DFARS 252.239.7001, and AR 25-2, 
contractor employees supporting or performing IA/IT functions shall be appropriately 
certified upon contract award. The baseline certification as stipulated in DoD 8570.01-M 
shall be completed upon contract award. 
 
1.4.5.10 Protection of Personally Identifiable Information (PII).  The contractor shall 
protect all PII encountered in the performance of services in accordance with Defense

Sources Sought/Request For Information (RFI) 
Education Platform Requirements 
1.  Purpose and Scope  
This Sources Sought/ Request for Information is issued solely for market research and 
acquisition planning purposes.  This notice does not constitute a Request for Quote (RFQ), 
Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) and does not obligate the Government to 
issue a solicitation or make an award. 
Responses are voluntary. No reimbursement will be provided for costs associated with 
responding to this notice.  
The Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) seeks information to better understand 
current industry capabilities, architectural approaches, data strategies, and maturity related to a 
single, cohesive enterprise education platform that supports DoWEA’s global Pre-K – 12 
mission. 
2.  Background and Objective 
DoWEA operates a globally distributed education environment supporting instructional delivery, 
student services, and enterprise operations. As part of long-term modernization and consolidation 
planning, DoWEA is conducting market research to assess platforms that can: 
• Unify instructional and enterprise systems on a shared or tightly integrated data 
foundation. 
• Reduce system fragmentation and manual data movement. 
• Enable secure, near-real-time reporting, analytics, and AI-enabled insights at global scale. 
• Support interoperability with external analytics platforms and DoWEA-managed data 
environments. 
3. Teaching, Learning & Student Systems 
3.1 Integrated Platform Approach 
DoWEA is interested in platforms that support tightly integrated, natively developed or fully 
supported modules operating on a shared identity and data framework. Vendors may describe 
point to point or loosely coupled integrations; however, such approaches should be clearly 
identified and explained.  
3.2 Student Information System (SIS) 

2 
 
DoWEA seeks information on Student Information Systems (SIS) that can serve as the primary 
system of record for managing student data across the full student lifecycle.  Areas of interest 
include, but are not limited to: 
• Enrollment, registration, scheduling, attendance, grading, gradebook management, 
transcripts, discipline/behavior tracking, and program participation. 
• Secure student records management with rolebased access control, audit logging, 
alignment with the Privacy Act of 1974 and applicable DoW privacy regulations, and 
configurable data retention rules. 
• Support for DoWEA specific calendars, grading policies, credits, and reporting 
requirements. 
• Standards based, documented APIs that support data import and export for students, 
enrollment, roster, attendance, grades, transcripts, behavior, and program status data, 
including near real time exchange where available. 
3.3 Learning Management System (LMS) – Optional Module with Mandatory 
Integration 
DoWEA seeks information on education platforms that either include a native LMS module or 
provide strong, production ready integration with commonly used third party LMS solutions (for 
example, Schoology and Google Classroom) but not limited to those solutions.   Areas of interest 
include the platform’s ability to support: 
• Seamlessly integrate with external LMS platforms using standards-based mechanisms 
(e.g., LTI 1.3/Advantage, OneRoster, and secure APIs). 
• Support automated provisioning and synchronization of:  
o Courses, sections, teachers, students, and roles. 
o Assignments and grading workflows. 
o Enrollment changes, schedule updates, and staff reassignments. 
• Enable bidirectional grade pass back so that instructional grading performed in the LMS 
flows reliably to the SIS gradebook and transcript processes. 
• Maintain consistent user identity, authentication (SSO), and role-based access across the 
SIS and integrated LMS environments. 
• Provide visibility for instructional activity and learning signals (e.g., assignment 
completion, engagement indicators) for reporting and analytics, regardless of whether 
instruction occurs in a native or third-party LMS. 
• Ensure mobile support and parity of experience where supported by the external LMS. 
If a native LMS module is offered, vendors may describe capabilities related to: 
• Course and content management, assignments, rubrics, discussions, collaboration tools, 
and mobile applications. 
• Standards-based grading aligned with SIS grade calculation and transcript workflows. 

3 
 
• Learning analytics focused on engagement, progress, pacing, mastery, and course 
completion. 
3.4 Assessment 
DoWEA seeks information on assessment capabilities that support formative, benchmark, and 
summative use cases.  Areas of interest include: 
• Centralized, reusable item banks with tagging, version control, and alignment to 
standards. 
• Accommodation management aligned to IEP/504 requirements and multilingual learner 
needs. 
• Secure test administration with support for offline or low-bandwidth operation in global 
environments. 
• Proctoring and academic integrity safeguards, as applicable. 
• Import/export APIs supporting assessment results, accommodations, and item metadata. 
• Integration with LMS platforms (native or third-party) for assignment-based and 
classroom-embedded assessments. 
3.5 Special Education and Student Support Programs 
DoWEA seeks information on platforms that support special education and student services 
workflows.  Areas of interest include support for: 
• IEP/504, Multilingual Learner Programs (MLP), Advanced Academic Programs (AAP), 
and MTSS/RTI frameworks. 
• Intervention planning, service delivery logging, progress monitoring, and compliance 
reporting. 
• Strict role-based privacy controls to safeguard sensitive student data. 
• Standards-based APIs supporting exchange of accommodations, service records, progress 
data, and compliance indicators. 
4. Reporting, Analytics, and Data Interoperability 
DoWEA is interested in understanding how platforms support reporting and analytics across 
instructional and enterprise domains.  Areas of interest include: 
• Real-time or near real-time reporting across SIS, Assessment, Special Programs, and 
LMS platforms (native or third-party). 
• Role-appropriate dashboards for teachers, school leaders, district/regional leadership, and 
headquarters personnel. 
• Reporting shall not be degraded or functionally limited using an external LMS. 

4 
 
Vendors should describe how reporting data is structured and made available for analytical and 
AI use cases.  
5. Enterprise Operations & Business Services 
DoWEA seeks information on enterprise education platforms that provide or integrate with 
operational and business services to support a global education environment.  The following 
areas represent capabilities of interest for market research purposes. 
5.1 Finance / ERP 
Areas of interest include: 
• General Ledger, Accounts Payable/Receivable, multi-fund accounting, grants 
management, budgeting and forecasting. 
• Procurement and eProcurement workflows. 
• Inventory management and school activity funds. 
• Auditability and reporting are suitable for federal oversight. 
5.2 Human Resources /Human Capital Management (HCM) 
Areas of interest include: 
• Manpower management, including position control, Staff Deployment (by school, 
program, or funding source), Trend and Forecasting (enrollment driven staffing models), 
and Scenario Planning and Forecasting. 
• Recruiting, onboarding, licensure and credential tracking, staff evaluations, and substitute 
management. 
• Alignment of staff roles and credentials with instructional and system access. 
• Integration with enterprise identity and access management systems. 
5.3 Facilities /Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) 
Areas of interest include: 
• Work order management, preventive maintenance scheduling, asset lifecycle tracking, 
and space utilization. 
• Safety, security, and facilities related compliance workflows. 
5.4 Transportation 
Areas of interest include: 
• Route planning, ridership management, and parent notifications. 

5 
 
• Fleet management and vehicle maintenance tracking. 
5.5 IT Service Management (ITSM) & End-User Computing 
Areas of interest include: 
• Device, software, and asset management. 
• IT ticketing and service workflows. 
• Integration with Unified Endpoint Management (UEM/MDM) platforms. 
• Classroom device management and instructional visibility. 
6. Unified Data, Analytics & Interoperability 
6.1 Unified Data Architecture 
DoWEA seeks information on platform support unified or federated data approaches across 
instructional and enterprise domains.  Areas of interest include: 
• A shared or tightly federated data model across SIS, LMS, ERP, HR, facilities, 
transportation, and IT operations. 
• Near real-time data flows with minimal manual reconciliation. 
6.2 APIs & Interoperability Standards 
 Vendors may describe support for open APIs and industry standards, including: 
• Open REST APIs with pagination, filtering, and webhook/event support. 
• Support for current and future standards, including but not limited to:  
o IMS OneRoster 1.1+ 
o Ed-Fi Data Standard 4.0+ (native or certified adapter) 
o LTI 1.3/Advantage 
o QTI/APIP (as applicable) 
o SCORM (legacy) and xAPI 
o Identity standards: SAML 2.0, OIDC/OAuth 2.0, SCIM 2.0 
6.3 AI-Enabled Analytics & Business Intelligence 
DoWEA is interested in understanding how platforms support analytics and AI enabled insights 
across instructional and operational domains.  Areas of interest include: 
• Executive, instructional, and operational dashboards. 
• Early warning indicators for attendance, grades, behavior, and course completion with 
configurable thresholds. 

6 
 
• Machine learning explainability, including feature importance and counterfactual 
explanations. 
• Intervention tracking linked to analytic triggers. 
• Self-service analytics, including natural language queries where appropriate. 
• Export or integration with DoWEA managed data warehouse or lakehouse infrastructure. 
• Availability of Metadata catalogs with data lineage visualization. 
7. Data Quality & Master Data Management 
Areas of interest include: 
• Automated validation for completeness, accuracy, timeliness, and consistency. 
• Pre-configured quality checks for critical data (student demographics, attendance, grades, 
staff credentials). 
• Data quality dashboards, alerts, and trend analysis. 
• Support for DoWEA defined custom validation rules. 
• Master Data Management for students, staff, schools, and courses. 
• Data classification, PII tagging. and retention/minimization controls. 
8. Reporting Integration with External AI-Enabled Analytics Platforms (e.g., MS Fabric) 
DoWEA seeks information on how platform reporting and analytics capabilities interoperate 
seamlessly with external, AI enabled enterprise analytics platforms, including but not limited to 
MS Fabric, Power BI, and DoWEA managed data warehouse or lakehouse environments. The 
reporting architecture must support both native platform reporting and advanced external 
analytics without data duplication, vendor lock-in, or loss of data fidelity.  Vendors shall

9. Data Access & Export 
The platform shall provide secure, documented, and supported mechanisms to expose

o REST-based APIs.

Request for Information V1 | April 2022  Page 1 
 
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR 
CYBERSECURITY SUPPORT SERVICES 
 
This announcement constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) for the purpose of determining 
market capability of sources or obtaining information. Response s to this RFI  may be used for 
market research for future solicitations.  
 
I. DISCLAIMER 
 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION ONLY.  
 
This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes – it does not constitute a Request 
for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the United 
States Senate Office of the Sergeant at Arms ( SAA) to contract for any product or service 
whatsoever. Further, the SAA does not seek proposals at this time; will not accept unsolicited 
proposals; and will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this 
RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s 
expense. If the SAA subsequently releases a solicitation, it may be published on the SAM.gov 
website. Potential contractors are responsible for  monitoring this site for possible additional 
information pertaining to this requirement.  
 
This synopsis contains the currently available information and is subject to change at any time.  
 
II. BACKGROUND 
The SAA the serves as the chief law enforcement and protocol officer for the Senate, with 
responsibilities encompassing the protection of Senate members, staff, visitors, and facilities. This 
function includes safeguarding critical information systems and networks that support legislative 
operations, such as email communications, document management, voting systems, and remote 
access platforms. In an era of escalating cyber threats —ranging from nation- state actors 
conducting espionage and disruption campaigns to cybercriminals deploying ransomware and 
phishing attacks—the SAA recognizes the imperative to fortify its cybersecurity posture. 
 
Recent high-profile incidents, including breaches of government agencies and legislative bodies 
worldwide, underscore the vulnerabilities inherent in interconnected digital infrastructures. The 
Senate’s role in the United States constitutional form of government  makes it a prime target for 
advanced persistent threats (APTs), supply chain compromises, and insider risks. To address these 
challenges, the SAA seeks to explore innovative cybersecurity services that leverage emerging 
technologies like artificial intelligence -driven threat hunting, zero- trust architectures, and cloud -
native security solutions. This RFI aims to identify industry capabilities that can integrate 
seamlessly with existing Senate systems, ensuring minimal disruption while maximizing 
protection against evolving cyber risks . By soliciting input from vendors and experts, the SAA 
intends to inform future procurement strategies that prioritize scalability, cost- effectiveness, and 
alignment with legislative security requirements. 
 
The SAA seeks to solicit services for a variety of cybersecurity services. Below are some key items 
of note respondents should be aware of: 

Request for Information V1 | April 2022  Page 2 
 
 
a. Services like vendor risk assessments may be solicited on an ongoing, annual basis. Other 
services like penetration testing may be limited to 90–180 calendar day periods of 
performance depending on the requirements.  
b. ServiceNow is used for a variety of Cybersecurity functions and the SAA would prefer any 
proposed platforms or tools used in support of those services to integrate with ServiceNow. 
c. The SAA supports a significant part of the Legislative Branch of the United States 
Government. Due to this unique environment, the SAA may choose to abide by all or 
portions of various federal requirements (OMB Circulars, FISMA requirements, etc.). 
Adherence is based on best practices and needs of the SAA;  it is not mandated by any 
Executive Branch action or directive.  
d. All personnel are required to have and maintain at a minimum a Secret clearance. 
Additional clearance levels may be required for certain tasks.  
 
III. SPECIFIC INFORMATION OF INTEREST 
 
The SAA is seeking information regarding industry capabilities to provide comprehensive 
cybersecurity services, including managed security services, vulnerability management, and 
strategic security consulting to bolster the current security postur e. Responses to this RFI may  
include a response to each of the questions and service requests descriptions listed below.  
Respondents are encouraged to provide detailed, non- proprietary information on the following 
areas.  
 
Core Cybersecurity Services 
 
a. What are your organization’s capabilities in providing managed security services, 
including but not limited to: 
1. Cyber threat intelligence 
2. Cyber risk assessments, vulnerability assessment and penetration testing 
3. Compliance audit 
4. Cyber hunt and threat detection 
5. End point detection and response 
6. Security Operations Center (SOC) as a service 
7. Incident response and recovery 
8. Risk Management Framework (RMF) implementation  
9. Training and workforce development 
10. Supply chain risk reviews and mitigations 
11. Technical writing support 
12. Cybersecurity architecture and planning 
 
b. How do your services align with federal standards (e.g., FedRAMP authorization levels, 
CMMC, NIST)? 
c. Provide examples of scalability for large -scale federal deployments (e.g., supporting 
50,000+ users). 
 
Emerging Technologies 

Request for Information V1 | April 2022  Page 3 
 
 
Describe your organization’s capabilities in providing: 
a. Detailed integration of AI/ML for predictive threat analysis and automated response.  
b. Approaches to zero -trust implementation, including identity and access management 
(IAM) and micro-segmentation. 
c. Solutions for cloud security (e.g., AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) and hybrid environments. 
d. Innovations in quantum-resistant encryption or post-quantum cryptography. 
 
Implementation and Support 
 
Describe your organization’s capabilities for: 
a. Estimated timelines and costs for deployment in a federal setting (high-level ranges only). 
b. Training and knowledge transfer programs for federal personnel. 
c. Metrics for measuring service effectiveness (e.g., mean time to detect/respond, false 
positive rates). 
d. Strategies for compliance with federal data sovereignty and privacy requirements (e.g. 2 
U.S.C. § 6628 handling). 
 
Challenges and Recommendations 
 
Describe your organization’s capabilities to:  
a. Identify potential challenges in providing cybersecurity services to federal entities (e.g., 
regulatory hurdles, integration with legacy systems). 
b. Suggest ways the SAA can streamline procurement or collaboration to foster innovation. 
 
Company Information 
 
Describe your organization by including:  
a. Provide a brief overview of your organization, including size, years in business, relevant 
certifications (e.g., ISO 27001), and past performance with government contracts. 
 
In addition, any background information about a proposed product, platform or tools including the 
knowledge, skills, and experience required to support the SAA’s Cybersecurity mission that may 
be helpful should be included in the response to this RFI.  
 
 
IV. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS and FORMATTING REQUIREMENTS  
 
The information contained in this RFI will be the only information provided by the Senate during 
this process. All respondents  should submit an information package in accordance with the 
instructions provided below.  
 
Responses to this RFI are due no later than 1:00pm EST on May 05, 2026 and shall be submitted 
electronically via email only to the attention of Mashonda Walston at acquisitions@saa.senate.gov.  
 

Request for Information V1 | April 2022  Page 4 
 
The subject of the email message shall be:  “RFI #2026-S-063 Cybersecurity Support". No other 
method of transmittal will be accepted. Access by the SAA to information in any files attached to 
the response is the responsibility of the submitting party. Neither the SAA nor the Senate is 
responsible for any failure to access respondent’s  information. Respondents are allowed a 
maximum of 15 pages, excluding cover page and appendices. The responses should be concise 
and include supporting data, case studies, or white papers where applicable. Proprietary 
information should be clearly marked and will be handled accordingly. The SAA has the sole 
discretion to follow up with selected respondents for clarification or virtual meetings. 
 
V. QUESTIONS AND POINT OF CONTACT  
 
Questions regarding this RFI may be sent to the following Procurement & Contract Specialist: 
 
Name: Mashonda Walston 
Title: Senior Procurement and Contracting Specialist 
E-Mail Address: acquisitions@saa.senate.gov   
 
THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. THIS NOTICE CONSTITUTES THE 
ENTIRE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND IS THE ONLY INFORMATION 
PROVIDED BY THE SERGEANT AT ARMS OR SENATE. THE SERGEANT AT ARMS 
WILL NOT RESPOND TO ANY REQUESTS FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMATION.

VENDOR QUESTIONS 
 
I. Set-Aside Designation 
Question 1. The solicitation is designated as a Total Small Business Set-Aside (FAR 52.219-6). MGM 
Solutions is a VA-verified SDVOSB. Under 38 U.S.C. § 8127(d), VAAR 819.7006, and Kingdomware 
Technologies, Inc. v. United States, 579 U.S. 422 (2016), the VA must apply the Rule of Two — 
determining whether two or more SDVOSBs can meet the requirement at a fair and reasonable price — 
before issuing under any other set-aside category, including general Small Business. Can the Contracting 
Office confirm that a documented Rule of Two determination was conducted and that fewer than two 
SDVOSBs were found capable? If not, we respectfully request the solicitation be reissued as a 100% 
SDVOSB set-aside. 
Answer 1: Market Research was conducted in accordance with Revolutionary FAR Part 10. Based 
on Market Research and the Non-Manufacture Rule (NMR), research confirmed that this 
requirement does not meet the Rule of Two. This procurement is and will remain a small business 
(SB) set-aside. 
 
II. Whole-Floor Coverage — Tamper and Battery Monitoring 
The SOW states (page 4): "The system will need tamper monitoring and battery monitoring for the 
bracelets. Coverage area on each floor is about 15,000 sqft." This language raises the following critical 
technical questions: 
Question 2. Must the system provide tamper and low-battery alerts anywhere on each monitored floor at 
all times — including patient rooms, corridors, and common areas away from covered exits — or only 
when a patient's bracelet is in proximity to a covered door or exit? Please clarify whether continuous 
whole-floor coverage (not door/exit-proximity-only detection) is required to satisfy this specification. 
Answer 2: Given the range limitation of BLE and the low elopement risk for our patients, whole 
floor coverage is not required.  Periodic nursing checks on the bracelets will be sufficient.   
Tamper monitoring and battery monitoring for the bracelets has been removed. 
Question 3. If a patient removes their bracelet away from a covered exit — for example, in their room or 
a corridor — must the system generate an immediate staff alert at that moment? Or is it acceptable for the 
alert to be generated only when the patient subsequently approaches a covered door? 
Answer 3: Notification in range of the covered doors is sufficient. 
 
Question 4. If a patient's bracelet battery reaches a low-battery threshold away from a covered exit — for 
example, in their room or a corridor — must the system generate an immediate low-battery notification to 
staff? Or is it acceptable for the notification to be generated only when the bracelet next comes within 
range of a covered door reader? 

Page 3 of 5 
Answer 4: Notification in range of the covered doors is sufficient. 
 
Question 5. The Salient Characteristics specify a "WanderGuard Blue Door Bundle/Starter Kit" with 
coverage at designated doors. WanderGuard Blue is a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) technology operating 
in the 2.4 GHz spectrum. BLE systems are physically limited to exit-proximity detection and cannot 
maintain continuous communication with a bracelet across 15,000 square feet of hospital floor 
construction (reinforced concrete, metal structures, lead-lined rooms). Can the Contracting Office confirm 
that a BLE exit-only topology meets the stated requirement for tamper and battery monitoring across the 
full 15,000 sq ft coverage area per floor? If not, will the Contracting Office consider performance-based 
specifications that allow offerors to propose a technically superior solution? 
Answer 5: BLE topology is sufficient.  Coverage in vicinity of the exit doors meets our 
requirements. 
 
III. Nurse Station Display and Alert Requirements 
Question 6: The SOW specifies 16 Nurse Station Annunciators providing "audible indication of door 
alert at 4 locations on 4 floors." Does the Government require visual display at nurse station workstations 
showing real-time patient location, bracelet identity, tamper status, and battery status — or audible-only 
notification? PatienTRAK provides floor-map workstation displays at nurse stations in addition to audible 
alarms; please confirm whether this capability is desired or required. 
Answer 6: Audible annunciation at 4 locations on each floor.  Control panel and visual display only 
necessary at primary nurse’s station on each floor. 
 
Question 7: Should nurse station alerts include the patient's name/identifier, location on the floor, tamper 
status, and battery status at the time of the alert — or only an audible door alarm signal? 
Answer 7: Audible alarm annunciation is sufficient.  Rest of the data displaying on main control 
panels is desired. 
 
Question 8: The SOW states "audible alarm only, door locking not required." However, the Salient 
Characteristics note the system is "capable of upgrade to provide Auto-Door Locking Mags." Can the 
Contracting Office confirm that future upgrade capability to door locking and access control is desirable, 
even if not required at initial installation? MGM PatienTRAK integrates with maglocks, access control, 
CCTV, elevator systems, and nurse call — all on the same infrastructure. 
Answer 8: Software that is compatible with the door locking infrastructure is sufficient to meet this 
requirement. 
 
IV. Installation and As-Built Plans 

Page 4 of 5 
Question 9: Will the Government provide AutoCAD as-built floor plans for the 4 monitored floors to 
allow offerors to accurately plan cable routing, reader/exciter placement, and workstation locations? For a 
system covering 15,000 sq ft per floor with whole-floor coverage, accurate as-built plans are essential for 
a complete and accurate quote. If as-builts are not in Autocad format, can you provide in PDF format? 
Answer 9: PDF plans are immediately available.  As-built PDFs and AutoCAD drawing may be 
available later in the process but not guaranteed. 
 
 
Question 10: The facility is described as a renovated building being activated in June 2026. Will the 
elopement system installation be coordinated with the construction contractor currently on-site? Who is 
the primary coordination contact — the VA COR, VHiT, or the construction contractor? 
Answer 10: Installation will be coordinated with the VA COR.  Construction completion is 
anticipated by early June. 
 
Question 11: The SOW requires integration with the Jeron Provider 790 nurse call system. Can the 
Contracting Office confirm the specific Jeron interface protocol required (dry contact relay, IP/TCP, 
serial)? MGM PatienTRAK has integrated with multiple nurse call platforms; confirmation of the 
interface type will ensure a complete and accurate quote. 
Answer 11: Dry contact will likely be sufficient for providing an elopement notification into the 
Jeron nurse call system, elopement management system will not be on the VA network for TCP/IP 
protocol. 
 
V. OEM Authorization Requirement 
Question 12: The SOW requires "written certification from the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) 
that authorizes the Contractor to provide and install the products and software." MGM Solutions is the 
OEM and developer of PatienTRAK —  we manufacture, install, and support our own system. Does this 
OEM authorization requirement apply to offerors who are themselves the OEM/manufacturer, or only to 
resellers/integrators of third-party products? 
Answer 12:  Self-certification of installers capability will meet this requirement. 
 
Question 13: On page 9, Section D of the attached PDF, it states that we must “complete and return 
provision 52.212-3.” However, when reviewing the document, I do not see a specific section or form to 
complete. 
Could you please confirm whether provision 52.212-3 is a separate document that needs to be provided 
and returned, or if this requirement is satisfied by the Contractors Administration Data. 
Answer 13: The requirement to complete form 52.212-3 has been removed. 

Page 5 of 5 
 
Question 14: Could you please confirm if the government will accept alternate "equal or better" technical 
proposals for this requirement?  
Answer 14: The solicitation states “Brand Name or Equal.” If you are an interested party, please 
submit a quote on your company letter head. 
 
Question 15: Will the government change this to SDVOSB set aside using NAICS 541519 given two or 
more SDVOSBs provide this solution? 
Answer 15: This procurement is and will remain a small business (SB) set-aside. Refer to question 
1.
