1.0  BACKGROUND 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), IT 
Budget and Finance (ITBF) provides leadership, resources, and financial expertise to 
deliver world-class IT products and services and improve end-user experience for 
Veterans, their families, caregivers, and survivors. Specifically, ITBF links the full IT 
budget process with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Secretary and Chief 
Information Officer’s (CIO) priorities, ensuring that budgets reflect the organization’s 
values and support innovation and modernization. ITBF also provides budgetary 
expertise for IT systems and operations for VA Administrations/Staff Offices, to optimize 
the reach and impact of investment dollars. 
 
The Technology Business Management (TBM) Branch, the IT Financial Management 
and Oversight Service (ITFMOS), and the Financial Data Management (FDM) Branch 
each play crucial roles within VA OIT ITBF, focusing on data integration, IT cost 
transparency, informed decision-making, and compliance with funding and procurement 
law, regulation, and policy. 
 
Through the implementation of financial data management and data governance 
practices, advanced analytical models, and ensuring compliance with regulatory 
frameworks, these branches contribute to the following initiatives: 
1. Efficiency and Accountability: By maintaining precise data management systems 
and robust financial models, these branches ensure that resources are allocated 
efficiently, and accountability is maintained at all levels of operation. 
2. Increase Transparency: The TBM Model and comprehensive reporting 
mechanisms provide clear visibility into IT costs and resource utilization, promoting 
transparency in government spending. 
3. Enable Data-Driven Decision Making: The analytical frameworks and data sets 
utilized by these branches enable informed decision-making at tactical, operational, 
and strategic levels, aligning with the goal of fostering a culture of data-driven 
governance. 
 
The TBM Branch's responsibilities include maintaining and enhancing the TBM Cost 
Transparency Model, a sophisticated analytical framework that provides detailed views 
of IT costs through a multi-layered approach encompassing resources, functions, 
products, and services. This model employs standard TBM taxonomy and activity-based 
costing, both of which are technical methodologies requiring expertise in financial 
modeling, data analytics, and IT cost management. By fostering IT cost transparency 
and improving decision-making through data-driven insights, the TBM Branch supports 
the priority of promoting efficient and accountable government operations. Additionally, 
the integration of TBM into existing business processes and its alignment with federal 
frameworks further demonstrates the technical nature and strategic importance of these 
activities. 
 

ITBF TBM and Accounting Technical Enablement 
VA-26-00004314 
 
Page 3 of 16 
The Travel, Purchase Cards, and Conferences (TPC) Branch within ITFMOS provides 
critical oversight for the proper funding of VA IT-related acquisitions, conducting 
technical reviews and audits to maintain compliance with Federal Travel Regulations, 
Federal Acquisition Regulations, and VA Financial Policies. It communicates necessary 
revisions of Travel, Charge Card, and Conferences policies for VA and OIT, and works 
actively to reduce fraud, waste, and abuse of government funds by monitoring these 
programs. The branch also ensures the accurate and timely updates to the charge card 
program bank’s system to reflect the current hierarchy of cardholders and their status. 
These activities require technical skills in financial systems, compliance auditing, and 
policy implementation.  
 
The core functions of the FDM Branch involve the unification and analysis of budget and 
finance data across the VA Office of Information and Technology (OIT). This unification 
aims to provide an authoritative enterprise data source that enhances business 
decisions at tactical, operational, and strategic levels. The utilization of these platforms 
for data aggregation, analysis, and reporting requires a strong technical foundation in 
data science, data analytics, and database management. These technical efforts enable 
accurate and efficient financial planning, resource allocation, and decision-making 
processes.

SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
 
FOR 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
 
PART 1 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
 
 
1.1
 General: This is a non-personnel services contract to provide on-site Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) High-
Performance Compute (HPC) system administration support services to be provided to the Naval Oceanographic Office 
(NAVOCEANO or NAVO) for a period of one year and is similar to the system administration support services provided 
on contract N0018925P0496. The Government shall not exercise any supervision or control over the contract service 
providers performing the services herein  
 
 
1.2 Background 
1.2.1 The Naval Oceanographic Office (NAVOCEANO) collects, processes, and disseminates complex oceanographic 
data, forecasts, and products to Fleet users using HPC technologies including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine 
Learning (ML) algorithms.  NAVOCEANO requires specialized services for the system administration, operational 
support, and cybersecurity compliance of a new Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) High-Performance Compute (HPC) 
cluster. This system is a strategic asset designed to run advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) 
algorithms. The architecture consists of cutting-edge technologies, including GPU-accelerated compute nodes, an HPE 
Slingshot high-speed interconnect, a Lustre-based parallel file system, and an image-based operating system deployment 
infrastructure. Due to the new technology and complexity of these components, expert contractor support is necessary to 
ensure the system's stability, security, and optimal performance to meet mission-critical objectives 
 
 
1.3 Description of Requirement 
The contractor shall provide specialized support services for system administration,
 operational support, and cybersecurity 
compliance of the HPE HPC system.  The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, 
and other items necessary to perform the services. 
 
 
1.4 Period of Performance, Place of Performance and Hours of Operation  
 
1.4.1 The period of performance shall be 12 months after award.  
1.4.2 The contractor shall perform services at NAVOCEANO. NAVOCEANO is located at Stennis Space Center, 
Mississippi. 
1.4.3 Recognized Holidays/Government Closure:  Federal law (5 U.S.C. 6103) establishes the public holidays for 
Federal employees.  Any other day designated by federal statute, executive order, presidential proclamation and/or local 
determinations relating to adverse weather conditions, national emergencies, administrative closings, or similar 
Government directed facility closings may require office closure.  During such periods of closure, contractor employees 
will not be allowed to work, nor will the contractor be compensated, however, offsite work is allowed, with Contracting 
Officer's (KO) approval, on a case-by-case basis when mutually agreed upon by the Government and the contractor. 
 
  
 
1.4.4 Hours of Operation 

 
Page 2 of 9 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
The contractor is responsible for performing support services during an 8-hour workday between the hours of 0700 and 
1630, Monday through Friday, except when the government facility is closed or government personnel are not in the 
designated office location. The contractor must maintain an adequate workforce for the uninterrupted performance of all 
tasks defined within this performance work statement when the Government facility is not closed.  The stability and 
continuity of the contractor workforce are essential. 
 
1.5 Post Award Conference/Periodic Progress Meetings 
1.5.1 The Contractor shall attend any post award conference convened by the contracting activity. The contracting 
officer and the Contracting Officers Representative (COR) may meet periodically with the contractor to review the 
contractor's performance. At these meetings, the contracting officer will apprise the contractor of how the Government 
views the contractor's performance and the contractor will inform the Government of problems experiencing, if any. The 
Government or the contractor, as applicable, shall take appropriate action to resolve outstanding issues. These meetings 
shall be at no additional cost to the Government.  
 
1.6 Program Management 
1.6.1 The contractor shall assign a Program Manager (PM)/Contract Manager (CM) to act as the single primary point of 
contact with the NAVOCEANO COR. The PM/CM specifically has the responsibility of communicating with the COR on 
all matters pertaining to this Performance Work Statement (PWS). The PM/CM shall direct the individual contractor 
employee’s effort through the company’s internal management system; this management system shall provide project 
progress visibility to assure on-time completion of all requirements. 
1.6.2 The contractor shall utilize standard processes based on industry best practices wherever applicable. 
1.6.3 The contractor shall sponsor quarterly program management reviews to monitor contractor performance and 
discuss any issues that the contractor and/or NAVOCEANO are experiencing with the project referenced herein with the 
COR and/or Contracting Office. NAVOCEANO COR will schedule this review; submit a suggested agenda to the 
contractor who shall be responsible for all briefing slides and materials. 
16.4 The contractor shall support other NAVOCEANO briefings and meetings as applicable by providing feedback 
and documentation/numbers concerning any efforts. 
 
1.7 Identification of Contractor Employees: All contract personnel are required to identify themselves as such while 
attending meetings, answering Government telephones, answering emails and working in other situations where their 
contractor status is not obvious to third parties. Identification of contractor status is required to avoid creating an 
impression in the minds of members of the public or other Government personnel that they are Government officials. 
They must also mark all documents or reports produced by contractors as contractor products or that contractor 
participation is appropriately disclosed. All contractor personnel shall obtain and wear badges in the performance of this 
service 
 
5 Personnel Education / Experience Requirements 
5.1 Education: 
5.1.1 All contractor personnel conducting system administration services, at a minimum, the combination of education 
and experience required to qualify for the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) General Schedule Qualifications 
Standard, IT Specialist Series 2210 or Computer Scientist series 1550.  The IT Specialist Series 2210 qualifications build 
upon the general requirements of the 2210 series with a specific focus on the technical skills needed to manage and 
maintain network infrastructures, operating systems, and applications.   The Computer Scientist Series 1550 qualifications  
Requires one of the following basic education requirements: 
Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science: A bachelor's degree in computer science from an accredited institution.  
Bachelor's Degree with Specific Coursework: A bachelor's degree with 30 semester hours in a combination of 
mathematics, statistics, and computer science. Of these 30 semester hours, at least 15 must have included a combination 
of statistics and mathematics, including differential and integral calculus. 
All academic degrees and coursework must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions 
  
 

 
Page 3 of 9 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
5.1.2 All contractor personnel conducting system administration shall have, at minimum, the combination of education 
and training required to qualify for the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) General Schedule Qualifications 
Standard, IT Specialist 2210 series at or above the GS12 level which is equivalent to four (4) years of specialized 
experience in the fields of IT system administration and IT network administration of HPC systems used for scientific 
data processing using AI/ML. More specifically LINUX based operating systems, parallel file systems, GPU-accelerated 
compute nodes, and high-speed network interconnects. 
 
5.2 All contractor personnel shall have specialized knowledge of HPC systems used for scientific data processing using 
AI/ML. More specifically LINUX based operating systems, parallel file systems, GPU-accelerated compute nodes, and 
high-speed network interconnects.  
 
 
 
PART 2 
DEFINITIONS & ACRONYMS 
 
 
 
 
2.1.  CONTRACTOR. A supplier or vendor awarded a contract to provide specific supplies or service to the Government. 
The term used in this contract refers to the Prime Contractor. 
 
2.2  CONTRACTING OFFICER.  A person with authority to enter into, administer, and or terminate contracts, and make 
related determinations and findings on behalf of the Government. Note: The only individual who can legally bind the 
Government. 
 
2.3   CONTRACTING OFFICER'S REPRESENTATIVE (COR).  An employee of the U.S.Government designated and 
authorized in writing by the contracting officer to perform specific technical or administrative functions. Such 
appointment shall be in writing and shall state the scope of authority and limitations. This individual has authority to 
provide technical direction to the Contractor if that direction is within the scope of the contract, does not constitute a 
change, and has no funding implications. This individual does NOT have authority to change the terms and 
conditions of the contract.  
 
2.4  DEFECTIVE SERVICE. A service output that does not meet the standard of performance associated with the 
Performance Work Statement. 
 
2..5  QUALITY ASSURANCE. The Government procedures to verify the services performed by the Contractor are within 
acceptable standards. 
 
2.6   QUALITY CONTROL. All necessary measures taken by the Contractor to assure that the quality of a product or 
service shall meet contract requirements. 
 
 
 
PART 3 
SPECIFIC TASKS 
 
 
3.1 Task 1: System and Network Administration 
The contractor shall provide expert system administration for the entire HPC ecosystem. 

 
Page 4 of 9 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
• 3.1.1 Hardware and Software Management: Install, configure, and maintain all HPC components, including 
compute nodes (CPU/GPU), Slingshot interconnect fabric, and the Lustre parallel file system. 
• 3.1.2 Image-Based OS Deployment: Manage the creation, maintenance, testing, and deployment of operating 
system images for compute and service nodes. Ensure a stable and consistent software environment. 
• 3.1.3 User and Resource Management: Manage user accounts (create, modify, delete), access controls, 
enforcing security policies, and resource allocation. Implement and manage a job scheduling system (e.g., Slurm) 
to ensure equitable and efficient use of computational resources. 
• 3.1.4 System Monitoring and Maintenance: Proactively monitor system health, performance, and utilization. 
Perform routine maintenance, apply firmware updates, and manage hardware repairs or replacements in 
coordination with the vendor. 
• 3.1.5 System Documentation: Maintaining detailed system documentation, including configuration information, 
troubleshooting procedures, and security protocols. 
• 3.1.6 Manage Network Architecture: Configure and manage the HPC network infrastructure, including 
switches, routers, and firewalls (HPE Slingshot).  Optimize network performance, investigate and resolve network 
connectivity issues, and ensure network security. 
• 3.1.7 Storage Management: Manage the HPC storage system, including configuring and maintaining the file 
system (e.g., Lustre, HPE Parallel File System Storage, GPFS). Optimize storage performance for HPE HPC 
workloads, implement data backup and recovery procedures. Monitor storage capacity and usage. 
• 3.1.8 Software Deployment and Management: Install, configure, and maintain HPC software applications, 
including compilers, libraries, and scientific applications. (e.g. HPE Cray System Management, HPE Performance 
Cluster Manager, Slurm, Docker).  Manage software licenses. Ensuring software compatibility. Supporting users 
in using HPC software. 
• 3.1.9 Provide Expertise: Provide advice and guidance on best practices for HPC system administration. 
 
3.2 Task 2: Operational Support 
The contractor shall provide operational support to end-users and technical staff to maximize the utility and performance 
of the HPC system for AI/ML workloads. 
• 3.2.1 User Support: Provide technical support to users and serve as the primary point of contact for resolving 
user issues encountered on the HPC system performance.  Develop user documentation and conduct user training 
sessions. 
• 3.2.2 Performance Tuning and Optimization: Analyze and optimize AI/ML algorithm performance on the HPC 
cluster. Provide expert guidance to users on code parallelization, GPU utilization, and efficient use of the 
Slingshot interconnect and Lustre file system. 
• 3.2.3 Software Stack Management: Install, configure, and maintain a robust software stack for AI/ML 
development, including compilers, scientific libraries, machine learning frameworks (e.g., TensorFlow, PyTorch), 
and containerization technologies (e.g., Docker, Singularity/Apptainer). 
• 3.2.4 Knowledge Transfer: Develop and deliver training sessions and comprehensive documentation for 
government personnel on the administration and use of the HPC system. The goal is to enable a smooth transition 
to full government ownership and support at the conclusion of the contract period. 
3.3 Task 3: Cybersecurity Compliance 
The contractor shall ensure the HPC system meets all applicable Department of War (DoW) and DoD cybersecurity 
standards. 

 
Page 5 of 9 
 
SUPPORT SERVICES FOR HEWLETT PACKARD ENTERPRISE HIGH PERFORMANCE COMPUTE NODE 
 
• 3.3.1 System Hardening: Implement and maintain system configurations in accordance with Security Technical 
Implementation Guides (STIGs) and other mandated security controls. 
• 3.3.1.1 Quarterly, at each STIG cycle release by DISA, evaluate cybersecurity compliance of the HPC 
system against the most recent DISA STIG and create updated security checklists. 
• 3.3.1.2 Implement cyber security requirements due to CTO, directives or DISA STIG updates. 
• 3.3.1.3 Maintain a system administration guide with details on how to remediate each STIG item and 
step-by-step directions on manual implementation details for those STIG items that must be implemented 
manually 
• 3.3.1.4 Create and/or modify scripts and documentation supporting STIG compliance. 
 
• 3.3.2 Vulnerability Management: Conduct regular vulnerability scanning of the HPC environment. Remed

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION

3DX Data Migration

March 27, 2026

1.0 Description 

1.1 The United States Air Force, Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, AFLCMC/WVSS is seeking information from interested companies with the capability to deliver a data migration solution for the 3DEXPERIENCE (3DX) platform. Previous efforts configured the application code to serve as a collaboration and approval platform to support the Government's migration to a digital-based acquisition program. The application integrates data from other supporting applications including Cameo and Teamwork Cloud (TWC) and CATIA.

1.2 THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes; it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Further, the Air Force is not at this time seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI; all costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested party’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the www.sam.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor these sites for additional information pertaining to this requirement.

2.0 Background

The United States Air Force (“Government” or “Customer”) is executing a digital engineering approach to program execution guided by the “e-Program” Digital Engineering criteria set forth in the Digital Building Code published by SAF/AQ on 3 May 2021.  This approach is consistent with the five goals identified in the 2018 DoD Digital Engineering Strategy and the guidance provided in the Digital Engineering DODI 5000.97 (Dec 2023). 

3.0 Work Description 

3.1 The contractor will deploy or develop and deploy a solution that exports data on a recurring basis from one air-gapped on-premises Windows hosted 2025x 3DX instance and imports that data into another air-gapped on-premises Windows hosted 2025x 3DX instance in a traceable manner while maintaining data integrity, digital threads, and all metadata.

3.1.1	Data types in use include all objects ingestible and all objects created by 3DX, including but not limited to PDFs, Word, CATIA, 3DXML, and Enovia business objects with the ability to add new objects/types desired.  3DSwym data is desired but not required.

3.1.2	Work will continuously be occurring in each 3DX instance so solution must add/merge and not just overwrite/delete existing data to the imported instance.  Data from exported instance cannot be deleted in this process.

3.1.3	Solution will need to move all data to start but ability to move only new and updated data for all subsequent runs is desired.  

3.1.4	Ability to make all transferred data read-only but linkable in the second 3DX instance is desired.  Updated data is desired to be flagged/marked to indicate changes occurred.

3.1.5	Data movement only occurs from one 3DX instance to the other instance in one direction, with no ability for the second instance to communicate back to the first.  

3.1.6	Data and digital threads will need to be validated in the new instance without reaching back to original instance.

3.1.7	For any solution that requires it, the Contractor will assist with the Authority to Use (ATU) and/or the Authority to Operate (ATO) certifications at the IL5, IL6, and IL6+ levels. 

3.1.8	The contractor will not be responsible for the Cross Domain Solution and will not be hosting any data.

4.0 Requested Information 

4.1 Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper addressing the following questions:

4.1.1. Please include a brief description of how you would develop a data migration solution. Alternatively, if you plan on utilizing an existing application, please provide additional specifications. 

4.1.2 If developing a solution, what team configuration do you feel would be needed to complete the solution in a timely manner? Please provide your suggested FTE and labor mix, along with the estimated timeframe. 

4.1.3 Do you have any additional questions or suggestions that you believe would be helpful for this data migration effort? 

5.0 Responses 

5.1 Interested parties are requested to respond to this RFI with a white paper. 

5.2 White papers in Microsoft Word compatible format are due no later than April 26, 2026 at 4:00 PM and shall be submitted via e-mail only to the Contracting Officer; Capt. Landon Smith, landon.smith.13@us.af.mil. 

5.3 Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. To aid the Government, please segregate proprietary information. Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Results will be reviewed and retained by the government and Government support contractors. Solicitation does not obligate the government to issue an RFP or award a contract. Responses must be at responders expense.

5.4 Section 1 of the white paper shall provide administrative information, and shall include the following as a minimum: 

5.4.1 Name, mailing address, overnight delivery address (if different from mailing address), phone number, fax number, and e-mail of designated point of contact. 

5.4.2 Recommended contracting strategy. 

5.4.3 Business type (large business, small business, small disadvantaged business, 8(a)- certified small disadvantaged business, HUBZone small business, woman-owned small business, very small business, veteran-owned small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business) based upon North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541512, Computer Systems Design Services. “Small business concern” means a concern, including its affiliates, which is independently owned and operated, not dominant in the field of operation in which it is bidding on Government contracts, and qualified as a small business under the criteria and size standards in 13 CFR part 121. 

Please refer to Federal Acquisition Regulation FAR 19 for detailed information on Small Business Size Standards. The FAR is available at https://www.acquisition.gov/browse/index/far

5.4.4 The facility security clearance of the offeror.

5.5 The number of pages in Section 1 of the white paper shall not be included in the 8-page limitation, which applies only to Section 2 of the white paper. 

5.6 Section 2 of the white paper shall answer the issues addressed in Sections 3 and 4 of this RFI and shall be limited to 8 pages of text (excluding pictures and graphs).

6.0 Questions 

Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by e-mail to the Contracting Officer, Capt. Landon Smith, landon.smith.13@us.af.mil.  Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Questions will be answered by posting answers to the www.sam.gov website; accordingly, questions shall NOT contain proprietary or classified information. The Government does not guarantee that questions received after 10 April 2026 will be answered. To access the website, go to www.sam.gov. Interested parties are invited to subscribe to the website to ensure they receive any important information updates connected with this RFI. 

7.0 Summary 

THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY to identify sources that can provide a data migration solution within 3DX. The information provided in the RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The Air Force has not made a commitment to procure any services discussed, and release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

Performance Work Statement

A. Introduction:  

The US Geological Survey (USGS), Denver Argon Geochronology Lab (DAGL), Denver, CO has a requirement for the automated operation of mass spectrometers and peripheral hardware (e.g. valves, lasers). The DAGL aims to achieve this by developing new, customized automation software modules built using a commercially available programming environment designed to enable construction of applications with graphical user interfaces for hardware automation, such as LabVIEW or an equivalent environment. This effort requires support for developing the overall application architecture, programming the custom automation software, and training laboratory staff in its construction, use, and maintenance.

B. Background: 

	

The US Geological Survey’s (USGS) Denver Argon Geochronology Lab (DAGL), located at the Geology, Geophysics, and Geochemistry Science Center (GGGSC), produces 40Ar/39Ar geochronology data for multiple USGS Programs, including the Mineral Resources Program and National Cooperative Geologic Mapping Program, among others. These data benefit a variety of stakeholders, from federal and state government agencies, to industry and academia.

The DAGL historically used a Macintosh-based, closed-source software application called Mass Spec for operating analytical instruments and associated peripheral hardware. Changes in USGS information technology (IT) regulations forced the DAGL to move away from Macintosh systems in the lab in 2022, and the developer of Mass Spec is nearing retirement and has indicated support will terminate. In response, the DAGL purchased a new open-source software application called Pychron that was being embraced by the 40Ar/39Ar community at that time. Although Pychron has allowed for intermittent operation of the lab, it has proven to not be sufficient for our needs. The Pychron developer is not regularly available for required bug fixes (which are abundant, especially following regular mandatory IT patching), and while the code is open-source, we have found the documentation is not sufficient for us to contribute meaningfully to code maintenance, and the lack of transparency of calculations has introduced significant issues for data management and quality.

The pivot to develop a customized LabVIEW (or equivalent)-based software application has the benefit of direct involvement by laboratory staff, enabling ongoing updates and improvements to be made after they are fully trained in the application. We aim to utilize an environment that represents a major software development environment and framework that is successfully deployed as customized applications in similar USGS labs (e.g. Denver Noble Gas lab, Moffett Argon Lab). We intend to build on the shoulders of these existing customized LabVIEW (or equivalent) applications to create new software specific to our analytical systems, but we do not currently have the expertise to do this.

C. Definitions:

40Ar/39Ar geochronology – an analytical method that involves the measurement of isotopes of argon in a material to determine a geologic age.

LabVIEW– a graphical programming environment and software framework provided for purchase by National Instruments that allows users to create custom applications (including graphical user interfaces) for hardware automation/control, and data collection.

D. Scope:

The USGS DAGL requires a complete LabVIEW (or equivalent)-based, custom software solution for acquiring data on the Thermo Scientific Argus VI mass spectrometers located within the DAGL. While developing the software, the Contractor shall actively involve laboratory personnel in the design and implementation of the new application(s) and simultaneously train them in the programming environment with a focus on components that will aid them in the long-term operation and maintenance of the software application(s). In addition to communicating with and operating the Argus mass spectrometers, the software application(s) will communicate with and/or control a variety of hardware peripherals, including Photon Machines lasers (and motorized sample stages), pressure gauges, ion pumps, Agilent DAQs, and thermocouples. The software application(s) will appropriately store analytical data and instrument metadata in files or a database, as needed by lab personnel. The software will integrate instrument/hardware communications and analytical data storage with required sample metadata for 40Ar/39Ar geochronology into an appropriate graphical user interface. 

E.  Technical Requirements.

The Contractor shall provide the following:

Basic Training. Train lab personnel in basic programming environment concepts and design patterns, with a focus on software components relevant to instrument control and data acquisition and storage.

Create modules in programming environment for communications with and control of:

Thermo Scientific Argus VI Mass Spectrometers

Pressure gauges

Ion pumps

Agilent DAQs for control of valves and readback of thermocouples

Photon Machines CO2 and UV laser systems

Create graphical user interface for sample metadata entry

Create module for data acquisition, to include:

Graphical user interface for building and executing run sequences 

Live instrument feedback (e.g., visuals of valve states and plots of data as they are acquired)

Create module for data storage to files and/or database

Create complete solution (including graphical user interface) for integrating the above modules

Lab personnel will be proficient in programming environment such that they can maintain and modify the resulting software application(s).

Modules will be accepted when they are able to control each piece of hardware.

User interface sufficiently captures sample metadata and stores in appropriate locations.

Data can be accurately and reliably acquired in an automated run sequence.

Data are accurately and reliably stored in appropriate file formats and/or database.

The complete solution is user-friendly and accessible to lab personnel. Source code will be version controlled and stored in one or more USGS DAGL GitLab repositories.

E. Performance standards:

If the Contractor fails to perform any task to the required technical standards, quality standards or time standards, the Government will notify the Contractor of the failure. The Contractor shall re-do or re-perform all substandard activities at no added cost to the Government.

Network (NCSN), Pacific Northwest Seismic Network (PNSN), Southern California Seismic Network 
(SCSN), and the USGS ShakeAlert® Earthquake Early Warning (EEW) Project.

(BPM) platform. In 2021, the agency selected and invested in the Camunda platform to automate and manage 
critical business processes. This procurement is a direct follow-on action to maintain the operational status of these 
existing systems and leverage the significant prior investment in technology, development, and personnel training.
 
The scope of this requirement includes the following: 
Software Licensing:
Procurement of Camunda Enterprise Edition software licenses is sufficient to support the agency's 
production, staging, and development environments.
Software Maintenance:
Access to all new versions, releases, security patches, and software updates for the Camunda 
platform to ensure it remains secure and up to date.
Technical Success Support:
Access to enterprise-level technical support from Camunda's subject matter experts to assist with 
troubleshooting, configuration, and best practices.
 
A.2       BACKGROUND 
The DFAS Portal Workflows team plays a critical role in driving efficiency and automation across the organization, 
supporting 29 distinct workflows that encompass a potential user base of up to 30,000 individuals. To further 
enhance its process automation capabilities, DFAS strategically selected Camunda Enterprise as its enterprise-wide 
solution in 2021. This acquisition will ensure continued support, modernization, and scalability of the Camunda 
Enterprise environment, including migration to Azure Government Cloud.

maintenance, and technical success support.

Request for Proposal 
Global Payroll Services 
21 April 2026 
 
 
OVERVIEW 
 
The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) has a requirement for a Global Payroll 
Servicer. For full details of this requirement, see the attached Performance Work Statement 
(PWS). All attachments for this RFP can be accessed at 
https://abmcgov.box.com/s/r9vag3qzvbu8el2zc2zby3wg6s1x16x0.  
 
The global payroll system must be capable of integrating with the Human Resources 
Information System (HRIS), procured under a separate solicitation; for information relating to 
the HRIS requirements, see solicitation 74330226R0044, available at 
https://www.abmc.gov/about-us/contracting-rfp/ and 
https://abmcgov.box.com/s/1q06rty7tqcl0z4g8ny05adbjo7952n3.   
 
CONTRACT TYPE 
 
ABMC intends to utilize a  predominantly time & materials  contract type, but vendors may 
propose any contract type they believe is most advantageous to the Government.   
 
PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
ABMC is seeking services for a base year plus four option years. 
 
PROPOSAL PREPARATION INSTRUCTIONS  
 
If interested in this requirement, please submit a proposal via email to the undersigned at 
nerenga@abmc.gov no later than 4:00 pm EDT on 29 May 2026. Questions must be received 
no later than 5 May 2026. Product demonstrations may be requested and scheduled with 
any or all vendors at ABMC’s discretion following receipt of proposals. 
 
If any portion of the Performance Work Statement cannot be addressed or complied with, 
it must be noted within the proposal . Alternative CLIN structures, including options , are 
permitted if in the Government’s best interest. The proposal should contain the following:  
 
1) Cover Letter. Submit a signed and dated cover letter to nerenga@abmc.gov at or before the 
exact time specified in this RFP. As a minimum, cover letters must show:  
 
a. The RFP number;  
b. The name, address, and telephone number of the offeror;  
c. The company’s CAGE or UID (if applicable);  
d. “Remit to” address, if different than mailing address;  

 
 
 
2 
 
e. Acknowledgment of any applicable RFP Amendments;  
 
2) Technical Volume. The PWS  provides the Government’s overall objectives for this RFP. 
Please ensure all aspects are addressed. The proposal should specify in clear, understandable 
terms the methodologies used to perform requirements of the type outlined in the PWS. 
Specifically, please include the following: 
 
a. Executive Summary 
b. Company Profile and Relevant Experience 
c. Detailed Response to the Scope of Work 
d. Three references that have a similar scope and demonstrate similar experience (including 
the client name, URLs to the websites, description of the work performed, and contact 
information) 
e. Implementation Timeline 
f. Service Level Agreement (SLA) terms  
Offerors should also submit a copy of the checklist in Attachment 2 to verify all questions have 
been answered in the proposal.

all taxes, including the VAT, as per agreements signed between the governments of the United

desired invoicing schedule.

Part One: Scope of Services 
1. General Information 
1.1 Background 
The American Battle Monuments Commission (ABMC) is an independent agency of the executive 
branch of the US government, established by legislation in 1923. It maintains military cemeteries 
and memorials in countries around the world commemorating the US war-dead. 
 
ABMC is staffed by around 575 full-time civilian employees, around 90 of whom are US citizens. The 
agency employs approximately 420 permanent and 50 temporary/seasonal civilian foreign nationals 
in the 10 countries where ABMC installations are located – six in Europe (France, Belgium, Italy, 
Netherlands, United Kingdom and Luxembourg), plus Tunisia, the Philippines, Panama and Mexico. 
See Appendix I for the list of covered countries and foreign national employee populations, which 
range from 300 in France, down to two in Mexico. 
 
The agency is headquartered in Washington, D.C. and has an Overseas office in Paris, France, where 
HR and finance directorates oversee the administration of foreign nationals, all of whom are directly 
employed and managed by the agency. 
 
ABMC has a requirement for payroll services for foreign national employees in 7 countries (France, 
Belgium, Italy, Netherlands, United Kingdom, Luxembourg, and Tunisia). The Philippines, Panama, 
and Mexico may be added at a later date.  Human Resources Information System (HRIS) 
requirements are covered under a separate solicitation  (see 74330226R0044, available at 
ABMC.gov). 
 
1.2 Special Conditions 
Please note that: 
• While ABMC is part of the foreign mission of the government of the United States it is not 
considered an “embassy” and is not exempt from local labor practices. 
• ABMC makes payroll and benefits payments directly from the United States Department of 
the Treasury and generally cannot use the services of a commercial bank to make payments. 
See Appendix II for more details. In the exceptional cases where benefits of payments are 
required to be paid or debited from a bank in the country of service, ABMC will require 
additional payroll services to act as the intermediary. Currently this is required in France 
(income tax) and Italy (social security and pension.  
• Accounting services are outsourced through a shared service agreement with the US 
Department of the Interior. This is an Oracle-based accounting system, and the new payroll 
service provider will be required to provide a balanced GL output file for accounting. (See 
Appendix III for more details.) 

3 
 
 
2. Objective 
The main objective is to deliver an accurate, timely monthly payroll to ABMC foreign national 
employees that is compliant with both local labor laws and ABMC internal regulations. The second 
objective is to reduce manual processes and dependency on country ‑specific workarounds. The 
third objective is to provide customer service to ABMC and provide consistent social and legal watch. 
 
3. Scope of services 
The scope of services for this project covers a typical set of payroll managed services across all 7 
countries listed in Appendix I, with the possible future addition of 3 more countries (the Philippines, 
Panama, Mexico). 
 
These services include: 
• Gross to Net Processing 
• Pay slips 
• U.S. Treasury disbursements 
• Inbound & Outbound interfaces 
• Legal & Statutory reporting 
• Lodgment service to local authorities 
• Employee queries 
• Year-end preparation 
• Year-end report distribution 
• Accounting interface 
  
4. Project Timeline 
ABMC will agree on a timeline with the chosen payroll supplier, in conjunction with the chosen 
human resources information system supplier that is being selected separately but concurrently. 
However, its goal is to select a provider and to go-live by January 2027.  

4 
 
5. Artiﬁcial Intelligence 
Interested Contractors shall provide proposals that are clearly written, technically sound, detailed, 
and tailored to each element of ABMC’s performance work statement.  Contractors shall not simply 
rephrase or summarize the specific requirements of this s olicitation without offering a clear 
solution.  
  
ABMC acknowledges the evolving role of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in content development. 
However, all submitted proposals shall reflect the Contractor’s own understanding, capabilities, and 
proposed approach. Proposals that are generic, lack relev ance, and/or contain AI -generated text 
drafted without thoughtful human analysis and input will be considered non-responsive.   
  
Contractors shall ensure that proposal submissions are written, reviewed and refined by subject 
matter experts familiar with ABMC’s specific requirements, and that proposals demonstrate a 
meaningful grasp of ABMC's mission, constraints, and operating envir onment. 
 
 
 
  

5

This section specifies ABMC’s detailed requirements. P lease answer all required questions in your

reporting, and employee service. Indicate where there are gaps in country/service capability. 
B. List which human resources information systems your payroll system can interface with,

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT 
FOR 
Transportation Command (TRANSCOM) Reference Data Management (TRDM) 
In Support of the United States Transportation Command 
 
Contract Number: TBD 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
DATE: TBD 
 
Prepared by 
UNITED STATES TRANSPORTATION COMMAND 
DIRECTORATE OF COMMAND, CONTROL, COMMUNICATIONS AND CYBER 
SYSTEMS 
 


 
 
Table of Contents 
1. Background ............................................................................................................................... 3 
2. Scope ......................................................................................................................................... 3 
3. Goal ........................................................................................................................................... 3 
4. Brief Summary of the Task Areas ............................................................................................... 3 
5. Brief Summary of the "Shall" Statements .................................................................................. 4 
6. Brief Summary of the Deliverables ............................................................................................. 5 
7. Period of Performance ............................................................................................................... 5 
8. Brief Summary of the DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) Code Assignments ............... 5 
 
 
 
 
  

1. Background 
The United States Transportation Command (USTRANSCOM) is a combatant command that 
provides global transportation and logistics support. The TRANSCOM Reference Data 
Management (TRDM) system is the official Program of Record for the command's enterprise 
reference data. TRDM's mission is to collect, maintain, and distribute standardized reference data 
from authoritative sources to ensure data interoperability and synchronization across all 
USTRANSCOM systems and partners. 
2. Scope 
The scope of this project is to provide the technical operation, maintenance, and distribution of 
the TRDM system and its data. The contractor will be responsible for a wide range of support 
tasks, including but not limited to: 
• Requirement analysis 
• Data collection and management 
• Interface and architecture validation 
• Data distribution 
• Implementation, planning, and documentation related to the software development 
lifecycle 
3. Goal 
The primary goal is to establish and maintain TRDM as a trusted and authoritative source of 
reference data for the entire USTRANSCOM enterprise, its users, and its interconnection 
partners. The program prioritizes adherence to key initiatives such as Data Governance, Data 
Security, Modernization, and Zero Trust. 
4. Brief Summary of the Task Areas 
The contractor is responsible for comprehensive management and support across five main areas: 
• Contract Management: Includes overall program management, regular reporting (weekly, 
monthly), progress reviews, security reviews, and managing the transition-in and 
transition-out processes. 
• User Access & Operations Support: Involves maintaining the TRDM websites on both 
unclassified and classified networks (AWS GovCloud), managing user access, providing 
help desk support during business hours (0800-1800 CT), and ensuring data access 
complies with DoD security policies. 
• System Service Management: Encompasses the management of incidents, system 
configuration, changes, software releases, and knowledge. This includes facilitating the 

Configuration Control Board (CCB), managing data change requests, and maintaining 
interconnection agreements. 
• System Operations Management: Focuses on the technical health and security of the 
system. Responsibilities include monitoring system resources, automating data exchange 
through web services, managing capacity and load balancing, executing the vulnerability 
management (IA VM) program, and performing database administration (PostgreSQL), 
backup, and recovery. 
• Data Management and Sharing: Requires advanced data engineering to build and 
maintain data pipelines (ETL/ELT), manage data quality, maintain the data catalog and 
metadata, oversee the data lifecycle, and document the data architecture. 
• Cybersecurity: Requires  comprehensive cybersecurity obligations for government 
contractors, detailing requirements for incident reporting, secure software development, 
workforce qualifications, and adherence to the Risk Management Framework (RMF). 
5. Brief Summary of the "Shall" Statements 
The PWS contains numerous mandatory requirements ("shall" statements). The most critical 
obligations related to security and compliance are summarized below: 
• Personnel Security: All contractor personnel shall be U.S. citizens and shall possess a 
minimum of a final Secret security clearance. This clearance shall be maintained for the 
duration of the contract. 
• Cybersecurity Framework and Policies: The contractor shall support all activities to 
obtain and maintain the Risk Management Framework (RMF) Authorization to Operate 
(ATO). The contractor shall also comply with all relevant DoD, USTRANSCOM, and 
Federal cybersecurity policies and shall participate in an Annual Security Review (ASR). 
• Vulnerability and Risk Management: The contractor shall execute the Information 
Assurance Vulnerability Management (IA VM) program, perform static and dynamic code 
scans before deployment, and remediate all "Critical" and "High" findings. A Plan of 
Action & Milestones (POA&M) for all vulnerabilities shall be developed and maintained. 
• Secure Development and Operations: All development shall adhere to secure coding 
practices. The contractor shall enforce role-based access controls and conduct annual 
failover and recovery exercises. 
• Incident Reporting: The contractor shall report all cyber incidents to the government 
within 72 hours of discovery and shall deliver a detailed Cyber Incident Report within 72 
hours of resolution. 
• General Reporting and Documentation: Beyond security, the contractor shall deliver 
regular reports (Weekly, Monthly), create and maintain management plans 
(Configuration, Backup, Transition), and provide materials and minutes for quarterly 
reviews. 

6. Brief Summary of the Deliverables 
The contractor is required to provide numerous deliverables throughout the contract period. The 
most significant ones include: 
• Regular Reports: Weekly Activities Report (WAR), Monthly Status Report (MSR), and 
Monthly Metrics Report (MMR). 
• Management Plans: A Contract Management Plan at the start of the contract, a 
Transition-In Plan, and a Transition-Out Plan. Several system-level plans (e.g., Failover 
Guide, CM Plan) must be reviewed and updated annually. 
• Reviews and Meetings: Presentation materials and minutes for quarterly In Progress 
Reviews (IPRs) and an Annual Security Review (ASR). 
• Security and RMF Artifacts: A Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) Report, Cyber-
Incident Reports as needed, and all necessary documentation to support the RMF 
Authorization to Operate (ATO). 
• Other Direct Costs (ODC) Purchase Requests: All ODC purchases require the contractor 
to submit a written request with competitive quotes to the COR at least five business days 
in advance. 
7. Period of Performance 
The contract is structured with a one-month transition period, a one-year base period, and four 
one-year option periods. 
• Transition Period: September 1, 2026 – September 30, 2026 
• Base Period: October 1, 2026 – September 30, 2027 
• Option Period One: Through September 30, 2028 
• Option Period Two: Through September 30, 2029 
• Option Period Three: Through September 30, 2030 
• Option Period Four: Through September 30, 2031 
8. Brief Summary of the DoD Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) Code Assignments 
The PWS mandates that all personnel performing cyberspace work be qualified according to the 
DCWF. Most positions are designated as IT Privileged Users and require specific certifications. 
• Key Roles Identified: The assigned codes correspond to roles such as Program Manager, 
Systems Administrator, Software Developer, Database Administrator, Systems Security 
Analyst, Information System Security Officer, and Data Architect/Engineer. 
• Required Certifications: The required Computing Environment (CE) certifications are 
primarily focused on Amazon Web Services (AWS), including AWS Certified Cloud 

Practitioner, Developer, Solutions Architect, and Data Engineer. SecurityX, CISM, 
Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Database certifications for 
PostgreSQL are also required.

2. Background Information

2.1.   Scope of the Requirement

2.2.   Place of Performance 
 
Primary place of performance is on-site at Scott AFB, IL, for up to 11 on-site contractor

Alternate Place of Performance – Contingency Only. As determined by the COR,

2.3.   Anticipated Award Timeline

Request for Information (RFI) for Enterprise Governance, Data Tagging, and Records Management Solution for Microsoft 365

1. GENERAL INFORMATION

Notice Type: Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought

RFI Number: RFI-ARMY-DTSPO-2026-0420

Issuing Office: Army Contracting Command – Aberdeen Proving Ground, Huachuca Division, Bravo Branch

NAICS Code: 541512 - Computer Systems Design Services

Date Issued: 20 April 2026

Response Due Date: 28 April 2026, 4:00 PM Arizona Time

DISCLAIMER: This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked “Proprietary” will be handled accordingly.

2. BACKGROUND

The U.S. Army operates one of the largest and most complex Microsoft 365 (M365) environments in the world, presenting significant challenges for governance, security, and compliance. The Government requires a technical solution to enforce policy, automate administrative and records management tasks, provide hierarchical visibility and control, and empower a delegated administration model across Major Commands (MACOMs) and subordinate organizations. The solution must seamlessly integrate with and enhance the native capabilities of the M365 platform while scaling to meet the Army's performance demands.

3. SCOPE OF REQUIREMENT

The Government is seeking a mature, scalable Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solution to meet requirements across several key functional areas, including Enterprise Governance, Data Sensitivity and Security (Data Tagging), Automated Records Management, SharePoint & Teams Management, and Storage Optimization. The solution must be a configurable, vendor-supported platform, not a custom software development effort.

4. INFORMATION REQUESTED

Interested parties are requested to provide a response that addresses the following sections.

PART I: CORPORATE INFORMATION

1.1 Company Name & Address:

1.2 Point of Contact: (Name, Title, Email, Phone Number)

1.3 CAGE Code & Unique Entity Identifier (UEI):

1.4 Business Size & Socio-Economic Status: (e.g., Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), WOSB, SDVOSB, etc.)

1.5 Federal Contract Experience: Briefly describe your experience providing IT solutions to DoD or other Federal agencies. Include relevant contract vehicles you currently hold (e.g., GSA MAS, SEWP, ITES-SW2).

1.6 Subcontracting: Does your approach for this requirement require subcontracting?

PART II: SOLUTION OVERVIEW

2.1 Solution Name & Description: Provide the name of your potential proposed COTS solution and a brief, high-level overview of its architecture (e.g., Software as a Service (SaaS), on-premises virtual appliance, hybrid).

2.2 Federal Security Compliance: Describe your potential solution's current security posture. Is it FedRAMP authorized? At what level (Low, Moderate, High)? Does the solution operate in Azure Government Cloud at DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5)?

2.3 Maturity: How long has the potentially proposed solution been commercially available?

PART III: CAPABILITY & TECHNICAL QUESTIONS

Please provide a direct response to each of the following questions regarding your potentially proposed solution.

How do you integrate with other capabilities? Particularly MS Purview and SharePoint Online.

What Admin permissions or API permissions required for the software to function?

How are admin permissions managed within the software?

How are logs handled?

How are reports and alerts managed? Are they customizable?

What administrative roles or service accounts from your solution require permissions within the Army’s Microsoft 365 (A365) tenant?

Do any components require tenant-wide administrative permissions (e.g., Global Admin, SharePoint Admin, Compliance Admin)? If so, how are these used?

Does the product use Azure Entra ID app registrations, and what Application Programming Interface (API) permissions are required?

Does the solution require any vendor access to Army M365 data or your solution’s supporting infrastructure during normal operations or troubleshooting?

Describe which functions of your solution run inside the Army M365 tenant versus within your hosted environment.

Does any processing leverage vendor-managed Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) models, and can AI/ML analytics be performed without exporting sensitive content or metadata?

What is the expected volume of API calls per day, and does the solution require elevated throttling limits?

Does your solution support Common Access Card/Personal Identity Verification (CAC/PIV), conditional access, and Entra ID-based identity?

What access (if any) do your personnel or systems require to Army M365 data or to your solution’s supporting infrastructure (e.g., SaaS back end, support tools, logs), including during troubleshooting, and what authentication/authorization controls govern that access?

Can the solution operate with zero vendor access after deployment, and can all vendor access be disabled or audited by Army Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM)?

Identify whether any Army data (including metadata, logs, labels, or content) is copied, stored, or processed outside the M365 boundary. Include any dependencies on vendor-managed infrastructure, hosting outside Department of Defense (DoD) IL5, or use of non-U.S. regions or subcontractors.

If your solution includes SaaS or vendor-hosted components, identify the compliance level of those environments (e.g., FedRAMP High, DoD IL5) and status of any relevant authorizations (e.g., DISA Provisional Authorization for IL5). 

How does your solution enforce Army-aligned delegated administrative scoping, and are all administrative actions fully audit-logged with the ability to export logs to Army Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) tools in near real time?

Where are audit logs, telemetry, and analytics data stored, and can all such data remain entirely within the Army’s M365 tenant? If any logs reside in vendor systems, identify what data elements are stored, for how long, and in what regions or environments.

How does the solution ensure compliance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) retention rules when performing:

Redundant, Obsolete, and Trivial (ROT) cleanup

lifecycle actions

metadata remediation

bulk operations

Does any processing leverage vendor-managed AI/ML models outside the Army environment?

Does your backup capability require extraction of data outside Microsoft’s boundary, and (if so) are backups stored in environments certified at IL5?

Can data restores be performed without violating retention or legal hold constraints?

Provide a complete list of all administrative actions your system can take on Army content or configuration, including:

Where the logic runs (tenant / vendor / hybrid)

Required permissions

How actions are validated and logged

Whether actions can be restricted by MACOM or command

What guardrails exist to prevent accidental or malicious bulk changes?

Audio Visual (AV) / Video Teleconferencing (VTC) Lifecycle Information Technology (IT) Support (AV LIT)

Hill Air Force Base 

Request for Information (RFI)

Overview 

The Air Force Nuclear Weapon Center (AFNWC) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) Systems Directorate (SD) team is conducting market research to define the scope and requirements of the Audio Visual (AV)/ Video Teleconferencing (VTC) Lifecycle Information Technology (IT) Support (AV LIT). For this RFI, Government is seeking input from industry on the capability to operate within a Special Access Program (SAP) environment. 

Scope

The primary objective of this contract is to provide lifecycle sustainment for current and future Traditional and Air Force Microsoft Teams (MS Teams) based Video Teleconferencing (VTC), Audio Visual (AV), and Information Technology (IT) hardware systems across ICBM Directorate Operating Locations in the Continental United States (CONUS). 

The Contractor shall provide comprehensive Consulting and Design Services for new and existing VTC and AV solutions, as well as for IT hardware installation. The Contractor shall also provide end-to-end Maintenance Services which include, but are not limited to, tier 3 support, decommissioning, and lifecycle replacement. 

To facilitate the procurement of necessary equipment and services, the Contractor shall follow the established Pricing Catalogue of pre-approved hardware, standard conference room hardware configurations, and associated services. Services and hardware may be requested in addition to the standardized configurations. This catalogue will be used for all purchasing and installation activities performed under this contract. Individual Task Orders may deviate from the Price Catalogue as negotiated between the requiring activity and the contractor. 

This contract requires the contractor to obtain and maintain necessary security clearances and to coordinate with ICBM personnel on all matters involving security impact and cybersecurity compliance, including the implementation and management of controls under the Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIG) and Risk Management Framework (RMF). The contractor shall provide the organizational resources, both technical and functional, required for managing contract performance. 

Request for Information (RFI)

Does your company have the ability to perform Video Teleconferencing (VTC)/Audio Visual (AV) Lifecycle Information Technology (IT) in a SAP space?

Does your company currently hold a top security clearance (TS/SCI/SAP)? 

Please state your company’s demographics (i.e., Small Business, Large Business, etc.)

Does your company have any current contracts under a Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) or Governmentwide Acquisition Contracts (GWACs)? If so, please specify.

Responses

Responses shall be UNCLASSIFIED

Please provide a cover sheet with the following company information: 

Interested parties are required to respond in the following format: 

Microsoft Word for office 2007 (or newer) compatible

1-inch margins 

12-point font 

Please submit the responses no later than 1200 MDT on Monday, 27 April 2026 to both Mr. Tanner Nielsen, Contracting Officer at tanner.nielsen@us.af.mil and Mr. Quade McGuire, Contracting Specialist at quade.mcguire@us.af.mil. 	

Disclaimer

This announcement constitutes an RFI issued pursuant to FAR 52.215-3 – Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes. No solicitation exists; therefore, please do not request a copy of the solicitation. This RFI is only to support market research for the ICBM AV LIT effort. The information provided in this RFI is subject to change and is not binding on the Government. The USAF has not made a commitment to procure any of the items discussed herein, and the release of this RFI should not be construed as such a commitment or as authorization to incur cost for which reimbursement would be required or sought. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned.

THE NGA SOFTWARE WAY
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
SOFTWARE METRICS
To deliver on its current and future mission, NGA needs to deliver useful software faster and more consistently. 
To measure progress toward this intent, NGA will track three key metrics for each software product: availability, lead time for 
changes, and deployment frequency. Additionally, each software product is expected to have its own product-specific metrics 
to track how well the product is working for its users. Together, these metrics balance speed and reliability and describe a product’s 
impact and value.
To consistently track these metrics and realize the above intent, this document provides a set of elements NGA and contractor teams 
must meet while building, iterating on, and operating software products. These elements ensure each software team has the people, 
processes, and tools in place to effectively operate at NGA. 
The metrics and elements in this document, collectively referred to as “The NGA Software Way,” serve as an implementation guide 
to supplement NGA’s Technology Strategy and provide additional specific guidance for teams building and operating software.

A NOTE FROM THE CTO 
To deliver on its current and future mission, NGA needs to deliver useful software faster 
and more consistently. To do this, the NGA Technology Strategy describes changes in 
approach, tools, and behavior that will result in faster iterations, more flexible products, 
and better-satisfied users and customers. The NGA Software Way is an implementation 
guide to supplement NGA’s Technology Strategy and provide additional specific 
guidance for teams building and operating software.
Our intent is to get to a place where NGA software products are designed and built 
with users, can be automatically updated in production daily, and use product-specific 
metrics to make decisions. We believe in small, empowered, cross-functional teams that 
deeply understand their users and constantly work directly with those users to deliver on 
their mission.
Implementing The NGA Software Way won’t happen all at once; we must start with 
iteratively tracking and improving these metrics and meeting each element below. As 
we do this together, and with an understanding of this intent, we will successfully deliver 
software products with the speed, accuracy, and precision NGA’s mission demands.   
SOFTWARE METRICS
The three initial metrics all programs must track for each software product delivered to users are availability, lead time for changes, 
and deployment frequency. It is important to note that NGA is not unique in using these metrics. These are three of the primary 
metrics DevOps Research and Assessment (DORA) has studied over the past six years. These metrics use data from over 31,000 
professionals worldwide as well as rigorous statistical methods to study the most effective ways to develop and deploy technology. 
More information about the DORA metrics and study can be found in this DORA report: https://services.google.com/fh/files/misc/
state-of-devops-2019.pdf.
These metrics provide visibility into how NGA balances speed (deployment frequency and lead time for changes) and stability 
(availability) during product development and operations. These two efforts, speed and stability, were once believed to be negatively 
correlated — increasing one would decrease the other. DORA research has conclusively shown that speed and stability are 
outcomes that enable each other and high-performing teams do better in both of these areas. This is what NGA is aiming for and 
moving toward. 
For software teams using NGA’s enterprise-managed version control and Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) 
pipeline, deployment frequency and lead time for changes will be automatically tracked within those services’ dashboards. To 
enable that automation, the recommended tagging method can be found in the appendix. For teams not using NGA’s enterprise-
managed version control and CI/CD pipeline, lead time for changes and deployment frequency must be independently calculated and 
transparently shared. All teams are expected to regularly share their metrics with teammates, stakeholders, users, and leadership. 
Eventually, teams will programmatically share these metrics to a central, NGA-managed location. 
AVAILABILITY
Availability is about ensuring a product or service is accessible to users when they need it. At a 
macro level, availability represents technology teams and organizations meeting user expectations 
about the software they are deploying and operating. Any time a user is not able to access a 
software product, that product is unavailable. Availability may be impacted by actions a product 
team itself takes or through issues with upstream or downstream dependencies. There is no 
distinction in availability to users based on what caused the issue; whether planned or unplanned 
and no matter where the issue originated, the impact of a product being unavailable when users 
need it is the same.
Alex Loehr
NGA Chief Technology Officer

PAGE |  3
Approved for Public Release, 22-195
Higher availability is better, as it means the product is accessible when users need and expect it. 
Tracking availability automatically enables teams to know when something goes wrong, giving the 
opportunity to investigate issues more rapidly and proactively. Although teams may have different 
availability requirements depending on mission and user needs, teams are generally expected to 
maintain at least 99.9% availability in production, which translates to about one business day of 
downtime per year.
LEAD TIME FOR CHANGES
Lead time for changes tracks how long it takes to deliver a feature for mission use once it has 
been developed. Lead time for changes is calculated as the median time between when code is 
committed to when it is deployed to a production environment, where it can be used during an 
actual mission (not in a test environment). That figure is measured across all commits within a 
given time period. Measuring this enables teams to understand where bottlenecks are in getting 
features to production and prioritize where to optimize. 
Shorter lead times are better because they enable faster feedback on what is built and allow 
teams to course correct more rapidly. Additionally, faster lead times allow faster fixes with higher 
confidence when there are issues, which directly impacts availability as well. DORA research 
shows high-performing teams have lead times for changes of less than one week. 
DEPLOYMENT FREQUENCY 
Deployment frequency is how often a product is deployed to production. A product team will 
do many additional deployments to testing, development, staging, and other non-production 
environments. The deployment frequency metric is specifically related to deployments to 
production, however, where users actually use the product to complete the mission or function. 
To the maximum extent possible, deployments are expected to be automated (see Automated 
Deployments on page 9), so increasing deployment frequency does not linearly increase workload 
on the team. 
Deployment frequency is a proxy for batch size. Reducing batch size has consistently been shown 
to accelerate feedback, improve efficiency, reduce risk and overhead, increase team motivation 
and urgency, and reduce costs (for more details, see Accelerate, page 16, by Nicole Forsgren, Jez 
Humble, and Gene Kim). DORA research shows high-performing teams deploy at least once per 
week. 
                    +
PRODUCT-SPECIFIC METRICS
In addition to the above three metrics that will be consistently tracked across all software programs, 
each software product is expected to have its own key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics to 
track how well the product is working for its users. While the first three metrics are about balancing 
speed and stability, these product-specific metrics are about product priorities and value. Software 
products contribute to NGA’s mission in different ways, so their success must be uniquely measured, 
and each team must define its own product-specific metrics.
