# Questions Answers w/ SOO Para. Reference
1
Point of clarification for 1.5.1.2 - will installations without local IT support require the vendor provide 
any additional vulnerability scanning and management capabilities? We noted the previous response 
that the request is to provide the critical oversight, analysis, remediation guidance and hands-on 
technical support to manage the vulnerability lifecycle, not on operating the testing tools themselves.
No additional vulnerability scanning and management capabilities are required.  
While tool provision is out of scope (SOO 1.5.2), the contractor is responsible for 
the technical support for ongoing vulnerability management, including monitoring, 
lifecycle management and remediation guidance, and hands-on support as 
required by installations, both remote and onsite as needed (SOO 1.5.1.2, 
4.1.3.1.1).
2
Is AFSVC open to a fully vendor-managed model for remote security operations (SOC, SIEM)?
No. The SOO outlines a collaborative model to empower local staff, not a fully 
vendor-managed operation. Your role is to augment, not replace, local personnel 
(SOO 1.3.1, 2.2.3).
3
To what degree is in-person / hands-on support expected, and for what geographic areas? Would a 
proposed solution for quarterly travel be acceptable, or is the vendor expected to provide permanent 
local staff to support installations?
On-site and remote assistance is required (SOO 3.1). Expect hands-on support at 
~20-30 of 104 locations (SOO 1.4, 1.5.1.2). Travel is as-needed for physical audits 
and audit preparedness; permanent local staff are not required (SOO 6.4.2).
4
What level of security clearance is expected for vendor personnel? Will all vendor staff engaged in 
supporting AFSVC require a Tier 1? Will any vendor staff require a Tier 3?
Tier 1 is sufficient, most of the work is unclassified (SOO 6.6.1). Refer to SOO 
6.7.2.2, Contractor personnel shall not be assigned to perform duties within IAT-II 
or IAT-III, and or requiring “Limited Privileged Access” such as system or database 
administration rights, to any NAFI application or network.
5
Will vendor interact with any CUI / does the proposed solution require a CMMC certification?
Yes, the vendor will handle CUI and require training per SOO 6.6.3. Refer to SOO 
3.2 Contractor Qualifications.
6
Are all assets centrally managed (e.g., centralized patching tools, endpoint management, 
configuration management)?If not, identify unmanaged or partially managed assets.
The objective is to achieve a "proactive, centrally-governed security posture" (SOO 
1.3.1), which indicates assets are not currently all centrally managed. The SOO 
notes that "critical gaps in security tools and on-site technical support prevent a 
proactive, centrally managed defense" (SOO 1.2.1). 
7 Are legacy or end of life systems present? If yes, list known unsupported software or systems and 
any business constraints.
Any in-scope legacy or end of life systems will be upgraded by August 2026.  Many 
are scoped out using P2PE terminals.
8
Are externally facing assets included in scope?(Web servers, VPNs, firewalls, cloud services, etc.)
External assets are out of scope of this SOO, penetration testing is being 
conducted, per SOO 1.5.2.  The SOO requires expertise with firewalls, VPNs (SOO 
3.2.1.4), and cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, and GCP (SOO 3.2.1.9). 
9
Is there any preference for fee arrangements - per endpoint, hourly, fixed fee, etc.
The contract will be fixed fee, based on deliverables (SOO 3.1). See Contract 
Admin Data, Paragraph 4.
10 Will any cloud workloads be in-scope? Do you utilize any cloud service providers (e.g., AWS, Azure, 
GCP) for any part of your payment processing environment?
Yes, some Aloha Cloud is in CDE scope. Required expertise in AWS, Azure, and 
GCP, and the directive to prioritize cloud-based tools, confirm cloud workloads are 
in scope (SOO 3.2.1.9, 4.1.1.3).
11
 Many installations have successfully achieved PCI compliance using validated P2PE solutions, 
hosted payment pages, or centralized enterprise payment gateways. Has AFSVC evaluated whether 
standardizing one or more of these proven, lower-scope approaches—where 
appropriate—could enhance consistency across installations while reducing lifecycle costs and 
simplifying compliance sustainment, as an alternative to deploying and maintaining separate 
tool suites at each location?
Standardization is underway, as AFSVC has moved from a decentralized to 
centralized approach. An enterprise Tool suite solution, where applicable, is being 
requested in this SOO (4.1.1).
12 The SOO currently directs the contractor to recommend and implement a “complete enterprise tool 
suite” (SIEM, DLP, MFA, etc.) and to prioritize “modern, automated, and cloud-based tools.”  As a full-
service QSA with experience delivering thousands of services to similar environments outlined in both 
the original and current SOO we find that the scope in the first SOO to more cost effective and timely. 
Would AFSVC consider modifying the requirement to include, as part of Phase 1, a QSA-
performed assessment that delivers a validated scope-reduction roadmap and presents 
multiple compliant implementation approaches—including both tool-enabled and scope-
optimized models—along with a side-by-side 3–5 year total cost of ownership analysis to 
support AFSVC decision making?
The SOO requires the contractor to conduct a "Gap Analysis" and deliver a 
"Solution Implementation Strategy" for a "complete enterprise tool suite" (SOO 
4.1.1.1, 4.1.1.4). The contractor's role is to provide technical support, not to 
perform a QSA function, although collaboration with a QSA vendor is expected 
(SOO 4.1.3.2.2).
13
The SOO emphasizes on-site technical support, 24/7 monitoring, ongoing tool management, and 
sustainment across up to 30 installations. Has AFSVC conducted, or would it consider conducting, 
a comparative analysis of total lifecycle cost—including personnel, licensing, maintenance, 
training, and option years—across alternative compliant approaches, such as tool-intensive 
implementations versus scope reduction and process simplification, which for many federal 
and DoD organizations has historically reduced compliance effort by 70–90%, to ensure long-
term operational sustainability and resource alignment?
The SOO establishes the requirement to deploy and manage a standardized tool 
suite (SOO 1.5.1). A comparative cost analysis of alternative compliance 
approaches is not a specified deliverable within the SOO. The contractor is 
expected to provide a detailed cost analysis for the recommended tools as part of 
the implementation strategy (SOO 4.1.1.4.2). 
A P2PE based scope reduction strategy is in place, while certain components 
remain within full PCI scope.  Supporting data and documentation will be provided 
upon contract award.  
14
The SOO states that the AFSVC intends to award all phases to a single vendor but that Phases 2 and 4 
are at the AFSVC’s discretion based on Phase 1 results. Would AFSVC consider adding language to 
allow the Phase 1 contractor to recommend and potentially execute a QSA-led scope-reduction 
strategy, as well as evaluate multiple compliant execution paths, so the AFSVC can select the 
approach that best aligns with cost, risk tolerance, and sustainment objectives—potentially 
eliminating the need for Phases 2 and 4—prior to proceeding to subsequent phases?
The Government is currently engaged with a QSA firm; however, the expectation 
is that you will collabrate to develop and execute a forward-looking strategy. 
15
DoD cybersecurity guidance (e.g., Zero Trust principles, Cloud Security Playbook elements, and 
integration with existing DISN/DoDIN frameworks) emphasizes risk-based, least-privilege controls 
over broad tooling deployment. How does the SOO's focus on implementing and managing a full 
suite of security tools (SIEM, DLP, MFA across CDEs) align with these mandates, and would the 
AFSVC be open to requiring Phase 1 recommendations to demonstrate compatibility with DoD-
wide security architectures to avoid redundant or conflicting implementations?
Refer to SOO  1.2 Background and 1.3 Objective.  As part of the Phase 1: Gap 
Analysis and Remediation (SOO 4.1.1), AFSVC is requesting a strategy and 
recommendation for the required  security tools and services to comply with PCI 
DSS (SOO 4.1.1.3 and 4.1.1.4).  The solution must align with DoD standards, 
including NIST SP 800-53, CISA directives, and the DoD RMF (SOO 6.9.2) while 
closing PCI control gaps and avoiding redundancy. For further clarification, the DAF 
NAFIs process payment card transactions over locally managed commercial 
netwoks rather than the NIPRNet.
16
PCI DSS best practices for sustainment emphasize repeatable, low-effort processes over complex 
tooling. Has the AFSVC evaluated whether the proposed enterprise tool suite—including 
licensing, configuration, monitoring, and update requirements—aligns with sustainable 
compliance models observed in other federal environments, and would AFSVC consider 
incorporating long-term sustainment factors, such as operational complexity, maintenance

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION 
 
 FA8307-26-R-CW02 
Request for Information (RFI) 
For 
 
Offensive Cyber Depot 
Operations & Sustainment 
 
 
1. Introduction 
 
(U) This Request for Information (RFI) is in accordance with the Revolutionary Far Overhaul 
(RFO) clause 52.215-3 (Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes - Oct 
1997) and is published only to obtain information for use by the Air Force Life Cycle 
Management Center(AFLCMC), Joint Base San Antonio - Lackland, Texas, for planning 
purposes only. 
 
(U) This RFI does not constitute an invitation for bids, a request for proposal, a solicitation, a 
request for quote or an indication that the Government will contract for the items provided by 
submitter. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the 
preparation or submission of the information requested. Response to this RFI is strictly voluntary 
and will not affect any potential offeror's ability to submit an offer if a solicitation is released. 
Any requests for a solicitation package will be disregarded. The Government does not intend to 
award a contract based on this RFI or otherwise pay for the information solicited. No entitlement 
to payment of direct or indirect costs or charges by the Government will arise as a result of 
preparing submissions in response to this RFI and the Government's use of such information. 
 
(U) Submittals will not be returned to the sender. Respondents of this RFI may be requested to 
provide additional information/details based on their initial submittals. 
 
2. Background 
 
(CUI) AFLCMC/HNCK Cryptologic and Cyber Systems Division, Contracting Branch Joint 
Base San Antonio - Lackland TX, is seeking a Depot Support contract from vendors who have 
the capability to perform Cost Plus operations and sustainment activities for cyber weapon 
systems within the AFLCMC/HNCO (Offensive Cyber Systems) portfolio.  Ideally, vendors will 
recommend use of an existing Indefinite Delivery / Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to which 
they are a party, and which is accessible by DoD Agencies. 
 
3. Objective 
 
Potential vendors will be required to perform the following:  
 
(CUI) 
 Provide Tier 1, 2, and 3 level support for complex information systems. 
 

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION 
 
(U) Repair, update, and return complex information systems to service. 
 
(CUI) Create virtual machines, networks, and infrastructures in an air-gapped environment. 
 
(U) Update and maintain hardware and software configuration baselines for these systems. 
 
(CUI) Software expected to be relevant to this effort includes (but is not limited to) 
 - Microsoft Server 2022 and beyond 
 - Red Hat Enterprise Linux 
 - VMWare / vSphere / ESXi 
 - Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise 
 - SecureView 
 - Etc. 
 
(CUI) Hardware expected to be relevant to this effort includes (but is not limited to) 
 - Servers 
 - Switches 
 - Firewalls 
 - Workstations 
 - Keyboard / Video / Mouse (KVM) devices 
 - Etc. 
 
(U) Install and maintain services under a service-oriented architecture. 
 
(CUI) Work within the government’s Risk Management Framework (RMF) to obtain and retain system 
Interim Approval to Test (IATT), Authority to Connect (ATC), and Authority to Operate (ATO) 
approvals. 
 
(U) Perform system scans in compliance with Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIG). 
 
(U) Perform continuous system monitoring to maintain RMF ATO including, but not limited to, 
performing system ACAS scans in compliance with DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides 
(STIG), performing weekly security posture reviews, and monitor Information Assurance Vulnerability 
Alerts (IAVMs) 
 
(U) Write, update and provide System User Manuals, System Description/Design Documents, System 
Installation Guides, and other types of technical reports and data. 
 
(CUI) Provide and operate a contractor Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) in the San 
Antonio Metropolitan Area.  The SCIF must have connected AFSCI terminals and provide sufficient 
space for the contractor workforce (estimated 8 - 10 positions) 
 
(CUI) Provide and operate an unclassified server space to host Test and Integration (T&I) system offsite. 
Space must have an internet connection to allow contractor team to download system updates that can be 
tested on the T&I before being brought on site. 
 
(CUI) Provide Help Desk services to our customers.  Help Desk ‘tickets’ will be maintained on the 
AFSCI system.  Help Desk will be available on a 24/7 basis via an ‘on call’ point of contact at all times. 
 
(CUI) The workforce will require TS/SCI eligibility and is anticipated to consist of a mix of the following 

CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION 
 
(or similar) labor categories: 
 - Network Specialists 
 - System Engineers 
 - System Administrators 
 - Help Desk Support 
 - Configuration Manager 
- Test Engineer 
 - Information System Security Manager (ISSM) 
 - Other, as deemed necessary by the contractor 
 
(CUI) Some members of the workforce will require Special Access eligibility. 
 
(U) Work with the incumbent contractor to ensure a smooth transition, if applicable. 
 
4. Requested Information. 
 
(U) This is not a request for competitive proposals.   If a vendor believes it can meet the 
Government's requirement, it may identify its interest and capability to Capt Charles Craig 
(Contracting Officer) at charles.craig.2@us.af.mil within ten (10) business days of this 
publication. Interested vendors are requested to submit a capability statement/white paper (no 
more than 5 pages, not inclusive of title page) and a ROM.  Hard copies will not be accepted. 
Respondents shall ensure submissions are sent at the appropriate security level. It is preferred 
that only non-proprietary information be submitted. However, proprietary information, if 
submitted, should be kept to a minimum and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. Respondents are 
advised that information submitted in response to this RFI may be released to non-Government 
advisors for review and analysis. 
 
5. Questions. 
 
(U) If you have any specific questions (relating to the above information only) please submit 
them in written format to the Contracting Officer listed above no later than April 20, 2026.  
Telephonic questions will not be entertained, and responses to this RFI will not be returned.

This Performance Work Statement (PWS) supports Naval Information Warfighting Development 
Center (NIWDC) warfighting capabilities with specific focus towards Electronic Warfare Data 
(EWD)production (using the Navy Information Operations Database (NIODB)) currently operated

interoperability, and improves mission planning through improved threat data fidelity.  OPNAV 
Instruction 3430.23D provides policy for United States Fleet Forces Command ( USFFC) and

36C26226Q0506 Question and Answers

1) Can you provide photographs of the installation locations?

ANSWER: We can mark the locations on the plan drawing. 

2) Can you describe the types of walls the screens will be mounted to? I.E. CMU, drywall with metal studs, drywall with wood studs, brick?

ANSWER: Mostly dry walls and some locations with tiled walls. 

3) Will the screens be mounted in Landscape or Portrait format?

ANSWER:  The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess and provide professional recommendations to determine the optimal orientation. As noted in the Statement of Work (SOW), the design must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements. 

4) You mention a range for screen size of 47"-65". Will you require different sized screens for different locations? Should screen size be standardized for all 16 installation locations?

ANSWER: The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess the space and provide professional recommendation to help the facility make an informed decision. 65” are most likely going near the main entrances and 47” for other locations.

5) Is there any branding, color pallet, or logo placement that should be incorporated into the design of the screens? 

ANSWER: Yes. Similar navy blue color and logo as seen on the main VA website: https://www.va.gov/ shall be used as a starting point for design. 

The contractor shall have design discussion sessions with VASD for interface design. VASD will be relying on the contractor's design expertise. 

6) Will power and data connections be available at each installation location?

ANSWER: Power will be VASD’s responsibility. Cabling and network set up will be the contractor’s responsibility. 

7) Will the installer be able to utilize the dumpster, compactors, or recycling facilities at each installation location? Or will they be responsible for hauling away all packaging material? 

ANSWER: No. Contractors are responsible for their housekeeping. Note that at the main La Jolla Medical Center contractors shall only use the service elevators. 

8) Can the screens be received at each facility prior to installation? Or can they be received at a central location? Or will the installer be responsible for bringing the screens to each installation location? 

ANSWER: The contractor is responsible for safely storing their materials and tools. No materials, screens, or tools shall be left or stored on-site unsupervised at any time. VASDHS is not responsible for the storage, damage, or loss of any items left at VASDHS's medical center or clinics.

9) Can you clarify the expected time frame for issuing a PO and the desired installation date for the 16 screens? 

ANSWER: The PO will be issued once the contract has an award.  Dates for the installation will be June 30-July 31.

2) Can you describe the types of walls the screens will be mounted to? I.E. CMU, drywall with metal studs, drywall with wood studs, brick?

ANSWER: Mostly dry walls and some locations with tiled walls. 

3) Will the screens be mounted in Landscape or Portrait format?

ANSWER:  The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess and provide professional recommendations to determine the optimal orientation. As noted in the Statement of Work (SOW), the design must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements. 

4) You mention a range for screen size of 47"-65". Will you require different sized screens for different locations? Should screen size be standardized for all 16 installation locations?

ANSWER: The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess the space and provide professional recommendation to help the facility make an informed decision. 65” are most likely going near the main entrances and 47” for other locations.

5) Is there any branding, color pallet, or logo placement that should be incorporated into the design of the screens? 

ANSWER: Yes. Similar navy blue color and logo as seen on the main VA website: https://www.va.gov/ shall be used as a starting point for design. 

The contractor shall have design discussion sessions with VASD for interface design. VASD will be relying on the contractor's design expertise. 

6) Will power and data connections be available at each installation location?

ANSWER: Power will be VASD’s responsibility. Cabling and network set up will be the contractor’s responsibility. 

7) Will the installer be able to utilize the dumpster, compactors, or recycling facilities at each installation location? Or will they be responsible for hauling away all packaging material? 

ANSWER: No. Contractors are responsible for their housekeeping. Note that at the main La Jolla Medical Center contractors shall only use the service elevators. 

8) Can the screens be received at each facility prior to installation? Or can they be received at a central location? Or will the installer be responsible for bringing the screens to each installation location? 

ANSWER: The contractor is responsible for safely storing their materials and tools. No materials, screens, or tools shall be left or stored on-site unsupervised at any time. VASDHS is not responsible for the storage, damage, or loss of any items left at VASDHS's medical center or clinics.

9) Can you clarify the expected time frame for issuing a PO and the desired installation date for the 16 screens? 

ANSWER: The PO will be issued once the contract has an award.  Installation shall begin before June 30th. 

Will floor plans, CAD drawings, or other layout documentation be provided for these locations?

ANSWER: VASD can provide archived floor plan drawings (CAD/PDF). Locations are still being finalized by end users. Generally expected areas include main entrances and lobbies. The VASD will also rely on contractors' expertise to assess the space and provide professional recommendations on this matter.  

Question 6 of the initial RFI response notes that power will be the responsibility of VASD, while cabling and network setup fall to the contractor.

Will both power and data be available at the installation locations? 

Or will the contractor be responsible for extending power and data to each location? 

ANSWER: Network cabling set up will be the contractor’s responsibility. Power will be VASD’s responsibility. 

Are there any active construction projects underway at these facilities? If so, who is serving as the General Contractor?

ANSWER: There are multiple active construction projects under different contractors. Pathfinding screen locations are not affected by these constructions. 

Pg 39 of the SOW requires all items to be delivered by 5-01-2026, however, per RFI response #9 the work is to be performed between 6-30-2026 and 7-31-2026. Further RFI response #8 states that the contractor is responsible for all tools and materials at all times. What is to be delivered on 5-01-2026? 

ANSWER: The PO will be issued once the contract has an award.  Installation shall begin before June 30th.

SECTION 1 – INTRODUCTION 
 
1. Combined Synopsis/Solicitation  
1.1. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial 
services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) part 12. 
This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a 
separate written solicitation will not be issued. 
 
Solicitation number 140D0426Q0324 is issued as a request for quotation (RFQ) for 
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chatbot Services to enhance agency Recruitment Efforts. 
 
This acquisition is a total small business set-aside. This solicitation incorporates 
provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be 
accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov.  
 
1.2. The period of performance for this Purchase Order will consist of a one-year Base 
Period estimated to begin on June 1, 2026, followed by four (4) one-year Option 
Periods, as outlined in the table below. If all options are exercised, the total period of 
performance will not exceed five (5) years. Continued performance under this 
Purchase Order is contingent upon the availability of funds and the Contractor’s 
acceptable level of performance. 
 
 Base Period: June 01, 2026, to May 31, 2027 
 Option Period 1: June 01, 2027, to May 31, 2028 
 Option Period 2: June 01, 2028, to May 31, 2029 
 Option Period 3: June 01, 2029, to May 31, 2030 
 Option Period 4: June 01, 2030, to May 31, 2031 
 
1.3. The U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), Interior Business Center (IBC), 
Acquisition Services Directorate (AQD), is issuing this RFQ on behalf of the Peace 
Corps (PC), Office of Volunteer Recruitment and Service (VRS), for Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) Chatbot Services to enhance agency Recruitment Efforts. 
 
The Peace Corps seeks a FedRAMP High authorized, commercially available SaaS 
conversational AI solution (“Chatbot”) to enhance recruitment, outreach, and public 
engagement across peacecorps.gov. The solution must deliver high-quality, secure, 
and scalable interactions with the public while integrating seamlessly with existing 
systems. 
 
Through the implementation of the integrated conversational AI chatbot service, the 
Peace Corps expects to: 

Solicitation 140D0426Q0324 
Page 4 of 23 
 Facilitate more effective and efficient interactions between potential 
applicants with recruiters and the marketing team. 
 Generate new leads through an additional marketing channel. 
 Increase the number of leads converted into applicants through better just-in-
time communications. 
 Decrease the time and effort Peace Corps staff spend responding to commonly 
asked questions and requests for guidance from the public that can be 
answered through thoughtfully constructed technology. 
 Provide smoother and more seamless interactions between the public and 
Peace Corps through escalation of AI generated conversations, when required, 
to the relevant Peace Corps staff. 
 
1.4. Place of Performance  
All services provided by the Contractor are to be conducted at the Contractor’s 
location within the Unites States of America; no on-site work at the Government 
facility is anticipated.

Statement of work – Sports Streaming Services 
 
Background 
 
The purchase of a sports streaming service for varsity sports statistics and online viewing services as 
required by NFHS.  
Objectives 
 
The objective of this service is to have digital records of all varsity sport activities and to be able to 
accurately track sports statistics, in compliance with NFHS.  
 
Scope 
 
The scope of this project is to obtain access to online streaming services to track varsity games. 
 
Tasks 
 
The task will be to deliver a compatible streaming service similar to the ones used in our region, 
southwest 1-A, to stream and record all varsity games.

SECTION L - INSTRUCTIONS, CONDITIONS, AND NOTICES TO QUOTERS 
L.1. OVERVIEW  
The USCB is issuing this competitive Request for Quotation (RFQ) under the General Services 
Administration (GSA) Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) for its CenTAM Acquisition 
Framework requirements. Through this effort, USCB intends to establish four (4) blanket 
purchase agreements (BPAs) under the MAS to acquire application development, 
modernization, data engineering, geospatial, and related technical services in support of its 
mission.  
All four BPAs under this RFQ are being competed as total small business set-asides.  
Only small businesses holding the applicable GSA MAS IT Category SIN 54151S are 
eligible to submit quotes.  
The Government will accept only quotes submitted by small businesses under GSA MAS SIN 
54151S. Any quote submitted by a Quoter that is not a small business will not be accepted and, 
therefore, not considered for evaluation or award.  
For the purposes of this RFQ “quoter” means a small business concern. Contractors that submit a 
proposal will be referred to as quoters.  
The Government intends to execute and award the initial orders for the single award BPAs based 
on initial quotes. Therefore, quoters are highly encouraged to propose their best technical and 
pricing quotes in their initial submissions. 
L.2. AUTHORITY (GSAR 538.71 – FSS ORDERING PROCEDURES) 
This RFQ is issued under GSAR Subpart 538.71 – Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) Ordering 
Procedures, as implemented via GSA’s Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) class deviation. 
Ordering will be conducted using RFQs and evaluation of quotations under FSS procedures. 
Unless otherwise prescribed, FAR Parts 5, 6, 13, 14, 15, 16, and 19 do not apply to these 
ordering procedures.  
These procedures constitute “competitive procedures” under 41 U.S.C §152, including 152(4) 
for procurements conducted under the Small Business Act. They enable the Government to 
conduct best-value evaluations consistent with GSAR 538.71 - FSS ordering procedures.  
L.3. COMMUNICATING INNOVATIVE TECHNIQUES WITH INDUSTRY 
This solicitation encompasses several innovative procurement techniques (see GSAR 538.7102-2 
for more coverage of streamlined processes and innovative procurement techniques). To increase 
transparency of them with industry, they are listed below. The Periodic Table of Acquisition 
innovations (PTAI), https://acquisitiongateway.gsa.gov/periodic-table, includes a full tile sharing 
the description, problems solved, benefits of use, small business benefit, and real sample 
documents (including training aids) for each:  
• Communicating Innovative Techniques with Industry (CITI)  

 
2 
 
• Confidence Ratings  
• Down-Selects 
• Fusion Procurements  
• Highest Technically Rated Vendors  
• On-the-Spot Consensus Evaluation  
• Streamlined Documentation  
L.4. CENTAM BPA STRUCTURE 
The CenTAM Acquisition Framework will consist of four BPAs to support the full spectrum of 
USCB application modernization, data engineering, analytics, geospatial, and related IT services 
needs. The Enterprise BPA is intended to support large-scale, more complex efforts across all 
USCB programs requiring broad technical depth and integration. The Systems and Program 
Support (SPS) BPA is intended to support smaller-scale, narrowly scoped efforts across all 
USCB programs. The Decennial BPA is dedicated to supporting the Decennial Program only, 
while the Geospatial BPA supports Geospatial initiatives across USCB.

L.5. QUOTER ELIGIBILITY AND TEAM PARTICIPATION LIMITATIONS 
L.5.1 QUOTER ELIGIBILITY

quotation submission.

L.5.2 TEAM PARTICIPATION LIMITATIONS 
A Quoter may participate in this acquisition either as a prime contractor or a subcontractor, 
but only on one team.  
Participation on multiple teams, whether across BPAs or within a single BPA, is prohibited.  
Enterprise, Decennial, and Geospatial BPAs:

may not participate (as a Prime or subcontractor) in Enterprise, Decennial, or 
Geospatial BPAs.

or subcontractor) in the Enterprise, Decennial, or Geospatial BPAs.

consideration.

non-compliant, and therefore ineligible for award for the affected BPA(s). 
L.6. GENERAL  
Quoters are instructed to read the entire RFQ document, including all attachments, prior to 
preparing your quote. Omission of any information from the quotation submission requirements 
may result in the quote being deemed “Noncompliant” and disqualified from further evaluation.  
To aid in the evaluations, quotes shall be clearly and concisely written, neatly prepared, properly 
indexed, and logically assembled. Quoters are asked to bear in mind that all material submitted

brochures, marketing materials, and so forth, shall not be submitted. All pages of each part shall 
be appropriately numbered, identified with the name of the Quoter, the date, and the solicitation 
number to the extent practicable.  
Quoter’s submissions shall address all requirements identified in Section L and the evaluation 
factors set forth in Section M of the solicitation. 
In responding to this RFQ, it is the Quoter’s responsibility to provide current, complete, and 
accurate information in their quotes. If in reviewing the quotes, the Government identifies or 
otherwise learns that the provided information is not accurate or misrepresents the Quoter’s 
status or capabilities, that information may be used by the contracting officer to determine the

1. BACKGROUND  
 
DISA currently manages mobile device services for the Department of Defense (DoD) and 
approved non-DoD users and is required to maintain compliance with evolving Commercial 
Solutions for Classified (CSfC) standards. The continuous evolution of CSfC Mobile Access 
Capability Package (MACP) requirements is essential for meeting growing security demands 
while improving functionality, usability, and compliance in a rapidly changing technological 
landscape. Earlier mobility solutions consisted of an End User Device (EUD), such as a phone, 
tablet, or laptop, paired with a Retransmission Device (RD) that functioned as a commercial 
mobile hotspot.  
 
2. PROBLEM STATEMENT  
 
The latest published CSfC MACP (version 2.7) requires the RD to be connected to the mobile 
device through a hardwired connection. In earlier versions of MACP, this requirement could be 
met by using a cellular hotspot device that connects to the mobile device via Wi-Fi connection. 
While a cable connection meets the new MACP technical standard, it is operationally untenable. 
The use of a visible cable between the EUD and the RD creates two critical issues: 
 
a. Degraded User Experience & Risk: Physical cables introduce significant user experience 
challenges and operational risks. From a user perspective, the cable is an encumbrance that 
can snag on other gear, get caught on the environment, and physically tether the user, 
restricting their mobility and creating a potential point of failure if disconnected. The 
physical cable makes the phone conspicuous and draws unwanted attention. This visibility 
creates a significant operational security risk. In environments where stealth and operational 
discretion are critical, such exposure could compromise the security of the mission and the 
individual, making it easier for adversaries to target or disrupt operations. The presence of a 
physical cable can serve as an indicator of the operator’s location, role, and equipment type, 
increasing the likelihood of detection and compromising the security of sensitive activities. 
 
b. Reduced Tactical Mobility: Forcing users to carry and physically connect separate devices 
is cumbersome, creates a logistical burden, and hinders the tactical mobility required for 
accessing networks like the Secret Internet Protocol Router (SIPR) Network in operational 
environments. 
 
This prototype OT seeks to develop an innovative and user-friendly Retransmission Device (RD) 
to bridge the gap between CSfC standards and operational needs. The ideal solution, likely a 
sleeve or integrated case, will satisfy the new CSfC hardwired connection requirement internally 
while appearing as a normal case to the outside observer. The goal is to eliminate conspicuous 
external cables, remove the logistical burden of separate devices, and restore full tactical 
mobility for users. 
 
3. DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES  
 
A fully functional prototype must include the following unique or innovative capabilities, 
functions, and/or features:  

Version 1.0  Page 3 of 7 
 
3.1. Core Compliance & Physical Design 
 
a. The solution must meet or exceed all requirements of the CSfC MACP version 2.7, and all 
subsequent versions released during the period of performance. 
 
b. The solution’s physical footprint shall be minimized to reduce its visual signature. While a 
form factor similar in size to a commercial smartphone case is the desired baseline, 
companies are encouraged to propose innovative solutions that achieve the core requirement 
of being inconspicuous. 
 
c. The solution must be an all-in-one form factor that eliminates the need for a separate device 
and connecting cable. 
 
d. The solution must be modular to enable rapid, cost-effective portability of capabilities across 
current and future EUD form factors.  
 
e. The solution or physical design (e.g., smartphone case) must support both current and future 
approved DoD mobile devices/form factors (e.g., Samsung Galaxy S25 or S26). The ability 
to support additional form factors (e.g., tablets, laptops, etc.) is a desired feature; however, 
support for additional form factors would only be required in a follow-on production OT or 
contract.   
 
3.2. Component & Supply Chain Security 
 
a. The solution must be compliant with CSfC and National Information Assurance Partnership 
(NIAP) requirements. All components used in the solution must be on the CSfC Components 
List and NIAP validated. The Government will not consider solutions that rely on achieving 
NIAP validation during the prototype period of performance.  
 
b. The solution must adhere to Supply Chain Risk Management principles throughout its 
lifecycle. 
 
c. The solution must adhere to the Trade Agreements Act statutes throughout its lifecycle. All 
manufacturing and assembly, throughout the prototype and any potential follow-on 
production, must be performed domestically in compliance with International Traffic in Arms 
Regulations (ITAR). 
 
d. All modem chips must be compliant throughout the period of performance with Section 
889(a)(1)(A)&(B) of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). 
 
e. The Company must describe their process for adapting the proposed solution to new 
Government-approved moblie devices and form factors. In their solution brief, the Company 
must commit to completing any future form factor change requests within 90 days of 
receiving a formal request from the Government. This capability is considered a required 
performance standard for the successful awardee. 

Version 1.0  Page 4 of 7 
 
f. The company must demonstrate the ability to produce at scale and meet demand via an ITAR 
regulated facility. 
 
3.3. Connectivity & Transport 
 
a. The solution must provide unlocked, Fourth-Generation (4G)/Long-Term Evolution wireless 
network transport that can provide service in Continental United States (CONUS) and 
Outside Continental United States (OCONUS) for the prototype OT. If a follow-on 
production OT or contract is awarded, the Company must be capable of further developing 
the solution to support both 4G and Fifth-Generation cellular transport. “Unlocked" is 
defined as not being bound to a specific carrier, supporting both embedded Subscriber 
Identity Module (SIM) and physical SIM cards.  
 
b. The proposed solution must have the ability to utilize CONUS cellular modems for the 
prototype. If a production OT is awarded, the solution must support both CONUS and 
OCONUS cellular connectivity. 
 
c. The solution must provide 802.11 a/b/g/ac (Wi-Fi 6E/7) transport options. 
 
d. The connectivity chip responsible for external communication must be physically distinct 
from the main processor and not integrated within the same chip. 
 
e. It is desired, but not required, that the capability be designed to support emerging transport 
options, such as Direct-to-Device satellite communications, where applicable.  
 
f. The prototype must demonstrate Wi-Fi connectivity only. If a follow-on production OT or 
contract is awarded, the Company must be capable of futher developing the solution to 
support both Wi-Fi and Cellular connectivity.  
 
g. The Company must demonstrate the ability to obatin Federal Communications Commission 
(FCC) Certification for any components requiring U.S. celleuar network access. Applicable 
FCC certifications would only be required for a follow-on production OT or contract.   
 
3.4. Security Features 
 
a. The ability to create an outer VPN on the RD is a desired feature. If the outer VPN 
capability is included, it must utilize a cryptographic key store that is physically and 
logically independent of the EUD. 
 
b. If the RD is used to create a VPN, it must be able to support the CNSA Suite 2.0 Profile for 
IPSEC in accordance with the draft CSfC Post Quantum Cryptography Guidance 
Addendum. 
 
3.5. Lifecycle, Service & Management 
 

Version 1.0  Page 5 of 7 
a. The solution must include full lifecycle support, if the prototype is successful and moved into 
production, to include planning, procurement, deployment, sustainment, and secure disposal. 
 
b. The solution must offer a framework to control lifecycle costs and provide comprehensive 
support. This framework must account for future hardware and software evolution, allowing 
for cost-effective scalability and ongoing upgrades throughout the lifecycle of the 
solution.The solution must support automated inventory and asset tracking. 
 
c. The solution must be administered via a centralized, cloud-based platform that is authorized 
at Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) High and/or DISA 
Impact Level 6. 
 
d. The platform must support secure, over-the-air firmware updates. 
 
e. The platform must provide tools for remote monitoring and reporting. 
 
4. AWARDING INSTRUMENT  
 
This AOI solicitation will be awarded in accordance with the Commercial Solutions Opening 
(CSO) procedures detailed within the DISA CSO HC108425S0001, posted to SAM.gov on 8 
January 2025. The CSO outlines the guidelines for submitting solution briefs, pitches, and 
proposals and how the Government will evaluate responses to this AOI. The CSO can be found 
at: https://sam.gov/opp/98c4a509d78f4f95ae21586d7004fd0e/view 
 
As identified in paragraph 3.2 of the CSO, the Affirmation of Business Status Certification is 
attached to this AOI.  
 
5. SOLICITATION NOTES 
 
In addition to the general guidelines included in the CSO, the following guidelines apply to this 
AOI. 
 
 The Government will give preference to submissions that demonstrate an existing, reference-
verifiable commercial ability to accomplish the desired solution attributes listed above.  
 
 If the Government does not receive any solution briefs that demonstrate an innovative, 
existing, and reference-verifiable commercial ability to accomplish the desired solution 
attributes listed above, preference will be given to submissions demonstrating existing and 
recent products that can be adapted for the solicited purpose with the least amount of non-
recurrent-engineering effort. 
 
 To align with the target schedule, proposals with a performance period of six months or less 
are ideal. This timeframe is preferred to ensure rapid development and deployment of the 
proposed solution, allowing for a timely transition from the prototype phase to full 
implementation if the prototype has been determined successful by the Government.  
 

Version 1.0  Page 6 of 7 
 The anticipated total cost for this prototype project is between $500,000 to $850,000 to 
deliver 20 devices over a 6-month project period, including all associated costs for 
development, implementation, and necessary support.  
 
The primary goal is to identify and select the best possible solution for the Government's needs. 
As such, all submissions are strongly encouraged for consideration, regardless of the proposed 
performance period or target cost. The Government will evaluate each proposal based on its 
merits, innovation, feasibility,

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Central Texas VA Health Care System (CTVAHCS) in Temple, Texas is seeking Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB), or Small Business sources capable of meeting the requirement listed below.  The acquisition will be accomplished using commercial item procedures in accordance with FAR Part 12.

NOTE: TO QUALIFY SDVOSB AND VOSB VENDORS MUST BE CERTIFIED IN THE SMALL BUSINESS SEARCH (SBS) DATABASE.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) is 541519.  Any SDVOSB, VOSB, or Small Business firms who wish to identify their interests and capability to provide this product must provide product specifications, performance and delivery information by notifying the Contract Specialist no later than TEN PM Central Time, April 24, 2026.  Notification shall be e-mailed to Akisha Woods, at Akisha.Woods@va.gov.

Any vendor who responds to this Notice must provide credentials to perform the requirement as outlined in the below scope. 

DISCLAIMER

This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation.  All information received in response to this Notice that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly.  In accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation, responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.  Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Notice.

SCOPE:

Introduction:  Central Texas Veterans Health Care System (CTVHCS) clinicians use Theradoc to provide medical technology that interprets records, alerts clinicians, and recommends patient-specific treatment options that are based on current medical guidelines and evidence, resulting in better healthcare decisions.  This favorably affects patients’ healthcare experiences and outcomes, while reducing costs.  VHA has purchased a license for TheraDoc, a Document Storage Systems (DSS) product, which requires an annual maintenance and telephone support services contract for those health care systems that use TheraDoc.      

		(1)	Background:  CTVHCS has a continuing need to use TheraDoc in support of safe, efficient and effective patient care, and must have a maintenance and telephone services contract in place to do so.  Use of TheraDoc is essential to patient care activities performed by many clinical staff, and it is imperative the maintenance service contract is established to make this possible.  Theradoc provides clinicians with patient information and medical knowledge to promote better patient care decisions.  It enables providers to make therapeutic interventions more quickly, improve appropriate use of antimicrobials, reduce adverse reactions, reduce the length of hospital stays, and more efficient, better and safer patient care.  Theradoc interprets records, provides alerts to clinicians, recommends evidence-based treatment options based on current medical guidelines, which results in better health care decision that improve patient outcomes while reducing costs.  It is imperative this medical surveillance capability for CTVHCS be maintained in fully operational status at all times in order to promote better patient care.

Scope of Work:  The Contractor to provide service and support to an existing TheraDoc for VistA Large Hospital-TESA Platform, that will include the following services, in addition to software upgrades as needed:

1) DSS-TDOC-VistA-LVL1: TheraDoc for VistA - TESA Platform, Pharmacy Assistant, Infection Control Assistant. Includes interfaces for ADT, Lab, Micro, Surgery, Inpatient Pharmacy, Radiology, BCMA, Vital Signs, Problem List. Annual Limited License. Includes Support and Maintenance and 24x7 monitoring support. Level 1 facility

2) DSS-TDOC-DBUSER: DSS TheraDoc EMR Embedded DB and ColdFusion Software.

3) DSS-OUTPT-PHARM-LL: DSS Outpatient Pharmacy Interface for TheraDoc, Annual Limited License per hospital. Includes support and maintenance for a period of one year 

4) DSS-MDI-VA-LL: DSS Medical Devices Interface (MDI) for TheraDoc, Annual Limited License per facility.  Includes support and maintenance for a period of one year.

5) DSS-PREMAPPSUPPORT-VAAF: DSS ADHOC Premium Application Workflow Support - Remote, per facility annual fee.

6) DSS-INST-R: DSS Remote Installation Services Per Day

7) DSS-TDOC-EMR: DSS TheraDoc EMR Project Management, Technical and Training Services Per Hour.

8) TRAVEL-Z: Travel Per Diem Expenses, per person, per week.

2.	REQUIREMENTS:

Type of Contract: Firm-Fixed-Price for the Base Year, followed by option years one through four. 

General Requirements:  To provide CTVHCS with continued support services performed by staff that are comprehensively trained in TheraDoc processes and procedures.

Period of Performance:  The maintenance and telephone support services contract to run for the Base Year from start of contract through the option years.  

3.	REFERENCES:  

Federal Standards and Guidance:	

		(1)	The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) of 1996

Computer Security Act of 1987, Public Law 10-235

	(2)	OMB Circular A-123, Management’s Responsibility for Internal Control – Revised (03/10/2026) (35 pages, 528KB)

	(3)	5 U.S.C. 552a, Privacy Act of 1974, 5 United States Code 552a, Public Law 99-08.

	(4)	5 U.S.C. 552, Freedom of Information Act, 5 United States Code 552, Public Law

	(5)	18 U.S.C. 1030 (a) (3), Fraud and related activity in connection with computers.

	(6)	Electronic Communications Privacy Act of 1986, Public Law 99-08, 100 Stat. 1848.

	b.	Agency Policy and Guidelines:

(1) VA Directive 6008, Acquisition and Management of VA Information Technology Resources

	(2) VA Directive 6102, Internet and Intranet Services

	(3) VA Handbook 6340, Enterprise Mail Management Procedures

	(4) VA Directive 6403, Software Asset Management

	(5) VA Directive 6500, VA Cybersecurity Program 

		(6) VA Handbook 6500, Risk Management Framework for VA Information Systems, VA Information Security Program

		(7) VA Handbook 6500.6, Contract Security

		(8) VA Handbook 6513, Secure External Connections

		(9) VA Directive 6515, Use of Web Based Collaboration Technologies

		(10) VA Directive 6517 Risk Management Framework for Cloud Computing Services

c. Local Policies:

VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 674-ISO-024, Management of Information Security and Privacy Incidents 

VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 00-25, Facility Information System Contingency Plan (ISCP) Business Impact Analysis (BIA) and Business Continuity Plan-Continuity of Operations Plan (BCP-COOP)

VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 003-001, Internet and Intranet-SharePoint Content Development

(4) VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 674-ISO-003 – Use of Electronic Mail and Internet Usage Guidelines

(5) VHA Field VAMC Policy MCP 674-008-003, Records Management Program 

4.	DELIVERABLES:  

Contractor to provide the following services as needed:

Work directly with users to address any issues with TheraDoc products.

Respond to issues within required response times.

Advise local OI&T and/or Biomedical Engineering staff regarding configurations for products, new installations of products, and end-user activities.

Assist local OI&T and/or Biomedical Engineering staff regarding issues with infrastructure requirements for products, including hardware, bandwidth, best practices, etc.

Advise local OI&T/Biomedical Engineering staff and/or other local points of contact regarding any issues which may impact usage of licensed products.

Provide software upgrades as required to resolve TheraDoc server vulnerabilities reported by the VA, as well as other application enhancements. This will include “release notes” for all versions included the upgrades, for Pharmacy and IP&C.

Provide reports upon request to local OI&T and/or Biomedical Engineering staff for:

Summary of tickets currently open, and those closed with the past 7 days

Summary of known issues impacting site use of products with current status, expected release date, and workaround if available

Requesting Support and Assigning Priority: Contractor staff will be considered second level support for local OI&T staff, and as such support can only be initiated by local OI&T staff.  Priority of response is based on the following:

0-Urgent:  Initial response within 1 hour, with follow-up response within 2 hours.  For catastrophic incidents such as server crash, one or more product applications being inaccessible to all users, etc.

1-High:  Initial response within 2 hours, with follow-up within 22 hours (2 business days).  For instances in which the system is functioning, but in a severely reduced capacity significantly impacting portions of business operations

2-Medium:  Initial response within 4 hours, with follow-up within 33 hours (3 business days).  For instances of non-critical functionality loss in which some operations are impaired, but users and/or applications are able to continue to function

3-Low:  Initial response with 8 hours, with follow-up within 44 hours (4 business days).  For instances in which there is minimal impact to business operations.

5.	QUALITY ASSURANCE SURVEILLANCE PROGRAM (QASP):  The Contractor will ensure support services staff and actions are in compliance with the terms of the contract. 

6.	SECURITY CONSIDERATIONS:  Safeguarding patient health information (PHI) is a primary concern for VA staff and for contractor personnel working in VA facilities and/or working with PHI or other confidential/sensitive information.  DSS will adhere to all VA Information Security, Privacy and HIPAA requirements when obtaining and reviewing diagnostic information.  This includes as log files, error traps, screen capture images and database query results used to aid in providing support services required by the contract.

	a.	The Computer Security Act requires federal agencies to provide for mandatory periodic training in computer security awareness and accepted computer security practices for all employees who are involved with the management, use, or operation of a federal computer system within or under the supervision of the federal agency.  This includes contractors as well as employees of the agency. OMB Circular A-130, Appendix III, revised in 1996, enforces such mandatory training by requiring its completion prior to granting access to the system and through periodic refresher training for continued access.  Therefore, each user must be versed in acceptable rules of behavior for the application before being allowed access to the system.  VA and VHA policies specify mandatory orientation training prior to access and annual refresher training for all employees.  The training program also informs users on procedures for reporting security incidents.  Contractor staff must comply with training and security requirements to the same extent as VA staff.

      b.  Information made available to the contractor or subcontractor by VA for the performance or administration of this contract or information developed by the contractor/subcontractor in performance or administration of the contract shall be used only for those purposes and shall not be used in any other way without the prior written agreement of the VA. This clause expressly limits the contractor/subcontractor's rights to use data as described in Rights in Data - General, FAR 52.227-14(d) (1).

     c.  VA information should not be co-mingled, if possible, with any other data on the contractors of subcontractor’s information systems or media storage systems in order to ensure VA requirements related to data protection and media sanitization can be met. If co-mingling must be allowed to meet the requirements of the business need, the contractor must ensure that VA’s information is returned to the VA or destroyed in accordance with VA’s sanitization requirements. VA reserves the right to conduct onsite inspections of contractor and subcontractor IT resources to ensure data security

controls, separation of data and job duties, and destruction/media sanitization procedures are in compliance with VA directive requirements.

    d. Prior to termination or completion of this contract, contractor/subcontractor must not destroy information received from VA, or gathered/created by the contractor in the course of performing this contract without prior written approval by the VA. Any data destruction done on behalf of VA by a contractor/subcontractor must be done in accordance with National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) requirements as outlined in VA Directive 6300, Records and Information Management and its Handbook 6300.1 Records Management Procedures, applicable VA Records Control Schedules, and VA Handbook 6500.1, Electronic Media Sanitization. Self-certification

by the contractor that the data destruction requirements above have been met must be sent to the VA Contracting Officer within 30 days of termination of the contract.

    e. The contractor/subcontractor must receive, gather, store, back up, maintain, use, disclose and dispose of VA information only in compliance with the terms of the contract and applicable Federal and VA information confidentiality and security laws, regulations and policies. If Federal or VA information confidentiality and security laws, regulations and policies become applicable to the VA information or information systems after execution of the contract, or if NIST issues or updates applicable FIPS or Special Publications (SP) after execution of this contract, the parties agree to negotiate in good faith to implement the information confidentiality and security laws, regulations and policies in this contract.

    f. The contractor/subcontractor shall not make copies of VA information except as authorized and necessary to perform the terms of the agreement or to preserve electronic information stored on contractor/subcontractor electronic storage media for restoration in case any electronic equipment or data used by the contractor/subcontractor needs to be restored to an operating state. If copies are made for restoration purposes, after the restoration is complete, the copies must be appropriately destroyed.

   g. If VA determines that the contractor has violated any of the information confidentiality, privacy, and security provisions of the contract, it shall be sufficient grounds for VA to withhold payment to the contractor or third party or terminate the contract for default or terminate for cause under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 12.

   h. If a VHA contract is terminated for cause, the associated BAA must also be terminated and appropriate actions taken in accordance with VHA Handbook 1600.01, Business Associate Agreements. Absent an agreement to use or disclose protected health information, there is no business associate relationship.

United States Capitol Police 
 
 
To Whom It May Concern, 
 
The United States Capitol Police (USCP), Office of Liebengood Center for Wellness 
(LCW) has a requirement for a comprehensive wellness application. You are hereby 
requested to submit a technical quote for a comprehensive wellness application in 
accordance with the enclosed Statement of Work. USCP intends to procure services 
under a Firm Fixed-Price contract type. 
 
 
Factors for Award 
 
Award will be made in accordance with the procedures of FAR Part 13 – Simplified 
Acquisition Procedures. The basis for award will be best value. In so doing, the 
Government may award to other than the lowest priced quote or other than the highest 
technically rated quote. This acquisition will be conducted using a phased approach. Phase I 
will consist of potential proposers submitting a document that addresses how it will address 
all elements under Factor 1. The next phase, a Pre-Award Demonstration will be scheduled at 
the conclusion of initial evaluation of quoters from Phase I. This demonstration will be 
considered Phase II of the RFQ. The purpose of the demonstration is to allow up to three (3) 
of the highest rated quoters to showcase the Wellness Application and present the 
functionality of the final product to USCP stakeholders.  All three Parts of the quote (listed 
below) will be considered when making the determination of the highest rated Quoters. 
Quoters that are selected to present for Phase II shall be required to prepare a virtual 
presentation (MS Teams) that shall not exceed one hour. Evaluation criteria for the 
Demonstration will be provided at the conclusion of Phase I evaluation.  
 
Phase I. The following technical evaluation factors are in order of importance:  
 
Factor 1 – Technical Capability and Understanding of the Requirements 
  
For Factor 1, the contractor shall demonstrate comprehensive understanding of the tasks 
outlined in Section C3-C7 of the SOW to include the following sub factors: 
  
1.1. Approach to accomplish scope elements in C3-C7 of the SOW 


1.2. Expertise accomplishing the elements in C3-C7 of the SOW 
1.3. Strategy for accomplishing the elements in C3-C7 of the SOW 
 
Factor 2 – Past Performance 
 
Past Performance: The Related Corporate Experience section shall briefly describe 
the experience of the vendor performing work similar to this one from the past three 
(3) years. Provide a demonstration of the contractor's knowledge and understanding 
of the SOW and stated requirements in general. Short abstracts of related work shall 
include the name, current affiliation and phone number of the sponsor's project officer 
(or equivalent), and dates the work was performed. Additionally, quoters shall provide 
at least three (3) references that have received services from the contractor, which are 
comparable to those described in this solicitation. Projects must have been completed 
within the last two (2) years or shall be currently in progress. 
 
The vendors past performance will be evaluated under existing and prior contracts for 
similar products and services over the last three years. The USCP will focus on 
information that demonstrates quality of performance relative to the complexity of the 
procurement under consideration. Please submit no more than three (3) Past 
Performance references for similar efforts as described in the SOW. For each contract 
or task order provided as a reference, the vendor shall send the Past Performance

Statement of Work 
Comprehensive Wellness Application for the United States Capitol Police 
C.1 Purpose 
The purpose of this requirement is to acquire a comprehensive digital wellness application 
that supports the physical, mental, emotional, spiritual, and occupational well-being of the 
United States Capitol Police workforce, including officers, civilian employees, supervisors, 
retirees, and family members. The Contractor shall provide a secure, confidential, user-
friendly mobile and web platform that delivers 24/7 access to wellness resources, 
professional support connections, peer support tools, educational materials, analytics, and 
crisis response pathways that are tailored to the needs of law enforcement personnel. 
C.2 Background 
The United States Capitol Police established the Howard C. Liebengood Center for Wellness 
to expand accessibility to wellness resources for its personnel and their families. The 
Department requires a modern, law-enforcement-focused wellness application that 
consolidates resources, enhances early support for employees, preserves confidentiality, 
and strengthens resilience across the workforce. The application shall incorporate best 
practices in law enforcement wellness, employee assistance, and behavioral health support 
technologies.

PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) 
SAFEGUARDS IT COMPUTER SECURITY SUPPORT 
1 
1.0 OVERVIEW 
1
.1   INTRODUCTION AND BACKGROUND 
T
he Office of Safeguards (Safeguards) within Governmental Liaison, Disclosure and Safeguards 
(GLDS) function of Privacy, Governmental Liaison and Disclosure (PGLD) is responsible for 
ensuring that Federal Tax Information (FTI) provided outside of the IRS is secured and used 
appropriately. Safeguards assess approximately 300 federal, state and local agencies, as well as 
their authorized contractors receiving FTI under various sub-sections of Internal Revenue Code 
(IRC) §6103 and other IRC provisions. Agencies must implement appropriate safeguards to 
protect confidentiality and prevent unauthorized access or use of FTI. Safeguards works in 
partnership with the recipient agencies to identify and mitigate risks to FTI. The specific 
safeguard requirements are outlined in IRC §6103(p)(4) and detailed in Publication 1075, Tax 
Information Security Guidelines for Federal, State, and Local Agencies. 
P
ublication 1075 is primarily based upon National Institute of Standards & Technology (NIST) 
Special Publication (SP) 800-53, Assessing Security and Privacy Controls for Information 
Systems and Organizations for moderate risk systems, IRC §6103 statutory requirements and IRS 
policy and procedure. All automated information systems and networks which receive, process, 
store, transmit, or protect FTI must meet these information protection requirements. 
2.0
 OBJECTIVE 
Th
e objective of this requirement is to increase security of FTI and to ensure consistent 
application of information security standards across all partner agency information systems. 
3
.0   REQUIREMENT TASKS 
T
he mission of Safeguards is to promote taxpayer confidence in the integrity of the tax system by 
ensuring the confidentiality of IRS information provided to federal, state, and local agencies.  
Safeguards verifies compliance with IRC §6103(p)(4) safeguard requirements through the 
identification and mitigation of any risk of loss, breach, or misuse of FTI held by external 
government agencies. 
T
he Contractor shall provide cybersecurity and information technology (IT) expertise. The 
Contractor shall optimize its processes, to reduce costs and minimize risk to FTI in possession of 
agency partners, while continuing to meet all regulatory and agency documented standards and 
guidance; and obtain information technology expertise and ancillary support to enable Safeguards 
to meet on-going and new regulatory objectives having an impact on the Safeguards Program. 
T
he Contractor shall collaborate with IRS leadership, staff, and other contractors in support of 
agency computer security reviews. Support shall include the following: conducting preparatory 
agency outreach; conducting pre-review research and analysis to determine scope and potential 
areas of concern; executing automated and manual computer security compliance scans of partner 
agency systems during the review; preparing reports, documenting scan results and other 
computer security findings; and analyzing and responding to various partner agency computer 
security information submissions. Other computer security review-related support includes 
stakeholder outreach, risk-based modeling for agency review selection, computer security review 
methodology updates, and general IT expertise. The Contractor shall provide ad hoc support for

 2 
the assessment of other projects, pilots, and new legislation that include provisions falling within 
the purview of Safeguards. 
 
In accordance with Executive Order (EO) 14179, the contractor is permitted to use Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) to assist in this task.  
 
The Contractor shall adhere to IRS Publication 1075 (Tax Information Security Guidelines for 
Federal, State, and Local Agencies), Federal Security Modernization Act (FISMA), Privacy Act 
of 1974, Internal Revenue Code  §6103, NIST Risk Management Framework and IRS Safeguards 
Program requirements when utilizing artificial intelligence tools to enhance technical support 
capabilities assisting in the management and updates of Safeguards Computer Security 
Evaluation Matrices (SCSEM’s) and associated automated evaluation files.  
 
Contractors shall not process, store, or have access to FTI, PII, SSI, Classified or controlled 
unclassified information and any agency specific confidential data.  
 
The Contractor shall utilize only publicly available information from approved sources including 
IRS Publication 1075, NIST Special Publications and Standards, IRS Safeguard Program public 
website materials, Federal regulations and guidance documents and publicly available industry 
best practice standards to include Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks and Defense 
Information Systems Agency (DISA) Secure Technical Implementation Guides (STIG). All 
queries submitted must contain no FTI or PII; referenced only publicly available information, 
comply with informational handling classifications and be reviewed for compliance prior to 
submission. 
 
3.1   TASK 1- ORIENTATION BRIEFING  
 
The contractor shall facilitate an orien tation briefing via a video conference call (Microsoft (MS) 
Teams, Zoom, etc.) with its representatives, ensuring all parties have a common understanding of 
the task order tasks and requirements. The contractor shall bring, at a minimum, its key personnel 
to this meeting. 
 
3.2   TASK
 2, RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE TRANSFER/TRANSITION-IN  
  
3.2.1 RAMP-UP KNOWLEDGE 
 
Ramp-Up Knowledge Transfer is defined as the contractor acquiring and understanding the 
necessary documentation, information, and processes related to any work in progress. The 
Government anticipates this task will be performed in conjunction with the Transition-In 
activities after the award of this task order.  
 
The contractor shall appoint a knowledge transfer manager serving as key personnel to oversee all 
areas of information that are accounted for and all knowledge of information is transferred from 
the current incumbent. This can be the Project Manager (PM) or other approved key personnel. 
Prior to the transfer of knowledge, the contractor shall develop a final Knowledge Transfer Plan 
(KTP). The final KTP shall identify the contractor resources and roles involved in the transfer 
process, provide a list of risks and mitigation strategies for the transfer, and contain a detailed 
resource balanced project schedule developed with Microsoft Project or compatible equivalent. 
Draft

 3 
The project schedule shall identify tasks, dependencies, deliverables, and milestones. The project 
schedule shall be at a sufficient level of detail to track progress on a bi-weekly basis. 
 
 
The contractor shall meet with the IRS bi-weekly (twice a month) to discuss the progress of the 
knowledge transfer. The contractor shall show an updated MS Project Schedule or compatible 
equivalent and discuss any risks or concerns at this time. 
 
In addition to the Ramp-Up activities in the approved KTP, the contractor shall perform the 
following activities during the Ramp Up: 
 
•
 Assign personnel and submit security background packages within 10 calendar 
days to ensure background investigations are completed efficiently and gain 
access to IRS’s network.  
• Create a project schedule at a sufficient level of detail to track progress on a 
weekly basis. 
•
 Request access within 2 business days to tools and documentation (based on 
                          successful adjudication of background clearance of contractor personnel) 
• Review and understand all the technical and process documentation.  
• Review and understand the case management system. 
•           Knowledge Transfer/Transition-In Status Reports, for the duration of  
                   the transition-in period only, shall detail status of activities identified  
                   in the final KTP. 
 
Note: Completed background requests shall be sent to IRS COR/Alternate COR via encrypted 
electronic file. Any incomplete packages will be rejected for re-submission within 2 workdays.
 
 
The contractor shall provide a KTP and a MS project or compatible equivalent schedule that is 
accepted by the Government and successfully completes knowledge transfer in accordance with 
the plan with a total transition-in project schedule not to exceed one hundred twenty (120) 
calendar days after Government acceptance of the KTP.  In addition, the Contractor shall provide 
complete and accurate status reports for the KTP. 
 
3.2.2 TRANSITION- IN  
 
The Transition-In task permits an effective transition from the incumbent Contractor to the new 
Contractor. The Government estimates this task will take approximately 120 calendar days to 
complete from date of award of the task order. Successful transition can be defined by its capacity 
to maintain full continuity of operations. To ensure a successful, low-risk transition, the 
contractor shall follow the approved Transition-In Plan and keep the government fully informed 
of status throughout the transition-in period. During the transition-in period, the incumbent is 
responsible for performance. This Task would be worked concurrently with Task 2, Ramp-Up 
Knowledge Transfer.  
 
In addition to the transition activities in the approved KTP, the contractor shall ensure the 
following activities have been successfully completed within 75 days of the transition-in period to 
ensure timely commencement of services after the 120-Day Transition-In period: 
 
1. Obtain final access to tools and documentation 
2. Comprehend and successfully perform all the technical and process documentation.

The Tran
sition-in Checklist provides a vehicle to verify completion of the necessary transition-in 
activities. The Transition-in Checklist shall be developed by the Contractor and shall include all 
necessary activities to ensure an effective transition from the incumbent Contractor to a new 
Contractor that were performed. The Transition-in Checklist shall be signed by both, the 
Contractor and the COR after completion of the task.

3.3.1 Gene
ral Requirements 
The Contractor shall provide personnel, including an equivalent contractor Subject Matter Expert 
(SME), to perform the requirements set forth herein. 
3.3.2 Monthly Status Report (MSR) Call 
The Contractor shall facilitate a Monthly Status Report (MSR) Call that includes presentation 
materials, such as a slide deck and supporting documentation, outlining expenditures, billings, 
progress, status, and any problems or issues encountered during task performance. The MSR shall 
include financial projections and an overview of support provided during the previous invoice 
period, including a list of all deliverables accepted and those in progress. All MSR materials and 
activities are subject to review and acceptance by the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) 
and the Technical Point of Contact (TPOC). 
3.3.3 Task Order Program Management Plan (PMP) 
The Contractor shall develop, implement, and maintain a Task Order Program Management Plan 
(PMP), subject to Government review and approval, manage, track, and evaluate performance 
throughout the period of performance. The PMP shall include control policies and procedures 
consistent with standard industry practices for project administration, execution, and tracking. 
The PMP may consist of multiple components, including, a project plan and performance status 
dashboards. The PMP shall include a consolidated roll-up of performance data for all active 
subtasks and shall be structured to support reuse for MSR Calls and other reporting requirements. 
The Contractor shall maintain the PMP in accordance with agreed-upon project management best 
practices. The PMP is subject to review and acceptance by the COR and TPOC. 
3.3.4 Adminis
trative Touchpoint 
The Contractor shall attend and facilitate a weekly Administrative Touchpoint meeting, not to 
exceed one (1) hour in duration, as scheduled by the COR. The purpose of this meeting shall be to 
address onboarding activities, Government Furnished Equipment (GFE), and other administrative 
matters. The Contractor shall prepare, update, and present a performance status dashboard that 
identifies completed deliverables, timeliness of performance, and any deliverables returned due to 
deficient quality. These meetings and associated materials are subject to review by the COR and 
TPOC.

3.3.5 Annual Planning Meeting 
The Contractor shall schedule, coordinate, and facilitate an Annual Planning Meeting with the 
COR, and the TPOC to discuss planned activities for the upcoming option year. The Contractor 
shall prepare and submit meeting materials to the COR for review and approval in advance of the 
meeting.  
3.4   
TASK 4, COMPUTER SECURITY REVIEWS 
T
he Contractor shall work with external partner agency stakeholders to execute system 
configuration checks, interview system users (e.g., administrators), and to examine system 
artifacts (including policies and procedures) against management, operational and technical 
requirements, Center for Internet Security (CIS )Benchmarks, NIST requirements, and current 
IRS standards (e.g., IRS Publication 1075, IRC §6103). The scope of the assessment (“review”) 
will include all hardware and software associated with the processing, storing, or exchange of FTI 
including mainframes, operating system, telecom devices, applications, multi-function devices, 
firewalls, servers, cloud infrastructure, and databases. The contractor shall use the Safeguards 
Computer Security Evaluation Matrices (SCSEMs) and automated evaluation files as a guide to 
perform Computer Security Reviews on local, state or federal agencies, and their authorized 
contractors, that receive FTI under IRC §6103.  
Completion of computer security reviews resulted in the Safeguard review report (SRR) being 
issued to the external partner agency. The SRR consists of Sections A through H. Sections A 
through G are completed by the IRS staff and Section H dealing with information technology is 
completed by the contractor.  The SRR serves to identify an agency’s compliance with their 
statutory obligations under IRC 6103(p)(4) and provide guidance to the agency to improve their 
security posture and meet the safeguarding standards described in Publication 1075. Please refer 
to the Computer Security Safeguards Review Report Standard Opera
