RESPONSIBILITIES 
 
1. Chief Information Officer (CIO). 
 
a. Establishes and oversees web standards for enterprise domains including 
administration, security, and sustainment of web infrastructure, services, tools, and 
Domain Name Service (DNS) directory development IAW Reference (l). 
 
b. Designates the Director, CIO and Information Technology Services (D/CIO-T), as 
the authority to manage the enterprise domain web property framework. 
 
2. D/CIO-T. 
 
a. Manages web properties residing on the enterprise domains. 
 
b. Assigns Director, Future Experience Office (D/TF), to develop NGA web property 
standards and guidelines for enterprise domains. 
 
3. D/TF. 
 
a. Establishes, assigns, and maintains DNS guidelines and standards. 
 
b. Maintains NGA web style guidance to ensure a consistent user experience across 
enterprise domains. 
 
c. Reviews, assumes control of, and removes NGA web properties that are not 
compliant with the standards and guidelines of this Instruction. 
 
d. Promotes usage of best practices to mitigate privacy risks and effectively protect 
personally identifiable information (PII) collected, stored, or transmitted on NGA web 
properties. (Reference (m)) 
 
e. Maintains the NGA Web Guidance and Resources website (hereinafter referred to 
as the Online Resources), located at https://www.intranet.nga.ic.gov/web/. 
 
4. Director, Office of Corporate Communications. 
 
a. Manages the review of all NGA products and information that are publicly 
released (where applicable), all external marketing (e.g., social media, correspondence 
with the press, and promotional products), and all writing for public release for 
adherence to NGA messaging standards on public-facing web properties available over 
the World Wide Web IAW Reference (n). 
 
b. Ensures that information released to the public is unclassified IAW Reference (n).

c. Coordinates and interacts with media and external sources regarding NGA web 
properties IAW Reference (n). 
 
5. Senior Component Official for Privacy collaborates with the D/CIO-T Chief 
Information Officer to ensure that protections and disclaimers are in place for web 
properties that collect, store, or transmit PII IAW Reference (m). 
 
6. Information Developers and Designers. 
 
a. Comply with web standards and guidance provided in the Online Resources when 
developing, modifying, and maintaining NGA web properties on enterprise domains. 
 
b. Comply with all header and footer guidance provided at the Online Resources, 
Content Delivery Network for all NGA web properties. 
 
c. Format and publish NGA web properties that enable all users to retrieve and use 
information, including Section 508 compliance, IAW References (d), (l), and (q).

ENCLOSURE 3 
 
NGA WEB PROPERTIES GUIDANCE 
 
1. Workflow processes for requesting and developing NGA web properties are provided 
in the Web Governance Concept of Operations (CONOPS), the relevant Standard 
Operating Procedures (SOPs), and this Instruction.  
 
2. The CONOPS, SOPs, and links to style guides, design elements, and best practices 
are provided in the Online Resources. 
 
3. Web Design Style Guidance. 
 
a. NGA web properties meet and maintain high standards of effectiveness and 
usability to provide quality information that is readily discoverable and accessible to 
authorized users. (References (d) and (q)) 
 
b. The UXD Web Style Guide is a resource to help developers and software 
engineers overcome common design problems when creating a new web property. A 
core function of the Online Resources is to provide assistance in the creation of a more 
consistent “look and feel” across NGA web properties. The Online Resources UXD Web 
Style Guide is located on the following networks: 
 
NGANet/Joint Worldwide Intelligence 
Communications System (JWICS) 
https://www.intranet.nga.ic.gov/web/ 
http://design.nga.ic.gov 
Secret Internet Protocol Router 
Network (SIPRNet) https://design.nga.smil.mil 
Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU) https://designsystem.digital.gov/ 
http://design.nga.mil 
 
c. The efficient, effective, and consistent use of NGA web properties and web 
services standards promotes a more citizen-centered Government and user-friendly 
experience. 
 
4. Writing in Plain Language. 
 
a. Plain language and communication have many benefits. Avoiding vagueness and 
unnecessary complexity makes it easier for users to understand information and use 
services. Plain writing assists the user in complying with applicable requirements to 
better understand the NGA web property. (References (b) and (j)) 
 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
9 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must conform to the plain writing 
memorandums and referenced materials identified in the content guidance provided in 
the Online Resources. 
 
5. Copyright Protections. 
 
a. Copyright is a form of legal protection grounded in the US Constitution and 
granted by law for original works created in any medium. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must comply with the US Copyright 
laws and referenced materials IAW Reference (f). Copyright guidance is provided in the 
Online Resources. 
 
6. Accessibility Guidance. 
 
a. Accessibility is one of the most important aspects of web development. 
Accessibility allows the greatest number of users to view content more completely. 
Users have a better experience if accessibility is built into web properties from the 
beginning. 
 
b. US Code and Public Laws require Federal Agencies to ensure electronic and 
information technology (EIT) is accessible to people with disabilities. Section 508 of the 
Workforce Investment Act of 1998 applies to all Federal agencies when developing, 
procuring, maintaining, or using EIT. (References (a) and (q)) 
 
c. NGA web properties on enterprise domains comply with Section 508 
requirements. Accessibility guidance and tools are located on networks identified in 
paragraph 3.b. of this Enclosure. 
 
d. For overall questions regarding Section 508 compliance, contact the Section 508 
coordinator at NGASection508Coordinator@coe.ic.gov. (References (a) and (q)) 
 
7. Analytics, Performance Metrics, and Feedback Guidance. 
 
a. Web analytics are the collection, analysis, and communication of web data for 
purposes of understanding and optimizing web usage. Web analytics measure web 
traffic and assess the effectiveness of a web property. The resulting analysis helps the 
organization determine the value of its content or an application, and provides insight to 
improve its offerings and the user experience. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains should have a web analytics 
collection capability. (Reference (d)) Web analytic solutions are provided in the Online 
Resources. 
 
8. Security Guidance. 
 

UNCLASSIFIED 
 
NGAI 8955.6 
10 
 
UNCLASSIFIED 
a. NGA web properties provide Government information and services to support the 
performance of NGA’s mission. Security and risk management are essential functions 
incorporated into the lifecycle of NGA web properties, including classification markings, 
public key infrastructure (PKI) certificates, and hypertext transfer protocol secure 
(HTTPS) IAW References (c), (k) and (p). 
 
b. Intelligence sources, methods, and activities are safeguarded IAW Reference (i). 
Additional information for classification marking requirements is provided in the Online 
Resources. 
 
c. Websites, services, and online resources available over the public internet that 
are maintained and operated in whole or in part by NGA are provided through HTTPS. 
(References (c) and (k)) Additional information for HTTPS implementation is provided in 
the Online Resources. 
 
9. Search and Discovery Guidance. 
 
a. Search functions are universal and an expected website feature commonly used 
to find information. Search engine optimization (SEO) is critical to reaching users who 
primarily rely on commercial search engines. 
 
b. NGA web properties on enterprise domains must provide search capabilities IAW 
References (d) and (h). D/TF provides search solutions, how to incorporate a search 
capability into an NGA web property, and how to maximize discovery of web assets via 
SEO and NGA search tools. Additional information is provided in the Online Resources. 
 
 
c. NGA web properties on enterprise domains are published to a registry to assist 
search and discovery of content and services. Search and Discovery Guides are 
available in the Online Resources. 
 
d. NGA web properties on enterprise domains contain metadata tags to assist 
search and discovery. Search and Discovery Guides are located on networks identified 
in paragraph 3.b. within this Enclosure provided in the Online Resources. 
 
10. NGA Dissemination on Domain Networks Guidance. 
 
a. IC computer domain networks disseminate intelligence information. NGA has 
multiple IC domain networks based on classification. Web properties are stored on 
servers that are connected to the domain networks and are reachable using DNS. 
When the DNS is translated into an Internet Protocol (IP) address, an information 
system (IS) can pinpoint the location of another IS/server where the web property is 
stored. 
 
b. NGA web properties on all enterprise domains must register for a DNS Uniform

Esprit Software Statement of Work

Provide the following licenses for 12-month period of performance. (New effective dates subject to change based on award date of contract.)

Continuous access to the latest software updates

• New 3-axis and 5-axis machining cycles

• Existing machining cycles are continually optimized and improved

• Feature recognition enhancements

• Read the latest native CAD formats

• User interface upgrades for improved ease of use

• Numerous productivity bonuses for milling, turning and EDM machining

- Faster programming

- Improved use of tooling

- Shorter cycle times

- New machining strategies

• Support for the latest generation of machine tools

Live technical support

• Assistance provided by factory certified ESPRIT Application Engineers (AEs)

• Call the regional office nearest you

• Your call is automatically routed to the next available engineer

• ESPRIT AEs use a highly evolved support / resolution tracking database

• Including a knowledge-base of stored solutions to quickly address your needs

On-line technical community

• Round-the-clock support via ESPRITWeb

• Tap into a national support network of ESPRIT users

• Search Technical Bulletins

• Access to Frequently Asked Questions

• File Library with valuable data - post processors, macros, and add-ins

C._1_ Submission of Recordable Injuries and Illness Cases (Dec 2012) Watervliet Arsenal is 
pursuing OSHA Voluntary Protection Program (VPP) recognition. The VPP impacts all contractors 
whose employees cumulatively work more than 1000 hours per quarter within a calendar year at 
Watervliet Arsenal (herein referred to as "applicable contractors"). It is the contractor's 
responsibility to ensure its employees and managers are in full compliance with OSHA 
requirements and have a general understanding of VPP. Detailed information on VPP is available 
on the OSHA website at http://www.osha.gov/dcsp/vpp/index.html . All contractors, whether 
regularly involved in routine site operations or engaged in temporary projects such as construction 
or repair, must follow the safety and health rules of Watervliet Arsenal.
Applicable contractors are required to annually submit to Watervliet Arsenal, ATTN: TAWV-XO-S
/Safety Office, Bldg. 10, 1 Buffington Street, Watervliet, NY 12189-4050 or email: usarmy.
watervliet.tacom.list.watesafety@army.mil the following documents (covering the previous 
calendar year quarters) by 15 January:
- Total Case Incidence Rate (TCIR)
- the number of recordable injuries and illness cases per 100 full-time employees that a site has 
experienced in a given time frame.
- Days Away, Restricted, and/or Transfer Case Incident Rate (DART)
- Number of recordable injuries and illness cases per 100 full-time employees resulting in days 
away from work, restricted work activity, and/or job transfer that a site has experienced in a given 
time frame.
- OSHA Form 300A

desired.

(b) WORK PERFORMED ON-SITE AT WATERVLIET ARSENAL:
The contractor agrees that each employee working at Watervliet Arsenal will sign the "Contractor 
Personnel Agreement on Non-Disclosure of Watervliet Arsenal Technology below. Signatures 
must be received by the Contract Administrator before work may begin and any resultant delay 
won't be considered an excusable delay to contract performance as defined in the contract clause 
"Default". Additional copies of this Non-Disclosure Statement can be found on the Internet at 
http://www.wva.army.mil/Documents/Contracting/nondis.pdf
(d)  CONTRACTOR PERSONNEL AGREEMENT ON NON-DISCLOSURE OF WATERVLIET 
ARSENAL TECHNOLOGY
(1)  The Undersigned, as an employee of  (Name of Firm) agrees to the following terms                
and conditions.
(2)  Any knowledge gained, as a result of my being permitted on Watervliet Arsenal's premises, 
concerning cannon production technology (as defined below) or other technology on any defense 
item being manufactured or developed at Watervliet Arsenal, will not be released outside of 
(Name of firm) and/or the United States of America (this prohibition includes, but is not                
limited to, the company's domestic and foreign subsidiaries, affiliates, etc.), nor will such 
technology be used to manufacture or assist another in the manufacture of cannon (as described 
below) or other defense items being manufactured or developed at Watervliet Arsenal, without the 
written prior approval of Watervliet Arsenal.
(3)  Definitions:
W911PT26QA026
Page 6 of 31

(a)  CANNON: is defined as any and all components/parts of a complete assembly consisting of a 
tube, breech mechanism, tube attachments, muzzle appendages, firing mechanisms, and all 
integral components. It may also be a component of a weapons system of 40mm Bore or over 
such as tank guns, towed and self-propelled howitzers, naval guns, mortars and recoilless guns.
(b)  CANNON PRODUCTION TECHNOLOGY: is defined as the technical data package and 
manufacturing technology.
(1)  TECHNICAL DATA PACKAGE: cannon engineering drawings, specifications and standards.
(2)  MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY: technical knowledge, documentation, assistance and 
equipment and machines used and/or useful in the manufacturing of cannon.
(c)  TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE: the know how collected, trade secrets, production experience 
and special skills necessary for the production of cannon and the technical information and 
inventions necessary for the manufacture of cannon and relating to the manufacture of cannon.
(d)  TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION: manufacturing technical data comprised of drawings, 
specifications, schemes, composition, descriptions, methods of calculations, instructions and other 
information necessary for the manufacture of cannon.
(e)  TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE: all assistance required to make practical and economical use of 
the technology required to manufacture cannon, such as delivery of documentation, training of 
personnel, instructions, consultations and acquainting of specialists with the most economical 
method of using this technology in the manufacture of cannon.
(f)   EQUIPMENT AND MACHINES: production machines, machine accessories, apparatuses, 
spare parts and tooling used for cannon manufacture.

This requirement will be solicited and released under Fair Opportunity on GSA Alliant 3.  Estimated release date is anticipated May 2026.

GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

This is an RFI/Source Sought for Network Engineering, Design, Implementation and Infrastructure Support (NEDIIS) ReCompete.  Please see the attached for more information. 

Request for Information 

Network Engineering, Design, Implementation and Infrastructure Support (NEDIIS)

VA-26-00019737

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal.  Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract.  No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response.  The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI.

This action may be competed under the Transformation Twenty One Total Technology Next Generation multiple award, indefinite delivery, indefinite quantity contract using fair opportunity procedures in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 16.505.  

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512 with a size standard of $34 million.  

2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 25 pages.  The Government will not review any other information or attachments included, that are in excess of the 25 page limit. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.  Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed.  Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PWS and must include the following:

Interested Vendors shall at a minimum, provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission:

Name of Company

Address

Point of Contact

Phone Number

Fax Number

Email address

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is the second-largest federal department, serving approximately 19 million Veterans in over 1,700 facilities and sites worldwide, making it the largest integrated health care system in the United States. This impressive service delivery is made possible through the coordinated efforts of three major line organizations: the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA), and the National Cemetery Administration (NCA). These efforts are orchestrated at the VA Central Office (VACO) located in Washington, D.C.  

OIT delivers available, adaptable, secure, and cost-effective technology services to the VA and acts as a steward for all VA's Information Technology (IT) assets and resources. Currently, 60% of the 16,000 plus OIT employees and contractors are Veterans. 

The Connectivity and Collaboration Services (CCS) team delivers world class Telephony, Network, and Collaboration Services in an environment that encourages transparency, innovation, flexibility, fiscal responsibility, and accountability with 100% focus on Veteran outcomes.​

CCS serves at the forefront of VA’s digital transformation, enabling enterprise collaboration and connecting Veterans to VA through secure and resilient voice, video, data, and messaging services. 

CCS is divided into three pillars.

Core Network Services (CNS) - This pillar fuses the development, engineering, and operation of VA network services into a single organization, driving efficiency and enabling a unified strategy for our network infrastructure.​​​​​​​

Collaboration Services (CS) - CS provides enterprise level support focused on providing dynamic, flexible and efficient collaboration amongst VA staff and Veteran outreach. CS nationally supports the Microsoft 365 suite of products that VA currently employs for enterprise messaging and collaboration. These products include Exchange, Teams, OneDrive and others.

Unified Communications (UC) - UC continues to modernize, enhance, and operate world class enterprise Unified Communications services and solutions to connect Veterans, their families and VA professionals to the resources and services they need.

Direct Contractor support for this Task Order (TO) will reside within CCS Division under the Office of Information and Technology.  Mainly under CNS with optional tasks under the CS, UC, and ETS Business Office pillars.

Under CCS, The CNS team is a vital team supporting the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) mission by providing robust and reliable network infrastructure that connects VA facilities, Clouds, Internet, contractors, guests, and Veterans to critical VA resources and services. CNS enables seamless access to essential applications, data, and services across all VA divisions, ensuring that VHA,(VBA, and NCA can deliver top-tier healthcare, benefits, and cemetery services to Veterans across the nation. In doing so, CNS directly impacts the quality and timeliness of the VA's service delivery by maintaining the infrastructure that powers every networked interaction within VA facilities.

CNS is responsible for overseeing the telecommunications and networking technologies that serve as the backbone for VA operations. This includes provisioning the high-speed, secure, and resilient connections that allow VA personnel to collaborate effectively, enable contractors to access necessary resources, support guests’ informational needs, and allow Veterans direct access to their own health and benefits information. By providing stable network connectivity, CNS plays a crucial role in critical system availability to the VA workforce, whether they are in medical centers, regional offices, veteran centers, or remote clinics.

CNS Priorities

Communications - internally within network operations, engineering, and provisioning teams

Site Availability - Uptime for sites, redundancy, resiliency, minimizing downtime, and data supporting this.

Compliance - baseline configuration compliance, code standards, time to deploy, tracking Known Exploited Vulnerabilities/Zero Days.

CNS operates a very large enterprise network for our customers. As of (FY26, CNS is responsible for the following:

Daily Remote Access Users: ~246,000 Unique Users

Sites: ~2,200

Circuits: ~2,600

Routers: ~5,000

Firewalls: ~4,000

LAN Switches: ~45,000

Wi-Fi Access Points: ~200,000

The VA Enterprise Network will consist of products and services which are increasingly automated, digitally assisted and integrated with security across all service domains.

Introduction

This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for market research and planning purposes and shall not be construed as an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Task Execution Plan (RTEP), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Request for Proposal (RFP). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation, does not commit the Government to issue a solicitation, and does not authorize the Government to negotiate or award a contract at this time.

The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified and capable vendors that can meet the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) Services in support of the Financial Management Business Transformation (FMBT) Program. The Government seeks to obtain information on industry capabilities, best practices, and feedback related to the scope provided (Please see attached Draft Performance Work Statement). Any potential contract or order resulting from information obtained through this market research will be competed in accordance with applicable Federal Acquisition Regulations.

The Government is not responsible for any costs incurred by respondents in developing or submitting responses to this RFI. Participation is strictly voluntary, and non‑participation will not preclude any vendor from future consideration under any forthcoming RTEP, RFQ, or RFP. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Respondents are responsible for clearly marking any proprietary, restricted, or competition‑sensitive information included in their submissions.

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519.  

2. Submittal Information:

All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below information.  

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 10 pages. 

The Government will not review any other information or attachments included, that are in excess of the 10 page limit. NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI.  Generic capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed.  Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached draft PWS and must include the following:

Interested Vendors shall at a minimum, provide the following information in the initial paragraph of the submission:

Company Name

CAGE/ Unique Entity ID under which the company is registered in SAM.gov

Company Address

Company Business Size and Status

 For small business concerns, indicate whether at least 50 percent of the total amount paid by the Government will be paid to firms that are similarly situated.

 Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB) and Veteran Owned Small Businesses (VOSB) must indicate whether at least 50% of the cost incurred would be expended for prime employees or employees of other eligible SDVOSB/VOSB firms. This should also include the prime planned percentage and if under 50%, the names of the potential team members that may be used to fulfill the 50% SDVOSB/VOSB requirement.

 If your company is a Small Business, also include the following:

The intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort.

Information as to available personnel and financial resources to support a requirement of this magnitude.

Information as to proposed team members, the percentage of work each is to perform and which PWS requirements would be subcontracted.

Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC)

Provide a summary of your capability to meet the requirements contained within the draft PWS for the following areas: 

List any existing contracting vehicles that you would recommend for this requirement to be solicited against. 

Detail your company’s capability and experience developing verification and validation approaches, risk and assessment criteria, for programs similar to Financial Management Business Transformation (FMBT) ensuring consistency with the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) verification and validation standards and compliance with applicable law and policy. 

Detail your company’s capability and experience developing verification and validation methods for independent testing, to include development and execution of manual and automated test scripts for coverage of business functional and technical requirements, business processes and interfaces for similar systems to the Integrated Financial and Acquisition Management System (iFAMS), software and configurations ensuring consistency with the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) verification and validation standards and compliance with applicable law and policy. 

Detail your company’s capability and certified Momentum federal financial management application subject matter expertise with regard to testing, configuring or supporting Momentum software or Momentum system implementations or enterprise federal financial management efforts. 

Detail your company’s capability and experience with Agile Scrum methodology and/or Scaled Agile Framework (or SAFe methodology) and managing IV&V work utilizing Agile or other industry’s best practices. 

Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI)

 

Any vendors that are currently providing any services (program management, development, sustainment, testing, etc.) for VA FMBT program or iFAMS will likely have an OCI that will preclude it from bidding on this effort as the scope of this work includes performance analysis of current work being performed by and within each portfolio, re-prioritization/investment recommendations for portfolios/programs/projects, and budget recommendations for the portfolios’ current states. In addition, any vendors that intend to bid on future work associated with these portfolios should consider that the successful awardee of the Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) services for Financial Management Business Transformation (FMBT) procurement will likely be excluded from bidding on that work as part of the scope of this effort is requirements analysis, strategic planning, and budget formulation for the portfolios’ future states. If so, please describe the contracted services being provided.

Please do not wait until the last minute to submit your responses! To avoid submission of late responses, we recommend the transmission of your response file 24 hours prior to the required response due date and time. Offerors are encouraged to review and ensure that sufficient bandwidth is available on their end of the transmission.

The VA OIT mission is to provide benefits and services to Veterans of the United States. In meeting these goals, OIT strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient IT services to VA components that are ultimately responsible for providing services to our nation’s Veterans. VA depends on IM/IT systems and services to meet mission goals.

The Financial Management Business Transformation (FMBT) program vision is to provide VA with a modern financial and acquisition management solution with transformative business processes and capabilities that enable VA to meet its goals and objectives in compliance with financial management legislation and directives. Through the FMBT program, VA is working to implement an enterprise-wide financial and acquisitions management system and integrated solution, known as the Integrated Financial and Acquisitions Management System (iFAMS), which will enable VA to improve service to Veterans, increase innovation, and enhance data integrity.

The iFAMS solution includes Momentum® a commercial Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system developed by CGI. VA is migrating to the Momentum commercial cloud solution, configured for VA as the Integrated Financial and Acquisition Management System (iFAMS), allowing VA to leverage CGI’s Software as a Service (SaaS) model. VA will gain increased operational efficiency, productivity, agility, and flexibility from a modern Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) cloud solution. The new cloud solution will also provide additional security, storage, and scalability. By implementing Momentum Acquisitions, VA is getting real-time integration with financials through a single, consolidated system.

VA has many financial systems related to veterans’ support that interface with the legacy Financial Management System (FMS) of record. VA is replacing FMS under its FMBT program. This Description of Need (DON) defines the requirement for the procurement of brand-name Camunda Enterprise 
Edition software licenses and associated annual maintenance and technical success services. The purpose of this

critical business processes. This procurement is a direct follow-on action to maintain the operational status of these

platform to ensure it remains secure and up to date.
Technical Success Support:

troubleshooting, configuration, and best practices.

1. BACKGROUND  
 
DISA currently manages mobile device services for the Department of Defense (DoD) and 
approved non-DoD users and is required to maintain compliance with evolving Commercial 
Solutions for Classified (CSfC) standards. The continuous evolution of CSfC Mobile Access 
Capability Package (MACP) requirements is essential for meeting growing security demands 
while improving functionality, usability, and compliance in a rapidly changing technological 
landscape. Earlier mobility solutions consisted of an End User Device (EUD), such as a phone, 
tablet, or laptop, paired with a Retransmission Device (RD) that functioned as a commercial 
mobile hotspot.  
 
2. PROBLEM STATEMENT  
 
The latest published CSfC MACP (version 2.7) requires the RD to be connected to the mobile 
device through a hardwired connection. In earlier versions of MACP, this requirement could be 
met by using a cellular hotspot device that connects to the mobile device via Wi-Fi connection. 
While a cable connection meets the new MACP technical standard, it is operationally untenable. 
The use of a visible cable between the EUD and the RD creates two critical issues: 
 
a. Degraded User Experience & Risk: Physical cables introduce significant user experience 
challenges and operational risks. From a user perspective, the cable is an encumbrance that 
can snag on other gear, get caught on the environment, and physically tether the user, 
restricting their mobility and creating a potential point of failure if disconnected. The 
physical cable makes the phone conspicuous and draws unwanted attention. This visibility 
creates a significant operational security risk. In environments where stealth and operational 
discretion are critical, such exposure could compromise the security of the mission and the 
individual, making it easier for adversaries to target or disrupt operations. The presence of a 
physical cable can serve as an indicator of the operator’s location, role, and equipment type, 
increasing the likelihood of detection and compromising the security of sensitive activities. 
 
b. Reduced Tactical Mobility: Forcing users to carry and physically connect separate devices 
is cumbersome, creates a logistical burden, and hinders the tactical mobility required for 
accessing networks like the Secret Internet Protocol Router (SIPR) Network in operational 
environments. 
 
This prototype OT seeks to develop an innovative and user-friendly Retransmission Device (RD) 
to bridge the gap between CSfC standards and operational needs. The ideal solution, likely a 
sleeve or integrated case, will satisfy the new CSfC hardwired connection requirement internally 
while appearing as a normal case to the outside observer. The goal is to eliminate conspicuous 
external cables, remove the logistical burden of separate devices, and restore full tactical 
mobility for users. 
 
3. DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES  
 
A fully functional prototype must include the following unique or innovative capabilities, 
functions, and/or features:  

Version 1.0  Page 3 of 7 
 
3.1. Core Compliance & Physical Design 
 
a. The solution must meet or exceed all requirements of the CSfC MACP version 2.7, and all 
subsequent versions released during the period of performance. 
 
b. The solution’s physical footprint shall be minimized to reduce its visual signature. While a 
form factor similar in size to a commercial smartphone case is the desired baseline, 
companies are encouraged to propose innovative solutions that achieve the core requirement 
of being inconspicuous. 
 
c. The solution must be an all-in-one form factor that eliminates the need for a separate device 
and connecting cable. 
 
d. The solution must be modular to enable rapid, cost-effective portability of capabilities across 
current and future EUD form factors.  
 
e. The solution or physical design (e.g., smartphone case) must support both current and future 
approved DoD mobile devices/form factors (e.g., Samsung Galaxy S25 or S26). The ability 
to support additional form factors (e.g., tablets, laptops, etc.) is a desired feature; however, 
support for additional form factors would only be required in a follow-on production OT or 
contract.   
 
3.2. Component & Supply Chain Security 
 
a. The solution must be compliant with CSfC and National Information Assurance Partnership 
(NIAP) requirements. All components used in the solution must be on the CSfC Components 
List and NIAP validated. The Government will not consider solutions that rely on achieving 
NIAP validation during the prototype period of performance.  
 
b. The solution must adhere to Supply Chain Risk Management principles throughout its 
lifecycle. 
 
c. The solution must adhere to the Trade Agreements Act statutes throughout its lifecycle. All 
manufacturing and assembly, throughout the prototype and any potential follow-on 
production, must be performed domestically in compliance with International Traffic in Arms 
Regulations (ITAR). 
 
d. All modem chips must be compliant throughout the period of performance with Section 
889(a)(1)(A)&(B) of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA).

Government-approved moblie devices and form factors. In their solution brief, the Company 
must commit to completing any future form factor change requests within 90 days of 
receiving a formal request from the Government. This capability is considered a required 
performance standard for the successful awardee. 

Version 1.0  Page 4 of 7 
 
f. The company must demonstrate the ability to produce at scale and meet demand via an ITAR 
regulated facility. 
 
3.3. Connectivity & Transport 
 
a. The solution must provide unlocked, Fourth-Generation (4G)/Long-Term Evolution wireless 
network transport that can provide service in Continental United States (CONUS) and 
Outside Continental United States (OCONUS) for the prototype OT. If a follow-on 
production OT or contract is awarded, the Company must be capable of further developing 
the solution to support both 4G and Fifth-Generation cellular transport. “Unlocked" is 
defined as not being bound to a specific carrier, supporting both embedded Subscriber 
Identity Module (SIM) and physical SIM cards.  
 
b. The proposed solution must have the ability to utilize CONUS cellular modems for the 
prototype. If a production OT is awarded, the solution must support both CONUS and 
OCONUS cellular connectivity. 
 
c. The solution must provide 802.11 a/b/g/ac (Wi-Fi 6E/7) transport options. 
 
d. The connectivity chip responsible for external communication must be physically distinct 
from the main processor and not integrated within the same chip. 
 
e. It is desired, but not required, that the capability be designed to support emerging transport 
options, such as Direct-to-Device satellite communications, where applicable.  
 
f. The prototype must demonstrate Wi-Fi connectivity only. If a follow-on production OT or 
contract is awarded, the Company must be capable of futher developing the solution to 
support both Wi-Fi and Cellular connectivity.  
 
g. The Company must demonstrate the ability to obatin Federal Communications Commission 
(FCC) Certification for any components requiring U.S. celleuar network access. Applicable 
FCC certifications would only be required for a follow-on production OT or contract.   
 
3.4. Security Features 
 
a. The ability to create an outer VPN on the RD is a desired feature. If the outer VPN 
capability is included, it must utilize a cryptographic key store that is physically and 
logically independent of the EUD. 
 
b. If the RD is used to create a VPN, it must be able to support the CNSA Suite 2.0 Profile for 
IPSEC in accordance with the draft CSfC Post Quantum Cryptography Guidance 
Addendum.

Version 1.0  Page 5 of 7 
a. The solution must include full lifecycle support, if the prototype is successful and moved into 
production, to include planning, procurement, deployment, sustainment, and secure disposal. 
 
b. The solution must offer a framework to control lifecycle costs and provide comprehensive

c. The solution must be administered via a centralized, cloud-based platform that is authorized

d. The platform must support secure, over-the-air firmware updates.

Request for Information  
Employee Recognition Service  
VA-26-00052104 
 
1. Introduction 
This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be 
considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for 
Quotation or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of 
the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your 
response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. 
You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in 
responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or 
the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been 
authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for 
adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information 
contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information 
submitted in response to this RFI. 
 
The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 
541519 with a size standard of 150 Employees.   
 
2. Submittal Information: 
All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the below 
information.  
 
There is a page limitation for this RFI of 10 pages. The Government will not review any 
other information or attachments included, that are in excess of the 10 page limit. NO 
MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI. Generic 
capability statements will not be accepted or reviewed. Your response must address 
capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PD and must include the 
following: 
 
a. Interested Vendors shall at a minimum, provide the following information in the 
initial paragraph of the submission: 
 
Name of Company 
Address 
Point of Contact 
Phone Number 
Fax Number 
Email address 
Company Business Size and Status 
For VOSB and SDVOSBs, proof of SBA certification.  
NAICS code(s) 
Socioeconomic data 
Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number 

Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC) 
 
b. Provide a summary of your capability to meet the requirements contained within 
the draft PD. 
 
c. Your company’s intent and ability to meet the set aside requirement in 
accordance with VAAR 852.219-10 (JAN 2023) (DEVIATION) VA Notice of Total 
Set-Aside for Certified SDVOSBs and 13 CFR §125.6, which states the 
contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the Government to it 
to firms that are not SDVOSBs. Your response shall include information as to 
available personnel and financial resources; full names of proposed team 
members and the PD requirements planned to be subcontracted to them, which 
must include the prime planned percentage or the names of the potential team 
members that may be used to fulfill the set aside requirement.  
 
d. Has the draft PD provided sufficient detail to describe the technical requirements 
that encompass the software development and production operations support 
services to be performed under this effort.  
 
______ YES  
 
_____    NO (if No, answer question e) 
 
e. If “NO”, please provide your technical comments/recommendations on elements 
of the draft PD that may contribute to a more accurate proposal submission and 
efficient, cost-effective effort. 
 
 
NOTE: Technical questions may be submitted as part of your response, however, 
questions directed to the customer are prohibited.  All questions in response to this RFI 
shall be included in a separate word document titled, Employee Recognition 
RFI_Questions. The answers to all questions received will be posted prior to/with the 
Solicitation. 
 
Responses are due no later than 2:00 PM Est, April 23, 2026 via email to Allison Fulton, 
Contract Specialist at Allison.Fulton@va.gov and Contracting Officer, Mina Awad at 
Mina.Awad@va.gov. Please note “RFI - Employee Recognition Service” in the subject 
line of your response. Mark your response as “Proprietary Information” if the information 
is considered business sensitive. The email file size shall not exceed 5 MB.

1.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
 
The Contractor shall provide a Healthcare driven digital, cloud-based employee 
recognition platform that enables employees, patients, caregivers, and family members 
to recognize Orlando VA Health Care System (OVAHCS) clinical and non-clinical staff 
for exemplary customer care and support. 
 
The platform shall utilize a push/pull technology approach to healthcare employee 
recognition by facilitating real-time feedback from patients, peers, caregivers, and family 
members (pull), and by delivering personalized recognition and actionable data to staff 
(push). 
 
The platform shall include, at a minimum, the capability to: 
• Generate detailed reports measuring patient satisfaction, patient safety, and staff 
recognition data. 
• Capture real-time, in-the-moment patient feedback. 
• Provide prioritized, real-time results and insights. 
• Offer marketing and communication tools that support efforts to improve patient 
experience and employee engagement. 
 
The platform shall be accessible on any Android or Apple device. The system shall 
support unlimited data pulls by the organization and must accommodate up to 6,648 
OVAHCS employees. The Contractor shall provide technical support services sufficient 
to ensure full and continuous functionality of the platform for all covered users. 
 
1.1 SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS 
 
1. Allow Veterans and family members to digitally recognize staff 
members who positively impact their care journey. 
2. Provide an easy-to-use, real-time interface that allows Veterans and 
families to submit recognition directly from mobile devices or digital 
access points during their visit. 
3. Enable Veterans to recognize individuals who impacted their 
experience across clinical and non-clinical roles. 
4. Support multiple languages to ensure accessibility for diverse 
populations. 
5. Deliver positive Veteran feedback directly to staff members through a 
platform accessible to their peers and leadership. While screening and 
redacting any protected health information (PHI) in compliance with 
HIPAA requirements. 
6. Enable real-time service recovery opportunities by privately routing any 
constructive feedback to relevant leaders. 
7. Integrate existing recognition programs (e.g., Diseases Attacking the 
Immune System (DAISY) Award nominations) into a unified workflow,

enabling Veterans and family members to submit nominations directly 
through the interface. 
8. Ask configurable questions related to a Veteran’s experience with 
specific staff members and provide individualized Veteran experience 
insights to employees and leadership. 
9. Enable real-time notifications to staff and leaders when recognition is 
received.  
10. Provide resources to support awareness and adoption of the 
healthcare patient driven recognition program.  
11. Ensure healthcare workers receive meaningful and frequent 
recognition by incorporating the voice of leaders, peers, Veterans, and 
their families. 
12. Reinforce Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect, and Excellence 
(ICARE) values by incentivizing and promoting mission-aligned 
behaviors across staff. 
13. Provide Veteran-to-staff, peer-to-peer, leader-to-staff, and leader-to-
team recognition capabilities. 
14. Enhance employee engagement by highlighting the impact of staff 
contributions through Healthcare patient driven recognition.  
15. Support employee celebrations including service anniversaries, new 
hires, milestones, and other culture-building events. 
16. Provide an internal social engagement environment that allows patient-
driven stories, positive experiences, and communication to be shared 
between individuals, teams, groups, departments, and across the 
organization.  
17. Enable leadership to communicate organizational priorities through 
digital communication tools within the platform. 
18. Provide opportunities to highlight positive care experiences across 
departments and service lines. 
19. Provide interactive challenges that promote teamwork, patient 
experience, quality, safety, and positive workplace behaviors. 
20. Provide platform user interface design with branding customization and 
data insights to drive organization improvements 
21. Provide real-time reporting and analytics to identify trends related to 
Veteran experience, staff engagement, and recognition activity. 
22. Deliver platform insights directly to leaders to surface areas of strength 
and share opportunities on how to make the biggest impact on your 
team  
23. Support data access and reporting capabilities to inform leadership 
decision making. 
24. Provide Software-as-a-Service based interactive software hosted in a 
secure cloud environment. 
25. Support access across Android and iOS devices. 
26. Include a companion mobile application. 
27. Provide Single Sign-On integration with existing authentication and HR 
systems.

28. Support at least 6,648 users and provide technical support. 
29. Provide ongoing technical support and system administration 
assistance. 
30. The Contractor shall implement an Information Security Management 
System (ISMS), that adheres to ISO27001 and HIPAA. 
31. The Contractor shall be SOC 2 Type II certified. 
32. Maintain an information security policy that complies with applicable 
regulatory and business requirements. This policy must protect all 
sensitive and confidential data stored, accessed, or transmitted by the 
software platform, including applications, components, infrastructure, 
and underlying code. 
33. The Contractor shall have a risk assessment program to assess the 
organization’s enterprise-level risk at least annually, or upon significant 
changes to the environment. 
34. Require employees with access to sensitive information to sign 
confidentiality agreements prohibiting unauthorized disclosure of 
system data 
35. The Contractor shall have a comprehensive security awareness 
training program that is fully implemented. A core set of security 
training, including HIPAA, for all employees onboarding. The training 
program also includes monthly updates of latest security threats; 
annual review of core security training; and team-specific training, as 
defined by security team. 
36. Strict control access to restrict private information to privileged users. 
These users are required to abide by their assigned responsibilities 
related to their elevated access. 
37. Data handling, retention, and disposal program to manage information 
in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, policies, and 
standards. This program establishes a formal data retention schedule 
and implements a data classification standard to ensure the 
confidential data is secured. 
38. Retains sensitive and confidential data only for as long as necessary to 
fulfill its purposes unless otherwise required by law or to meet legal 
and client contractual obligations. 
39. Network segmentation to prevent direct or unauthorized connections 
between an external network and its information systems, in particular 
confidential data in cloud environments. 
40. A vulnerability management program to ensure the confidentiality, 
integrity, and availability (CIA) of the organization’s information 
systems landscape, which includes all critical system resources. The 
program includes internal and external scans, penetration testing, and 
issue remediation for the purposes of identifying, detecting, classifying, 
prioritizing, remediating, validating, and continuously monitoring 
vulnerabilities.

Performance Work Statement 
AFLCMC Engineering Directorate (EN-EZ) 
Collateral Conference Room 162 
 
1.0 Background 
The U.S. Government requires a technology upgrade for the conference room located at 
conference room 162 located in Building 28, Area B, WPAFB, OH The purpose is to integrate 
a modern Uniﬁed Communications (UC) capability using Microsoft Teams into a Collateral 
Secret SIPRNET environment. The room contains existing VTC equipment that is outdated 
and scheduled for decommissioning but will remain in place temporarily. The new solution 
must be integrated with certain remaining components while replacing those that are 
incompatible. 
2.0 Scope 
The contractor shall provide and install a complete, turn-key solution to enable MS Teams 
functionality within the designated conference room. The work includes providing and 
installing a new camera, microphone system, and control system processor, and 
integrating these components with the existing displays and control interface. The ﬁnal 
system must be capable of dual operation, allowing users to select either the new MS 
Teams capability or the legacy VTC system until it is decommissioned. The solution must 
be engineered to function independently after the legacy system is removed without 
requiring rework. 
3.0 Speciﬁc Tasks 
The contractor shall: 
• 3.1 Install New Camera System: Provide and install one (1) 4K-capable web camera. 
The camera shall be mounted on the front wall, centered between the two existing 
wall displays. 
• 3.2 Install New Microphone System: Provide and install a microphone solution 
optimized for MS Teams. The preferred solution is a single tabletop device capable 
of capturing audio from all participants in the room. The device must feature a 
readily accessible physical mute/unmute control. Ceiling-mounted microphone 
solutions are not desired. 
• 3.3 Integrate Audio: Conﬁgure the audio output from the new MS Teams system to 
be routed through the two (2) existing 75-inch wall-mounted displays. 

• 3.4 Replace Control System Processor: Replace the outdated, end-of-life Crestron 
rack-mounted controller with a modern processor unit that is capable of supporting 
both the new MS Teams integration and the legacy VTC system. 
• 3.5 Reprogram Control Interface: Reprogram the existing Crestron touch panel to 
provide a single, intuitive user interface. The control panel must allow users to easily 
select and operate one of the following modes: 
• Microsoft Teams Session 
• Legacy GVS VTC System 
• PC-based Presentation (local display) 
• 3.6 System Integration and Dual-Use Functionality: Integrate the new MS Teams 
equipment with the legacy VTC system to allow for seamless switching between the 
two. The technical solution must be designed so that the future removal of the 
legacy VTC hardware does not disable or negatively impact the functionality of the 
newly installed MS Teams solution. 
4.0 Security and Compliance Requirements 
All equipment, software, and conﬁgurations provided under this contract must comply with 
all applicable security requirements for operation on SECRET networks. This includes, but 
is not limited to: 
• 4.1 DISA STIGs: The system and its components must be conﬁgured in compliance 
with all relevant Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) Security Technical 
Implementation Guides (STIGs). 
• 4.2 IA Accreditation: All hardware and software components must be listed on the 
DoD Information Network (DoDIN) Approved Products List (APL) and meet the 
requirements for use in a secure environment. The solution must be capable of 
achieving Information Assurance (IA) accreditation. 
  
See BOM for more details.

Justification & Approval  
For Other than Full and Open Competition 
 
As a legislative branch agency, the Library is subject to the competition and advertising requirements of 41 U.S.C. § 6101. Like the Competition in 
Contracting Act and the FAR, 41 U.S.C. § 6101 does not require competition when a contracting officer certifies that only one source or brand-name 
item is available, when dictated by public exigency, or when otherwise authorized by law.  
 
This document sets forth the justification and approval for award of a contract or order by means providing for other than full and open competition 
per 41 U.S.C. § 6101, LCR 7-210, and, as applicable, FAR 6.302, FAR 13.106-1, FAR 8.405, and FAR 16.505. Contracting without competition 
shall not be justified on the basis of a lack of advance planning or concerns related to availability of funds.  
 
This form shall be used to support instances where competition will be limited to a single source, a limited number of sources, including where a 
brand name product is required.

6. DESCRIPTION OF EFFORTS MADE TO ENSURE THAT OFFERS ARE SOLICITED 
FROM AS MANY POTENTIAL SOURCES AS POSSIBLE. 
 
A competitive solicitation for the follow-on requirement to this task order was issued, and an award was 
made. That award is now under protest, creating an urgent and compelling need for a bridge action to 
prevent a lapse in service. 
 
In accordance with FAR 5.202(a)(2), the Government will not publicize this sole-source bridge 
modification. The unusual and compelling urgency of this requirement, driven by the protest and the 
impending expiration of the current task order on 31 March 2026, does not permit the time required to 
solicit offers from other sources. 
 
Publicizing a competitive action for this short-term bridge would delay the award, resulting in an 
unacceptable interruption of the critical JOPES and TransViz functional management support services 
detailed in Section 4 of this justification. Therefore, this J&A authorizes a sole-source modification to 
the incumbent, GDIT, as they are the only source capable of providing these services without a break in 
performance. 
 
7. DETERMINATION BY THE CONTRACTING OFFICER THAT THE ANTICIPATED 
COST TO THE GOVERNMENT WILL BE FAIR AND REASONABLE. 
 
The Contracting Officer will determine that the final negotiated price is fair and reasonable. The 
Government will conduct a price analysis in accordance with FAR 15.404-1(b)(2). This analysis will 
primarily consist of comparing the incumbent's proposed price for this bridge action to the historical 
pricing paid under the current task order and, most significantly, to the pricing recently evaluated for the 
protested follow-on competitive award, which was determined to be fair and reasonable. 
  
8. THE REASON MARKET RESEARCH WAS NOT CONDUCTED. 
 
Market research for this specific bridge modification was not conducted due to the unusual and 
compelling urgency detailed in Section 5. The Government is leveraging the recent and comprehensive 
market research conducted for the full and open competition of the follow-on award. That research 
confirmed the state of the market for these services. 
 
The urgent need to have a contractual vehicle in place by 1 April 2026 to prevent a critical service gap 
does not permit the time to conduct a new, stand-alone market research effort for this short-term action. 
 
9. ANY OTHER FACTS SUPPORTING THE USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN 
COMPETITION. 
 
In addition to the unusual and compelling urgency, a transition to a different contractor for this short-
term bridge period would introduce unacceptable mission risk. 
 
The functional management of JOPES and TransViz requires deep, specialized knowledge of 
USTRANSCOM's specific operational procedures, data structures, and key mission partner 
relationships. The incumbent, GDIT, possesses this unique institutional knowledge and has the cleared

Department of Homeland Security Customs & Border Protection (CBP) Statement of Work 
(SOW) for Illegal Transshipment Pilot 
1.0 BACKGROUND  
 
U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) plays a critical role in the enforcement of trade 
regulations and the collection of customs revenue, positioning itself as the nation’s second 
largest revenue collection agency. In Fiscal Year 2025, CBP successfully collected $216.7 
billion in duties, taxes, and fees, continuing a legacy of robust enforcement that has led to the 
collection of 99.5% of all customs tariff revenue owed to the U.S. since 1992.  
 
Despite this high collection rate, unscrupulous importers continue to engage in deceptive 
practices to evade antidumping and countervailing duties, tariffs, and other trade regulations, 
harming compliant business and eroding the revenue base. Chief among these deceptive 
practices are illegal transshipment schemes, or the act of routing of goods through a third country 
to obscure their true country of origin and avoid higher tariffs.  
 
To combat illegal transshipment, CBP has intensified its enforcement efforts by leveraging 
advanced technology, data analytics, and partnerships with other federal agencies 
and industry partners. These measures aim to detect and prevent illegal transshipment and other 
illicit schemes, ensuring compliance with trade laws and protecting U.S. economic interests.  
 
Under the Illegal Transshipment Pilot, CBP will explore whether Artificial Intelligence (AI) 
technology solutions offered by the private sector can help uncover illegal transshipment 
schemes at scale and with a high degree of accuracy. This technology demonstration presents 
opportunities for the private sector and CBP to identify enforcement efficiencies and maximize 
revenue collection.   
 
 
2.0 SCOPE   
CBP will assess the value of Artificial Intelligence (AI) driven commercial solutions that identify 
imports which pose a high risk for illegal transshipment. The development and implementation of 
these private sector solutions will enable CBP to explore how cutting -edge technologies may be 
leveraged to inform enforcement actions that prevent high- risk imports from entering the U.S. 
and/or lead to the identification of additional duties owed. 
 
Vendors will deliver insights about illegal transshipment risk via  referral packages  to CBP. 
Referral packages shall articulate specific risk factors that vendors believe are indicative of illegal 
transshipment. Referral packages must also identify or be easily traced to imports that are in transit 
and have not yet arrived in the U.S . To support this requirement, vendors may choose to receive 
the below manifest information for imports originating from countries that CBP identifies as being 
higher risk for illegal transshipment. CBP will make manifest information available to vendors no 
later than 72 hours before imports are expected to arrive in the U.S.   
 
• Port of Unlading 
• Port of Lading 
• Arrival Date 
• Bill Number 

5 
 
• HTS Code 
• Shipper 
• Consignee 
• Cargo Description 
• Declared Country of Origin 
 
Vendors will be given an opportunity to prove out the scalability and accuracy of their illegal 
transshipment solutions over the course of a no-cost, 180-day base period of performance. 
Scalability will be measured by the number of actionable referral packages vendors submit to 
CBP. Accuracy will be measured by the percentage of referral packages that lead to the 
prevention of high-risk imports from entering the U.S. and/or the identification of additional 
duties owed. CBP will have full discretion over which referral packages to investigate based on 
confidence levels, potential revenue impact, ongoing or previous enforcement actions, and 
resource availability. Only referral packages that CBP chooses to investigate and act upon will 
be factored into its assessment of accuracy.  
 
Vendors who achieve the performance milestones defined in Section 6.0 may have their option 
periods exercised by CBP.  
 
The solutions delivered under the Illegal Transshipment Pilot as outlined in this SOW must drive 
enhancements and efficiencies around targeting for illegal transshipment, maximizing the 
collection of revenue owed to the U.S., and allocation of CBP resources towards areas of highest 
revenue risk. The desired end state for this SOW is to identify AI-driven solutions that 
demonstrate the ability to accurately detect illegal transshipment at a rate of 90 percent or 
higher—all without exposure to law enforcement sensitive algorithms , CBP’s targeting models, 
and other sensitive data sets.  
 
 
3.0 PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE   
The contract base period of performance is intended to be 180 days and may contain up to two 
options.  
 
 
4.0 TYPE OF CONTRACT 
This award will establish a Non-FAR Contract through the DHS Commercial Solution Opening 
Pilot Program (CSOP). 
 
5.0  POINTS OF CONTACT 
Contracting Officer: Peter Giambone 
Email: PETER.A.GIAMBONE@CBP.DHS.GOV  
  Contract Specialist: Aristide Horugayve 
   Email: aristide.horugavye@cbp.dhs.gov

Based Period Deliverables 
Vendors shall submit illegal transshipment referral packages to CBP via email in accordance 
with the below performance milestone schedule. Referral packages must be actionable, meaning

they:  
• Must identify and trace to imports that are in transit and have not yet arrived in the U.S.; 
and,  
• Must contain substantive supporting evidence (minimum of five pages) with which to 
make high-confidence decisions about illegal transshipment risk.  
During the base period of performance, vendors will be asked to progressively demonstrate the 
scalability and accuracy of their solutions in 60-day increments. CBP will provide regularly 
scheduled feedback on whether referral packages:  
• Meet the above criteria for being considered actionable; and,  
• Lead to the prevention of high-risk imports being released into the U.S. and/or the 
identification of additional duties owed.  
CBP may at any time issue a stop work order to vendors who are unable to meet or exceed the 
scalability and accuracy thresholds for each 60-day increment.

7.1 Information Technology Security Compliance Requirements 
The contractor shall adhere to all DHS and CBP IT security policies and the basic requirements,

7.1.1 DHS Security Policy Compliance Requirements  
All hardware, software, and services provided under this CSOP contract must be compliant with

7.1.2 Basic Requirements

mandates DHS organizational elements, including contractors, follow guidelines outlined in the 
DHS MD 4300A, DHS Sensitive Systems Directive, Information Technology Security Program, 
Version 13, with attachments or any subsequent, replacement or revised publication. 
DHS Directive 4300A, Basic Requirements outlines the management, operational and

B.2  STATEMENT OF WORK

BACKGROUND

VA Long Beach Healthcare System (VALBHS) is requested services for the implementation of an RTLS/RFID Asset Tracking solution to support the needs of the healthcare system. The Department of Veterans Affairs’ Real Time Location System (RTLS) Program affects areas of clinical and administrative workflows by providing process improvement and automation efficiency. Significant potential uses and benefits of this technology throughout VA are numerous and include improved quality of patient care and satisfaction, reduced health care asset management costs, improved capacity/resource planning, improved employee, and patient safety, and improved general asset management and inventory. The RTLS solution is comprised of multiple applications impacting the logistics supply chain, inventory accountability, Biomedical Engineering, Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Sterile Processing, Dental and Surgical Services, Cardiac Catheterization Labs, and a host of other clinical departments. RTLS applications are deployed to more than 225 VA medical centers. Current installations use proprietary CenTrak and Infor Location-Based Intelligence (LBI) software for tagging, tracking, and integration into a single database.  CenTrak® proprietary active Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) hardware and software provide zonal, room-level, and within-room level accuracy regarding asset location, staff location, patient location, as well as environmental variables.

SCOPE

This Statement of Work establishes the requirements for Information Technology (IT) services, hardware, and software to implement CenTrak and Infor LBI-based Asset Tracking (AT) at the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. The Contractor shall provide RTLS hardware, software, documentation, and services to authorized users in VHA. Services include installation, end user acceptance testing, training, warranty services, engineering, and professional services.  The scope of this order shall include completion of implementation already started and expansion of current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System. 

GENERAL REQUIREMENT

The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, supplies, parts, batteries, software (needed for the general operation of the system), tools, equipment, testing equipment, travel, transportation expenses and other related costs to provide the completion of implementation of the current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System.

The contractor will provide the additional necessary hardware that will work with the currently installed RTLS equipment in all buildings within the main campus and update any necessary outdated hardware to enable functional asset tracking. Any parts before being replaced must be approved by Biomedical Engineering.

Throughout this process the vendor will ensure communication with Biomedical Engineering. This will include but not limited to working with Biomedical Engineering to schedule the installation, confirm installation is complete and have it inspected and provide proper documentation of installation in a timely manner when requested.

PERFORMANCE DETAILS

PERFORMANCE PERIOD

The period of performance will be 12 months from date of award.

This is for a full-service contract to include all necessary scheduled service during normal working hours five (5) days per week, Monday through Friday 7:30AM-4PM unless otherwise stated and approved ahead of time by Biomedical Engineering. This excludes any national holidays. There are eleven (11) Federal holidays set by law (USC Title 5 Section 6103) that VA follows. Under current definitions, five (5) are set by dates:

If any of the above falls on a Saturday, then Friday shall be observed as a holiday. Similarly, if one falls on a Sunday, then Monday shall be observed as a holiday. 

The other six (6) are set by a day of the week and month:

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

Facility implementation shall be limited to all buildings within the VA Long Beach Healthcare System main campus at 5901 E 7th St. Long Beach, CA 90822. Tasks under this PWS shall be performed at the VA facility listed above (primarily for hardware installation, tagging, and system administration). Project management tasks can be performed remotely.

TRAVEL

The Government anticipates travel under this effort to perform the tasks associate with the effort, as well as to attend program-related meetings and conferences throughout the Period of Performance. All travel costs shall be the responsibility of the vendor and included in the firm-fixed price line items. These costs will not be directly reimbursed by the Government.

CONTRACTOR DETAILS

5.1 CONTRACTOR QUALIFICATIONS

Personnel performing installation and other services for this requirement must be fully qualified Field Service Engineer (FSE) who has been trained on the specific equipment in accordance with the original manufacturer’s installation, maintenance, and repair procedures. The personnel shall be fully certified by the Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) Centrak and Infor LBI before performing work at VA Long Beach Healthcare System. “Fully certified” is defined as factory-trained or equivalent and experienced to work on the equipment assigned. The contractor shall provide a narrative that describes its specialized experience providing installation and maintenance on Centrak and Infor LBI hardware and software. 

5.2 CONTRACTOR BADGING

Compliance with VA Handbook 0735 – HSPD-12 Program

To comply with Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Handbook 0735, Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12) requirements, the Prime Contractor shall coordinate with the Point of Contact (POC) regarding all site visits to the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. Badges are mandatory for all contractors and subcontractors entering the facility.

The Prime Contractor is responsible for ensuring that all required information and documentation are submitted to the POC with sufficient lead time to allow for proper processing of badge requests. No contractor or subcontractor may begin work onsite without an approved badge, except under emergency conditions as outlined below.

Processing Time

Badge issuance may take up to 30 calendar days due to required background checks. The Prime Contractor must begin coordination with the POC immediately upon contract award to avoid repair, service, or project delays.

Onsite Visits for Badging

Contractors should anticipate at least two separate onsite visits:

One visit for fingerprinting.

One visit to pick up the issued badge.

Mandatory Training

All contractors and subcontractors must complete mandatory training assigned through the VA’s electronic Training Management System (TMS) before badges are issued. This training typically requires approximately two (2) hours to complete. Badge issuance and retention are contingent upon successful completion of this training.

5.3 CONTRACTOR ONSITE REPORTING PROCEDURES

The Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall wear their VA issued badge and identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site. 

For services to be performed outside normal working hours, the Contractor must obtain approval from the Biomedical Engineering POC prior to performing any after-hour work. If the afterhours request is approved, the Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook and pick up a visitor badge. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site.

Prior to leaving the facility, the Contractor shall communicate status of equipment to the Using Service and sign out of the logbook in the Biomedical Engineering Department

PROJECT MANAGEMENT

STAFFING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide a single Contract Implementation Manager, and one standby Backup Manager, as the sole points of contact to coordinate and manage all interactions, engagement, and services provided to the Government under this contract. The Contract Implementation Manager and Backup Managers shall be separate from the System Administrator.

REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall provide the POC with Monthly Progress Reports in electronic form in Microsoft (MS) Word, MS PowerPoint, or MS Project formats for this contract. The report shall include detailed instructions/explanations for each required data element to ensure that data is accurate and consistent. These reports shall reflect data as of the last day of the preceding month.

The Monthly Progress Reports shall cover all work completed during the reporting period and work planned for the subsequent reporting period.  The report should also identify any problems that arose, and a description of how the problems were resolved.  If problems have not been completely resolved, the Contractor shall provide an explanation including a plan and timeframe for resolving the issue.  The Contractor shall maintain communication with VA, so issues that arise are quickly identified and visible to both parties to prevent unnecessary escalation of outstanding issues. 

The Contractor shall hold a monthly status meeting with the POC and other technical Point of Contacts (POC), as specified by the primary POC, to discuss all items identified in the Monthly Progress Reports and other issues as identified by the primary POC.

Deliverable:

Monthly Progress Reports

TECHNICAL KICK OFF MEETING

A technical kickoff meeting shall be held within 10 days after contract award.  The Contractor shall coordinate the date, time, and location (can be virtual) with the Contracting Officer (CO), the VA lead(s), the Contract Specialist (CS), and the POC.  The Contractor shall provide a draft agenda to the CO and VA lead(s) at least five calendar days before the meeting.  Upon Government approval of the final agenda, the Contractor shall distribute to all meeting attendees.

During the kickoff-meeting, the Contractor shall present, for review and approval by the Government, the details of the intended approach, work plan, and project schedule for each effort via a Microsoft Office PowerPoint presentation.

The Contractor shall submit the final updated Final Technical Kickoff Meeting Presentation to the CO for review and signature within three calendar days after the meeting.  The Contractor shall also work with the CO, the Government’s designated notetaker, to prepare, finalize, and distribute CO-approved meeting minutes of the kickoff meeting to the CO, POC, and all attendees within three calendar days after the meeting.  The Contractor shall obtain concurrence from the CO on the content of the meeting minutes prior to distribution of the document and distribute the Technical Kickoff Meeting Minutes to all attendees.

Deliverable:

Final Technical Kickoff Meeting Presentation

Technical Kickoff Meeting Minutes

RTLS DESIGN

RTLS TIME STAMP

The Contractor shall ensure all applications synchronize with internal VA site time standard. The synchronization of time on this network is critical to every aspect of managing, securing, planning, and debugging as it identifies when an event occurred.

WIRELESS TECHNOLOGY

The Contractor shall utilize the existing Wi-Fi infrastructure at each facility, where possible, to meet standards of location accuracy or shall implement clinical grade location hardware where requirements cannot be met using the existing Wi-Fi. 

JUNIPER MIST

The Contractor shall work with the VA to align existing maps with Juniper Mist including, but not limited to Mist Map exports and Metadata. 

HARDWARE DESIGN DOCUMENT

PRELIMINARY HARDWARE DESIGN DOCUMENT

The Contractor shall ensure there is a valid and updated Hardware Deployment Design Document (HDDD) for the facility throughout the implementation period. The Contractor shall review the existing HDDD and provide a preliminary HDDD with its proposal.  The preliminary HDDD shall indicate the planned design for asset tracking at VA Long Beach Healthcare System.

The preliminary design to include the proposed quantity and location of supplemental Wi-Fi infrastructure to include hardware locations and type, as well as a survey of network closets, the availability/need of closets, POE switches for providing power to hardware, existing and additional hardware including replacement of existing hardware, and wiring plan for hardware to achieve the goals of the RTLS applications and room coverage requirements. 

Changes, corrections and/or updates to the VA-provided maps and Engineering Space Files as noted during the Contractor’s site assessment.

1. Contracting Activity: Departm ent of Veterans Affairs (VA)
