DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY 
NAVAL INFORMATION WARFARE CENTER PACIFIC 
53560 HULL STREET 
SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA 92152-5001 
J&A No. 26-225 
 
JUSTIFICATION AND APPROVAL 
 FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION 
 
1. Contracting Activity.  
 
Department of the Navy, Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific (NIWC PAC). 
 
2. Description of the Action Being Approved.  
 
The proposed action is to increase the ceiling for contract N00039-19-D-0006 awarded to 
Lockheed Martin (LM) by $30,000,000 from $104,242,344 to $134,242,344 in support of 
Radiant Mercury (RADMERC). The cost-plus-fixed-fee (CPFF), Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite 
Quantity (IDIQ) contract was awarded on a sole source basis on 01 September 2019 with a five-
year base period and one five-year option period. Based on the higher than expected burn rate, 
the option period was exercised on 27 October 2021, roughly three years earlier than initially 
planned. While the current contract’s ordering period ends on 30 September 2029, the remaining 
contract ceiling has been allocated and is expected to be obligated by Third Quarter, Fiscal Year 
2026. The ceiling increase is necessary to avoid a gap in services critical to the Department of 
War (DoW).  
 
3. Description of Supplies/Services.  
 
The ceiling increase to contract N00039-19-D-0006 will provide continued support for the 
Department of the Navy and other Agencies’ RADMERC operations  
The current contract provides for 
installation, program management, maintenance, modernization, and sustainment of RADMERC 
systems and will provide system security authorization support, and logistics and training 
services. The work scope also includes sustainment of existing  
 
 
 
 
Due to a software baseline compromise identified around March 2022, the National Cross 
Domain Strategy and Management office and NCDSMO and DoW Chief Information Office 
(CIO) directed the CDS developer, Lockheed Martin (LM), to ramp up efforts to deliver a new 
version. This directive,  
 have resulted in an increase in demand on 
current requirements, unplanned costs, and a higher demand for RADMERC services. To 
support the substantial unanticipated demand on the current contract’s requirements, a ceiling 
increase of $12,028,735 was awarded on 13 February 2025, to avoid a gap in capability while the 
follow-on contract was pending.  


 
 
 
 
   
 
Despite the February 2025 ceiling increase, the ceiling on N00039-19-D-0006 contract was 
nearly exhausted within seven (7) months, as NIWC Pacific  
Customers not being prepared, changing/increasing their 
RADMERC order allocation, and updating their baseline, also resulted in a significant increase 
in changes to the RADMERC schedule, which further caused LM to bid for more support hours.   
 
Contractually, multiple customers (new and existing), have asked for additional support with the 
current baseline, from upgrading existing systems, to requiring additional CDS installations. 
Since the transition of the RADMERC contract to NIWC Pacific, seventy-six (76) task orders 
have been awarded and the customer base has grown from  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
4. Identification of Statutory Authority:  
 
The statutory authority is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition 
Regulation (FAR) Subpart 6.302-1: Only one responsible source and no other supplies or 
services will satisfy agency requirements. 
 
5. Rationale Justifying Use of Cited Statutory Authority. 
 
 


 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 




 
6. Description of Efforts Made to Solicit Offers from as Many Offerors as Practicable.   
 
The proposed contract requirement will be synopsized on SAM.gov and any responses received 
will be considered prior to award. No additional market research was conducted because it is not 
practical, for the reasons discussed in paragraph 5 above, for any company other than LM to 
provide the required supplies and services. The USG did synopsize the previous procurement on 
the FEDBIZOPS via the NIWC PAC E-Commerce Central website on 03 December 2018. This 
announcement was posted for fifteen (15) days and resulted in only one question requesting the 
name of the incumbent contractor.  No other questions were received before the end date of 18 
December 2018. To date, no other potential sources have expressed interest in this requirement.  
 
7. Determination of Fair and Reasonable Cost.   
 
The Contracting Officer has determined that the anticipated cost to the Government for the 
supplies/services covered by this J&A will be fair and reasonable.   
 
8. Actions to Remove Barriers to Future Competition. 
 
Market research will be conducted for future contract requirements of this nature to determine 
the most advantageous method of fulfilling the Government’s need. As part of any future market 
research, the Government will monitor the NSA certification activity to determine if any other 
CDS can meet the Navy’s CDS certification requirements. 
 
The Government has established a CDS Working Group specifically to identify a viable long-
term solution that meets the requirements of all customers. The future solution is anticipated to 
be implemented incrementally over the next ten (10) years due to the complexity of the 
capability and the cost and time it takes to obtain NSA accreditation.

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) 
 
MADE IN AMERICA MARKET RESEARCH HUB 
 
THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) NOTICE ONLY.  THIS IS NOT A 
REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS (RFP). NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. 
1. AUTHORITY 
This initiative supports statutor y domestic preference requiremen ts including the Buy American 
Act (41 U.S.C. § § 8301-8305) and E.O. 14005 Ensuring the Future is Made in All of America by 
All of America’s Workers. 
The objective is to strengthen co mpliance, transparency, and anal ytic capability across Federal 
procurement and Federal financial assistance programs. 
2. DESCRIPTION 
The Office of Management and Budget’s Made in America Office (MIAO) is exploring options to 
establish a centralized, scalable  capability to support domestic sourcing de terminations across 
Federal procurement and Federal financial assistance programs.  
Federal agency procurement officials and recipients of Federal financial assistance grants perform 
market research for two (2) main  reasons: (a) to identify a domestically manufactured product in 
compliance with Made in America laws, or (b) to verify that a domestic product is not available to 
justify a waiver from Made in America laws. Agencies and grantees currently utilize a wide range 
of market research methods, such as time-co nsuming phone calls to manufacturers, costly 
commercial market research platform licenses, and broad web searches that often result in out-of-
date or incomplete results.  
There is a clear need to provide Federal procurem ent officers and grantees a single, trusted, and 
continuously updated data source to help identify  domestic products effici ently and effectively. 
This effort seeks to improve th e consistency, defensib ility and efficiency of market research 
processes.  
3. VISION  
Federal procurement officials and grant recipients should be able to: 
 Reduce duplicative and burdensome market research 
 Quickly and accurately identify domestic manufacturers by product category 
As a result, desired outcomes are: 
 Increased Federal spending on American rather than foreign products 
 Increased Federal agency compliance with Made in America laws  

The long-term vision is to integrate this capa bility into the broader Federal acquisition and 
financial assistance ecosystem. 
4. OBJECTIVE 
The desired solution is a standardized, continuou sly updated dataset and an alytic capability that 
enables agencies to: 
a) Identify domestic manufacturers and suppliers by category; 
b) Support waiver review determinations with traceable documentation; and 
c) Reduce compliance burden while increasing the accuracy and defensibility of domestic 
sourcing determinations. 
d) The objective is not merely data  aggregation, but to create sust ainable infrastructure that 
improves compliance government-wide. 
A core objective of this effort is to reduce duplicative market research and compliance burden 
across agencies while improving consistency of domestic sourcing determinations.  
5. SCOPE OF EFFORT 
The anticipated scope of effort is laid out below. These phases are subject to change based on the 
path forward for development as a result of this RFI. 
Phase 1: Data Identification and Gathering. Identify and gather structured and unstructured market 
data sources from outside the Federal government. Integrate these with structured and unstructured 
data from within the Federal government (i.e., historical procurement, agency-submitted waivers) 
into a central data lake. 
Phase 2: Data Governance and Contextualiza tion. Develop governance po licies to regulate and 
manage data. Apply ontologies to accurately characterize data relationships between suppliers and 
across specific statutory domestic content requirements. 
Phase 3: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Layer. Utilize generative and/or agentic AI to easily interface 
between data and users. 
Phase 4: Reporting and Analytics. Extract insights from market research data, such as a report that 
identifies American-made products with probabili ties and suggestions for verification. Ability to 
integrate and scale advanced analytics capabilities in future phases. 
Any potential solution should be modular and scalable, capable of expansion across procurement 
and financial assistance contexts as policy requirements evolve.  
6. SYSTEM INTEROPERABILITY 

Solutions of interest should be capable of integration with existing Federal procurement and grants 
systems, including but  not limited to the Federal Pr ocurement Data System (FPDS), 
www.SAM.gov, and agency contract writing or grants management systems. 
Application Programming Interface (API) based or structured data exchange capabilities are 
strongly preferred to enable scalability and long-term sustainability.  
7. DATA GOVERNANCE AND SECURITY 
Solutions should enable: 
a) Traceability and auditability sufficient to s upport waiver review and Inspector General 
oversight; 
b) Clear documentation of data sources and validation methodologies; 
c) Secure handling of confidential, proprietary, or national security-sensitive information; and 
d) Mechanisms for continuous updating to reflect evolving manufacturing landscapes. 
Respondents are encouraged to describe proposed data ownership structures, licensing terms, and 
any restrictions on Government use of aggregated data. 
8. USER STORIES 
Illustrative use cases include:  
a) An agency procurement official can qui ckly and easily identify a domestically 
manufactured product, or verify that no domestic suppliers exist. 
b) A state or local recipient of Federal grant funding can quickly and easily identify a 
domestically manufactured product, or verify that no domestic suppliers exist. 
c) A MIAO staff member can quickly and easily verify an agency’s market research submitted 
through a waiver. 
 
9.  QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY 
MIAO seeks input on the following: 
Technology Architecture 
 What technical approaches are recommended for aggregating and maintaining large, 
disparate manufacturing datasets? 
 What methodologies are most effective for ensuri ng data quality, verification, and 
validation? 
 What level of effort and resources would be required to achieve these technical solutions? 
Data Sources 
 What commercially available data sources could enhance existing Federal data? 
 How should structured and unstructured data be harmonized? 

Security 
 In addition to government security requi rements, what additional safeguards are 
recommended for protecting business confidential or sensitive data? 
Updates and Sustainability 
 What approaches ensure continuous updating and scalability over time, given the rapidly-
evolving nature of manufacturing data? 
Licensing and Access 
 What licensing models are typical for soluti ons of this nature within the Federal 
Government or in the private sector? 
 
10. CONSIDERATIONS 
To the extent possible, the MIAO is seeking to leverage existing technology solutions that could 
be leveraged by the Federal government rather than developing a custom solution. 
The success of any solution will depend on the quality, relevance, and sustainability of underlying 
data sources, as well as the ability to integrate with existing Federal systems. 
This initiative is not intended to duplicate, replace, or conflict with existing Federal procurement, 
grants management, or market re search platforms. Rather, it is intended to complement existing 
systems by enhancing visibility  into domestic manufacturing cap acity and supply chain data 
relevant to statutory Made in America requirements.  
The Government has not made a determination regarding the appr opriate technical approach or 
acquisition strategy, if any. Responses will inform future planning decisions. 
The Government welcomes respons es from interested parties to include small businesses and 
innovative commercial providers with relevant capabilities.  
11. RESPONSES 
Interested parties are directed to respond to this RFI with a written response. Response shall be in 
Microsoft Word for Office or compatible format and shall not exceed 10 pages. A page is defined 
as each face of an 8½”  x 11” sheet with information contai ned within a one-inch margin on all 
sides. Font type shall be Times Roman 12 point. Responses are due no later than 11:00 pm ET on 
Wednesday, April 01, 2026  and should be sent via email to Salman.Shahid@oa.eop.gov (cc: 
Franky.M.Awuvey@oa.eop.gov)  with “Response to MIA Market Research Hub RFI” in the subject 
line. 
 
12. QUESTIONS: 

Questions regarding this announcement shall be submitted in writing by e-mail to 
Salman.Shahid@oa.eop.gov (cc: Franky.M.Awuvey@oa.eop.gov) with “Questions to MIA 
Market Research Hub RFI” in the subject line.  Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. Answers 
to questions will be posted to www.SAM.gov. The Government does not guarantee that questions 
received after March 18, 2026 at 11:00pm ET will be answered. The Government will not 
reimburse companies for any costs associated with the submissions of their responses. 
 
13. EVAULATION OF RESPONSES 
Responses will be reviewed for relevance, scalability, data quality methodology, security posture, 
and demonstrated experience supporting large-scale data aggregation efforts. After evaluation of 
responses, MIAO may conduct a virtual industry engagement session. If scheduled, details will be 
posted via SAM.gov and/or shared with respondents. 
14. DISCLAIMER 
This RFI is issued solely for Market Resear ch purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. This 
notice does not constitute a solicitation and does not commit the Fe deral Government to contract 
for any supplies or services. Responses are voluntary, will not be formally evaluated and will be 
used for planning purposes only.  
Participation in this RFI does not confer any competitive advantage in any future potential 
procurement.  
 
All information contained in the RFI is preliminary as well as subject to modification and is in no 
way binding on the Government. FAR clause 52. 215-3, “Request for Information or Solicitation 
for Planning Purposes”, is incorporated by reference in this RFI. The Government does not intend 
to pay for information received in response to this RFI. Responders to this invitation are solely 
responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. This RFI will be the basis for 
collecting information on capabilities available. This RFI is issued solely for information and 
planning purposes. Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, must be clearly marked on all 
materials. All information received in this RFI that is marked “Proprie tary” will be handled 
accordingly.  Please be advised that all submissions become Government property and will not be 
returned nor will receipt be c onfirmed. In accordance with FAR 15.201(e), responses to this RFI 
are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract.

The Office of Management and Budget’s Made in America Office (MIAO) is exploring options to 
establish a centralized, scalable capability to support domestic so urcing determinations across 
Federal procurement and Federal financial assistance programs.  
Federal agency procurement officials and recipients of Federal financial assistance grants perform 
market research for two (2) main reasons: (a) to identify a domestically manufactured product in 
compliance with Made in America laws, or (b) to verify that a domestic product is not available to 
justify a waiver from Made in America laws. Agencies and grantees currently utilize a wide range 
of market research methods, such as time- consuming phone calls to manufacturers, costly 
commercial market research platform licenses, and broad web searches that often result in out-of-
date or incomplete results.  
There is a clear need to provide Federal procuremen t officers and grantees a single, trusted, and 
continuously updated data source to help identify domestic products efficiently and effectively. 
This effort seeks to improve the consistency, defensibility and efficiency of market research 
processes.  
3. VISION  
Federal procurement officials and grant recipients should be able to: 
• Reduce duplicative and burdensome market research 
• Quickly and accurately identify domestic manufacturers by product category 
As a result, desired outcomes are: 
• Increased Federal spending on American rather than foreign products 
• Increased Federal agency compliance with Made in America laws  

The long- term vision is to integrate this capability into the broader Federal acquisition and 
financial assistance ecosystem. 
4. OBJECTIVE 
The desired solution is a standardized, continuously updated dataset and analytic capability that 
enables agencies to: 
a) Identify domestic manufacturers and suppliers by category; 
b) Support waiver review determinations with traceable documentation; and 
c) Reduce compliance burden while increasing the accuracy and defensibility of domestic 
sourcing determinations. 
d) The objective is not merely data aggregation, but to create sustainable infrastructure that 
improves compliance government-wide. 
A core objective of this effort is to reduce duplicative market research and compliance burden 
across agencies while improving consistency of domestic sourcing determinations.  
5. SCOPE OF EFFORT 
The anticipated scope of effort is laid out below. These phases are subject to change based on the 
path forward for development as a result of this RFI. 
Phase 1: Data Identification and Gathering. Identify and gather structured and unstructured market 
data sources from outside the Federal government. Integrate these with structured and unstructured 
data from within the Federal government (i.e., historical procurement, agency-submitted waivers) 
into a central data lake. 
Phase 2: Data Governance and Conte x tualization. Develop governance policies to regulate and 
manage data. Apply ontologies to accurately characterize data relationships between suppliers and 
across specific statutory domestic content requirements. 
Phase 3: Artifi cial Intelligence (AI) Layer. Utilize generative and/or agentic AI to easily interface 
between data and users. 
Phase 4: R eporting and Analytics . Extract insights from market research data, such as a report that 
identifies American-made products

1.0  PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS 
 
The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), 
Office of Information Security (OIS) requires a comprehensive Zero Trust Data 
Monitoring and Sensing - Structured Data Protection solution that provides a data 
protection solution to address on-premises structured data, and structured data in the 
VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) Cloud environments to include- Amazon Web Services 
(AWS) and Azure. Data Monitoring and Sensing is essential for enhancing cybersecurity 
measures across VA’s enterprise environments, supporting VA's Zero Trust Architecture 
Strategy in line with Executive Order 14028, Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity.  The 
Zero Trust Data Monitoring and Sensing - Structured Data Protection solution shall 
provide robust Data Loss Prevention (DLP) capabilities, including automated 
enforcement of policies to prevent unauthorized access, transfer, or exfiltration of 
sensitive structured data. In addition, the solution must support automated and 
persistent data labeling, ensuring labels are applied consistently to structured data 
assets and integrated with DLP policies for dynamic access control and compliance. 
 
DLP and labeling integration should align with VA’s Zero Trust principles and 
classification standards, enabling continuous verification, least privilege access, and 
adaptive policy enforcement across on-premises and cloud environments 
 
This solution shall be a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) product or an equivalent 
turnkey implementation that delivers end-to-end security capabilities, including 
management, threat detection, runtime policy enforcement, support, and virtual 
patching.

36C26226Q0506 Question and Answers

1) Can you provide photographs of the installation locations?

ANSWER: We can mark the locations on the plan drawing. 

2) Can you describe the types of walls the screens will be mounted to? I.E. CMU, drywall with metal studs, drywall with wood studs, brick?

ANSWER: Mostly dry walls and some locations with tiled walls. 

3) Will the screens be mounted in Landscape or Portrait format?

ANSWER:  The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess and provide professional recommendations to determine the optimal orientation. As noted in the Statement of Work (SOW), the design must comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requirements. 

4) You mention a range for screen size of 47"-65". Will you require different sized screens for different locations? Should screen size be standardized for all 16 installation locations?

ANSWER: The VA San Diego Healthcare System will rely on the contractors' expertise to assess the space and provide professional recommendation to help the facility make an informed decision. 65” are most likely going near the main entrances and 47” for other locations.

5) Is there any branding, color pallet, or logo placement that should be incorporated into the design of the screens? 

ANSWER: Yes. Similar navy blue color and logo as seen on the main VA website: https://www.va.gov/ shall be used as a starting point for design. 

The contractor shall have design discussion sessions with VASD for interface design. VASD will be relying on the contractor's design expertise.

RFI VA-26-00059598 – Questions for Vendor Responses 
The Department of Veterans AƯairs (VA), Veterans Canteen Service (VCS), requests vendor 
feedback regarding the modernization and migration of the Oracle Retail Merchandising 
(RMS) and Store Inventory Management (SIM) platforms to Oracle Retail Merchandising 
Foundation Cloud Service (MFCS) and Store Inventory and Operations Cloud Service 
(SIOCS). 
Please provide concise responses to the following critical questions aligned with Section 5 
of the Performance Work Statement (PWS). 
1. Pricing & SaaS Subscriptions 
1. Subscription Bill of Materials (BOM):   
Provide a line-item, tabular price list for all proposed Oracle Retail SaaS 
subscriptions (MFCS, SIOCS, RPCS, ReIM, Allocation, RICS). For each product, 
include the unit of measure (tenant, user, store, message volume, environment), 
quantities, and pricing for the 12-month base period and each of the four 
12-month option years. Identify any environment-speciﬁc premiums (Dev, Test, 
Prod), overage charges, and price protections.   
Please present the BOM in the following table format: Product, UOM, Quantity 
(Base & Option Years), Unit Price, Extended Price, Overage. 
2. What’s Included vs. Customer Managed:   
Using Oracle’s SaaS shared responsibility model, clearly delineate which 
services are covered by Oracle SLAs versus contractor managed tenant 
responsibilities (e.g., integrations, workﬂows, KPI refreshes, IAM, regression 
testing). Map your delineation to the PWS SLA assignments (Incident Response, 
Integrations, Batch/Orchestration, Reporting/KPIs, IAM). 
3. Assumptions & Dependencies AƯecting Price:   
List any pricing assumptions (e.g. store count, message volume, batch windows, 
mobile devices/peripherals, training seats, third party connectors) and 
dependencies on Oracle environment provisioning & release cycles. State any 
price change triggers.  
4. Discounts & True Up:   
Describe tiered or enterprise discounts, true up/true down mechanisms for 
user/store counts, and how you handle mid-term adds (e.g., new canteens). 
2. Program Approach & Implementation Strategy 

1. Implementation methodology:  
Describe your recommended implementation approach (e.g., Agile, iterative, 
hybrid). How do you manage scope, risks, dependencies, and schedule for SaaS 
modernization programs of similar size and complexity?  
2. Migration feasibility:  
Based on your experience, what major risks or blockers do you anticipate when 
migrating from RMS v13/SIM to MFCS/SIOCS, and how do you mitigate them? 
3. Timeline:  
How long does your assessment phase typically take for comparable 
MFCS/SIOCS migrations? 
3. Assessment, Fit/Gap & Solution Design 
1. Assessment approach:  
Describe your approach to conducting a SaaS migration assessment, including 
discovery of current state integrations, customizations, data structures, and 
store workﬂows.  
2. Fit/Gap minimization:  
How do you ensure the solution maximizes use of standard Oracle cloud 
capabilities and reduces or eliminates the need for extensions? 
4. Data Migration & Data Quality 
1. Migration tools and methods:  
Provide your methodology for conducting data proﬁling, cleansing, 
transformation, and migration into MFCS/SIOCS.  
2. Mock conversions:  
How many mock conversions do you recommend, and what criteria do you use 
to determine readiness for cutover? 
3. Limitations:  
What limitations should VCS expect when migrating legacy RMS/SIM reports to 
MFCS/SIOCS? 
5. Integrations & Technical Architecture 
1. Integration experience:  

Summarize your experience integrating MFCS/SIOCS with ERP , POS, EDI, data 
warehouse, and reporting systems. Identify any recommended redesign 
considerations for VCS’ existing interfaces.  
2. Standards & tools: 
Identify which Oracle integration technologies (e.g., BDI, RIB-Cloud, OIC) you 
typically use for Retail SaaS implementations and why. 
3. Existing tool integration:   
Identify any issues you Forsee with integrating MFCS/SIOCS with existing VCS 
systems.  How do you evaluate whether existing integrations must be rebuilt, 
redesigned, or retired? 
6. Conﬁguration & Store Operations 
1. MFCS/SIOCS conﬁguration:  
Describe your approach to conﬁguring roles, hierarchies, store workﬂows, and 
SIOCS mobile operations.  
2. Environment strategy:  
How do you ensure conﬁguration consistency and traceability across 
Development, Test, and Production environments? 
7. Reporting & Custom-Built Components 
1. Reporting modernization:  
Provide your recommended approach for modernizing or replacing existing 
custom reports and legacy OBIEE/Analytics artifacts within the Oracle Retail 
Cloud ecosystem. 
2. Limitations:

4. Authority for Contracting Without Competition Over $350,000

For this requirement up to $350,000, using simplified acquisition procedures under FAR part 13, the basis for contracting without 
providing for full and open competition is:  
Only one responsible source is reasonably available to meet Library requirements. 41 U.S.C. § 6101(b); FAR 13.106-1.  
 Product or service is reasonably available from only one source.

The Product is listed the Library of Congress Enterprise Architecture Repository (LCEAR) database (Attach applicable  
IT Standard Data Sheet)
 
5. Rationale for Contracting Without Competition 
We are authorized to limit competition on the basis of the citation in section 4 because:  
 
The Library of Congress’s BIBFRAME Linked Data System (BFLDS) previously operated in tandem with Voyager and, as of 
June 2025, now interfaces with FOLIO as the Library’s system of record. BFLDS consists of the BIBFRAME database 
(BFDB), Linked Data Service (LDS ID), and the Marva editor, with LDS ID and BFDB built on the MarkLogic platform, 
which incorporates triplestore functionality. BFLDS and FOLIO were developed using distinct and not fully compatible 
architectures, requiring specialized middleware to enable efficient interoperability. 
Under contract LCLGD25C0002, IndexData conducted a comprehensive analysis, working directly with the original 
FOLIO developers, of how BFLDS and FOLIO can be integrated. This effort produced detailed, implementation-ready 
recommendations for middleware design, workflow optimization, and data exchange. 
 
IndexData is uniquely qualified to perform this work due to its direct role in both the design and development of FOLIO 
and the development of core components of BFLDS. As a result, IndexData possesses institutional and technical 
knowledge of system architecture, design decisions, and integration constraints that is not documented to a level 
sufficient for transfer to another contractor without additional time and cost. 
 
Awarding this requirement to another contractor would require the new contractor to independently reconstruct 
IndexData’s prior analysis, reverse-engineer design decisions across both systems, and develop equivalent expertise. 
This would result in significant duplication of effort, increased cost to the Government, and schedule delays. 
 
Accordingly, IndexData is the only responsible source capable of meeting the Library’s requirement within the required 
timeframe, without duplication of costs. 
6. Actions to Overcome Barriers to Competition Before Subsequent Contract Is Required  
To increase competition, we will: continue to survey the environment for possible expertise.

the basis for this justification are accurate and complete.

Upton, NY 11973-5000

for the U.S. Department of Energy  
 
 
STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Workday Human Capital Management System 
Subscription Renewal 
March 31, 2026 
 
 
    
 
   
    
    
    
    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
2 
 
1. INTRODUCTION 
 
Brookhaven Science Associates (BSA) is the management and operating contractor for the U.S. 
Department of Energy (DOE) at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL). BNL is a 
multidisciplinary research institution supporting advanced scientific discovery and operational 
excellence. 
 
As part of its digital modernization strategy, BSA transitioned from a legacy, internally 
developed Human Capital Management System (HCMS) to Workday Human Capital 
Management (Workday HCM), a cloud-based Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platform. Workday 
HCM has served as BSA’s enterprise system of record since its production deployment on 
September 23, 2023. 
 
This SOW defines the scope, requirements, and expectations for the renewal and potential 
expansion of Workday HCM services to ensure continuity of operations, system optimization, 
and scalability to meet evolving organizational needs. 
 
2. SCOPE 
2.1 Current Functional Modules in Use 
Workday HCM currently supports approximately 3,000 employees and includes the following functional 
areas: 
• Absence Management 
• Advanced Compensation 
• Benefits Administration 
• Compensation Management 
• Core Human Capital Management 
• Learning Management 
• Onboarding 
• Payroll (U.S.) 
• Recruiting 
• Talent Management 
• Time Tracking 
These modules support the full employee lifecycle, including recruitment, onboarding, development, 
compensation, time reporting, and separation. 
2.2 Subscription Renewal Requirements 
The Contractor shall provide: 

 
3 
 
• Continued subscription access to all currently licensed Workday HCM modules 
• System availability in accordance with Workday’s Service Level Agreements (SLAs) 
• Ongoing system updates, patches, and enhancements 
• Data hosting, backup, and disaster recovery services 
• Security controls compliant with federal and DOE requirements 
2.3 Optional Module Expansion 
BSA reserves the right to expand functionality through additional Workday modules, including but not 
limited to: 
• Workday Extend (application development platform) 
• Workday Help (case management and employee support) 
• Workday Journeys (employee experience workflows) 
• Workforce Planning (strategic workforce modeling and forecasting) 
• Workday Success Plans (WSP) Accelerate Plus (Enhanced technical support) 
Implementation of additional modules may be executed under this SOW. 
2.4 Tenant and Environment Requirements 
BSA requires multiple Workday tenants to support development, testing, and production operations. 
Current and future needs include: 
• Existing Production Tenant (e.g., BNL5) 
• Additional Implementation Tenants (minimum of two) 
• Sandbox and testing environments as required 
The Contractor shall ensure proper provisioning, maintenance, and synchronization of these 
environments. 
3. DELIVERABLES 
The Contractor shall deliver continuous access to the Workday HCM platform along with all associated 
services required to maintain system functionality and performance. This includes ensuring system 
availability in accordance with SLAs, providing regular system updates and release management, and 
maintaining documentation related to system changes and enhancements. 
The Contractor shall also provide support services for incident resolution and service requests, ensuring 
that issues are addressed in a timely and effective manner to minimize disruption to BSA operations. 
4. PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS (SLAs) 
The Workday HCM system must meet defined performance and availability standards to support 
mission-critical operations at BNL. The Contractor shall ensure system uptime of no less than 99.7 
percent, excluding scheduled maintenance windows. 

 
4 
 
In addition, the Contractor shall provide timely responses to incidents based on severity levels, maintain 
acceptable system response times consistent with industry SaaS benchmarks, and ensure that data 
backup and recovery processes meet established standards for reliability and continuity of operations. 
5. SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE 
The Contractor shall implement and maintain security controls consistent with federal and DOE 
requirements. All data must be encrypted both at rest and in transit, and access to the system must be 
governed through role-based access controls. 
The system must support audit logging and monitoring to ensure accountability and traceability of 
system activities. 
BSA retains full ownership of all data within the Workday system. The Contractor shall not access, use, 
or disclose BSA data except as required to perform services under this scope. 
6. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
The Contractor is responsible for delivering and supporting the Workday SaaS platform, including 
coordination of infrastructure, system availability, security, and ongoing updates in alignment with 
Workday’s standards and services. The Contractor shall also provide customer support services, 
including defined escalation procedures for critical issues. 
BSA is responsible for system configuration, business process management, user access administration, 
and oversight of integrations with other enterprise systems.  
7. GOVERNANCE AND SUPPORT 
The Contractor shall provide a structured support model that includes defined service tiers, escalation 
paths, and communication protocols. Regular communication regarding system updates, releases, and 
potential impacts shall be provided to BSA. 
The Contractor shall work collaboratively with BSA to ensure alignment on system changes, issue 
resolution, and continuous improvement efforts.

Request for Information (RFI) No.: 475671 
Title: Workday Human Capital Management (HCM) 
Subscription Renewal  
Brookhaven Science Associates, LLC (BSA), operator of Brookhaven National Laboratory 
(BNL) under contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), is conducting market research 
to identify qualified organizations authorized to provide Workday Human Capital Management 
(HCM) subscription services. 
This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for market research purposes only and does not 
constitute a solicitation (RFP/RFQ). BSA is not obligated to issue a solicitation or make an 
award, nor will BSA reimburse any costs associated with responding. 
Objective 
The purpose of this RFI is to identify organizations that are: 
• Authorized Workday partners and/or resellers 
• Value-Added Resellers (VARs) capable of providing Workday HCM subscription 
licensing and related services 
Requested Information

1. Identification of the agency and the contracting activity, and specific identification of the
document as a 'Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity.
This justification was prepared in accordance with FAR 16.505 by the Federal Communications
Commission {FCC), Headquarters {HQ), Office of the Managing Director {OMD), Enterprise
Acquisition Center {EAC) located at 45 L Street NE, Washington, DC 20554. The managing
program is the Public Safety and Homeland Security Bureau {PSHSB).
2. Nature and/or description of the action being approved.
To effectively manage risks to the U.S. communications sector and all dependent critical
infrastructure sectors and resources, the FCC requires an integrated solution enabling FCC staff
to analyze data from disparate sources and identify entities, equipment, and services that are
potentially owned, controlled, or influenced by foreign adversarial countries.
The Secure and Trusted Communications Networks Act of 2021 directed the Federal 
Communications Commission {FCC) to publish and update on its website a list of any 
communications equipment or service that poses an unacceptable risk to the national security 
of the United States or the security and safety of United States persons. These determinations 
are made by executive branch interagency bodies with appropriate national security expertise, 
including the Federal Acquisition Security Council {FASC); by the Department of Commerce 
pursuant to Executive Order No. 13873; by an appropriate national security agency; or for any 
communications equipment or services defined as covered telecommunications equipment or 
services under section 889{f){3) of the John S. McCain National Defense Authorization Act of 
2019. Updating this list-particularly identifying subsidiaries and affiliates of entities on the 
covered list-requires the ability to access and analyze official company filings and other public 
data available across hundreds of thousands of sources in multiple formats. 
Further, PSHSB is responsible for responding to requests for information from the determining 
bodies mentioned in the STCNA, the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States 
{CFIUS), and the Committee for the Assessment of Foreign Participation in the U.S. 
Telecommunications Services Sector {Team Telecom) which may solicit FCC feedback on 
investigations and cases which assess the national security risks of certain communications 
companies, equipment, and services. These requests for support require a rapid response in 
order to meet statutory deadlines. For these purposes, the FCC is in need of one or more 
solutions enabling the expedited analysis of aggregated data from multiple data streams and 
sources. Data sources would provide insights into company ownership; investment and investor 
stakeholders and percentages; consumers; tariff or sanction data. 

3. A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency's needs (i ncluding the
estimated value).
Product: Quantifind GraphyteSearch Licenses
Description: Quantifind is a readily-available, Artificial Intelligence-enabled research database
that persistently inventories publicly available information relating to business ownership,
investment, trade, tariff, sanction data, and media information relating to specific businesses,
people, research entities, and academic institutions. Quantifind automatically scans across a
broad range of public and online data including on line news sources, company registration data,
and leaks databases; seeds queries with minimally available information as a name or email
address to cultivate analyses leading to the discovery of supply chain risk factors on transaction
counterparties and other non-customers; assesses risk relationships by revealing the entities
related to a known individual or business that are surfaced from across the external data and
rank-ordered for risk and relevancy; verification of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership {UBO) when
risk exposure is high; automated report generation; and the ability to integrate FCC-specific data
and enable case management. Further, Quantifind offers the ability to integrate external data
sources through Application Programmable Interface {API) management.

Selected Exception: FAR 16.505{b){2){i){B) - Only one brand name is capable of providing the
supplies or services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services
ordered are unique or highly specialized.
Brand Name Justification: This acquisition is for Quantifind GraphyteSearch, a brand name 
product. Market research confirmed that no other solution meets FCC's technical requirements 
for integrated supply chain risk analysis, API integration, and automated risk scoring at the 
required quality and price point.

to industry, academia and nations for their input to NATO’s requirement for AFSC eTacC. 
 
Industry, academia and nations wishing to respond to this RFI should read this document

All requests for clarifications, questions and responses to this RFI must be sent

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
HQ Supreme Allied Commander Transformation 
RFI-ACT-SACT-04-2026

1. INTRODUCTION 
Headquarters Supreme Allied Commander Transformation (HQ SACT) is issuing this 
Request for Information (RFI) to engage with industry to conduct a current state of abilities 
for commercial industry to provide solutions to NATO capability requirements. The intention 
is to evaluate what could be immediately available, the art-of-the-possible, and current 
state-of-the-art capabilities with respect to eTacC capability, products, services, 
technologies, and methodologies. 
 
This Request for Information (RFI) does not constitute a commitment to issue a future 
request for proposal (RFP). The purpose of this request is to involve industry through 
collaboration, in an examination of future capabilities and an analysis of potential 
alternatives related to the implementation of the eTacC Capability Program Plan (CPP). 
 
Further, respondents are advised that HQ SACT will not pay for any information or 
administrative costs incurred in responding to this RFI. The costs for responding to this RFI 
shall be borne solely by the responding party. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude 
participation in any subsequent RFP if issued in the future. All information shared with ACT 
might be shared with contracted third parties to support the capability development process 
as needed. Provision of data, or lack of, will not prejudice any respondent if there is a 
competitive bidding process later as part of NATO Common-Funded Capability 
Development. 
2. BACKGROUND 
2.1. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is exploring communication, networking, and data 
transformation solutions that will enable increased connectivity at the tactical edge across 
a multitude of legacy and emergent bearers, waveforms, and protocols.   
2.2. NATO's Enhanced Tactical Connectivity (eTacC) capability is envisioned to be a node 
which acts as a relay, gateway, and translator enabling the realization of Multi-Domain 
Operations through the bridging of heterogenous tactical networks based on operational 
demands. 
 
This is not a formal request for submissions as part of a procurement; but rather a 
general request intended to determine whether any possible solutions exist that 
should be included in one or many alternatives during the development. 
 
3. PROJECT DESCRIPTION 
3.1. Vision 
3.1.1. The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is exploring communication, networking, 
and data transformation solutions that will enable increased connectivity at the 
tactical edge across a multitude of legacy and emergent bearers, waveforms, 
and protocols.  NATO's Enhanced Tactical Connectivity (eTacC) capability is 
envisioned to be a node which acts as a relay, gateway, and translator enabling 
the realization of Multi-Domain Operations through the bridging of heterogenous 
tactical networks based on operational demands. The intent of this RFI is to 
solicit feedback from industry to help shape NATO's ambition. 

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
HQ Supreme Allied Commander Transformation 
RFI-ACT-SACT-04-2026 
 
Page 4 of 9  
3.1.2. The eTacC capability seeks to enhance NATO’s ability to execute duties across 
the SACEUR AOR to provide the capability to communicate beyond line of sight 
during multidomain operations.  The eTacC capability will use a meshed 
communications capability enabling operations in a contested environment and 
bring spaced based information to the tactical level. 
 
3.1.3. The implementation of eTacC requires coherent alignment with other related 
and interconnected work strands. Therefore, based on eTacC operational and 
associated Capability Requirements (CRs), NATO is issuing this RFI to gain a 
better understanding of the national capabilities (GOTS/MOTS solutions) and of 
the commercial market and that is to provide this capability that NATO could 
potentially use to acquire eTacC solutions that meet the CRs. 
 
3.2. Objectives 
3.2.1. NATO has started developing the capabilities required for eTacC to align with 
the ORs which were stated in the ORS. 
 
3.2.2. With the development of capabilities, eTacC implementation efforts will neither 
supersede any existing NATO processes, nor impact initiatives that are not the 
responsibility of NATO AFSC. NATO eTacC efforts will support these processes 
and initiatives where applicable, thus avoiding any duplication of efforts. 
 
3.2.3. The eTacC capability seeks to identify broad areas of connectivity and 
communications gaps and lead to their rapid closure. This RFI will provide the 
ability to leverage assets and resources coming from related NATO 
Programmes capabilities, assets, and resources coming from Nations, their 
Industry, and their Academia, and finally filling the gaps of missing capabilities, 
assets, resources needed to achieve tactical level interoperability and 
connectivity.

NATO UNCLASSIFIED 
HQ Supreme Allied Commander Transformation 
RFI-ACT-SACT-04-2026 
 
Page 5 of 9  
 
3.2.4. Allied Command Transformation (ACT) is surveying Industry and Academia to 
understand what solutions may be able to support eTacC requirements. 
 
3.2.5. This survey seeks to gather information from Industry and Academia on existing 
eTacC solutions, as well as those in development that could potentially be 
procured by NATO. 
 
3.3. Expected Benefits to Respondents 
3.3.1. Market research to increase services provided that could broaden future 
markets and client base. 
3.3.2. Potential to broaden into military sector and international market. 
 
3.4. Expected Benefits to NATO 
3.4.1. Resilient and persistent eTacC capability solutions that meet current NATO 
Operational and Capability Requirements. 
3.4.2. Increased operational and tactical advantages over potential threats. 
 
4. REQUESTED INFORMATION 
4.1. The response(s) to this RFI shall be submitted by e-mail. 
Submissions must include both the Contracting and Technical POCs 
listed on page 2. The responses shall not contain proprietary and/or classified 
information. HQ SACT reserves the right to seek clarification on submissions. 
 
4.2. Eligibility to Respond: 
Only NATO Nations, Industry, and Academia that originate or are chartered/incorporated 
within NATO Nations are eligible to respond to this RFI. Companies from Partner Nations 
who want to participate should collaborate with a primary company headquartered within 
a NATO Nation. 
 
4.3. Response Template: 
4.3.1. Provide name, mailing address, overnight delivery address (if different from 
mailing address), designated point of contact (phone number, e-mail). 
 
4.3.2. Respondents can collaborate with other providers, but all 
companies/organizations must be clearly identified and their role/services clearly 
stated. 
 
4.3.3. Identify current services your company offers, which most closely match the 
capabilities, specified in this RFI and the questionnaire posted on HQ SACT P&C 
website (https://www.act.nato.int/opportunities/contracting) with the same title of

this document, or portions of. 
 
4.3.4. Available product brochures, specification sheets, photographs, illustration and 
technical descriptions that describe your company’s current services are welcome. 
Companies are encouraged not to include marketing informational materials that do 
not relate to the services described in this RFI as they will be discarded; however, 
responses may include URL links to technical documentation materials (i.e., technical 
data sheets for products) are welcome. 
 
4.3.5. Response limited to a single main document and enclosures for a total not-to- 
exceed 15 pages (material provided as per paragraph above not included). 
 
4.3.6. The document should be single-spaced, have one-inch margins, assume US

4.3.7. Submissions should be named according to the following convention:

similar services, including a customer/company name and point of contact, phone

4.3.8. Responses shall not be classified above NATO UNCLASSIFIED. 
 
4.3.9. The information may be considered in developing any future potential

4.4. Price Estimates

reach out to those respondents who meet the certain NATO requirements to gain 
information on any pricing or ROM for the solutions provided. Provision of data, or lack 
of, will not prejudice any respondent if there is a competitive bidding process later as

4.5. Response Due Date 
Responses to this RFI must be received by 0900 am ET on 29 May 2026. The 
responses shall not contain any classified information. HQ SACT reserves the right to 
seek clarification on submissions. 
 
5. CLARIFICATIONS AND QUESTIONS 
 
Technical inquiries about this RFI shall be submitted by e-mail solely to the POCs by 0900 
am ET 11 May 2026. Accordingly, questions in an e-mail shall not contain proprietary 
and/or classified information. Answers will be posted as soon as possible on the HQ SACT 
P&C website at: https://www.act.nato.int/opportunities/contracting 
 
All questions should be submitted by 11 May 2026 to allow for appropriate response time 
prior to the 29 May 2026 response due date. 
 
6. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION 
 
6.1. Non-disclosure Principles and/or Non-disclosure Agreement (NDA) with Third 
Party Company. 
 
6.1.1. Please be informed that HQ SACT may contract a company to conduct the 
Analysis of Alternatives (AoA) investigation in support of this project. HQ SACT will 
follow nondisclosure principles and possibly conclude an NDA with that company to 
protect submitted information from further disclosure. As the third-party beneficiary of 
this nondisclosure, this RFI serves to inform you how HQ SACT plans to proceed and 
HQ SACT’s intent to protect information from unauthorized disclosure. This requires 
the third-party company to protect the disclosed information using the highest degree 
of care that the company utilizes to protect its own Proprietary Information of a similar 
nature, and no less than reasonable care. 
6.1.2. The third-party company receiving the information shall not, without explicit,

1. Contracting Activity: Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) 
     Office of Procurement, Acquisition, and Logistics 
      Technology Acquisition Center 
      2 3 Christopher Way 
      Eatontown, NJ 07724 
       
2. Description of Action: 
 
The proposed action is for a firm-fixed price (FFP) order to be issued under National 
Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solutions for Enterprise-Wide 
Procurement (SEWP) V Government-Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) for brand 
name Laurel Bridge enterprise products supporting VA Office of Information & 
Technology (OIT) Health, Clinical Imaging, Digital Imaging and Communication in 
Medicine (DICOM) facility operations teams by supporting routing of image data, 
streamlining workflow processes through automation, enables robust DICOM message 
handling in VistA, and ensures historical and new imaging studies remain accessible at 
the point of care throughout VA’s nationside modernization efforts. 
 
Facility Operations: 
1. Lighthouse Licenses 
2. Compass Store DICOM Router Licenses 
 
3. Description of the Supplies or Services: 
 
The VA, OIT, Health, Clinical Imaging, has a requirement for renewal of existing 
maintenance license subscriptions for compass routers, Lighthouse licenses, and 
support services current fielded brand name Laurel Bridge products that supports 
imaging facility operations and technical development/implementation.  The base period 
will include the Laurel Bridge operational DICOM compass routers and Lighthouse 
perpetual licenses maintenance supporting enterprise-wide image data activities among 
VA facilities, community providers, and Department of War (DOW). Required software 
maintenance and support includes periodic updates, enhancements, and corrections to 
the software as well as technical/help desk support.  The period of performance for this 
action will include a 12-month base, and the total estimated price of the proposed action 
is  
   
4. Statutory Authority:  
 
Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 16.505(a)(4), the following brand 
name requirement is being justified and approved as an exception to fair opportunity 
under the statutory authority of Section 41 U.S.C. 4106(c)(2) as implemented by FAR 
16.505(b)(2)(i)(B), entitled “Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or 
services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services 
ordered are unique or highly specialized”. 
 


  CONTROL NUMBER VA-26-00047245 
Page 2 of 5 
JA Template_FAR 16.5_(08-AUG-2024) 
5. Rationale Supporting Use of Authority Cited Above:  
 
Based on the market research, as described in Section 8 of this justification, it has been 
determined that limited competition is available among resellers of the required annual 
maintenance for the existing VA owned Laurel Bridge DICOM DCF local server runtime 
licenses, compass routers, Run-time licenses, PowerTool Suite, developer toolkits, 
Lighthouse licenses, and support services. VA utilizes Laurel Bridge DCF software to 
develop VistA Imaging applications for all VHA facilities. VA anticipates the need to 
utilize these Laurel Bridge products for for at least the next six (6) years. The required 
annual maintenance for products supports the Government daily imaging activites 
required to support critical health care services to Veterans timely and efficiently 
ensuring the VistA Imaging applications are operational and accessible with minimal 
interruption for patient care services. 
 
To maintain the existing Laurel Bridge products, a source must have access to its 
proprietary source code to provide the required support, configuration, and software 
updates.  No other source has the capability of developing/issuing software updates for 
the Laurel Bridge software due to the proprietary nature of the source code.  In addition, 
any other source would need access to this code to ensure all services provided are 
properly configured.  Therefore, only Laurel Bridge, or its authorized resellers, can 
provide the required maintenance support services for the currently fielded software and 
the annual maintenance of the Laurel Bridge DCF products and services required for 
VistA Imaging.  
 
If Laurel Bridge DCF is not procured, reengineering VistA Imaging to use an alternate 
toolkit is currently estimated to cost approximately $7M for the first year and take a 
minimum of 12 months to complete, in addition to the cost of the alternate toolkit 
estimated at $660,000 per year. This estimate is based on previous acquisition history, 
and it is not expected these duplicative costs would be recovered through competition. 
 
Failure to procure the required annual maintenance of the existing Government owned 
Laurel Bridge products and services would result in VA’s inability to evoke existing VistA 
Imaging applications to acquire, store and provide DICOM medical images among 150+ 
VA Medical Centers, the Department of War (DOW) medical care system and 
community providers resulting in negative outcomes from delays of health care services 
to Veterans. 
 
6. Efforts to Obtain Competition:  
 
Market research was conducted, details of which are in section 8 of this justification. 
This effort did not yield any additional sources that can meet the Government’s 
requirements. However, the undersigned VA technical representative determined 
that limited competition is available among authorized resellers for brand name 
Laurel Bridge, as well as software maintenance and support. In accordance with 
FAR 16.505(a)(4)(iii)(A)(1), this justification will be provided with the solicitation to all 
appropriate NASA SEWP V GWAC holders.  Furthermore, in accordance with FAR 
5.301, 16.505(b)(2)(ii)(D), and 16.505(a)(4)(iii), the award notice for this action will 

  CONTROL NUMBER VA-26-00047245 
Page 3 of 5 
JA Template_FAR 16.5_(08-AUG-2024) 
be synopsized on the Contract Opportunities website and this justification will be 
made publicly available within 14 days of award. 
 
7. Actions to Increase Competition:  
 
The Government will continue to conduct market research to ascertain if there are 
changes in the market place that would enable future actions to be competed. 
 
8. Mar
ket Research:  
 
The Government’s technical experts conducted market research from February to 
March 2026 by reviewing maintenance support services available from resellers of 
Laurel Bridge software.  Specifically, the Government’s technical experts reviewed 
products/services available from resellers (Minburn, V3 Gate) and Laurel Bridge to 
determine which sources can provide software maintenance licenses and support on 
the existing Laurel Bridge software.  Based on this review, it was determined that no 
other source could provide required licenses and maintenance support for Laurel 
Bridge software other than Laurel Bridge or one of its resellers because they lacked 
access to the proprietary source code necessary to provide the required support, 
configuration, and software updates.  Only Laurel Bridge or its resellers can access 
the proprietary source code to maintain the current fielded Laurel Bridge licenses. As 
described in Section 5 above, use of any other brand of software is not tenable due 
to the embedded code in the current infrastructure that is currently used at VA sites. 
 
The Government’s technical experts also reviewed public data to determine if 
applications developed by other vendors utilizing the Laurel Bridge products could 
be evoked either without using Laurel Bridge products or using an alternate 
manufacturer’s (Medical Connections, Ltd, MicroDicom, LeadTools, Merge 
Healthcare by IBM, Intelerad, DICOM Systems, AGFA, Sectra and Fujifilm Medical 
Systems, etc.) products, to which the results were inconclusive. As described above 
in section 5, the VistA Imaging software components that leverage the Laurel Bridge 
DICOM toolkit would need significant redesign to use another toolkit.  VistA Imaging 
neither has the funding, nor the development flexibility to support this redesign at 
this time. 
 
Given the VA legacy version of the Laurel Bridge software is proprietary or closed 
sourced, meaning the code is not made available to the general public for use, 
market research confirms that only Laurel Bridge (or its authorized resellers) can 
provide the annual maintenance requirements for the usage of the fielded Laurel 
Bridge products.  VA currently has government-owned copies of Laurel Bridge 
products, but these copies still rely on Laurel Bridge’s proprietary DCF SDK, which is 
embedded inside VistA Imaging. Even though the VA owns the deployed software 
version, the intellectual property inside it still belongs to Laurel Bridge.

BACKGROUND

The purpose of this Performance Work Statement (PWS) is to define system functional support services for Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy Business Process Support Directorate (BPSD), DLA Energy Procurement Process Support Directorate (PPSD), and DLA Finance Energy. As the Integrated Materiel Manager for petroleum products and services for the Department of Defense (DOD), DLA Energy is responsible for providing innovative logistical support in relation to Energy products to its customers. The focus of this PWS is to provide support for Energy related Supply Chain Management involving products and services to Global customers on 24-hour basis 365 days a year. DLA personnel interface with CONUS and OCONUS offices and personnel daily.

SCOPE

The DLA Energy Business Process Support Directorate (BPSD), Procurement Process Support Directorate (PPSD), and the DLA Finance Energy Process Lead have been established to provide process support to all aspects of the DLA Energy supply chain and enabling systems. This specifically supports the DLA Energy system architecture in a single environment with ancillary integrated system components (e.g. Fuels Manager Defense and Energy Procurement System Tools) known as “Digital Business Transformation”. This system architecture consists of the following:

Systems, Applications and Products (SAP) -S4 HANA (High Analytics Application)

Integrated Business Planning (IBP)

Supplier Relationship Management (SRM)

Industry Solution for Oil and Gas (IS-Oil)

Bulk Fuel Management (BFM)

Procurement for Public Sector (PPS) 

System knowledge beyond the scope of organic Business Process Analysts in these areas of the organization is required to execute aspects of this mission.

Ongoing analytics and troubleshooting services are required in all operational areas of mission, to include performance and impacts of Digital Business Transformation in use for DLA Energy.

Supplemental expertise to support development of new system-based processes is also required as part of this effort. Examples include ongoing definition and implementation of Audit Readiness protocols and data reconciliation strategy, or adaptation of existing system capability to support new commodities/business lines.

Provide technical insight, assistance, Course of Actions (COAs) to resolve issues, testing, research, and training to support the activities required for the integration and management of system functionality and business functions pre, during and post migration to the Enterprise Resource Planning Software package: SAP Business Suite 4 SAP HANA.

The Contractor will be provided access to Enterprise Business System (EBS), the system the contractor will be operating in.

Task Order and IDIQ Task:	There are three categories of EBS support required: Project Plan Development; Strategic Project Support and Subject Matter Expertise.

This Task Order falls under IDIQ RFP: SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Areas:

This task order is: unrestricted (i.e. open to other-than-small businesses, Group A contractors).

This task order is to be evaluated in accordance with Tradeoff source selection procedures. Award of this task order shall be made on a competitive best value basis, using “tradeoff” procedures between non-price and price. In evaluating task order proposals, the non-price factor is considered significantly more important than price. The Government may consider award to other than the lowest priced offeror or other than the highest technically rated offeror.

Current Incumbent Information: Energy Functional Support

ACCENTURE FEDERAL SERVICES LLC DBA ACCENTURE NATIONAL SECURITY 800 NORTH GLEBE RD #300

ARLINGTON VA 22203-1807 USA

Firm Fixed Price

TASK REQUIREMENTS

The vendor will be required to perform the following tasks:

TASK 1 - Project Plan Development (Reference IDIQ RFP SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Area 10)

The Contractor shall develop a project plan to accomplish the requirements of this PWS to include, but not limited to, the deployment phases: Initiation, Site Survey, Implementation, Post-Installation and Sustainment. Project plans will also be developed for specific tasks assigned by the Government within the scope of this PWS.

The contractor shall conduct In-Process Reviews (IPRs) as needed and provide information regarding task order status. IPRs shall provide for an interchange between the Government and contractor during the execution of the task order (e.g., review of the system design, reviewing the results of functional testing).

Sixty (60) calendar days prior to the end of this contract (base or option period), the Contractor shall deliver a written Transition Plan to the COR for the tasks to be performed.

Deliverable 1: Initial Overarching Project Plan and Schedule identifying initial scope of requirements identified in Tasks 2 through 3. Due within 4 weeks of task order award.

Deliverable 2: Updates to Overarching Project Plan identifying changes in timelines, expectations, or requirements. Due by 5th working day of each month.

Deliverable 3: IPR briefing and Review of Project Plan with DLA Energy Leadership. Due Monthly by 5th working day of each month.

Deliverable 4: Transition Plan- 60 calendar days prior to the end of this contract (base or option period). Plan shall include all aspects of transition cost analysis, propose schedules and document risks associated with such transition.

TASK 2 - Strategic Project Support (Reference IDIQ RFP SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Area 4) Strategic Project Support is required to achieve DLA Energy mission objectives. Each objective is concurrent with the Process Area’s operations. The contractor shall collaborate with the Process Area Leads to achieve objectives. A review of mission tasks will be conducted by the Process Area Leads, and reviewed with the contractor to establish project requirements, (i.e. outline of the issue, the value proposition, scope, approach, timeline, total cost and associated costs, mission impacts, potential shortfalls, actions for remedy, and results).

Work complexity will vary based on task, workload, and root cause analysis. The more complex an issue the longer the Government will allow for resolution. The Government Process Area Leads will manage the determination and application of complexity in concert with the contract resource assigned to each project. The Contractor will provide a recommended complexity level within one (1) business day of task identification. In the event the task is later determined to be more or less difficult, the Contractor will request in writing an authorization from the process area lead to modify the level of difficulty categorization. Task Delivery Timelines are identified in Table 3 at Section 2.5.

Provide technical expertise regarding the required and optimal use of SAP systems to meet DLA objectives, which includes the purchase, receipt, sales, storage, issue, transfer and transport of: bulk, packaged, containerized petroleum and other DLA products transportable by land, sea, air, pipeline, barrel, rail, or other as well as advising on emerging functionality available in EBS upgrades.

Provide Subject Matter Expertise (SME) and assist DLA in developing and supporting processes related to Audit Readiness, e.g., inventory reconciliation across system components within the Digital Business Transformation architecture.

Provide Subject Matter Expertise (SME) and assist DLA in identifying the value proposition of proposed projects during project planning or identification. This encompasses providing project and individual task planning to ensure the best value is delivered, communicated, and acknowledged to the customer base or services organization.

Provide recommendations and assist in the creation and execution of standard project lifecycle processes and templates across all projects. This process and template need to be identified and used for all projects in the planning phase of the project(s).

Provide current project status and subject matter expertise (SME) support during command level briefings for each project, to include, scope, and approach, timeline, results, and recommendations.

Project Documentation Minimum Requirements:

Executive Summary of the issue

Outline of the issue, value proposition, scope, approach, timeline, resolution, and results.

Project plan for the completion of the project

Deliverable 1: Weekly Executive Summary outlining all meetings attended during the previous week related to the project(s). Due 3 p.m. on the first working day of each week.

Deliverable 2: Monthly Executive Summary Status Report to review with Business Process Support Directorate (BPSD), Procurement Process Support Directorate (PPSD) and DLA Finance Energy Directorate Leadership. Due by the 5th working day of each month.

Deliverable 3: Task coordination, categorization, and documentation in accordance with table 3.

TASK 3 - Subject Matter Expertise (Reference IDIQ RFP SP4701-15-R-0030 Task Area 4)

Work complexity will vary based on project assignment, workload, and root cause analysis. The more complex an issue the longer the Government will allow for resolution. The Government Process Area Leads will manage the determination and application of complexity in concert with the contract resource assigned to the task. For each project the vendor will provide a recommended complexity level within one (1) business day of project identification. In the event the project is later determined to be more or less difficult, the vendor will request in writing an authorization from the process area lead to modify the level of difficulty categorization. Project Delivery Timelines are identified in table 3.

The vendor must have the capability to perform the same elements as Task 3 at other DLA Energy Regional Offices. In the event support is needed at another DLA Regional Office, the Contractor shall provide resources local to the applicable Regional Office Performance will be coordinated with the COR; contractor personnel shall interface with BPSD, PPSD, and DLA Finance Energy Process Leads in Ft. Belvoir and local leadership/personnel at the office assigned. A modification to the Task Order will be issued if resources are deemed necessary at other locations. Deliverables will be the same as Task 3.

The Contractor is required to provide Subject Matter Expertise (SME) to the Government, based on an comprehensive understanding of the SAP functionality as well as the functional and design specifications associated with the Reports, Interfaces, Conversions, Extensions, Forms and Workflows (RICE- FW) utilized within these EBS and other System modules:

Support reconciliation of inventory and other financial postings across multiple systems (EBS, Fuels Manager Defense (FMD), Fuels Depot System (FDS), Electronic Point of Sale (EPoS), Wide Area Work Flow (WAWF), Treasury Department’s G Invoicing, Salesforce) including accounting for variations and parity checks between external systems and EBS which is key to meeting Audit Readiness requirements and objectives. Additionally, this support will provide DLA Energy with the expertise and resources needed to quickly identify and address audit inquiries and concerns in a timely manner. Supplemental expertise to support development of new system-based processes is also part of this effort. Examples include EBS modifications in support of the implementation of the Treasury Department’s G-Invoicing system and DLA’s business management to Salesforce, ongoing definition and implementation of Audit Readiness protocols and data reconciliation strategy, or adaptation of existing system capability to support new commodities/business lines.

Creation of operational reports/metrics as they pertain directly to Digital Business Transformation, and as identified by BPSD, PPSD, or the DLA Finance Energy Directorates.

Assist in tracking projected savings and performance metrics against actual outcomes over the duration of a project. This does not involve oversight of other contractors.

Gather, review and submit changes to the Workbench documentation to support DLA Energy’s efforts.

Provide analysis of SAP solutions, data, and interfacing tools.

Providing detailed explanations of system functionality for Business Process Analyst in the assigned process area.

Draft and assist in implementation strategy development for system modifications.

Answering approximately 2 or 3 questions per week from each of the 90+ Business Process Analysts pertaining to EBS functionality and design.

Assist Government in identifying the functionality and implementation strategy to fully leverage existing EBS capabilities for Aerospace commodity support by learning Aerospace current business model and advising proper EBS tenets for maximum efficiency.
