The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking sources for Defense Enterprise Office Solution (DEOS) Department of Defense (DoD) Office 365 Operations and Maintenance. This requirement will support DISA Portfolio Acquisition Executive Services (PAE Services) (SD), Enterprise Collaboration Services Division (SD3). 

CONTRACTING OFFICE ADDRESS:  

DISA/DITCO-NCR 

6910 COOPER AVE, 

FT. MEADE, MD 20755

INTRODUCTION:

This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE to determine the availability and technical capability of large and small businesses (including the following subsets: Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Certified 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Businesses and Woman-Owned Small Businesses) to provide the required products and/or services. 

DISA SD / SD3 is seeking information from potential sources for: providing engineering, operations and cybersecurity support for the sustainment of and engineering of the DEOS DoD Office 365 Non-classified Internet Protocol Router Network (NIPRNet) and Secret Internet Protocol Router Network (SIPRNet) Tenants and potentially a Top-Secret Office-365 Tenant. 

DoD selected Microsoft Office 365 (M365) as the solution to provide common communication, collaboration, and productivity capabilities that are mission-effective, efficient, widely accessible, and facilitate DoD operations worldwide. DISA, in support of the Deputy Secretary of Defense’s direction to accelerate DoD’s adoption of cloud computing technology, plans to continue to build on its seamlessly integrated enterprise M365 as a replacement for disparate DoD legacy enterprise information technology services, such as individual voice, video, collaboration, email, content management, information management, and productivity suites. 

DEOS PMO operates the DoD365-Joint tenant (IL5) with approximately 137k users across Defense Agencies and Field Activities (DAFA) and Combatant Commands (CCMD) organizations; and the DoD365-Sec tenant (IL6) with approximately 350k users across the Department’s DAFAs, CCMDs, and MILDEPs. Additionally, at IL6, DEOS PMO operates two Five Eyes (FVEY) tenants for United Kingdom and Australia with the potential to add additional FVEY partner nations. Planning estimates for an IL7 environment are at approximately 150k users across DoD. DEOS PMO continuously evolves DoD365 capabilities as Microsoft 365 service offerings are enhanced and mission requirements emerge.  

The anticipated period of performance is a one-year base period and four one-year optional periods.

The anticipated period of performance is:

Base Year		April 3, 2027 – April 2, 2028 

Option Year 1		April 3, 2028 – April 2, 2029 

Option Year 2		April 3, 2029 – April 2, 2030 

Option Year 3		April 3, 2030 – April 2, 2031 

Option Year 4		April 3, 2031 – April 2, 2032

The anticipated place of performance is at DISA Headquarters (6910 Cooper Ave, Fort Meade, MD, 20755), DISA Columbus, Ohio (3990 E. Broad St., Bldg. 23 Columbus, OH 43218-1152), and any DISA-approved contractor Secure Facility at the convenience of the contractor.

DISCLAIMER: 

THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS NOTICE. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY.

CONTRACT/PROGRAM BACKGROUND: 

The DEOS DoD365 Operations and Maintenance requirement is a recurring requirement currently being executed under the following contract:

Contract Number: 47QTCA21A0001 / 47QFSA21F0023

Contract Vehicle: General Services Administration (GSA) Single-Award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA)

Incumbent: General Dynamics Information Technology, Large Business

Method of previous acquisition: Task Order under Single Award Blanket Purchase Agreement 

Period of performance: 05 Mar 2021 - 4 May 2026 

The DISA DEOS also requires optional tasks to be incorporated into the follow-on contract for an IL7 (Top-Secret) solution. Therefore, in addition to the recurring requirements being performed in the existing Task Order above, the IL7 optional task requirements will also be included.

Additionally, the DISA anticipates awarding an additional one-year task order under the above single-award BPA, Contract Number 47QTCA21A0001, for a period of performance of 05 May 2026 - 04 May 2027.

REQUIRED CAPABILITIES: 

The DISA DEOS DoD 365 team requires a contractor to sustain, operate, engineer, and provide common communication, collaboration, and productivity capabilities to facilitate DoD operations worldwide. The Government is seeking contractors capable of providing subject matter expertise in support of this effort. 

Microsoft 365 (M365) Engineering and Operational Expertise (IL5, IL6, & IL7): Responses shall demonstrate experience and technical expertise in providing engineering, operations, and cybersecurity support for M365 environments at Impact Level 5 (IL5 – NIPRNet), Impact Level 6 (IL6 - SIPRNet), and Impact Level 7 (IL7 – Top-Secret) including integrated third-party products.  Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience, successful M365 deployments, troubleshooting complex issues, and optimizing configurations for large-scale DoD environments. Specific experience with Azure Government Unclass (IL5) and Secret (IL6) infrastructure is highly desirable. 


Cybersecurity and Risk Management: Responses shall demonstrate experience providing comprehensive cybersecurity services within DoD cloud environments (Azure preferred), including experience with Risk Management Framework (RMF) implementation, security control assessments, incident response, cyber threat hunting, and compliance with DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides, Information Assurance Vulnerability Management, and other DoD security policies and procedures. The ability to contribute to and maintain an Authority to Operate is critical. Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience providing comprehensive Cybersecurity and RMF Compliance in Cloud Environments (specifically M365, IL5 at a minimum) and DoD cloud environments.  


Knowledge Management and Training Capabilities: Given the need to create and maintain knowledge repositories and potentially develop training materials, responses shall demonstrate capabilities in knowledge management best practices, content creation, and online and virtual instructor-led training development. Describe and provide an example of improving user adoption and satisfaction through effective knowledge sharing and user engagement.

Staffing and Transition Management: Requires a smooth transition-in demanding rapid staffing. Responses shall showcase the ability to rapidly mobilize qualified personnel, manage staffing plans effectively, and execute seamless transitions. Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience managing staffing and transition for large-scale efforts (75-100 people) within 15-30 days of period of performance start date.

SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Facility Clearance Level. The work to be performed under this contract is up to the Top-Secret level. Therefore, responses shall demonstrate an interim or final Top Secret Facility Clearance from the Defense Security Service Facility Clearance Branch, which will be required at time of proposal submission.  Please include your company’s current facility clearance level in your reply to this notice.

Personnel Security. The work to be performed under this contract is up to the Top-Secret level.  All contractor staff are required to have a minimum of a Secret clearance and a Top Secret clearance will be required as needed to support specific DEOS projects. Describe and provide an example of your company’s experience managing security clearance requirements.    

Key contractor personnel shall be Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert Certified and the vendor shall be authorized to provide Enterprise Cloud Service Offering certified staff support.

Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) Certification: Because of the complexity of the integration and operational management of the DEOS effort and ongoing requirements to develop and integrate new collaboration capabilities, prime contractors shall be at least CMMI Services V3.0 Maturity Level 5 for all contract work and supporting subcontractors shall be at least CMMI Services V3.0 Maturity Level 3 for the life of the contract. Please include your company’s current CMMI level in your reply to this notice and demonstrate the ability to have this certification at time of proposal submission.  

SOURCES SOUGHT:  

The North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) for this requirement is 541511 (https://www.census.gov/naics/), with the corresponding size standard of $34 million. In order to make a determination for a small business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small businesses shall submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications. Responses shall demonstrate the company’s ability to perform in accordance with FAR clause 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting.

To assist DISA in determining the level of participation by small business in any subsequent procurement that may result from this Sources Sought Notice, provide information regarding any plans to use joint ventures (JV) or partnering. Please outline the company's areas of expertise and those of any proposed JV/partner who combined can meet the specific requirements contained in this notice.

SUBMISSION DETAILS:

Responses should include:

Responses to the Required Capabilities and Special Requirements above;

Business name and address; 

Name of company representative and their business title; 

Small Business Socio-economic status (if small); 

Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) Code;

Prime contract vehicles; to include ENCORE III, SETI, NIH CIO-SP4, NASA SEWP V, GSA: OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, MAS (including applicable SIN(s), groups or pools), or any other Government Agency contract vehicle that allows for decentralized ordering. (This information is for market research only and businesses with a valid CAGE code that lack prime contract vehicles are still encouraged to respond to this notice.) 

Businesses who wish to respond shall send a response via email no later than 4:00 PM Eastern Standard Time on  to elizabeth.a.bono.civ@mail.mil and michelle.l.rand.civ@mail.mil . Interested businesses should submit a brief capabilities statement package addressing the specific questions above (no more than seven pages), demonstrating the ability to perform the services listed under Required Capabilities.

Proprietary information and trade secrets, if any, shall be clearly marked on all materials. All information received that is marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. All Government and contractor personnel reviewing submitted responses will have signed non-disclosure agreements and understand their responsibility for proper use and protection from unauthorized disclosure of proprietary information as pursuant to 41 USC 423. The Government shall not be held liable for any damages incurred if proprietary information is not properly identified.

For information on DISA’s requirements, you can find current information on our home page: www.disa.mil – that includes current forecast and the current acquisition strategies. NATIONAL AERONAUTICS AND SPACE ADMINISTRATION 
Information Technology Procurement Office (ITPO) 
Justification for an Exception to Fair Opportunity 
Agency-Wide Hexagon MSC Software Renewal 
 
Description of the action being approved: This justification documents the basis for issuing a 
Delivery Order (DO) under the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solutions 
for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP), Government Wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC), 
using an exception to the Fair Opportunity process.   
 
Description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs: This competitive 
action establishes a Firm-Fixed-Price delivery order issued under the NASA SEWP GWAC for the 
Agency-Wide Hexagon MSC-software renewal. MSC’s software products include integrated (such 
as Actran, Adams), modeling (such as Patran) and solver (such as Dytran, Nastran, Sinda) 
solutions and many other applications, the majority of which are in two token delivery system 
environments, the legacy MasterKey Plus perpetual licensed application environment and MSC 
One, a subscription-based system with core applications bundled into the system. The total 
estimated price of the proposed order is  and the period of performance is a one-year 
base period with one one-year option period commencing on April 1, 2026 with a potential end 
date of March 31, 2028. 
 
Identification of Exception to Fair Opportunity: 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(A), The agency need for the supplies or services is so urgent that 
providing a fair opportunity would result in unacceptable delays. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(B), Only one awardee is capable of providing the supplies or 
services required at the level of quality required because the supplies or services 
ordered are unique or highly specialized. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(C), The order must be issued on a sole-source basis in the interest 
of economy and efficiency because it is a logical follow-on to an order already issued 
under the contract, provided that all awardees were given a fair opportunity to be 
considered for the original order. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(D), It is necessary to place an order to satisfy a minimum 
guarantee. 
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(E), For orders exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold a 
statute expressly authorizes or requires that the purchase be made from a specified 
source.  
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(F), In accordance with section 1331 of Public Law 111-240 (15 
U.S.C. 644(r)), contracting officers may, at their discretion, set aside orders for any of 
the small business concerns identified in 19.000(a)(3). When setting aside orders for 


2 
Rev.:3/2025 
small business concerns, the specific small business program eligibility requirements 
identified in part 19 apply.  
 
 FAR 16.505(b)(2)(i)(G), The order satisfies one of the exceptions permitting the use 
of other than full and open competition listed in 6.302 (10 U.S.C. 3406(c)(5). The 
public interest exception shall not be used unless Congress is notified in accordance 
with 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(7). 
 
Supporting Rationale:  
 
ImmixTechnology is the only responsible source capable of providing the agency-wide 
Hexagon MSC software. MSC’s software products are acquired from ImmixTechnology 
through the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) Hexagon. The OEM letter verified that 
no other vendor could provide MSC software licenses, updates, or support due to Hexagon’s 
exclusive reseller structure.  MSC’s software (MSC) provides multidisciplinary simulation, 
modeling, and solver environment required to support NASA’s mission-critical engineering 
programs, due to proprietary model compatibility, unique solver capabilities, and the agency’s 
extensive legacy model base. 
 
Market research of current simulation software shows that several major vendors—such as 
ANSYS, Siemens, and Dassault Systèmes—offer advanced virtual‑analysis tools, yet none 
fully match the integrated capabilities provided by Hexagon’s MSC Software. While these 
competing platforms focus primarily on traditional structural, thermal, and multi‑physics 
simulation, they do not incorporate the tightly connected ecosystem that sets MSC apart. 
 
MSC Software uniquely blends its decades‑proven solvers with Hexagon’s precision 
metrology, digital‑twin technologies, and real‑world sensor integration. This combination 
creates a closed‑loop environment in which models are continuously calibrated and validated 
against sub‑millimeter physical measurement data and high‑accuracy digital‑reality 
representations. As a result, MSC enables engineering teams—such as those at NASA—to 
verify spacecraft structures, materials, and mission scenarios with a level of real‑world 
fidelity that simulation‑only platforms cannot achieve. 
 
Competitor tools provide powerful virtual analyses, but they lack MSC’s ability to seamlessly 
integrate physical measurement and sensor data into simulations, maintain continuously 
updated digital twins grounded in real‑world conditions, deliver real‑time engineering insight 
through automated validation workflows, and reduce uncertainty through persistent 
model‑to‑measurement correlation. These attributes make MSC Software the only solution in 
its class that bridges the gap between virtual simulation and physical truth. This not only 
enhances reliability and mission readiness but also significantly reduces risk in environments 
where accuracy is critical. 
 
MSC’s simulation and CAE software technology has been used to support NASA for several 
years. NASA owns and maintains a variety of MSC software products including Nastran, 
Patran, Adams, Marc, Easy5, CAEfatigue, Actran, and Apex. These MSC software products 
are Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) software tools which allow users the ability to create 
multidisciplinary simulation models and perform structural, nonlinear, composite, dynamic, 

3 
Rev.:3/2025 
load, thermal, aeroelastic, fatigue, and acoustic analyses. These products include multi-bodied 
dynamics modeling, aeroelastic simulation, 2D-3D modeling, and solver analytical solution 
software among other tools sets, including a unified CAE environment for virtual product 
development. 
 
MSC is unique among simulation platforms because it combines decades‑proven structural, 
thermal, and multi‑physics solvers with  a broader ecosystem of precision metrology, 
digital‑twin technology, and real‑world sensor integration. While competitors such as 
ANSYS, Siemens, and Dassault focus primarily on virtual simulation, MSC stands out by 
tightly linking its analysis tools to physical measurement data and high‑accuracy 
digital‑reality models. This enables NASA to validate spacecraft structures, materials, and 
mission scenarios with a level of fidelity that bridges the gap between simulation and 
real‑world performance. MSC’s sub‑millimeter metrology, real‑time engineering insight, and 
automation capabilities provides a uniquely closed‑loop environment where models can be 
continuously calibrated, verified, and improved. As a result, MSC reduces uncertainty, 
improves reliability, and strengthens mission readiness in ways that traditional 
simulation‑only platforms cannot match. 
 
The Aerostructures Branch at AFRC relies on MSC software to perform the full range of 
structural analyses needed to support research activities and verify the airworthiness of new or 
modified flight hardware. These analyses—linear and nonlinear static, dynamic, vibration, 
and thermal, it is critical for predicting stress, deformation, buckling, and fatigue, and for 
establishing margins of safety required for mission success. At Glenn Research Center, the 
Materials and Structures and Propulsion Divisions also use MSC tools as primary FEA 
resources for major efforts such as Artemis, Hypersonics, Lunar Gateway, and future Mars 
missions. Engineers at GRC use products like Nastran, Patran, Easy5, and Adams to validate 
and optimize designs through virtual prototypes, supported by flexible Masterkey and MSC 
One licensing. LaRC similarly depends on MSC Nastran and Patran for coupled loads 
analysis on programs such as SLS and Commercial Crew, as well as for multi-year research 
efforts including SCALPSS, NGUS, ARC-LSI, SVTT, HSF, and HiCAM. LaRC also uses 
MSC Adams, Nastran, and Actran for multi-body dynamics, nonlinear simulations, and 
independent verification and validation of contractor analyses. Together, these centers 
demonstrate NASA’s broad and sustained reliance on MSC software for high-fidelity 
structural modeling, mission-critical analysis, and long-term program support. 
 
Determination that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable:  
 
Pricing will be assessed against the Independent Government Cost Estimate (IGCE), historical 
data, previous orders, and the current commercial price list to enable the Contracting Officer to 
determine fair and reasonable pricing. Based on this approach, the Contracting Officer believes 
this approach will ensure a fair and reasonable price.  
 
Other Facts:   
 
None.  
 

4 
Rev.:3/2025 
A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers 
that led to the restricted consideration before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies 
or services is made:   
 
The CO will continue to examine the market in the future for alternative solutions or new sources 
before executing any subsequent acquisitions for the same requirements.

### Sheet: Instructions
Response to Business, Functional, and Non-Functional Requirements (Appendix A).
Key Definitions
Business Requirement: the business goal and outcome that needs to be achieved.
Functional Requirement: the specific behavior or action the system must perform.
Non-Functional Requirement: the quality, performance, or constraint the system must operate within.
1. Vendors must respond to all requirements listed in Appendix A using the provided response template.
2. For each requirement, indicate the level of support in the “Vendor Response” column using one of the following: Fully Supported/Partially Supported/Not Supported
Fully Supported - The requirement is completely met by the proposed solution as described, without the need for custom development or significant workaround. Any necessary configuration is standard and does not materially alter core functionality.
Partially Supported - The requirement is only partially met. Some aspects are available, but gaps remain that may require configuration, integration, workaround processes, or limited custom development. Vendor must clearly identify what is and is not supported.
Not Supported - The requirement is not met by the proposed solution in its current form. No native capability exists, and significant custom development or third-party solutions would be required to address the requirement.
3. In the “Capability Level” column, indicate whether the capability is available Out-of-the-Box, Configurable, requires Custom development or Not Available.
Out-of-the-Box (OOTB) - The capability is delivered natively within the base product and is available for use upon deployment with minimal or no configuration.
Configurable - The capability is available within the product but requires standard configuration (e.g., settings, workflows, rules) to enable or tailor it. No coding or custom development is required.
Custom Development Required - The capability is not available natively and must be built through custom code, scripting, or significant modification of the platform (including use of APIs or development frameworks).
Not Available - The capability does not exist within the product and cannot be delivered without external tools or solutions not included in the vendor’s offering.
4. In the “Comments” column, vendors are encouraged to include any additional relevant information to clarify their response, such as dependencies (e.g., integrations, modules, or third-party components), assumptions or constraints, and relevant product features or capabilities.

2.  Contract Title 

GLAVA Radio Communications System Expansion with Additional Motorola APX NEXT & Lifecycle Support Services.

3.  Background  

The VA Police Service at the Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System operates one of the largest federal law enforcement agencies within the Veterans Health Administration, providing law enforcement and emergency response services across multiple VA medical centers, outpatient clinics, and veteran housing facilities throughout the Greater Los Angeles region. Current operations require the expansion of radio communications infrastructure and dispatch capabilities to support growing mission requirements, officer safety, and interoperability with local, state, and federal law enforcement partners including the Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD), Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

This procurement effort is also in support of the Executive Order on the National Center for Warrior Independence (NCWI), which necessitates enhanced communication capabilities to ensure efficient coordination and secure communications. The procurement includes adding 100 new Motorola APX NEXT portable radios to the existing fleet to meet the demands of increased personnel and expanded operational requirements.

The expansion aligns with the goals of the National Emergency Communications Plan (NECP) to ensure effective interoperability, coordination, lifecycle management, and strengthening the cybersecurity posture of public safety communications as a whole.

4.Objective

The objective of this procurement is to expand the existing radio communications system and dispatch capability with modern, secure, fully interoperable equipment that meets federal law enforcement standards and supports VA Police operational requirements for the next five years. The system expansion shall provide:

Secure, encrypted voice communications for additional VA Police personnel

Seamless integration with existing ASTRO 25 infrastructure

Advanced digital features including voice control, smart programming, and connectivity management

Lifecycle support ensuring system reliability, security patching, and operational readiness

Compliance with federal information security standards and VA policy requirements

5. Scope

This Statement of Work / Performance Work Statement (SOW/PWS) defines the requirements for the procurement, implementation, and lifecycle support of 100 additional Motorola APX NEXT portable radio communications equipment. The Contractor shall provide all equipment, software, licensing, installation support, training, maintenance, and technical support necessary to establish and sustain a fully operational, secure, interoperable radio communications system supporting VA Police operations at the Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System (GLA).

Statement of Work (SOW) 

PURPOSE:


The purpose of this contract is to acquire updated two-way communications equipment, which in-turn shall enhance and improve the existing equipment and system used by the Northern Arizona Veterans Affairs Health Care System (NAVAHCS) Police Department.  The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, supervision, equipment supplies, materials, materials, and travel to provide the equipment at NAVAHCS.  Furthermore, the NAVAHCS Police Department is seeking a portable radio, created specifically for mission-critical first responders who need to communicate across all frequency bands using the same device.  In order to maintain 100% complete compatibility with other VAPD stations within District 2, the Motorola model APX 8500 compatible with Programming over Project 25 (POP-25) that currently is in use within the district should be used.

BACKGROUND:


The United States Department of Veterans Affairs Police (VA Police) is the uniformed law enforcement service of the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, responsible for the protection of the VA Medical Centers (VAMC) and other facilities such as Outpatient Clinics (OPC) and Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOC) operated by United States Department of Veterans Affairs and its subsidiary components of the Veterans Health Administration (VHA), as well as the National Cemetery Administration (NCA) and the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) respectively. 

The Department of Veterans (VA) requires VA Police Officers to carry communications equipment.  Effective physical security requires the planning and protection of persons, resources, and property; prevention of loss and theft of supplies and property, and practical and economical application of technical security aids to augment police staff for the protection of VA facilities.  

Per VA Handbook 0730, The Radio Policy for requirements on communications throughout the Police service on VA campuses as well as the surrounding CBOCs states that  

VA Police officers will be always provided portable two-way radio units for use while on duty. 

Such radios will include a frequency dedicated exclusively for Police use to facilitate instant communication and direction during emergencies.  

The radio system is designed to prevent “dead spots’ from interrupting communications and will ensure that voice transmission is easily heard. 

REQUIRED SERVICES:


The Contractor shall provide all personnel, travel, parts, materials, labor, supervision, test equipment and technical manuals necessary to perform the requirements of the NAVAHCS Police Radio Communications System requirements along with the capability to expand.

● Dual networking equipment for redundancy

○ Two (2) LAN Switches 

● Edge Availability trunking subsystem for local redundancy/fallback operations 

○ Redundant networking equipment

Statement of Work 1 
 
Introduction 
The mission of the Indian Health Service (IHS) is to raise the physical, mental, social, and 
spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level. As part of this 
mission, the IHS is committed to providing a reliable and efficient health information 
system, modernizing IT infrastructure, improving access to care, and reducing medical 
errors through technology. 
Statement of Work (SOW) 
Enterprise Cisco UC/Collaboration & RPMS Systems Support 
The Indian Health Service (IHS) Great Plains Area (GPA) seeks a single contractor to provide 
comprehensive support services that encompass the full scope of work contained in both 
the Enterprise Cisco Unified Communications (UC) and Collaboration Support requirements 
and the Resource Patient Management System (RPMS) Systems Support requirements. The 
selected contractor will deliver unified communications engineering, system 
administration, maintenance, troubleshooting, modernization, and Tier 2/Tier 3 support for 
both the Cisco collaboration ecosystem and RPMS/EHR platform environments across all 
GPA facilities. These services will be consolidated under one contract to ensure coordinated 
oversight, streamlined support, and high system reliability for mission-critical 
communication and clinical information systems. 
Section C —  Statement of Work 
C-1. Overview 
The Great Plains Area requires comprehensive, integrated IT support services across two 
major operational domains: 
• Enterprise Cisco UC and Collaboration Systems supporting voice, video, telehealth, 
conferencing, and communication. 
• Engineering Services to migrate Billings into the GPA Calling Cluster 
• RPMS/EHR Systems supporting clinical operations at nineteen facilities, including 
four 24/7 hospitals. 
The contractor shall ensure the stability, performance, compliance, and modernization of 
both environments. 
C-2. Place of Performance 
Support will be provided primarily remotely using IHS-approved secure connectivity. On-
site work will occur only when authorized in writing by the COR. All RPMS and Cisco UC 
support may involve phone or VPN access. All travel must be pre-approved and reimbursed 
under relevant policies. 

Statement of Work 2 
 
C-3. Period of Performance 
Base Period: One (1) year 
Option Periods: Four (4) one-year option periods 
C-4. Background 
The GPA Cisco environment includes UCM, Unity, Expressway, IM&P, Webex, and related 
systems. RPMS systems run on Windows or AIX and support 19 locations including four 
hospitals. Both environments support mission-critical healthcare and administrative 
operations. 
C-5. Objectives 
Cisco UC Objectives: 
- Ensure stable and optimized Cisco UC operations. 
- Provide Tier 3 engineering support. i.e. Networking issue resolution, infrastructure 
equipment support, ISP escalations, last mile carrier / local Telco POC, cloud configurations, 
SME for related projects. 
 
RPMS Objectives: 
- Maintain continuous RPMS/EHR operations. 
- Provide Tier 2 support and coordinate Tier 3 escalations. i.e. Restart RPMS services and 
interfaces for RPMS servers, disaster recovery and restore functions, beta testing and  
installing patches and RPMS updates, Server maintenance; physical and virtual. 
C-6.1 Scope of Work – Cisco UC Support 
Tier 3 Engineering and Escalation Support 
• Serve as the senior technical resource for Cisco UCM, Webex, and associated 
collaboration technologies. 
• Troubleshoot and resolve complex call flow, SIP trunking, voice gateway, 
Expressway-C/E traversal, and media resource issues. 
• Manage cluster-level operations and interoperability between on-premises and 
cloud-based platforms. 
• Interface with Cisco TAC for major incidents, software defects, and root cause 
analysis. 
System Optimization and Performance Management 
• Monitor system performance, call quality, and resource utilization. 
• Perform scheduled backups of Cisco Unified Communications applications, 
Expressway-C/E clusters, and related collaboration components, and validate 
restore integrity per IHS configuration and continuity requirements 
• Conduct QoS audits and implement configuration adjustments to enhance service 
reliability. 

Statement of Work 3 
 
• Optimize integration between Cisco UCM and Webex for seamless collaboration and 
conferencing. 
• Provide quarterly reports summarizing performance trends and improvement 
recommendations. 
Configuration and Lifecycle Management 
• Plan and execute upgrades, patches, and system refreshes for UCM clusters, Unity, 
and Expressway. 
• Maintain standard configuration baselines and ensure consistent call routing and 
dial plan policies. 
• Support onboarding of new sites, users, and call flows within the enterprise 
environment. 
• Document configurations, workflows, and system dependencies in accordance with 
IHS change management. 
Security and Compliance 
• Ensure systems adhere to IHS and HHS security baselines and hardening standards. 
• Coordinate vulnerability mitigation and patch management activities. 
• Support required compliance standards through documentation and evidence 
gathering. 
• Collaborate with IHS cybersecurity and ISSO teams for remediation and audit 
support. 
Reporting and Knowledge Transfer 
• Deliver monthly reports detailing incidents, system performance, and optimization 
activities. 
• Provide updated documentation following significant changes or upgrades. 
• Participate in technical reviews and meetings with IHS leadership as requested. 
C-6.2 IHS Billings Migration to GPA UC Cluster: 
Migrate up to 1600 phones and 6 sites from two (2) separate Communications and Unity 
Connection clusters into the existing IHS Great Plains Area (GPA) Communications Manager and 
Unity Connection clusters 
• Configure up to six (6) new sites in the GPA cluster 
• Configure up to six (6) gateway routers with SRST in the GPA cluster 
• Migrate existing PSTN and analog gateway routers to register with the GPA CUCM 
cluster 
• Activate PRI for Little Shell site with new DIDs for users/phones 
• Modify existing dial plan to fit into GPA’s 10-digit dial plan 
• Configure up to ten (10) paging groups into GPA’s existing InformaCast Advanced (ICVA) 
cluster with up to ten (10) legacy paging interfaces (LPI/analog overhead speakers) 

Statement of Work 4 
 
• Duplicate/Import all Auto-Attendant features into new Unity Connection cluster 
• Configure up to ten (10) E911 locations into GPA’s existing CER based on IP subnet – 
Required for E911 support 
• E911 locations based on dedicated DID availability 
• Migrate sites/users in seven (7) separate migration events 
• Perform testing, troubleshooting and support post site migration 
Assumptions: 
• All devices (phones and gateways) will be migrated in a like-for-like manner.   It is 
assumed that all devices are currently Cisco supported. 
• Current paging gateways are of a hardware version that will support a firmware upgrade 
to version 2.X 
• Utilize existing IHS/GPA UC and ICVA licensing 
C-6.3 Scope of Work – RPMS Systems Support 
The Subcontractor is responsible for ensuring that the Resource and Patient Management 
System/Electronic Health Record (RPMS/EHR) operates reliably across the Great Plains Area 
(GPA). To meet Indian Health Service (IHS) standards, the Subcontractor must maintain 99% 
system uptime and ensure all RPMS systems follow standard configuration guidelines across 
both IRIS and Windows environments. This includes providing continuous monitoring, timely 
maintenance, technical expertise, and coordination with federal staff. 
The Great Plains Area’s Office of Information Technology (GPA OIT) requires both Tier 2 and 
assistance with Tier 3 engineering-level support. Approximately 400–600 tickets per year are 
handled through Tier 2 services, making the subcontracted support a critical operational 
function. 
Support is provided to nineteen facilities (four of which are 24/7 hospitals) and is conducted 
remotely via phone or VPN. 
 
Core Technical Responsibilities 
1. RPMS Platform & Operating System Support 
The Subcontractor must provide full support for: 
• Server hardware and OS environments: This includes IBM AIX servers and Windows-
based systems. 
• RPMS patching and updates: Ensuring systems remain synchronized with IHS National 
Release cycles. 
• IRIS database environments: Installation, upgrades, configuration, and ongoing 
maintenance of IRIS databases, journaling, and mirroring. 

Statement of Work 5 
 
• Backup management: Ensuring consistent and reliable site backups. 
• General RPMS issue resolution: Troubleshooting system failures, data issues, and 
performance concerns. 
• OS and application patching: Applying updates to operating systems, RPMS applications, 
IRIS, and any related RPMS/EHR tools. 
2. System Monitoring & Reliability Assurance 
To maintain the required 99% uptime, the Subcontractor must: 
• Perform proactive monitoring of all systems to detect potential issues early. 
• Notify GPA OIT about emerging issues before they become operational problems. 
• Ensure system performance remains optimal through tuning, testing, and analysis. 
• Provide technical guidance to improve reliability, stability, and security. 
 
Tier 2 Support Responsibilities (Detailed) 
Tier 2 support includes direct issue resolution, troubleshooting, and technical intervention 
across all 19 facilities. 
Key responsibilities include: 
• Patch Management & Break-Fix 
Applying patches and resolving failures affecting Windows and AIX systems, including 
real-time operational disruptions. 
• Help Desk Support 
Offering help desk services for federal, tribal, and urban RPMS systems. 
• Transmission and Connectivity Issue Resolution 
Fixing failures in system communication between AIX and Windows environments. 
• Coordination with On-Site Admins 
Scheduling maintenance with local system administrators to minimize operational 
impact. 
• Documentation Requirements 
All steps taken to resolve issues must be documented in the centralized repository 
within 2 hours of ticket closure. 
• Rapid Downtime Response 
Subcontractor personnel must respond “as soon as possible” for any downtime events 
and must be reachable 24/7 for emergencies. 
Specialized Technical Responsibilities: 
• Providing qualified specialists for IBM AIX High Availability administration. 
• Supplying experienced personnel skilled in IRIS/Caché environments for Windows and 
AIX. 
• Assisting with RPMS server conversions from AIX to Windows. 

Statement of Work 6 
 
• Providing remote user support, including RPMS password resets and server 
troubleshooting. 
• Troubleshooting:  
o Vista Capture and Display client issues 
o ACHS Web Printing Module setup 
o RPMS-Dentrix dental integration 
o IRIS Management Portal errors 
o Great Plains Area DI server issues 
o BMW application problems 
o RPMS Error Trap investigation and resolution 
 
Tier 3 Support Responsibilities 
Though Tier 3 engineering support is provided by IHS headquarters, the Subcontractor must: 
• Identify issues requiring Tier 3 assistance, track them, and coordinate the escalation 
process. 
• Provide monthly status reports documenting:  
o All support calls handled 
o Risks identified and their mitigation 
o Final resolutions 
• Recommend improvements to enhance RPMS reliability based on proactive monitoring. 
• Maintain full tracking of escalated tickets through their final resolution. 
• Prepare and organize training materials, presentations, and documentation 
(PowerPoints, meeting notes, reports). 
 
Staffing Requirements 
• Provide the equivalent of one full-time employee, which may be composed of multiple 
specialists (AIX expert, IRIS specialist, Windows engineer, etc.). 
• A single dedicated Project Manager/Point of Contact must oversee all activities, ensure 
communication, and enforce best practices. 
• Staff must be able to provide:  
o Business-hours support for standard maintenance windows 
o After-hours emergency support without additional overtime costs 
o Adjusted work schedules to meet facility needs 
C-7. Personnel Qualifications 
• Cisco UC Engineer: Senior-level Tier 3 engineer with expertise in UCM, Unity, 
Expressway, Webex, SIP, and QoS. 
• RPMS/IRIS Team: 4–5 personnel experienced in AIX, IRIS, and RPMS administration, 
coordinated by a Project Manager.  
• All staff must hold required IHS credentials. 

Statement of Work 7 
 
C-8. Government-Furnished Resources 
IHS will provide system access, administrative permissions, documentation, network 
diagrams, and maintenance coordination. 
C-9. Security, Privacy & Access Requirements 
All personnel must pass background checks and comply with IHS/HHS security 
requirements. All work must safeguard PII and PHI and follow site-specific security 
processes. 
C-10. Accessibility Requirements 
All services procured under this contract must conform to 36 CFR Part 1194 accessibility 
standards unless exempt. 
C-11. Deliverables 
- Monthly performance and activity reports. 
- Quarterly optimization reports. 
- Preventive maintenance schedule. 
- Updated documentation after major changes. 
- Quality control plan.

Draft Statement of Work (SOW) 
Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) Implementation 
Indian Health Service (IHS) 
Division of Information Technology (DIT) 
 
1. INTRODUCTION 
The Indian Health Service (IHS), an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human 
Services (HHS), is initiating a strategic modernization program to establish a Cloud Center of 
Excellence (CCoE). The CCoE will utilize Cloud (GovCloud - FedRAMP) to centralize, secure, 
and automate cloud operations while supporting mission-critical health IT objectives. 
This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the tasks, deliverables, roles, and performance 
expectations for designing, implementing, and sustaining the CCoE in alignment with federal 
compliance frameworks including: 
• FedRAMP (High Baseline) 
• NIST 800-53 Rev 5 
• Executive Order 14028 
• OMB M-22-09, M-24-04 
• CISA’s Zero Trust Maturity Model (ZTMM) 
• Post Quantum Computing (PQC) Readiness meeting PQC Mandate Enablement   
• Secure AI ready platform  
 
2. BACKGROUND 
IHS currently operates in a decentralized IT environment that contributes to fragmented 
infrastructure, inconsistent security enforcement, and risk exposure. GAO Report GAO-21-20 
identified several deficiencies in cloud governance, visibility, and cybersecurity readiness. 
To address these gaps, IHS will implement a secure Cloud GovCloud-based environment that 
consolidates infrastructure, automates security workflows, and incorporates role-based AI tools. 
The CCoE will enable continuous compliance, reduce operational overhead, and support 
innovation across IHS facilities. 
 
3. SCOPE OF WORK 
The Contractor shall provide a comprehensive solution that includes, but is not limited to, the 
following capabilities: 

• Cloud Landing Zone Design & Deployment 
o Multi-account Cloud architecture with governance controls 
o Use of Cloud Control Tower, Service Catalog, and Cloud Organizations 
o Identity and access management aligned with Zero Trust principles 
• Secure Enclave Provisioning 
o Configured enclaves for development, staging, and production workloads 
o FedRAMP-compliant storage, compute, and networking (e.g., EC2, S3, VPC, 
PrivateLink) 
o Hardened environments using CIS benchmarks and Cloud best practices 
• Automation and Orchestration 
o Automated workflows for ATO lifecycle management 
o Continuous POA&M generation, patch validation, and compliance reporting 
o Integration with SIEM (e.g., Splunk), SOAR tools, and Cloud Security Hub 
• Data Engineering and ETL 
o Extract-Transform-Load (ETL) pipelines for ingesting and transforming log and 
event data 
o Integration with Cloud   native telemetry (e.g., CloudTrail, GuardDuty) and third-
party tools 
o Masking and classification of PHI/PII in compliance with HIPAA and FISMA 
• Large Language Model (LLM) Enablement 
o On-premise or enclave-deployed LLMs for secure, role-based inference 
o AI-assisted document generation (e.g., SSP, SAR, RAR, POA&M) 
o Local semantic search and summarization of compliance materials 
o Use of containerized, GPU-accelerated inference in isolated VPCs 
• Compliance Dashboards and Risk Analytics 
o Real-time compliance status dashboards for executive reporting 
o Dashboards showing ATO progress, open vulnerabilities, audit readiness 
o Integration with natural language interfaces for querying compliance data 
• Zero Trust Architecture Implementation 
o Aligned with CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model (ZTMM) 
o Support for microsegmentation, encrypted remote access, and continuous 
validation 
o Maturity benchmarking and optimization across all ZTA pillars 
• Security Operations and Monitoring 
o Centralized log aggregation and threat detection via SIEM 
o Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), vulnerability management 
o Continuous diagnostics and mitigation (CDM) support 
• Secure Data Vault and Metadata Governance 
o Encrypted storage with tagging and classification aligned with NIST 800-60 
o Role-based tagging, automated metadata parsing, and retention policies 
o AI-assisted classification and redaction for secure document handling 
• Stakeholder Support and Role-Based Toolkits 
o Interfaces and workflows tailored to ISSOs, POA&M Analysts, Auditors, System 
Owners 
o Embedded help systems and LLM-based support assistants 
o Training materials and job aids customized per role 

 
4. OBJECTIVES 
The objectives of the Cloud Center of Excellence (CCoE) initiative are to modernize, secure, and 
automate IHS cloud operations across the enterprise, in alignment with federal mandates, audit 
recommendations, and the agency’s mission to improve healthcare delivery through digital 
transformation. This section outlines the business, technical, security, and strategic outcomes the 
initiative is expected to achieve. 
4.1 Business Objectives 
• Establish a centralized cloud governance model to address findings in GAO Report 
GAO-21-20 and reduce operational fragmentation. 
• Enable secure, compliant testing and deployment of mission-critical applications through 
standardized Cloud environments. 
• Implement a cost accountability framework via a chargeback model supported by Cloud 
Budgets and Cost Explorer. 
• Reduce total cost of ownership through tool rationalization, license consolidation, and 
automation of manual compliance functions. 
• Improve leadership visibility into risk posture, operational performance, and compliance 
status through real-time executive dashboards. 
4.2 Technical Objectives 
• Design and deploy a secure Cloud Landing Zone architecture with multi-account 
governance, VPC segmentation, and centralized identity and access management. 
• Automate core compliance and operational workflows including: 
o ATO package generation 
o POA&M lifecycle tracking 
o Patch deployment validation 
o Security incident ticketing and audit response 
• Integrate telemetry, logs, and vulnerability scan results into a unified SIEM and 
dashboarding platform. 
• Establish secure ETL pipelines from Cloud  and third-party telemetry sources into 
centralized compliance dashboards and data lakes. 
• Deploy GPU-enabled container environments for operating fine-tuned, enclave-hosted 
LLMs in support of documentation generation, compliance analytics, and secure 
information retrieval. 
4.3 Security and Compliance Objectives 
• Achieve continuous compliance monitoring and FedRAMP alignment across deployed 
systems and workflows. 
• Implement Zero Trust Architecture (ZTA) principles throughout the environment in 
accordance with CISA’s ZTMM framework. 

• Provide role-specific support tools for ISSOs, Security Control Assessors, POA&M 
Analysts, and System Owners, enhancing their efficiency and audit-readiness. 
• Enable enclave-based LLMs to support automated generation of SSPs, SARs, SAPs, and 
other required documentation with no data egress. 
• Monitor compliance posture in real-time through dashboards that provide insights into 
ATO progression, vulnerability resolution, patch coverage, and audit gaps. 
4.4 Strategic Outcomes 
• Empower IHS leadership with defensible, data-driven insights into cybersecurity, 
operations, and cloud utilization. 
• Institutionalize a scalable, repeatable cloud operations model that supports future IHS 
initiatives, including EHR modernization and AI-driven analytics. 
• Reduce the burden on IHS security and compliance staff by automating routine 
workflows and documentation tasks using enclave-secured LLMs. 
• Increase IHS agility in adopting and securing commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) tools by 
establishing pre-authorization environments. 
• Create a foundation for continual innovation by deploying cloud-native and AI-native 
technologies in a secure and governed manner. 
 
5. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE 
One Year. All core implementation phases (enclave setup, automations, training) are to be 
completed within the Base Year. 
 
6. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE 
All work shall be performed remotely unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer. The 
Contractor shall use IHS-approved virtual collaboration platforms for meetings, training, and 
reviews. 
 
7. PHASED IMPLEMENTATION PLAN & DELIVERABLES 
The CCoE shall be delivered in three integrated phases. Each phase builds on the previous to 
ensure secure design, operational automation, and sustainable cloud governance. All activities 
will comply with IHS, HHS, and federal cybersecurity mandates. 
7.1 Phase 1: Foundation — Secure Enclave and Cloud  Infrastructure 
Deployment 

Objective: 
Establish the secure Cloud GovCloud infrastructure, deploy baseline logging, identity, and ETL 
capabilities, and prepare for authorization under FedRAMP and IHS-specific requirements. 
Key Activities: 
• Deploy Cloud Landing Zone using Cloud Control Tower and multi-account best practices 
• Configure core services: EC2, S3 (Standard, Glacier IR, Deep Archive), IAM, VPC, and 
PrivateLink 
• Enable centralized logging, auditing, and threat detection with Cloud CloudTrail, 
GuardDuty, and Config 
• Provision ETL servers and data pipelines to Splunk/Data Lake 
• Deploy GPU-enabled container environments for local LLMs in isolated VPCs 
• Draft core ATO documentation including SSP, SAP, RAR, and ConMon strategy 
• Establish compliance governance alignment with NIST, ZTMM, and FedRAMP High 
Deliverables: 
• Cloud Landing Zone Architecture and Configuration Artifacts 
• IAM and VPC Security Configuration Documentation 
• Hardened ETL Server Deployment Package and Logging Setup 
• Baseline Data Classification and Masking Policy 
• Initial LLM Hosting Blueprint with Secure Container Deployment 
• Draft ATO Documents: SSP, SAP, RAR, Continuous Monitoring Strategy 
• Cloud Governance and Risk Register (Initial Baseline) 
7.2 Phase 2: Automation — Compliance, Risk Visibility, and ATO Enablement 
Objective: 
Automate security workflows, compliance operations, and risk analytics; integrate dashboarding, 
vulnerability scanning, and AI-powered documentation assistance. 
Key Activities: 
• Configure automation engines for POA&M tracking, ATO artifact generation, and patch 
lifecycle management 
• Integrate Cloud Security Hub, SIEM, SOAR, and ticketing systems (e.g., ServiceNow) 
• Deploy real-time dashboards for ATO progression, risk indicators, and vulnerability 
metrics 
• Train enclave-hosted LLMs on redacted historical data for audit RFI generation, 
SSP/POA&M summarization, and classification 
• Conduct full UAT with compliance and security teams across workflows and dashboards 
• Finalize all ATO documentation for formal submission 
• Document governance procedures for automation use and LLM assistance 
Deliverables: 

• Validated Automation Playbooks for ATO, POA&M, Patch, and IR workflows 
• Deployed Compliance Dashboards with Export/Reporting Capabilities 
• Integrated SIEM/EDR/Vulnerability Dashboard and Alerting Interfaces 
• Enclave-Based LLM Toolkits: Prompt Libraries, Summary Engines, Audit RFI Generator 
• Peer-Reviewed Codebase and QA Documentation for Security Automations 
• Completed ATO Package: SSP, SAP, SAR, POA&M Workbook 
• UAT Report, Change Logs, and Final QA Sign-off 
7.3 Phase 3: Transition — Training, Knowledge Transfer, and Operational 
Readiness 
Objective: 
Ensure IHS personnel are fully equipped to operate, sustain, and enhance the CCoE platform 
through structured training, documentation, and role-specific toolkits. 
Key Activities: 
• Deliver role-specific training for ISSOs, System Owners, Engineers, Analysts, and 
Auditors 
• Provide instructional resources: slide decks, recordings, quick-reference guides 
• Conduct operational exercises in staging environments to validate training 
comprehension 
• Finalize SOPs for Cloud, ETL, automation workflows, and LLM-based compliance 
tooling 
• Complete knowledge transfer and governance handoff with defined ownership and 
escalation paths 
• Deliver final project documentation package and operational readiness checklist 
Deliverables: 
• Training Curriculum by Role (ISSOs, DevSecOps, Security Analysts, etc.) 
• Admin Manuals, Reference Guides, and Recorded Training Sessions 
• SOPs for Enclave Management, ETL, Compliance Automation, and LLM Use 
• Knowledge Transfer Package with Architecture, Workflows, and Configuration Artifacts 
• Operational Readiness Check

1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market research to 
identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to support the upcoming 
acquisition of Level 1 and Level 2 services support of the NATO Security Support and Training 
to Ukraine (NSATU). The goal is to  transfer the responsibility of such services within defined 
national locations, from NCIA to a qualified external service provider  . To that end, we are 
issuing the attached Request for Information (RFI) MS-424359-NSATU to solicit feedback from 
capable and interested industry partners. 
 
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids. It is part of NCIA’s 
effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available capabilities, and 
potential acquisition strategies.

1. Background 
 
The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA)  requires industry feedback on their 
readiness to provide Level 1 and Level 2 support services for NATO Security Assistance and 
Training for Ukraine (NSATU) . This capability supports the NCIA’s mission to ensures secure, 
interoperable, and rapidly deployable CIS capabilities that maintain reliable command‑and‑control 
(C2) continuity in dynamic operational environments. 
 
2. Scope 
 
The Contractor shall provide Level 1 and Level 2 support services of all systems, services and 
facilities located in the specified National locations as outline in Section C. This effort includes day-
to-day system operation, management, maintenance, technical assistance and the provision of 
required support personnel including, but not limited to: 
1. Service Desk 
2. Event Management 
3. Incident Management 
4. Problem Management 
5. Change Management 
6. Lifecycle Management 
7. Routine Preventative Maintenance Level1 and Level 2 
 
The main infrastructure includes the following: 
1. Work Space Services and End User Devices, but not limited to: 
a. Laptops and Workstations 
b. Laptop and Workstation peripheral devices 
i. Keyboards 
ii. Monitors 
iii. Mice 
iv. KVM switches 
v. Desk Top Uninterrupted Power Supplies (where deployed) 
vi. Headsets 
vii. Web Cameras 
viii. Speakers 
c. VOIP/ VOSIP phones 
d. VTC systems/ facilities 
e. Multifunctional Printers and Scanners 
f. Mobile Phones 
g. Cabling and access points. 
2. Back End Infrastructure in Host Nation Locations, but not limited to: 
a. Uninterrupted Power Supplies 
b. Routers 
c. Switches 
d. Firewalls 
e. Crypto Systems 
f. Servers and Mass Storage devices  
g. Cabling and access points. 
3. Deployable CIS Systems, but not limited to: 
a. FB1-DragonFly HQ (DFHQ)  
b. Remote Network Modules (RMN) 
c. Theatre Liaison Kits (TLK) 

     
UNCLASSIFIED 
UNCLASSIFIED 
d. Deployable Satellite Ground Terminal (DSGT) 
4. Security domains or networks in Host Nation locations: 
The solution should be able to serve 3 (three)  different networks, each of which 
should be physically separated to meet different security classification criteria  
 
3. Objectives 
 
The Contractor shall deliver Level 1 and Level 2 support services by:  
A) Undertaking all required operational activities need to guarantee the service continuity and 
downtime reduction through instant access to a single point of contact. 
B) Undertaking all the assigned tasks to ensure  traceability and decision- making through a 
complete historical log of all support activity. 
C) Undertaking all routine preventive maintenance tasks at Levels 1 and 2, making sure that 
all equipment is maintained following approved procedures, manufacturers' guidelines, and 
other applicable standards. 
D) Undertaking all corrective maintenance activities at Levels 1 and 2, including 
troubleshooting, repairing, and fully restoring equipment back to normal operation. 
E) Undertaking proactive steps to correct any issues identified, taking necessary actions to 
avoid downtime and keep services running smoothly 
F) Undertaking accurate troubleshooting through structured tracking and categorization. 
G) Undertaking recurrent problems detection

NATIONAL ARCHIVES AND RECORDS ADMINISTRATION  
REQUEST FOR INFORMATION   
DIGITAL ASSET MANAGEMENT SYSTEM  
1.0 Introduction  
The National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) is an independent federal agency 
that helps safeguard and preserve our nation's history by overseeing the management of all 
federal records. The mission is to ensure ready access to the essential evidence that documents 
the rights of American citizens, the actions of federal officials, and the national experience.  
The purpose of this RFI is to obtain technical information about approaches and commercially  
available software products that can be used to manage several categories of audio-visual 
assets used for multiple purposes.  
 
This RFI requests information on potential tools and price points for two related use 
cases. We are interested in responses that address both use cases together if feasible, 
or separately if the combination results in significant price and capability variations.  
 
1. The first use case is limited to internally-accessed audiovisual business 
records and associated metadata. This approach has an estimated storage 
requirement of 120 TB over five years.  
2. The second use case builds on the first, adding the maintenance and external 
distribution of high quality digital reproduction masters of accessioned 
records. This approach would require approximately 1330 TB over five 
years. Additionally, all users and access for this use case would need to be 
managed separately from the first. 
NARA is a small agency with limited internal IT development and systems 
engineering resources, so we are interested in solutions that:   
 
● Do not require extensive technology configuration and integration efforts  
● Can support migration and ingest of approximately 65 terabytes of existing 
data from the current system, if limited to use case one. 
● Can support ingest of an initial 400 TB of existing data from various storage 
solutions for use case two. 
 
2.0 Description/Objective  
NARA requires a system to efficiently manage audiovisual business records so that they remain 
authentic, accessible, usable, and retrievable throughout the records’ lifecycle. Any solution shall 
have the capability to manage working files as well as implement records schedules and 
associated dispositions on agency electronic photo, video, graphic design, and audio records. The 
system will need to migrate NARA corporate records from the current system to a new one that 
will maintain, store, and access all of NARA's photo, video, audio, and graphic corporate 
records. Current storage is 49 TB. The estimated storage requirement is 120 TB over five years. 
A second use case would be to maintain, manage, and distribute high quality reproduction 
masters of Moving Image and Sound accessioned records. These files are currently stored on 

Linear Tape Open (LTO) tape, various networked on-premise storage servers, and NARA’s 
Google Drive. There is no distribution solution; when files are needed they are exchanged by 
external hard drive. Estimated base volume is 400 TB with projected annual additions of 
approximately 230 TB per year. The estimated storage requirement is 1330 TB over five years.  
The objectives are to:   
● Ensure that authentic, accessible, and usable audiovisual records and accompanying 
metadata are available to all appropriate NARA staff whenever needed 
● The areas of content that need to be addressed are: photos, graphics, audio and video 
productions, and if possible .csv, .dat, .txt, .cdf files, and proprietary formats for 
scientific instruments such as FTIR, XRF and GCMS. 
2.1 Requirements  
NARA is seeking a flexible long-term digital asset management system (DAMS) that will 
serve as both a continually accessible repository for audiovisual working files and high 
quality digital reproduction masters  of accessioned holdings, as well as a reliable digital 
records management system for federal records prior to archival accessioning.  
NARA requires a solution that has the ability to:   
● Provide file storage, management, discovery, and sharing functionality for NARA’s photo, 
video, audio, text, graphic design, CSV, and proprietary scientific instrument data. 
● Allow employees to upload, view, and download working assets as needed to accomplish 
their work.   
● Ingest records and manage them according to their records lifecycle, and apply a full range 
of retention rules and other records management functionalities to the records.  
● Support agency-wide audiovisual corporate records management and be available to 
designated users in every office, totalling at least 100 accounts. 
● For the second use case, system should support an additional 10 accounts for external 
users. 
● Incorporate policies to govern the metadata and transfer of assets, enrich the value of the 
assets in perpetuity, and create an organized pipeline for eligible digital assets to be 
transferred into the holdings of the National Archives for permanent preservation. 
● Connect to Amazon Web Services S3 buckets. 
● Migrate approximately 65 terabytes (TB) of existing audiovisual data currently in the 
system.  
● Reliably manage a total of 1450-2000 TB of data over the next five years,  
 
2.2 Functional Requirements  
NARA seeks to obtain from prospective contractors how their proposed digital asset 
management system meets and/or exceeds the following high-level functional requirements 
and complies with all requirements listed as Requirement Priority “MUST” within 
Attachment 1: ADAMS_RVTM_v.2.0_2026Feb26. 
2.2.1 Access: The solution shall provide timely, efficient, and accurate access to records, 

including the capability by individual or administrative users to set access permissions for 
actions such as preventing unauthorized access, modifying, uploading, or deleting  
records.   
2.2.2 Administration. The solution shall provide insight into user behavior through 
reporting and audit trail logs and allow user account creation at varying permission levels. 
Appropriate user tiers will have the ability to control, configure, and manage all records 
management-related features and functionalities (including the final classification of business 
records).   
2.2.3  Upload Assets. Authorized internal and external users shall be able to upload 
digital special media assets and their associated metadata in the user interface, both 
individually and in bulk. The solution shall support secure and encrypted data transfer 
capabilities using a NARA-approved protocol.  
2.2.4 Download Assets. Authorized internal and external users shall be able to export 
(download) digital special media assets in any format and file size from the system, both 
individually and in bulk. 
2.2.5 Scheduling and Disposition. The solution shall provide the capability to schedule, 
manage, and retain records for the approved time frames (based on NARA Records Control 
Schedule and General Records Schedules) and take appropriate retention and disposition 
actions (such as secure deletion or transfer) at the appropriate time. This also includes the 
ability to retain records approved for destruction beyond the period outlined in the records 
schedule if the records in question pertain to a court order, executive order, law, or approved 
business justification.   
2.2.6 Metadata. The solution shall collect and manage metadata about objects under 
management control (to include file extension, file size, creator name, date created, location 
created, unique identifier, access and use restrictions, captions, record disposition instructions, 
keywords, and checksum). Metadata may consist of descriptive data, structural data, 
administrative data, reference data, statistical data, or legal data about objects without including 
the content of the object itself.  See NARA guidance on metadata, all of which is applicable.   
2.2.7 Search. Authorized users shall be able to perform searches for digital special media assets 
within the system, based on keywords, associated metadata, embedded metadata, advanced 
search filters, file type, file name, record format, disposition status, and folder name. 
2.2.8 Organization Authorized users shall be able to organize digital special media content 
within the system using folders or collections. The solution shall control access to folders of 
corporate digital special media assets separately from folders of archival digital special 
media assets. 
2.2.9 Storage. The solution shall provide data storage and/or integration with existing cloud-
based NARA data stores. 
2.2.10 Integration. The solution shall integrate with existing NARA IT solutions (i.e., 
Google  Suite, AWS, etc.).  
2.2.11 Support. The provider shall support the system from development through disposition,  
to include (documentation, training, configuration management, business rules development  
and implementation, change management, security patching, and data migration).  

2.2.12 Data Migration. The provider shall manage the data migration from the existing DAMS. 
2.2.13 Training. The provider shall fully develop, implement, and train NARA users and  
administrators on the selected product.  
3.0 RFI Content  
3.1 RFI Questions  
Interested and capable vendors should respond detailing the following: 
1. Describe your DAMS solution(s) and indicate ability to meet each of the functional 
requirements of Section 2.2 and Attachment 1, RVTM. Provide any feedback on 
NARA’s functional requirements and identify whether any cannot be implemented 
without modifying the COTS software. Identify any possible constraints or potential 
risks to NARA’s stated objectives. 
2. Is your proposed DAMS product capable of providing the total dual-use case solution 
(managing both business records and separate archival holdings, with separate access 
and use restrictions, up to a total of 1450-2000 TB of data) without modification? If not, 
or if combining the two functions would result in a significant variation in pricing and 
functionality, please provide a separate estimated cost breakout for the different system 
or solution types you propose to meet these two needs individually. If your system is 
able to meet only one or the other use case, please explain the technical limitations that 
NARA should consider in addressing these related needs. 
3. Describe your customary commercial practices for your DAMS solution in terms of 
pricing structure and approach for implementation, licensing, support, and any unique  
circumstances wherein those would change. Describe whether your DAMS solution has 
been deployed within other Federal Civilian Agencies. Describe your experience and 
approach  to deploying and maintaining your DAMS solution (i.e., installation, 
configuration, customization, and enhancements, maintenance, technical support). 
Provide any comments or recommendations on the most suitable acquisition approach 
for this type of requirement, along with a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) Cost 
estimate for the different components of any identified solutions to include licensing, 
maintenance, technical support and any professional services that should be considered 
as part of any new system implementation. 
4. Indicate whether your product is commercially available or is on the General Services 
Administration Federal Supply Schedule or other Governmentwide Acquisition 
Contract (GWAC).  
5.  What tools and metrics do you use to measure system performance?   
6. Does the SaaS provider have Voluntary Product Accessibility Template(s) version 2 
published to demonstrate how it meets the updated Section 508 accessibility 
requirements? If yes, please provide a link. If not, please explain how your product 
meets the updated Section 508 accessibility requirements.  
7. Is the solution IPv6 compliant?   
8. Would your firm be interested in giving an informational presentation to the 

government?  
9. What are the common risks and issues encountered when implementing and/or 
integrating a DAMS?  
3.1 RFI Submission Instructions  
1. Responses shall include a brief description of your company, products and services, history,  
ownership, financial information, and other information you deem relevant. Provide points of  
contact, company address, phone/fax number, email, website, and business size and type (i.e., 
large business, small business, small disadvantaged business, HUBZone small business, woman 
owned small business, service- disabled, veteran-owned small business).   
2. Each RFI response should be e -mailed to Kevin Monahan at kevin.monahan@nara.gov. The  
subject of the email should be " RFI Response – Digital Asset Management System". Responses  
to this RFI should be received by 1:00 PM ET on May 1, 2026.   
3. DISCLAIMER: This RFI is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not  
constitute a solicitation. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this  
RFI or to otherwise pay for information received in response to this RFI. All information  
received in response to this RFI that is marked “Proprietary” will be handled accordingly.  
Responses to the RFI will not be returned. Information provided in response to this RFI will be  
used to assess tradeoffs and alternatives available for determining how to proceed in the  
acquisition process and may lead to the development of a work statement. Responders are solely  
responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. NARA may choose to  
engage with responders. However, such engagement is intended to clarify aspects of the 
response.

DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS

INSTITUTE FOR LEARNING, EDUCATION AND DEVELOPMENT 

MARQUIS PROJECT PARKING SUPPORT AGREEMENT

Version 1.0

Dated

January 20, 2026

Background    

Institute for Learning, Education and Development [ILEAD], Production and Delivery [PD] Service Line in Saint Louis, MO and Salt Lake City, UT operates Avid post-production edit suites and an Avid Media Asset Management [MAM] system with a Quantum LTO 8 library for archiving. 

To archive Avid project files, including sequences, video, audio, and graphics separately for possible editing after the files have been archived, ILEAD requires the Marquis Project Parking system. Project Parking takes all the files and compresses them into a Tape Archive [TAR] file, which can then be sent to the archive directly or through the MAM if the editor selects the MAM to manage the file. 

The Marquis Project Parking system is a proprietary software system and support is only available through Marquis. 

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is currently undergoing a reorganization that may result in future changes to its organizational structure, processes, responsibilities, and priorities. Such changes could affect the customers, services, or support described in this Product Description. Accordingly, the Contractor shall remain adaptable and responsive to evolving VA requirements and work in close coordination with the Government to assess and implement necessary adjustments, as needed. Any resulting changes will be completed by bilateral contract modification.

Applicable Documents

No documents.

Product Specifications and Deliverables

The Contractor shall deliver the Marquis Project Parking System SLA which includes:

[1] Annual Support Contract – Saint Louis;

[1] Annual Support Contract – Salt Lake City;

[1] Annual Support Contract Workspace Sync – 60TB;

[1] Fotonflite Remote Service; and

[1] Fotonflite Client License.

Required Products

Support Requirements

The Contractor shall:

Provide off-site maintenance support for the Marquis Project Parking System on a 24/7/365-day basis. This maintenance support shall be obtainable via telephone, email, and/or Virtual Private Network [VPN] connection as needed. The Contractor shall resolve critical configuration and management issues within 24 hours and non-critical issues within 72 hours, unless major code modification, regression testing, or hardware replacement is required. The Contractor shall contact the local service ticket originator and the Contracting Officer Representative [COR]/Program Manager [PM] within one [1] business day of the service ticket origination.

Assist users and administrators in resolving issues encountered while using the  Marquis Project Parking System. The Contractor shall provide solutions within 24 hours for critical configuration and management issues and within 72 hours for other non-critical issues, unless major code modification and regression testing are required.

 

Install and deploy manufacturer patches, fixes and workarounds for the Marquis Project Parking System. Prior to any maintenance actions, the Contractor shall coordinate with the COR and hosting environment POC for approval to ensure any updates, patches and fixes do not impact hosting environment operations.

Coordinate with the COR to schedule maintenance activities.

 

Perform maintenance activities during off business hours [after 7:00 PM and before 7:00 AM weekdays] or on weekends.

 

Provide support for a period of performance which shall be for one [1] year from the award date, with four one [1] year option periods for continued service.

None

and
