STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) 
Eastern Oklahoma VA Health Care System 
Elopement Alarm System 
At the new Tulsa VA Medical Center 
GENERAL 
PURPOSE / OBJECTIVE: Eastern Oklahoma VA Health Care System (EOVAHCS) requires a 
contractor to supply and install an Elopement Alarm System to notify nursing staﬀ of 
monitored patients leaving that are identiﬁed at elevated risk for elopement at the Tulsa VA 
Medical Center.  The contractor will be required to supply and install all components and to 
monitor 8 doors on 4 ﬂoors and 16 annunciating stations including wiring between all devices 
in accordance with this statement of work in a cost eﬀective, eﬃcient, and safe manner, while 
in accordance with the VA Mission.  
BACKGROUND: A facility in Tulsa, Oklahoma, is currently being renovated for the purpose of 
being used as the new Tulsa VA Medical Center (VAMC) in June 2026.  The facility will need an 
Elopement Alarm System between May 2026 and August 2026.  The facility is currently under 
control of VHiT and the construction contractor remodeling the facility.  The Elopement Alarm 
System is required to be installed during the hospital activation period so that it is functional 
before ﬁrst patient is seen. 
LOCATION: The new Tulsa VA Medical Center will be located at 440 S. Houston Ave, Tulsa, 
Oklahoma 74127. 
PERFORMANCE PERIOD/DELIVERY TIMES: The VA requires delivery and installation of product 
between May 2026 and August 2026 as required by the construction contractor.  After award 
delivery times will be coordinated through the COR. 
The Contractor shall furnish all contract oversight, management, Technically Trained Personnel, 
OEM authorizations to support provision and installation of OEM products, applicable licenses, 
uniforms, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, storage, insurances, shipping and delivery costs, 
and transportations necessary to provide the products, and associated installation, for EOVAHCS 
in accordance with this SOW. Any services associated with this product are considered non-
personal services. The Contractor, its employees, agents, and subcontractors shall not be 
considered VA employees for any purpose of fulﬁlling the SOW and shall be considered 
employees of the Contractor.  
 
Qualiﬁcations of Contractor : For a contract of this size, scope and complexity, the successful 
Contractor must provide products and perform in a professional manner and quality as 
recognized by commercial industry standards as good to excellent.  Contractor must provide to 

 
the COR and CO, and maintain for the life of the contract, written certiﬁcation from the Original 
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) that authorizes the Contractor to provide and install the 
products and software, as detailed in the Contractor’s quote and identiﬁed in this SOW. 
 
SCOPE: EOVAHCS requires a contractor to provide  equipment and installation that meets or 
exceeds the physical, functional, and performance of the listed salient characteristics in the 
following sections. The equipment features are essential to the technical requirements to meet 
the department's needs and account for retroﬁtting an existing structure.  
 
SALIENT CHARACTERISTICS  
Contractor is required to provide the following products, brand name or equal, including 
installation at the location outlined in this SOW.  Elopement system must be compatible with 
and integrated with the Jeron Provider 790 nurse call system. 
 
Equipment: 
8 Each  Wanderguard Blue  Door Alarms Controller 
 
• Wirelessly identiﬁes bracelets within range and issues alert 
• Capable of upgrade to provide the following: 
o Proximity Awareness 
o Auto-door locking mags 
o Access Keypads/Badge Readers 
 
16 Each Wanderguard Blue  Nurse Station Annunciators 
 
• Provides audible indication of door alert at 4 locations on 4 ﬂoors 
 
50 Each Wanderguard Blue Bracelets 
   
• Durable/Cut-Resistant Bands 
• IP67 or better water ingress protection 
• Smooth surface for easy sterilization 
 
INSTALLATION AND TRAINING: Installation and staﬀ training are to be provided as part of this 
procurement. Delivery and installation must be coordinated with the local COR. See the 
Performance section below.  
 

 
Manuals: Contractor shall provide electronic copies of the user manuals and repair 
manuals for each diﬀerent model of product and software installed under this order or 
contract at no additional cost to the government. 
Installation, in addition to the time required for setup of the individual cells and 
cabinets.  The contractor will provide a senior technical expert for server setup and 
testing 
 
QUALITY 
 
Conformance Standards 
Refer to section on Safety and Compliance in this SOW. 
 
Rework or Remedy 
Rework or Remedy is deﬁned as performing the Service again until the Purpose of this 
SOW is achieved in full.  This involves less than Satisfactory Service by the Contractor 
and as noted by the COR. Rework or Remedy occurs at no additional cost to the 
Government. Payment will be withheld until all services are performed to the 
Satisfactory level in accordance with this SOW and as documented by the COR.

resultant inspection shall be documented and provided to the COR within 7 days of 
installation along with any inspection documentation or checklists required by the 
manufacturer.  Any changes in inspection requirements during the period of installation 
will be communicated to the Contractor immediately.  
Inspection and Acceptance of Products and Services: The Government reserves the 
right to inspect and test services in accordance with this SOW and the Contract. The only 
individual authorized to oﬃcially accept services is the COR. While inspection of services 
may be delegated by the COR and a shared responsibility with departmental 
management staﬀ, the COR is ultimately the only authorized individual to approve and 
accept services on behalf of the VA. 
 
WARRANTY OF EQUIPMENT: Government requirement for standard manufacturer industry 
warranty term. The government does not accept an extended warranty, which requires 
advance payment. 
PERFORMANCE PERIOD AND DELIVERY:  

 
• All items to be delivered and installed after receipt of purchase order starting on or 
around May 2026 through August 2026.

identiﬁed below. Conﬁrmation of delivery location will be provided by the VA COR post-
award. Delivery must be coordinated with VA COR before any delivery attempts. Any 
item that has not been coordinated will be turned away and any additional charges will 
be the responsibility of the sender/transportation company.

the equipment to the correct delivery location in the space, uncrating or unboxing the 
equipment, removing all trash, and setting up the equipment according to the

to the approved government contact onsite.

through 5:00 p.m. for the construction site, Monday through Friday, not including

Background:    Institute for Learning, Education and Development (ILEAD), Production and Delivery (PD)Service Line in St. Louis, MO maintains a live broadcast facility and contracts support services for closed captioning on both “live” and “offline” captioning for all ILEAD video deliverables.  ILEAD automates its captioning services with the use of closed captioning appliances that automatically convert speech to text captioning.

ILEAD owns EnCaption closed captioning automatic speed recognition (ASR) appliances requires support and software upgrades.  

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is currently undergoing a reorganization that may result in future changes to its organizational structure, processes, responsibilities, and priorities. Such changes could affect the customers, services, or support described in this Product Description. Accordingly, the Contractor shall remain adaptable and responsive to evolving VA requirements and work in close coordination with the Government to assess and implement necessary adjustments, as needed. Any resulting changes will be completed by bilateral contract modification.

Records Management Language for Contracts

When Federal agencies acquire goods or services, they need to determine what Federal records management requirements should be included in the contract. Federal contractors often create, send, or receive Federal records. Federal contracts should provide clear legal obligations describing how the contract employees must handle Federal records. 

Agency records officers, procurement counsel, and acquisitions officers must discuss how to integrate records management obligations into their existing procurement processes. NARA has developed the following language to be included as an agency-specific term and condition in Federal contracts for a variety of services and products. The majority of contracts should include language on records management obligations, but each contract should be evaluated individually. For example, the data-rights paragraph (Paragraph 10 below) may not be appropriate for all contracts. Instead, agencies may be better served by one of the established data-rights clauses in the Federal Acquisition Regulations. 

This language should not replace specific records management requirements included within Federal information system contracts. 

RECORDS MANAGEMENT OBLIGATIONS

A.  Applicability

This clause applies to all Contractors whose employees create, work with, or otherwise handle Federal records, as defined in Section B, regardless of the medium in which the record exists.  

B.  Definitions

“Federal record” as defined in 44 U.S.C. § 3301, includes all recorded information, regardless of form or characteristics, made or received by a Federal agency under Federal law or in connection with the transaction of public business and preserved or appropriate for preservation by that agency or its legitimate successor as evidence of the organization, functions, policies, decisions, procedures, operations, or other activities of the United States Government or because of the informational value of data in them.  

The term Federal record:

includes Institute for Learning, Education and Development (ILEAD) records. 

does not include personal materials.

applies to records created, received, or maintained by Contractors pursuant to their ILEAD contract.

may include deliverables and documentation associated with deliverables.

C.  Requirements

Contractor shall comply with all applicable records management laws and regulations, as well as National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records policies, including but not limited to the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. chs. 21, 29, 31, 33), NARA regulations at 36 CFR Chapter XII Subchapter B, and those policies associated with the safeguarding of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a). These policies include the preservation of all records, regardless of form or characteristics, mode of transmission, or state of completion. 

In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, all data created for Government use and delivered to, or falling under the legal control of, the Government are Federal records subject to the provisions of 44 U.S.C. chapters 21, 29, 31, and 33, the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), as amended, and the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a), as amended and must be managed and scheduled for disposition only as permitted by statute or regulation. 

In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, Contractor shall maintain all records created for Government use or created in the course of performing the contract and/or delivered to, or under the legal control of the Government and must be managed in accordance with Federal law. Electronic records and associated metadata must be accompanied by sufficient technical documentation to permit understanding and use of the records and data. 

ILEAD and its contractors are responsible for preventing the alienation or unauthorized destruction of records, including all forms of mutilation. Records may not be removed from the legal custody of ILEAD or destroyed except for in accordance with the provisions of the agency records schedules and with the written concurrence of the Head of the Contracting Activity. Willful and unlawful destruction, damage or alienation of Federal records is subject to the fines and penalties imposed by 18 U.S.C. 2701. In the event of  any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of records, Contractor must report to ILEAD. The agency must report promptly to NARA in accordance with 36 CFR 1230.

The Contractor shall immediately notify the appropriate Contracting Officer upon discovery of any inadvertent or unauthorized disclosures of information, data, documentary materials, records or equipment. Disclosure of non-public information is limited to authorized personnel with a need-to-know as described in the [contract vehicle]. The Contractor shall ensure that the appropriate personnel, administrative, technical, and physical safeguards are established to ensure the security and confidentiality of this information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is properly protected. The Contractor shall not remove material from Government facilities or systems, or facilities or systems operated or maintained on the Government’s behalf, without the express written permission of the Head of the Contracting Activity. When information, data, documentary material, records and/or equipment is no longer required, it shall be returned to ILEAD control or the Contractor must hold it until otherwise directed. Items returned to the Government shall be hand carried, mailed, emailed, or securely electronically transmitted to the Contracting Officer or address prescribed in the [contract vehicle]. Destruction of records is EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED unless in accordance with Paragraph (4).

The Contractor is required to obtain the Contracting Officer's approval prior to engaging in any contractual relationship (sub-contractor) in support of this contract requiring the disclosure of information, documentary material and/or records generated under, or relating to, contracts. The Contractor (and any sub-contractor) is required to abide by Government and ILEAD guidance for protecting sensitive, proprietary information, classified, and controlled unclassified information.

The Contractor shall only use Government IT equipment for purposes specifically tied to or authorized by the contract and in accordance with ILEAD policy. 

The Contractor shall not create or maintain any records containing any non-public ILEAD information that are not specifically tied to or authorized by the contract. 

The Contractor shall not retain, use, sell, or disseminate copies of any deliverable that contains information covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 or that which is generally protected from public disclosure by an exemption to the Freedom of Information Act. 

The ILEAD owns the rights to all data and records produced as part of this contract. All deliverables under the contract are the property of the U.S. Government for which ILEAD shall have unlimited rights to use, dispose of, or disclose such data contained therein as it determines to be in the public interest. Any Contractor rights in the data or deliverables must be identified as required by FAR 52.227-11 through FAR 52.227-20.

Training.  All Contractor employees assigned to this contract who create, work with, or otherwise handle records are required to take ILEAD-provided records management training. The Contractor is responsible for confirming training has been completed according to agency policies, including initial training and any annual or refresher training. 

[Note: To the extent an agency requires contractors to complete records management training, the agency must provide the training to the contractor.] 

D.  Flowdown of requirements to subcontractors

The Contractor shall incorporate the substance of this clause, its terms and requirements including this paragraph, in all subcontracts under this [contract vehicle], and require written subcontractor acknowledgment of same. 

Violation by a subcontractor of any provision set forth in this clause will be attributed to the Contractor.

STATEMENT OF WORK

BACKGROUND

VA Long Beach Healthcare System (VALBHS) is requested services for the implementation of an RTLS/RFID Asset Tracking solution to support the needs of the healthcare system. The Department of Veterans Affairs’ Real Time Location System (RTLS) Program affects areas of clinical and administrative workflows by providing process improvement and automation efficiency. Significant potential uses and benefits of this technology throughout VA are numerous and include improved quality of patient care and satisfaction, reduced health care asset management costs, improved capacity/resource planning, improved employee, and patient safety, and improved general asset management and inventory. The RTLS solution is comprised of multiple applications impacting the logistics supply chain, inventory accountability, Biomedical Engineering, Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Sterile Processing, Dental and Surgical Services, Cardiac Catheterization Labs, and a host of other clinical departments. RTLS applications are deployed to more than 225 VA medical centers. Current installations use proprietary CenTrak and Infor Location-Based Intelligence (LBI) software for tagging, tracking, and integration into a single database.  CenTrak® proprietary active Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) hardware and software provide zonal, room-level, and within-room level accuracy regarding asset location, staff location, patient location, as well as environmental variables.

SCOPE

This Statement of Work establishes the requirements for Information Technology (IT) services, hardware, and software to implement CenTrak and Infor LBI-based Asset Tracking (AT) at the VA Long Beach Healthcare System. The Contractor shall provide RTLS hardware, software, documentation, and services to authorized users in VHA. Services include installation, end user acceptance testing, training, warranty services, engineering, and professional services.  The scope of this order shall include completion of implementation already started and expansion of current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System. 

GENERAL REQUIREMENT

The Contractor shall provide all necessary labor, materials, supplies, parts, batteries, software (needed for the general operation of the system), tools, equipment, testing equipment, travel, transportation expenses and other related costs to provide the completion of implementation of the current inactive system at VA Long Beach Healthcare System.

The contractor will provide the additional necessary hardware that will work with the currently installed RTLS equipment in all buildings within the main campus and update any necessary outdated hardware to enable functional asset tracking. Any parts before being replaced must be approved by Biomedical Engineering.

Processing Time

Onsite Visits for Badging

One visit for fingerprinting.

One visit to pick up the issued badge.

All contractors and subcontractors must complete mandatory training assigned through the VA’s electronic Training Management System (TMS) before badges are issued. The Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall wear their VA issued badge and identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site.

If the afterhours request is approved, the Contractor must report to the Biomedical Engineering Department (Building 5, Room 138) to sign the visitor logbook and pick up a visitor badge. In addition to signing-in, the Contractor personnel shall identify him/herself to the Using Service before proceeding to the job site.

Prior to leaving the facility, the Contractor shall communicate status of equipment to the Using Service and sign out of the logbook in the Biomedical Engineering Department

The Contract Implementation Manager and Backup Managers shall be separate from the System Administrator.

Please explain your experience executing revenue centric workflow management services. Workflow that generates items that are both automated and set for manual review and subsequently distributed to staff throughout a large enterprise. 

Please provide your past or present approach to providing robotic process automation services that support automation assistance to approved work processes that reduced manual staff intervention to increase business process efficiencies.

Please provide your past or present experience in providing claims scoring, reporting and payment efficacy for a large healthcare entity.

Please provide your approach to past or present enterprise-wide operational process and staffing improvement support for a large organization in support of tactical and strategic goals/metrics.

Change management support on large scale initiatives and operational activities.

HIPAA / X12, NCPDP EDI subject matter expertise in a Healthcare Revenue cycle environment.

The development of executive level operations reports and business case products on both a regular and as needed (ad hoc) basis. These briefings often require a comparison of private sector Revenue Operations’ best practices, business standards or metrics.  These executive level documents and briefings may be extended to VA under-secretary, Legislative and Office of the Inspector General (IG) personnel.

BACKGROUND

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), is one of the world’s largest health care delivery organizations. The Revenue Operations (RO) team is seeking ongoing healthcare revenue industry modeled best practice management consulting services and healthcare revenue operations business information technology tools to sustain, transform and continuously improve revenue cycle activities within the Office of Finance (OF). Revenue Operations (RO) and the seven (7) regionally aligned Consolidated Patient Account Centers (CPACs) support a vast healthcare enterprise in the service of our Nation’s Veterans. The goal of RO is to support the field in the management of the revenue cycle. As part of that effort, RO provides a variety of program services including the following: payer relations, metric-based quality / policy operational analyses, rate development, eBusiness EDI solutions and best practice modeling with a focus on process standardization to enhance revenues.

The Consolidated Patient Account Center (CPAC) uses standardized methods, tools, and processes to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability in revenue operations. CPAC’s state-of-the-art business processes ensure that VA collects revenue from private health insurance carriers for nonservice-connected care provided to insured Veterans. These funds go back to the VA Medical Centers (VAMCs) to provide health care services to our Veterans. There are seven regional CPACs located around the country that provide revenue cycle management to all the  Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISNs) and their associated VAMCs. GENERAL INFORMATION

PLACE OF PERFORMANCE

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

DESCRIPTION

The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) is seeking information concerning the availability of capable contractors to provide a possible Replacement of IBM COBOL Mainframe System for Veteran Benefit Debt Management, NAICS - 541519

 

This is a Request For Information (RFI) only and is limited to seven pages.  Do not submit a proposal or quote.  There is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI.  Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider for Market Research purposes.  You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI.  This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract.  No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort.  Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. 

If interested, please provide the following: 

Provide a high-level response that describes your ability to meet the technical requirements described below. If additional information is required by VA to determine a contractor’s capability to provide the full requirement and the economic feasibility of the information provided, additional information may be requested at a later date.  A draft version of the requirement is below. 

Provide a Rough Level of Effort which would be required to complete this project. Include Labor Categories, Labor Category Descriptions, and project number of hours per Labor Category. This will be based upon your estimate of how long the Replacement of IBM COBOL Mainframe System for Veteran Benefit Debt Management will take to complete.

Please direct all responses to David Gabrysiak, david.gabrysiak@va.gov and Debra Clayton, debra.clayton2@va.gov.

Replacement of IBM COBOL Mainframe System for Veteran Benefit Debt Management

Scope


The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires contractor support to modernize a legacy Veteran Benefit Debt Management system that is running on an IBM COBOL mainframe system. The Contractor shall provide the technical expertise necessary to design, develop, implement, test, and transition to a modernized solution that fully replaces the legacy mainframe capabilities while ensuring continuity of operations.

2.0 Background


The current Veteran Benefit Debt Management system supports agency-wide Veteran Benefit and Debt operations. It performs debt aging, generates demand letters, and conducts file-based integrations with approximately ten external systems. Each external system integration utilizes a unique file-based interface. Approximately two million debt records are maintained in Virtual Storage Access Method (VSAM) and sequential file structures.

The legacy environment consists of:

257 COBOL modules totaling approximately 258,000 lines of code

540 JCL files totaling approximately 43,000 lines of code

87 PROCS totaling approximately 8,000 lines of code

18 COPYBOOKS totaling approximately 14,000 lines of code
These programs are executed daily or on demand via the CA7 scheduler.

Additionally, the system includes approximately 300 Java programs (126,000 lines of code) executed on Microsoft Windows servers, also via Computer Associates Workload Manager 7 (CA7) or on demand.

The legacy mainframe serves as a backend system and transmits updates to a Microsoft SQL Server database that supports APIs running on the MuleSoft AnyPoint Platform. These downstream systems are expected to remain in operation and must be fully supported by the contractor’s solution.

Requirements

Solution Development and Modernization


The Contractor shall provide a replacement solution that:

Replicates or enhances all existing functional capabilities of the Veteran Benefit Debt Management system.

Supports all debt management operations including, but not limited to, debt aging, demand letter generation, and batch processing.

Accommodates the migration and processing of approximately two million debt records currently stored in VSAM and sequential files.

Integration Requirements


The Contractor shall:

Provide interfaces that support all current file-based integrations with approximately ten external systems.

Maintain compatibility with each system’s unique integration format and operational requirements.

Ensure continued interoperability with the existing Microsoft SQL Server environment and MuleSoft Anypoint Platform APIs that depend on mainframe-generated updates.

Operational Requirements


The Contractor shall ensure the modernized solution:

Supports scheduled and on-demand execution of batch processes analogous to those performed using CA7.

Provides equivalent or improved performance, reliability, and auditability compared to the legacy environment.

Supports secure, reliable data transfer between all interfacing systems.

3.4 Data Migration


The Contractor shall:

Migrate all legacy VSAM and sequential file data without loss or corruption.

Conduct validation of migrated datasets to ensure data integrity and functional continuity.

3.5 Transition and Implementation


The Contractor shall:

Provide a detailed transition plan that ensures uninterrupted operations during system cutover.

Deliver training materials and training sessions to VA personnel as required.

Provide post-implementation support during stabilization.

4.0 Constraints and Considerations

All existing downstream systems (SQL Server, MuleSoft APIs) must remain operational throughout.

The Contractor shall ensure compliance with VA security, privacy, and data-protection requirements.

All modernization efforts must minimize disruptions to current business operations.

ATTACHMENT A

Red Hat Professional Services

Ansible Automation Platform Integration

for: 

Abacus Visual Playbook Builder and Automation Orchestrator

Department of Veterans Affairs

Veterans Health Administration (VHA)

Veterans Integrated Service Network 23 (VISN 23)

Healthcare Technology Management / Biomedical Engineering

Document Purpose

This document serves as Attachment A to the Performance Work Statement (PWS) for the Abacus Visual Playbook Builder and Automation Orchestrator acquisition. It defines the scope and requirements for Red Hat Professional Services engagement.

This document covers the interconnected technical areas requiring Red Hat expertise:

VM Provisioning and VLAN Management — API-driven infrastructure automation across multiple Nutanix sites

Windows Certificate Authentication — Secure, scalable authentication for managing Windows hosts

Certificate Management Workflows — Git-based certificate lifecycle management with four (4) distinct workflows

Presigned URL Workflow — S3 asset retrieval for playbook execution without direct AWS credentials

Real-Time Job Output Streaming — WebSocket integration for live job status in external UI

AAP Infrastructure and Self-Management — Operational best practices for running AAP

Abacus: The Orchestration Application

Abacus is the external application that orchestrates all user interaction and workflow coordination. Understanding Abacus's role is essential context for the AAP integration design.

Abacus Responsibilities

User interface for all VM provisioning and configuration requests

Determines which AAP job templates to invoke based on user actions and site context

Specifies which playbooks to execute (via Git commit reference)

Manages S3 asset references and coordinates presigned URL workflow

Handles user authentication and authorization before calling AAP APIs

Displays real-time job execution output streamed from AAP

Retrieves workstation onboarding script from Git

AAP's Role

AAP serves as the automation backend — it does not provide user-facing interfaces for end users. All user interaction happens in Abacus; Abacus calls AAP APIs; AAP runs playbooks against target infrastructure.

VM Provisioning and VLAN Management

This section describes the requirements for automating Windows VM provisioning and network management across multiple Nutanix sites.

Multi-Site Architecture

The Government has eight (8) geographically distributed sites, each with its own Nutanix Prism Element cluster. A single AAP installation serves all sites with strict security boundaries between them.

Multi-Site Security Model

The primary security requirement is strict site isolation. Users at Site A shall not have access to, view, or modify resources at Site B — even through misconfiguration.

Implementation approach:

One (1) AAP Organization per site (e.g., Minneapolis, Omaha, Fargo)

Organization-scoped Nutanix credentials (each credential can only access its site's cluster)

AD group to AAP Team mapping for RBAC

Site-specific VLAN configuration files in Git (vars/sites/{site}_vlans.yml)

Physical Sites:

Fort Meade, Fargo, Sioux Falls, Saint Cloud, Minneapolis, Omaha, Iowa City, Central Iowa

Logical Site:

VISN23 (administrative; no dedicated cluster; staff can work across all physical sites)

Each physical site has its own Prism Element cluster and AD security groups. VISN23 staff are granted cross-site access via AD group membership.

VLAN/Network Configuration Support

VLAN and network configuration management requirements are specified in Category LV [LV1-LV22]. The implementation mechanism (Abacus-native functionality, AAP workflows, dedicated service, or equivalent) is at Contractor discretion.

Red Hat Scope for VLAN-Related Work:

Red Hat's involvement in VLAN management is limited to technical guidance and integration support if the Contractor selects an AAP-based implementation approach:

API-Driven VM Provisioning

VM creation is triggered by Abacus via AAP's REST API — not through AAP's self-service portal. Abacus specifies the site, and the appropriate job template is invoked.

API Design:

One (1) Job Template per site (eight (8) total): minneapolis-vm-create, omaha-vm-create, etc.

Abacus determines which endpoint to call based on user's site

Site identifier implicit in endpoint (not passed as parameter)

VM Creation Parameters:

VM Creation Workflow Steps

The VM creation workflow shall execute the following steps:

Load VLAN configuration from Git for the target site

Perform "subnet math" to determine which VLAN the IP address belongs to

Validate IP is within usable range (not gateway, broadcast, etc.)

Check for IP conflicts (query existing VMs in Nutanix)

Create VM in Nutanix using specified template

Configure disks and CD-ROMs

Configure Windows hostname and network settings (mechanism at Contractor discretion per [L25])

Power on VM

Onboard VM for Windows authentication (see Section 3.6)

Add host to AAP inventory based on site, project, and group

Return result to Abacus

Automated VM Onboarding

After a VM is created and powered on, it must be onboarded into the Windows certificate authentication system before it can be managed by Ansible. This onboarding is an extension of the VM creation workflow.

Workflow continuation after VM power-on:

Wait for VM to complete initial Windows setup (sysprep completion)

Execute onboarding configuration (either via sysprep or initial connection)

Validate WinRM connectivity using certificate authentication

Add host to AAP inventory with correct Organization, Inventory, environment group, and component group memberships

Tag host with appropriate metadata (creation date, template used, etc.)

DRY Architecture Requirement

All eight (8) sites shall use identical playbook code — a single Git repository with no per-site playbook copies. Site-specific differences shall be handled via:

Organization-scoped credentials

Job Template extra variables (site_name, nutanix_cluster)

Site-specific variable files in Git (vars/sites/{site}_vlans.yml)

Benefit: Update playbook logic once; all eight (8) sites automatically receive the update.

VM Template Registry (Admin-Only)

Infrastructure administrators need the ability to register new Windows VM templates so they become available for VM provisioning. This shall be restricted to admin AD groups only.

Windows Certificate Authentication

This section describes the certificate-based authentication design for managing Windows hosts with Ansible.

Problem Statement

The Government needs to manage a mixed environment of Windows machines where some are domain-joined and others exist in workgroups. Several critical constraints eliminate traditional authentication methods.

Why Traditional Methods Do Not Work:

Solution: Two-Certificate Architecture

The solution is a certificate-based authentication system where Ansible uses WinRM over HTTPS with client certificate authentication. This approach uses two (2) separate certificates with distinct purposes.

Certificate 1: Windows Host Server Certificate

Purpose: Encrypts the WinRM communication channel (like HTTPS for a website)

Location: Each Windows host generates its own self-signed certificate

Private key: Never leaves the Windows host; never shared with Ansible

Validation: Ansible ignores validation (ansible_winrm_server_cert_validation: ignore)

Certificate 2: Ansible Client Certificate

Purpose: Proves Ansible's identity; replaces username/password authentication

Location: Single CA-signed certificate from Venafi on Ansible controller

Private key: Stored on Ansible controller only

Public key: Distributed to all Windows hosts (Trusted People store)

Mapping: Windows hosts map this certificate to local ansible_admin user

Git Repository for Platform Configuration

All certificate materials, root CAs, and generated scripts are stored in a dedicated Git repository. This design provides several benefits:

No TLS trust dependency: Git access via SSH requires no TLS certificate validation

Version history: All changes are tracked with full audit trail

Single source of truth: One authoritative location for all certificate-related materials

Resilience: If S3 or other infrastructure becomes untrusted due to CA rotation, Git remains accessible

Certificate Management Workflows Overview

Certificate management is divided into four (4) distinct workflows, each with a specific purpose and scope:

Initial Host Onboarding Workflow

When adding a new Windows host to Ansible management, an administrator performs an initial RDP session to execute a PowerShell setup script. This is the "moment of physical presence" to establish trust relationships.

The onboarding script performs these steps:

Generate self-signed certificate and configure WinRM HTTPS listener on port 5986

Import the root CA certificate that signed the Ansible controller certificate into Trusted Root store

Read Ansible controller certificate thumbprint

Create local ansible_admin user account with strong random password (generated locally, never transmitted)

Create certificate mapping: "when this certificate is presented, authenticate as ansible_admin"

After onboarding, Ansible can connect using certificate authentication without passwords transmitted over the network.

Workflow 1: Certificate Preparation and Staging

This workflow extracts certificate materials from a Venafi export, stages them in Git, and generates the onboarding script. It is a "safe" operation that does not touch any Windows hosts.

Trigger:

Admin uploads venafi-export.pfx (or ZIP containing PFX) to controller-certificate/ folder in Git, then runs the job template with the decryption password.

Steps:

Pull latest from Git repository

Detect file format (PFX directly, or ZIP containing PEM files, etc.)

Decrypt/extract using provided password: Private key → Store in AAP credential storage; Public certificate → Write to controller-certificate/public-cert.pem; Thumbprint → Extract and write to controller-certificate/thumbprint.txt; Signing root CA → If not already in root-ca/ folder, add it

Render onboarding-workstation.ps1 from Jinja2 template, embedding the root CA, thumbprint, public certificate, and logic for local user creation and certificate mapping

Write rendered script to generated/onboarding-workstation.ps1

Commit and push all changes to Git

Job completes successfully

Workflow 2: Certificate Rotation to Existing Hosts

This workflow pushes the new certificate to all managed Windows hosts. It requires careful design for reliability and rollback safety.

Pre-Conditions:

Workflow 1 has completed — all materials staged in Git

The old certificate is still valid (running 45-60 days before expiration)

AAP currently authenticates to Windows hosts using the old certificate

Both old and new credentials are available to AAP

Safety Mechanism: Scheduled Task Rollback

Before changing anything on a host:

Create a Windows scheduled task that will restore the old certificate mapping

Task triggers either on system reboot OR after a timeout (e.g., 10-15 minutes)

Then make the change:

Apply new certificate mapping (new thumbprint → ansible_admin)

Validate immediately:

Attempt to connect using the NEW certificate

Based on result:

Success: Delete the scheduled task (disarm the rollback), mark host as rotated

Failure: Leave scheduled task in place, mark host as failed — the host will auto-recover when the task fires or on next reboot

Workflow 3: Root CA Distribution to Windows Hosts

This workflow pushes all root CA certificates from the Git repository to all managed Windows hosts. It is idempotent — Windows handles "already present" gracefully.

Purpose:

Ensure Windows hosts trust all internal root CAs. This is needed for presigned URL downloads from Nutanix Objects S3 endpoint and any other internal HTTPS services Windows hosts may need to access.

Trigger:

Admin runs job template after adding new CA to root-ca/ folder in Git.

Steps:

Pull latest from Git repository

Read all .crt files from root-ca/ folder

For each managed Windows host: Push all CA certificates to Trusted Root Certification Authorities store (Windows handles idempotency natively)

Track per-host status: success, failed, unreachable

Persist state so re-runs can target only incomplete hosts

Report summary

Workflow 4: Execution Environment CA Trust Update

This workflow updates the AAP Execution Environment's CA trust store without requiring a container image rebuild.

Purpose:

Ensure the Execution Environment trusts all internal root CAs. This is required for amazon.aws.aws_s3 collection connecting to Nutanix Objects (presigned URL generation) and any other collections/modules that connect to internal TLS endpoints.

Desired Outcome:

Pull latest from Git repository

Read all .crt files from root-ca/ folder

Transform to format required by EE (Red Hat to recommend appropriate format)

Update the EE's CA trust source via the recommended mechanism

Result: Collections use system CA trust, which now includes new CAs — without rebuilding the EE image

Administrator Certificate Renewal Workflow

The annual certificate renewal should be as simple as possible for the administrator.

Desired admin experience:

Admin requests new certificate from Venafi portal, downloads the export (typically a ZIP containing an encrypted PFX)

Admin uploads the raw Venafi export (unmodified) to the Git repository (controller-certificate/ folder) via the Git web interface

Admin triggers Workflow 1 through AAP

Admin provides the PFX decryption password when prompted (this password shall be treated as sensitive data and not persisted after the workflow completes)

Admin reviews the generated onboarding script and staged materials

Admin triggers Workflow 2 to rotate existing hosts

If a new root CA was added, admin triggers Workflow 3 and Workflow 4 (or these may be automatically chained)

Key requirement:

The administrator should not need access to Linux command-line tools, OpenSSL, or manual file manipulation. The goal is that an administrator can complete annual certificate renewal by performing two (2) primary actions: uploading a file and providing a password.

CA Certificate Updates

When a new internal root CA is issued (for example, when the certificate authority used to sign the Nutanix Objects TLS certificate rotates), the administrator commits the new CA certificate file to root-ca/ in the Git repository.

Required propagation:

Workflow 3: Push new CA to all existing managed Windows workstations

Workflow 4: Update Execution Environment CA trust via ConfigMap/Secret

Workflow 1 (if re-run): Regenerate onboarding script (though new hosts only need the controller certificate's signing CA)

Operational Visibility and Recovery

All certificate management workflows involve changes across hundreds of hosts or critical infrastructure. Red Hat shall design these workflows with operational visibility as a fir

Synopsis/Notice of Intent to Sole Source 
 
The F-35 Joint Program Office (JPO) of Arlington, V A, intends to solicit, negotiate, and award a 
sole source contract under the authority of Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Federal 
Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1, “Only One Responsible Source And No Other Supplies 
or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements”, to Lockheed Martin Aeronautics (LM Aero). 
The proposed North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition 
is 541512, Computer Systems Design Services, with a small business size standard of $34.0 
million. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to Free Trade Agreements. 
 
All responsible sources may submit a capability statement in response to this notice of intent to 
sole source. The F-35 JPO will consider all capability statements received within fifteen (15) 
days after the date of publication of this pre-solicitation notice. 
 
Potential offerors must have a Top-Secret security clearance to be eligible for award. If the 
Government chooses to release a solicitation for the requirements described herein, the 
Government will provide a DD-254 form. 
 
The F-35 JPO has a requirement to support the Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers by (1) 
establishing connectivity between a Mission Data (MD) development site at Eglin AFB, FL, and 
a MD Validation & Verification (V&V) site at Lockheed Martin Aeronautics in Fort Worth, TX, 
and (2) providing the required hardware and software for said development and test. This effort 
is referred to XRL Integration and supports the creation of FMS Mission Data Files (MDF). The 
contractor shall be responsible for procuring, delivering, and installing the necessary hardware, 
software, and network infrastructure that supports MDF efforts and for interconnectivity.   
 
LM Aero is the sole designer, developer, and integrator of the F-35 aircraft, and the only entity 
with the experience, proprietary software, and technical expertise needed to equip the 
reprogramming laboratory and integrate it with a complimentary reprogramming facility. As a 
result, LM Aero is the only known qualified source able to fulfill the requirements specified 
herein. 
 
Points of contact are Jonathan Chen, Contract Specialist, at Jonathan.Chen@jsf.mil, and Colin 
McCarthy, Contracting Officer, at Colin.McCarthy@jsf.mil.

Takata Airbag Recall Data Compilation and 
Visualization Support 
  
Draft Statement of Work 
693JJ926RQ000286 
 
U.S. Department of Transportation (US DOT) 
 National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  


 
SECTION C – DESCRIPTION, SPECIFICATION, WORK STATEMENT 
1.0 Background 
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is an agency of the U.S. 
Department of Transportation (DOT).  NHTSA’s mission is to save lives, prevent injuries, and 
reduce traffic-related health care and other economic costs. The agency develops, promotes, and 
implements effective educational, engineering, and enforcement programs with the goal of 
ending preventable tragedies and reducing economic costs associated with vehicle use and 
highway travel.  NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) is responsible for identifying 
vehicle safety defects.  This is done by analyzing data received from numerous sources, 
including consumer complaints, tips and referrals, and manufacturer-submitted data such as 
warranty claims, death and injury reports, and manufacturer communications and technical 
service bulletins.  ODI also administers, on average, over 1,000 safety recalls each year, which 
include millions of motor vehicles, child seats, tires, and other automotive equipment.   
 
The Takata air bag inflator recalls are the largest and most complex automotive recalls in U.S. 
history.  These recalls involve over 60 million Takata air bag inflators in tens of millions of 
vehicles in the United States.  The recalls are due to a design defect whereby the phased-
stabilized ammonium-nitrate (PSAN) propellant used in the air bag inflator degrades, causing it 
to burn too quickly when ignited.  This defect can result in the inflator rupturing during 
deployment, essentially exploding and shooting sharp metal fragments (like shrapnel) at vehicle 
occupants.  Rupturing Takata inflators have resulted in 18 deaths in the United States and 
hundreds of injuries, including a significant number of serious injuries involving lacerations and 
other serious consequences to the occupants’ face, neck, and chest area. 
 
To address the unprecedented and varied challenges presented by the Takata recalls, NHTSA 
established a Coordinated Remedy Program in November 2015 to accelerate and coordinate the 
recalls, NHTSA appointed an Independent Monitor in December 2015 to assist NHTSA in the 
ongoing oversight of Takata and the vehicle manufacturers’ repair programs.  The Independent 
Monitor and his team have been heavily involved in the recalls for the past five years, and 
accordingly have developed a unique and nuanced understanding of the multitude of issues and 
challenges that the recalls pose. 
 
 
2.0 Scope 
The objective of this Statement of Work (SOW) is to enter into an agreement to acquire expert 
consulting services for the management of a Tableau-based data-reporting and data-visualization 
platform specifically tailored to the Takata recalls. 
  

 
3.0 Purpose 
This SOW supports NHTSA’s mission to save lives, prevent injuries, and reduce traffic-related 
health care and economic costs, as the rupturing of Takata inflators has resulted in 18 deaths in 
the United States and hundreds of injuries, including a significant number of serious injuries 
involving lacerations and other serious consequences to the occupants’ face, neck, and chest 
area. 
 
4.0 Specific Tasks 
Task 1:  Takata Recall Data Analysis 
The contractor shall support the intake and analysis of Takata recall data by providing: 
• Management of data intake and visualization output derived from vehicle manufacturer 
data submissions in the Takata recalls (containing recall-related information such as 
completion percentages, repair activity by dealer, and unrepaired air bag inflators by ZIP 
code). 
 
• Quality-control processes and data analyses, with reports accessible to registered users 
through a web-based portal for general reference as well as use in conjunction with 
owner-outreach and earned-media campaigns. 
 
 
• Utilization of the Tableau platform for the management of data intake and visualization 
output from vehicle manufacturer submissions as described above, using this platform for 
analysis and to facilitate segmentation analysis of vehicle owner populations 
(demographic and geographic), which in turn can be used to inform potential outreach 
strategies. 
 
The contractor shall: 
• Deliverable 01:  Provide NHTSA with access to data from vehicle manufacturer 
dashboard data submissions as incorporated into contractor’s data environment (SQL and 
Tableau) each month. 
  
• Deliverable 02:  Provide NHTSA with monthly quality-control reviews of vehicle 
manufacturer dashboard data submissions.  
 
• Deliverable 03:  Coordinated monthly conference calls and make available its data 
science experts to provide support to NHTSA throughout the duration of the contract. 
 
Task 2:  Project Meetings 
The contractor shall participate in regular on-site or virtual project meetings to discuss status 
specifications, work plans, schedule and related topics.  A bi-monthly status meeting shall be 
held with the task order COR. 

 
The contractor shall conduct presentations and briefings directly related to the project as 
requested by the government. 
• Deliverable 04: Status meetings held every other month with the COR and other NHTSA 
personnel. 
 
Task 3 – Kick-Off Meeting 
Resources:  Program Manager 
Within fifteen days (15) of award, the contractor shall meet with NHTSA program personnel via 
video conference to discuss the objective and performance of the contract.  During this time, the 
contractor shall present a briefing that discusses the detailed scope of the project: 
• Deliverable 05:  Kick-Off meeting notes and point of contact information. This report 
shall include: 
o Points of contact on this project 
o Background/Experience of staff who will be active on this project 
o Review and agree on status meetings 
o Schedule 
o Method (face-to-face, telephone, etc.) 
Any questions or other issues regarding the technical approach and staffing plan will be 
addressed at this time.  In addition, the administration of the contract will be discussed to ensure 
all parties understand their contractual duties and responsibilities. 
 
Task 4:  Project Management and Work Plan 
The contractor shall provide a Project Manager (PM) to provide overall management of the task 
order, and prepare meeting notes, deliverable schedule, and biweekly activity reports. 
The PM role includes, but is not limited to, the following major work streams: Project 
Management, Communications, Stakeholder Management, and Requirements Elicitation. The 
PM shall maintain daily communication and coordination with the COR when communicating 
with system stakeholders. The Contractor shall establish a solution that complies with Federal 
and DOT security requirements. 
 
• Deliverable 06:  Within two (2) weeks of task order award, the contractor shall prepare a 
Work Plan, based on the contractor’s proposal, task order negotiations with NHTSA, and 
information discussed at the kick-off meeting.  The work plan shall include: 
 
o Description of how the contractor will record information 
o Description of how the contractor will present/communicate findings to NHTSA 
 
The Work Plan shall be in written/electronic format and provided to the COR two (2) weeks after 
task order award. 
  

 
 
Task 5:  Bi-Monthly Progress Report and Teleconference 
 
Beginning thirty (30) days after Contract award, the Contractor shall provide twelve (12) bi-
monthly project status reports to the COR of the Contract by the 15
th calendar day of the month, 
following the month being reported.  The purpose of this report is to: 
 
o Describe the status of the technical tasks. 
o Update NHTSA on costs and schedule.   
 
• Deliverable 07:  The bi-monthly report shall include the following information: 
 
General Information: 
 
• Contractor name 
• NHTSA contract number 
• Contract number 
• Project title 
• Period of performance 
• Reporting period 
• Name and phone number for the NHTSA COR 
• Name and phone number for Project Manager 
 
Project Status 
 
• Accomplishments made during the reporting period; 
• Preliminary or interim results, conclusions, trends or other items of information that are 
of interest to NHTSA; 
• Plans for accomplishments in the next reporting period; 
• Problems that the contractor has experienced in conducting their services; and specific 
action that NHTSA should undertake to alleviate a problem; 
• Remaining milestones and deliverables, and their status; 
• An updated risk register; 
• Projected costs for the duration of the project; and 
• A comparison of actual versus projected costs 
 
• Deliverable 08: Pull Option -  The contractor shall provide secured (FIPS 140-2) 
compliant, read only connection accessible to authorized NHTSA personnel for the 
entirety of the period of performance (PoP).  The connection will access the data via:   
 
o Direct database connection to all relevant database objects (e.g. tables, views) 
o Database view as defined by NHTSA, or 
o Repository contain raw data file in the format of, but not limited to: 
o CSV file with a format defined by NHTSA 
o XML file with a schema defined by NHTSA 

 
• Deliverable 09:  Push Option – The contractor will email a password protected data file 
to selected NHTSA personnel every month and when requested by NHTSA during the 
period of performance (PoP).  The data file will be in the format of, but not limited to: 
 
o CSV file with a format defined by NHTSA 
o XML file with a schema defined by NHTSA

STATEMENT OF WORK (SERVICES) 
(SOW) 
 
GENERAL INFORMATION 
Title of Project: 
Support for XNAT instance for FMRIF. 
 
Statement of Need and Purpose: 
The Functional MRI Facility (FMRIF) in the National Inst itute of Mental Health (NIMH) is seeking support 
for its data and workflow management platform, XNAT, which currently aggregates data from multiple  MRI 
scanners in the NMR Center (where FMRIF’s and other  IC’s scanners are located), provides access to 
these data to the users of these scanners, and also serves as platforms for managing, sharing, and 
processing these data. 
 
Background Information and Objective: 
Since its inception, FMRIF has operated a series of web-based platforms that serve to both aggregate 
image data from the MRI scanners ow ned and operated by the FMRIF, and to share these data out to its 
users, so they could securely retrieve their data using a web browser, or other web-based tools.  The first 
such service used by FMRIF was a commercial PACS system from Intelerad.  However, as both the number 
of scans conducted on FMRIF scanners rose, along with the volume of Functional MRI data generated, 
FMRIF encountered significant performance issues that could not be resolved by the vendor of that system.  
FMRIF then investigated multiple options to replace the Intelerad system, exploring both commercial and 
open source software (including, but not limited to, dcm4chee, XNAT, COINS, and  NiDB).  In all cases, 
there were either significant deficiencies, and / or la ck of flexibility, that prec luded use of any of these 
packages by FMRIF.  Ultimately , a custom database and web application was created in-house, by a 
FMRIF-employed programmer, and that platform served FMRIF for almost a decade.  However, in 2020, 
because of a loss of staff and expertise with FMRIF’s in-house data management systems, FMRIF sought 
a commercial option, with support, to replace its in-house data management solution.  That contract 
(75N95020P00651) was awarded to Radiologics to help FMRIF deploy, migrate data to, and support a 
single instance of XNAT.  This was successfully rolled out to FMRIF’s and other Facilities’ users, and now 
FMRIF seeks an agreement to continue supporting it s XNAT instance for its data warehousing, 
management, and processing needs. 
 
Period of Performance: 
Support for 1 year is required, starting on ASAP in FY 26, with 4 additional opti on years of support also 
being requested. 
 
SCOPE OF WORK 
General Requirements: 
Independently and not as an agent of the Government, the Contractor shall furnish all the necessary 
services, qualified personnel, material, equipment, and facilities, not otherwise provided by the Government 
as needed to perform the Statement of Work below:

Page 2 of 4 
 
Specific Requirements: 
 
Support of FMRIF’s XNAT platform includes: 
• Updating XNAT software on supported instances to provide new capabilities, and address any 
emergent performance and security issues. 
• Updating integration with institutional authentic ation system (LDAP and Active Directory) to 
facilitate user authentication and system access. 
• Maintaining and updating interfaces with multiple MR scanner vendors to allow automatic capture 
and aggregation both raw (k-space) and DICOM data generated by these vendors’ platforms. 
• Supporting transport of acquire d and computed DICOM data between (i.e. send to and receive 
from) the platform and commercial PACS systems, and MR scanners 
• Continue to provide training and training materi als for FMRIF staff and users to administer and use 
the system. 
• Continue to develop and provide tools for versi on tracking and maintaining provenance of data and 
analysis pipelines. 
• Support scaling of compute and storage needs as the number of scanners, aggregated studies, 
and data processing compute loads increase.  
• Develop and support interfaces for visualizi ng and analyzing data, including, but not limited to, 
derivation of basic quality assurance metrics. 
• Continue supporting tools and / or interfaces for metadata search and management.  
• Supporting and developing tools to leverage OCI-compliant containers for data processing, 
including, but not limited to, containers providing tools such as AFNI, FreeSurfer, and FSL. 
• Support interfacing with large- scale batch processing system such as slurm and PBS on local HPC 
and commercial cloud compute resources. 
• Support exporting image and study data into BIDS  (Brain Imaging Data Structure) compliant data 
sets. 
• Support providing automated and customizable dat a anonymization / de-identification for exported 
datasets. 
• Support open REST-based APIs to all services  and data, and support for external language SDKs 
(e.g. MATLAB, Python, and R). 
• Provide mechanisms and interfaces for validat ion of data uploads into the system, and detection 
and logging of errors or omissions with such uploads. 
• Support command line integration access to API to facilitate scripting, data import and export, job 
scheduling and status, and building analysis pipelines. 
• Provide guaranteed response times to customer qu eries about issues, acknowledging of receipt of 
report of issues within 24 hours, with a 4 week window to resolving any issues raised. 
• Develop and provide options to consolidate dat a storted by XNAT on disk into fewer objects, 
allowing backup of XNAT to tape, and providing a more streamlined path for XNAT sites to migrate 
their instnaces to cloud services. 
• Keeping software deployed at, developed for, NIH open source, and available to the wider research 
community. 
• Provide at least 3 references wh o can attest to ability and experience supporting XNAT instances. 
 

Version 11-30-2016-1 
FAR Part 11—Describing Agency Needs 
Page 3 of 4 
 
LEVEL OF EFFORT: 
The contractor is expected to employ staff fa miliar with DICOM communication protocols, understand 
various computer network communication protocols and security standards, and also familiar with medical 
imaging data processing requirements.  Staff should be intimately familia r with the XNAT application, its 
operation, and should have extensive experience developing software and features that work both within, 
and interact with, the XNAT application. 
 
GOVERNMENT RESPONSIBILITIES: 
The government will supply all information necessary for contractor to complete their efforts. The 
government will also provide either physical or virtual computer systems on which the software platform will 
be deployed.  Under a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the contractor and government, the 
government will also provide remote access to vendor to system(s) on which the platform is deployed, to 
facilitate trouble-shooting, and performance and feature enhancements. 
 
DELIVERY OR DELIVERABLES: 
The contractor must deploy the scientific imaging data management system to a FMRIF-operated physical 
or virtual computers, and demonstrate how its operations meets and conforms to the above-listed “Specific 
Requirements.”  The contractor must also help ma intain the performance of the system, as well its 
adherence to all security policies and requirements. 
 
REPORTING REQUIREMENTS: 
The contractor should report general performance me trics of the platform (relative compute load, and 
storage usage).  The contractor should also report  when systems are access ed, and for what purposes 
was access made.  The contractor should also notify when system patches and updates become available, 
to enhance performance of the platform, as well as satisfy security and policy requirements. 
 
OTHER CONSIDERATIONS: 
Travel: 
No travel costs are anticipated to execute tis contract.  Any and all travel costs are expected to be covered 
by the costs of this contract. 
 
Key Personnel: 
The relevant key personnel have been specified under the “Level of Effort” section. 
 
Information System Security Plan: 
This statement of work requires the contractor to (1) develop, (2) have the ability to access, and (3) maintain 
a federal information system.  All work on this pla tform, and access to the machines on it will be under a 
Memorandum of Understanding betw een the contract and NIH’s Center  for Information Technology.  
Contractor will maintain systems to provide best perf ormance, and also maintain compliance with current 
NIH policies and requirements. 
 
Data Rights: 
Any data generated by this procurement or system will belong to the Government.  The Government will 
retain all rights over any generated data.

the Workforce Investment Act of 1998 (P.L. 105-220), August 7, 1998.  This system will not be accessible 
to the general public – it will only be accessible NIH employees with the relevant training. 
 
Publications and Publicity: 
This SOW is not expected to generate any publications. 
Confidentiality of Information: 
This SOW is not expected to utilize or generate any confidential information.

### Sheet: Experience
PBES RFI - Experience
Questions
What experience, if any, do you have with supporting the Department of Air Force (DAF) Planning, Programming, and Budgeting (PPB) processes--both MAJCOM and Air Staff?  Please provide examples.
Describe your experience and internal process for creating system training materials.  Based on your familiarity with PBES what are your recomendations to implement changes and improvements to the current training material.
Describe your level of experience and/or any certifications held with each the following: Enterprise Performance Management (EPM), Oracle Analytics Server (OAS), Oracle DB Server, Oracle Data Integrator (ODI), Oracle DRM, Oracle HTTP Server (OHS), Oracle Hyperion Planning, Essbase, Oracle Internet Directory, Oracle Weblogic Server, RHEL, Windows Server 2019 and newer.   If so, please describe how those experiences would be used to support PBES and it's mission to generate Program Objective Memorandum, Budget Estimate Submissin, Rapid Allocation Process, and President's Budget seamlessly. Describe your specific experience managing and configuring Oracle DRM or a similar Master Data Management (MDM) tool within a federal financial context. How do you ensure data governance and stewardship?
Describe your experience in developing, maintaining, and troubleshooting automated data interfaces between a primary system like PBES and external authoritative data sources. Please provide an example where you successfully automated an interface that was previously a manual process.
Please provide contract number, name of customer/organization supported, customer/organization POC including contact information for the questions listed above, if applicable.

### Sheet: Staffing
PBES RFI - Staffing
Questions
What certifications or qualifications would you recommend your staff hold in areas such as software development, cybersecurity, database/system administration, or project management? Do you currently have personnel with the recommended certifications and qualifications to work PBES should they receive authorization to do so?
PBES is hosted on the SIPR network; can you provide a capability support team that has the appropriate security clearances and IA (IAT II or higher) Workforce Certifications to sustain a classified system?
Do you currently have Functional Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) on staff? Functional SME’s must be experts with the POM (Program Ojective Memorandum) , BES (Budget Estimate Submission) and PB (President's Budget) processes from Major Command level to Office of Secretary of Defense.  This includes the Programming function with the different AF panels through the Appropriation Managers on the Budget side of the process. The SMEs must also be familiar with the entire PPB&E process and how it all ties together.  They must be able to integrate the 30-year Plan with the Programming and Budget FYDP (Five Year Defense Plan).
Please provide contract number, name of customer/organization supported, customer/organiztion POC including contact information for the questions listed above, if applicable.

### Sheet: Management
PBES RFI - Management
Questions
Can you describe the recommended team structure, including roles (e.g., system analysts, software engineers, database administrators)?  Can you describe how your team would collaborate with the functional customer (e.g. a Functional Management Office (FMO)) and the Program Management Office (PMO) to ensure seamless POM, BES, PB development?
How would you plan to allocate staff resources for a POM/PB project?  Can you provide details on staffing levels, including full-time equivalents (FTEs) and any subcontractors?  What contingency plans would you put in place to address unexpected staff shortages or turnover?
How would your company handle data validation for rounds (versions within the cycle that add rates, manpower, DAF decisions)  during budget cycles? What steps would you take to update financial or performance data? How would you manage changes and ensure consistency in the data?
Describe your management approach for supporting cybersecurity readiness and providing software ugrades to PBES while delivering new capabiilty and keeping PBES operational (minimum downtime).
How would you manage the project timeline, milestones, and deliverables?  What communication channels would you use to keep the Government informed of your progress and to address any issues?  How would you manage risk and how would you share those risks with the FMO and PMO?
How would you handle changes to requirements, scope, or priorities during the project? Outline your change management process.  What mechanisms would you use to communicate changes to the Government?
Describe your approach to quality assurance (QA) and testing. How would you verify the accuracy and reliability of the IT system the DAF uses to generate a POM and PB?  What testing methodologies (e.g., unit testing, integration testing) would your team employ?
This customer operates under very stringent timelines.  What project management tools and techniques do you use to ensure timely and within-budget delivery?
Regarding standing up/building development environments, what  critical milestones or phases would you include in a schedule or timeline? How would you account for potential delays or unforeseen challenges?  What resources (human and technical) would you allocate to meet the timeline? On average, what is the timeline to build a development environment?
The Government will provide a development environment (DevLab). Describe your experience working within a Government-Furnished Environment. How do you manage configurations, dependencies, and documentation when you do not control the underlying infrastructure?
Please provide contract number, name of customer/organization supported, customer/organiztion POC including contact information for the questions listed above, if applicable.

### Sheet: Processes
PBES RFI - Processes
Questions
Would you provide training to government personnel on using the IT system for POM and PB generation?  How would you transfer knowledge and documentation to ensure long-term sustainability?
Describe how you would align domain subject matter expertise with leading technologies to drive transformation for DAF financial planning/financial management information systems—specifically program and budgeting systems—while leveraging leading commercial software and best practices.
How would your company ensure accurate and reliable data within the annual PPB (POM, RAP, BES, PB) process?  What validation rules or procedures would you follow to verify data integrity?  Are there any specific tools or methodologies you would employ for data validation?  Are there opportunities to leverage BOTS or other automated technology for accelerating data validation exercises?
Provide examples of risks encountered in previous similar projects and how you managed them to ensure project success.
How would you deliver—using Agile, CI/CD, DevSecOps processes—new capabilities for approved requirements while addressing/reducing significant technical debt in a Cloud One environment?
How would you provide "over the shoulder" support to PBES end users in the Pentagon to include supporting with data loading, data validation, use of PBES, etc?
Describe the process you would use to support the PBES PMO/FMO with requirements development, requirements prioritization, product backlog refinement, program increment planning, sprint planning, daily scrum, sprint review, sprint retrospectives, leadership reviews, demonstrations, technical interchanges and engineering reviews.
Tell us about your PPBE experience and experience with systems that supports that process.  Expand how you would validate accuracy and support the system workflow processes and procedures.
What processes would you use in PBES to support Financial and Program Structures such as PE numbers, appropriate codes, program codes, operating agency codes, weapon system codes, program activity codes, and J-books?
Beyond general quality assurance, what is your specific approach to performance and load testing, particularly in preparation for peak usage during critical POM/BES/PB budget cycles? Describe the tools and metrics you would use to ensure the system remains stable and responsive under stress.
Please provide contract number, name of customer/organization supported, customer/organiztion POC including contact information for the questions listed above, if applicable.
