standards.  The contractor shall develop and maintain an effective Quality Control 110 
Plan (QCP) (CDRL A001), which outlines quality procedures and includes a self-111 
inspection and internal coordination plan. The QCP shall establish a formal 112 
Change Control process to manage, document, and validate any modifications to 113 
the system or its configuration post-deployment. Required revisions must be made 114 
within 5 working days. 115 
• Staffing Plan: The contractor shall develop, maintain, and deliver a Staffing Plan 116 
(D003) that details the roles and labor categories required to successfully execute 117 
all tasks specified in the task order.  118 
• Contract Reporting and Administration: The contractor shall manage the 119 
timely development and submission of all contract deliverables as delineated in 120 
the PWS and Sections 33-36.  121 
• Financial and Contract Reporting: The contractor shall provide a Monthly 122 
Progress Report (D00) detailing performance against schedule, budget, and 123 
objectives.  124 
• Kick-Off Meeting: The contractor shall conduct a kick-off meeting with the 125 
Government for each awarded task order. The purpose of this meeting is to ensure 126 
a shared understanding of the task order requirements, establish lines of 127 
communication, and review the contractor's planned approach.  128 
3.2 Deployment Planning and Execution 129 
The contractor shall employ an adaptable framework for planning and executing all 130 
deployments. This framework ensures that each project, regardless of scale or location, 131 
moves from concept to sustained operation in a deliberate and controlled manner. 132 
3.2.1 Initiation and Planning 133 
During initiation and planning, the focus shall be on discovery and creating the blueprint 134 
for successful deployment. 135 
• The Deployment Approach (CDRL A003) is the foundation for the 136 
Implementation Plan (CDRL A010). The contractor shall provide the overall 137 
approach and methodology for deployment, training, user adoption, change 138 
management, and communications across multiple environments/networks, 139 
fixed/expeditionary facilities for multiple products, and with different federal 140 
partners (DoW and non-DoW).  The contractor shall include any potential 141 
opportunities, risks, issues, and dependencies for each area, and mitigation plans. 142 
• Deployment Readiness Assessment (D008): The contractor shall provide a 143 
Deployment Readiness Assessment, which is a formal and systematic evaluation 144 
used to determine if an organization, its users, and the technology itself are fully 145 
prepared for a successful "go-live" event. This assessment is a comprehensive 146 
review that measures preparedness against a predefined set of criteria, moving 147 

 
5 
 
beyond just technical functionality to include people, processes, and support 148 
systems. The contractor shall identify risks, gaps, and potential points of failure 149 
that could jeopardize the deployment's success, disrupt operations, or hinder user 150 
adoption.   151 
• Implementation Plan (CDRL A010): Based on the Readiness Assessment, the 152 
contractor shall develop, maintain, and actively manage an implementation plan, 153 
to include a detailed Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) (CDRL A011). The 154 
Implementation Plan is the detailed tactical execution plan that operationalizes the 155 
approach outlined in the Deployment Approach. 156 
3.2.2 Configuration, Validation, and Implementation 157 
As specified in the task order, the contractor shall perform configuration, validation, and 158 
implementation activities required for deployment, culminating in the formal cutover 159 
event. 160 
• Data Collection: As specified by the task order, the contractor shall facilitate the 161 
timely and accurate collection of all required product configuration data (Product 162 
Configuration Data (D009)).  163 
• Product(s) Configuration: The contractor shall execute the configuration 164 
activities as specified in the task order.  DHMS products may include hardware 165 
and/or component installation and configuration across various networks. This 166 
may include user role assignment, security permissions, and system-level 167 
parameters. 168 
• Cutover: The contractor shall manage the cutover to the new product(s).  Specific 169 
activities will be specified in individual task orders.   170 
 171 
3.2.3 Stabilization and Transition 172 
The contractor shall stabilize the new environment and ensure a seamless hand-off to 173 
sustainment teams. 174 
• Post-Deployment Stabilization Support: The contractor shall implement and 175 
manage a multi-tiered user support structure to provide rapid and effective 176 
assistance, including on-site "at-the-elbow" and remote support as defined in the 177 
task order. 178 
• Post-Deployment Stabilization Report (D010): The contractor shall provide a 179 
daily report during the Post-Deployment Support period as defined in the task 180 
order. This report will include status of tickets, devices, user support, and other 181 
key indicators of a successful transition.  182 
• Transition to Sustainment: The contractor shall execute a formal transition plan 183 
to hand off the fully deployed and stabilized product(s) to the Government 184 
sustainment and operations teams. 185 

 
6 
 
3.3 Hardware Delivery and Connectivity 186 
The contractor shall manage the procurement, end-to-end logistics using DD Form 1149 187 
(D011), installation, and network integration of all required hardware as delineated in the 188 
task order. The desired outcome is that all physical components are identified, delivered, 189 
installed, connected, and functioning as intended in their designated operational 190 
environment based on Government requirements. 191

The contractor shall ensure seamless integration with existing network infrastructure, 193

1 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) PURPOSE AND GOVERNMENTS 
DISCLAIMERS  
1.1 PURPOSE 
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to request 
detailed data, innovative approaches, and strategic insights from industry partners regarding their 
capabilities and readiness to (1) support the transition of the National Airspace System (NAS) and its 
supporting Air Traffic Control (ATC) infrastructure to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) and (2) support 
the transition of FAA business systems to PQC. 
The NAS is undergoing a generational transformation to realize a modern, resilient, and globally leading 
ATC system capable of integrating new entrants ( e.g., drones, Advanced Air Mobility (AAM), and 
commercial space operations). Achieving this vision requires a secure foundation capable of withstanding 
emerging threats, including those posed by quantum computing. W ithout quantum‑resistant, crypto‑agile 
security, the NAS cannot achieve the reliability, performance, or international leadership required in th e 
decades ahead. FAA therefore views PQC not as a compliance exercise, but as a foundational enabler of 
modernization—one that must be embedded into every vendor solution, every system upgrade, and every 
step of the Brand New Air Traffic Control System (“BNATCS”)1. 
Specifically, th is RFI seeks industry input on the challenging and mandatory transition of both FAA 
enterprise IT and FAA NAS safety-critical ATC systems to quantum-resistant algorithms to meet federal 
mandates, while managing the high cost, complex recertification, and potential operational disruption of 
integrating new cryptography into FAA operations.  The Government is also seeking information regarding 
the most effective architecture for the enterprise-wide transition to PQC. As National Institute of Standard 
(NIS) standards continue to finalize, the Government is evaluating the feasibility of a "One -Stop Shop" 
(Integrated Suite) approach versus a "Best-of-Breed" (Modular Component) approach. The goal is to ensure 
FAA NAS and FAA non-NAS systems remain "crypto-agile" while minimizing implementation risks and 
interoperability gaps.  FAA recognizes that the PQC market is still maturing and that potential vendors may 
not currently possess the internal capability to execute a fully  integrated solution. Specifically, the FAA 
acknowledges that: 
• A single provider may not have validated all necessary cryptographic primitives across all hardware 
and software layers.   
 
1 https://www.faa.gov/new-atcs 

 
 
2 
 
• A provider’s offerings may not support both FAA Information Technology (IT) and FAA 
Operational Technology (OT) systems. 
• Integration of PQC into legacy National Airspace System (NAS) infrastructure or legacy FAA 
business infrastructure may require specialized expertise that exceeds the scope of a single product 
suite. 
1.2 REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. 
This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a Request for 
Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Your response will be treated as information 
only, and it shall not be used as a proposal. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any 
supply or service whatsoever. 
The Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept unsolicited proposals. 
Respondents are advised that the Government will not reimburse any costs associated with preparing or 
submitting a response to this RFI. Submission of a response does not guarantee participation in any future 
solicitation or resulting contract award. Information obtained through this RFI may be used to inform the 
FAA’s acquisition strategy for PQC modernization. The FAA, at its sole discretion, may contact one, some, 
all, or none of the respondents to the RFI and ask for additional information. 
 
1.3 GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT  
Jackson LeMay 
Contract Specialist 
Jackson.T.LeMay@faa.gov  
 
Kristin Frantz 
Contracting Officer 
Kristin.T.Frantz@faa.gov  
1.4 RESPONSE INSTRUCTION  
Vendors are requested to respond to the questions in Section 3 in a clear, concise, and thorough manner. 
Responses to this RFI must be received electronically by email to the government points of contact in 
Section 1.3 above no later than 4:00 PM Eastern Time on April 24, 2026. Responses received after this date 
and time may not be considered.  The email subject line MUST adhere to the following format: RFI 
Response: [697DCK-26-RFI-PQC– Company Name]. 

 
 
3 
 
ZIP files, executable files (.exe), or links to external cloud storage drives will NOT be accepted for security 
reasons. 
Responses must use a standard 11-point font (e.g., Times New Roman, Arial, or Aptos) with at least 1-inch 
margins on all sides. All pages must be sequentially numbered.  The total response (excluding the cover 
page, table of contents, and proprietary legends) should NOT exceed 30 pages in length.  The Government 
reserves the right to disregard any content beyond the 30-page  limit.  All content responding to RFI 
questions, diagrams, charts, graphs, and executive summaries ARE included in the page count.   The 
following are excluded from the total page count: Cover Page, Table of Contents, Corporate 
Background/PQC Expertise, and Glossary/Acronym List. 
 
1.5 PROPRIETARY INFORMATION  
Respondents are strongly advised not to include in their responses any (1) information that they consider to 
be a trade secret (as defined under the Trade Secret Act (18 U.S.C. § 1905)) and (2) commercial or financial 
information that is  privileged or confidential  (“Proprietary Information”) , unless such information is 
essential for the Government to evaluate the response.  Respondents grant to the Government unlimited 
rights to use, modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose the information contained in the 
responses, except for Proprietary Information. Respondents grant to the Government limited rights to use, 
modify, reproduce, release, perform, display, or disclose Proprietary Information for government purposes, 
including competitive procurement. Government purposes do not include public disclosure. 
Proprietary Information  submitted in  response to this RFI must be clearly and conspicuously marked . 
Proper marking is necessary for the Government to identify Proprietary Information as such , including for 
exemption from the public disclosure requirements under the Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) 
(FOIA), specifically Exemption 4 (which protects against public disclosure of trade secrets and confidential 
commercial or financial information). The marking should be included in the transmittal page and on each 
page of the response clearly and with specificity identifying therein the Proprietary Information. Responses 
without appropriate markings will be treated as having been submitted with unlimited rights . The 
Government will not be liable for any use, disclosure, release, reproduction, modification, display and/or 
performance of any Proprietary Information not properly marked by the vendor.  
If the submission contains any proprietary information, a second, redacted version suitable for public 
release MUST also be provided as a separate PDF file. The file name for the redacted version must be 
clearly marked: RFI_ 697DCK-26-RFI-PQC_[Company Name] _PublicRelease.pdf.

2 POST-QUANTUM CRYPTOGRAPHY (PQC) MIGRATION FOR FAA 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND NAS AIR TRAFFIC CONTROL 
(ATC) SYSTEMS 
The migration of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) systems, encompassing both enterprise 
Information Technology (IT) and the safety-critical National Air Space (NAS) infrastructure, to Post -
Quantum Cryptography (PQC) represents an immediate and foundat ional security imperative.  The 
transition to enhanced cryptography is paramount due to the nature of FAA operations and the focus on 
safety, security, data integrity, confidentiality, and system authentication. This transition must be initiated 
now, given the inherent conflict between the rapid progression toward cryptographically relevant quantum 
computers (CRQC), which some projections estimate may appear in less than 10 years, and the 
characteristically slow, multi-year integration timelines required for the deployment of new cryptographic 
algorithms across large, complex information systems 
  
The industry responses to this RFI will help to inform FAA of the development of cost estimates required 
by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for strategic planning and resource allocation.  
Introducing PQC, which may necessitate deep structural modifications to both hardware and software 
across the NAS, could profoundly affect the projected benefits, costs, and timelines of ongoing Air Traffic 
Control (ATC) System improvements.  This RFI explicitly requests vendor analysis on the potential 
disruption or delay caused by PQC insertion into both NAS ATC as well as FAA Information Technology 
systems.     
 
Since FAA is currently in the fact-finding phase of its transition to PQC, it is not committed to any specific 
procurement model and is evaluating the feasibility of both a "One -Stop Shop" (Integrated) approach and 
an "Individual Component" (Modular) approach. 
 
• Model A: Integrated Enterprise Solution (One-Stop Shop)  
In this model, a single lead integrator or vendor provides a comprehensive, pre -validated PQC suite 
including algorithm implementation, key management, and hardware integration. The Government is 
interested in understanding the trade -offs regarding vendor lock -in versus the speed of deployment and 
simplified compliance auditing. 
 
• Model B: Modular Component/Subsystem Approach  
In this model, the Government would source individual subsystems —such as NIST -standardized Key 
Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEMs), Digital Signature algorithms, and PQC -ready Hardware Security

B.4 STATEMENT OF WORK

1. Background. 

The Environmental Management Service (EMS) at the VA San Diego Healthcare System requires a customer feedback monitoring service to support restroom cleanliness monitoring and service response. The system will allow patients, visitors, and staff to provide real-time feedback regarding restroom conditions and notify EMS personnel when cleaning or supply services are required.

The objective is to improve restroom cleanliness, responsiveness to service issues, and overall patient experience through real-time data collection and reporting.

2. Scope. 

The contractor shall provide a software-based restroom feedback monitoring service that collects real-time customer feedback data and alerts EMS personnel of restroom service needs.

The contractor shall provide all software, system hosting, communications services, data processing, reporting capability, and technical support necessary to operate the restroom feedback monitoring system.

The service shall support approximately 58 restroom feedback terminals currently installed throughout the VA San Diego Medical Center. The Government will provide the existing feedback terminals. The contractor shall ensure system connectivity, monitoring capability, and data reporting functionality.

3. Salient Characteristics  

Real-Time Feedback Monitoring
3.1 Collect and process customer satisfaction feedback from restroom feedback terminals in real time.
3.2 Record timestamp and terminal location associated with each feedback response.
3.3 Allow EMS personnel to monitor restroom conditions through a centralized interface.

Alert Notification Capability
3.4 Provide automated alerts when restroom service issues are reported (e.g., dirty restroom, missing supplies).
3.5  Notifications shall be capable of delivery via email alerts, SMS text alerts, mobile application notifications, or web dashboard alerts.

Reporting and Analytics
3.6  Provide real-time dashboard capability.
3.7  Generate restroom cleanliness and performance reports.
3.8 Identify trends in restroom satisfaction and service response times.
3.9 Reports must be exportable in Excel, PDF, or CSV format.

System Access
3.10  Secure web-based administrative dashboard.
3.11 Multiple user accounts for EMS personnel.
3.12 Mobile access capability for authorized users.

Data Management
3.13 Provide system hosting and data storage.
3.14 Ensure data integrity and security.
• Allow export of raw data for VA analysis.

Technical Support
3.15 Provide system troubleshooting, maintenance, and updates.
3.16 Support availability Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM Eastern Time, excluding federal holidays.

4. Quality Assurance 

The contractor shall ensure the feedback monitoring system remains operational and capable of transmitting and reporting data from all active terminals.

The contractor shall perform periodic system checks to verify system connectivity and reporting functionality.

5. Period of Performance

The task order shall cover services for a base period of one (1) year with option to exercise up to (4) one-year option periods.

Call for Solutions for

Airspace Common Operating Picture

Note: Please advise the cognizant Procurement Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist as soon as possible via the email above if your organization intends to submit a Solution Brief in response to this Call for Solution.

Any submissions that are received by the Procurement Contracting Officer (PCO) after the suspense date/time listed above will be deemed late and not evaluated. It is the sole responsibility of the company to ensure that its submission is received in the inbox listed above before the deadline specified.

Description:

The U.S. Army Contracting Command - Orlando (ACC-Orlando) is issuing this Call for Solutions under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 3458 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Subpart 212.70. This Call for Solutions is intended to competitively acquire innovative commercial products or technologies to support the development and deployment of the: 

Airspace Common Operating Picture (A-COP) 

The U.S. Army requires an advanced airspace management capability to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant operations within Special Use Airspace (SUA) at Army installations. Current systems lack the ability to provide real-time surveillance, monitoring, and deconfliction of manned aircraft and Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Groups 1-5, as defined by AR 95-2, AR 350-52, AR 385-63, and TC 3-04.15. This capability gap poses significant risks to safety, operational effectiveness, and compliance with Army regulations.

The envisioned solution must integrate real-time data from manned and unmanned platforms, including Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) equipped military and civilian aircraft, and provide situational awareness to Range Management Authorities (RMA). The system must operate continuously, with minimal latency, and deliver precise positional data to support safe operations in high-density environments. Additionally, the solution must align with the Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) to ensure compatibility with current and future tactical networks, such as the Tactical Awareness Kit (TAK) and Range Facility Management Support System (RFMSS). The solution must also be scalable, customizable, and capable of supporting operations across multiple installations listed in the Basis of Issue Plan. It must provide flexible data relay options, customizable alerts, and ensure secure operations within a limited-access network. 

1.1	The U.S. Army seeks innovative commercial solutions that address the following attributes: 

Real-Time Airspace Surveillance and Monitoring:

Systems capable of integrating data from multiple sources, including ADS-B, radar, and other sensors, to provide a comprehensive airspace picture.

Solutions that support continuous, low-latency operations in high-density environments.

Deconfliction of Manned and Unmanned Aircraft:

Tools for real-time deconfliction of UAS Groups 1-5 and manned aircraft operating within SUA.

Capabilities to provide automated alerts and recommendations to Range Management Authorities (RMA).

Integration with Tactical Networks:

Solutions that align with the Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) and are compatible with existing Army systems, such as the Tactical Awareness Kit (TAK) and Range Facility Management Support System (RFMSS).

Systems that support future scalability and interoperability with emerging technologies.

Scalability and Customizability:

Solutions that can be deployed across multiple Army installations and adapted to varying operational requirements.

Customizable alerting mechanisms, data relay options, and user interfaces to meet mission-specific needs.

Secure Operations:

Systems that ensure secure data transmission and operations within limited-access networks.

Compliance with Army cybersecurity standards and protocols.

Advanced Data Analytics and Visualization:

Tools for advanced data processing, visualization, and reporting to enhance situational awareness and decision-making.

Capabilities to provide predictive analytics for airspace management.

Awarding Instrument

This Call for Solution solicitation will be awarded in accordance with the Army Open Solicitation procedures detailed within Solicitation W9128Z-25-S-A002, posted to SAM.gov on 01 May 2025. This Call for Solution will utilize CSO procedures. Use of a CSO in accordance with DFARS Subpart 212.70 in conjunction with FAR 35 and DFARS 235 is considered to be a competitive procedure for the purposes of 10 U.S.C. chapter 221 and FAR 6.102.

Solicitation Notes

In addition to the general guidelines included in the Open Solicitation, the following guidelines apply to this Call for Solution.

Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for any amendments to this solicitation that may have updated information.

The Government will give preference to submissions that demonstrate an innovative, existing, and reference-verifiable commercial ability to accomplish the desired solution attributes listed above.

Resellers and academic research proposals are not desired.

All solution briefs will be valid for 180 calendar days after the submission date.

The Solution Brief must identify any intellectual property involved in the effort and associated restrictions on the Government’s use of that intellectual property.

The Government reserves the right to go directly from Solution Brief to award.

General Information and Questions

Questions are to be sent only to the Procurement Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist (POCs) listed in this Call for Solution. The following shall be utilized in the email subject line: Call for Solution – CPE-STRI-ACOP (reference the section area). Material questions and answers will be published and updated on www.sam.gov.

Phase 0: Solicitation for Solution Briefs

Interested offerors must submit a concise solution brief (maximum 10-page white paper or 20 slides) addressing the following:

Executive Summary: Overview of the proposed solution and its relevance to the desired solution under this Call for Solutions.

Technology Concept: Description of the innovative aspects of the solution, including any required development or adaptation. Show and/or describe how your proposed solution or potential new capabilities represent an application of innovative commercial products, innovative commercial technologies or adaptations/modifications of existing commercial product technologies to the A-COP.

Company Viability: Overview of the company including relevant experience.

Intellectual Property (IP): Description of any proprietary technologies or data rights.

Submission Guidelines:

Interested offerors shall include Company Name, Title, Date, Point of Contact Name, E-Mail Address, Phone, and Address.

The title page does not count against page limit, however, the executive summary does.

The period of performance of the contract resulting from this Call for Solutions should generally be no greater than five (5) years.

Technical data with military application may require approval, authorization, or license for lawful exportation.

All solution briefs, presentations, and proposals must be Unclassified. Do NOT mark any documents as “CONFIDENTIAL”. Solution briefs, presentations, and proposals containing data that is not to be disclosed to the public for any purpose or use by the government except for evaluation purposes shall include the following general disclaimer on the cover page:

“This [select one: solution brief, Presentation, or Proposal] includes data that shall not be disclosed outside the government, except to non-government personnel for evaluation purposes, and shall not be duplicated, used, or disclosed - in whole or in part - for any purpose other than to evaluate this submission. If, however, an agreement is awarded to this company as a result of - or in connection with - the submission of this data, the government shall have the right to duplicate, use, or disclose the data to the extent agreed upon by both parties in the resulting agreement. This restriction does not limit the government's right to use information contained in this data if it is obtained from another source without restriction. The data subject to this restriction are contained in sheets [insert numbers or other identification of sheets]” 

Submissions must be submitted electronically.

Offerors that are not chosen for the presentation phase will be notified in writing as soon as practicable. Further verbal feedback may be provided, upon request, at the Contracting/Agreements Officer’s discretion.

Phase 1: Solution Brief Evaluation

The Government will conduct an initial down select based on solution briefs submitted in Phase 0. Upon review of a solution brief, the Government may elect to invite “all, some or none” of the proposed solutions into Phase 2, the presentation/pitch based on the merits of the solution brief. In Phase 2, companies are invited to pitch and further discuss their proposed concept/technology/solution in person or virtually. During Phase 2, the Government may request and/or provide additional information to the company.

Solution Briefs will be evaluated on the following criteria:

Technical merit of the proposed solution, including the extent to which the proposed solution is unique, and/or innovative to fulfill the requirement for the A-COP. Technical Merit is defined as having direct relevance to the stated requirement, addressing identified capability gaps, and providing innovative technological advancements. 

The government may elect to use external market research in the evaluation of a company’s viability.

Phase 2: Solution Presentation/Pitch

Down selected offerors will be invited to present their solutions to the Government and to participate in a live demonstration. The presentation shall include:

Detailed technical and business viability of the solution

Proposed schedule and milestones

Anticipated data rights assertions

Explanation of Data Rights

Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) pricing: Estimated cost and payment terms.

7.2.		Participation in the live demonstration in a relevant environment will be coordinated by the Government.

Phase 2: Presentation/Pitch Evaluation

Individual presentations/pitches will be evaluated against the evaluation criteria below and not against any other presentations/pitches. Presentation/pitch submissions will be valid for 120 days after pitch evaluation. The government will aim to complete evaluation of presentation/pitches within 30 calendar days of the presentation/pitch. After completing the evaluation of presentation/pitch submissions, the government will notify the company that: they may submit a Full Proposal for evaluation in Phase 3; or their proposed concept/technology/solution is not of continued interest to the Government, and they will not be required to submit a Full Proposal and advance to Phase 3. 

Presentation/Pitch evaluation criteria are listed in order of importance from top to bottom. Presentation/pitches shall be evaluated/scored on the following factors:

Level of relevancy of the solution in addressing the A-COP with a commercially available product and/or process;

The technical merit of the proposed solution adequately addressed the A-COP and demonstrated feasibility for the Government to pursue the proposed solution;

Level of uniqueness, and/or innovative approach to solve the Government’s need;

Level of technical risk/maturity;

Level of risk placed with the proposed ROM;

Level of risk in the proposed milestone schedule and its ability to meet the A-COP requirement within a relevant time period;

Level of risk in the company’s viability and business solution; and

Level of potential risk in anticipated IP and data rights assertions

 Phase 3: Full Proposal

Based upon the results of market research, Phase 1 and/or Phase 2 evaluation(s) above, the government may request a proposal. If that occurs, a company, or companies will be invited to develop and submit a written proposal as well as negotiate appropriate terms and conditions, as applicable, governing the requirement. At this stage, the selected companies may discuss proposal development details during the proposal writing process with their assigned government expert(s) or government teaming partner(s).

Additionally, companies are invited to provide their own internal terms and conditions that may be consolidated with those of the government. This includes, but is not limited to, Service License Agreements (SLA) and/or User License Agreements (ULA).

Companies should note that there are certain terms and conditions the government may be unable to accept. However, projects awarded through the CSO may provide flexibility to adopt customary industry standards where it is otherwise legal and meets the government’s general public responsibility.

Offerors advancing to this phase will submit a detailed proposal, including:

Technical Volume: The technical volume shall include a detailed work plan indicating how each aspect of the objectives is to be accomplished. The technical volume should be in as much detail as the offeror considers necessary to fully explain its proposed technical approach or method, including all assumptions utilized to develop its proposed solution and associated costs. The technical volume should reflect a clear understanding of the nature of the work being undertaken. The technical volume must include information on how the project will be organized, staffed, and managed. Information should be provided that demonstrates Offeror’s understanding and management of important events or tasks. The technical volume must include a list of suggested deliverables and deliverable dates.

NOTE: The government reserves the right to further define the required technical proposal content based upon the specific contract requirements for the A-COP.

Price Volume: Detailed cost breakdown and justification. The government reserves the right to request any other price data or supporting cost information the government deems necessary to determine the total overall price is fair and reasonable. This can include but is not limited to commercial price catalog(s), previous commercial sales receipts, and/or other proprietary information to help the government determine reasonableness and future budgetary cost estimates. The Government reserves the right to further define the required price proposal content based upon the relevant requirements of the proposed solution.

NOTICE OF INTENT – BRAND-NAME 
Solicitation Number: PR15893854 
 
 
This is not a solicitation; this is a NOTICE OF INTENT to award a brand-name procurement action as 
follows: 
 
The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement (INL) at the U.S. Embassy in Bogotá -
Colombia intends to award a firm fixed-price purchase order for the supply of Financial Investigation 
Software Licenses. For this requirement, ALTIA SOFTWARE LICENSES is considered the only 
brand, and no other supplies or services will accomplish Embassy Bogota requirements. 
 
A brand name restriction is required for this software procurement due to integration and compatibility 
issues with the software currently in use by the Colombian National Police (CNP)  and to meet 
operational requirements. CNP investigators are trained exclusively with Altia software, and it is the 
only brand authorized for use by the CNP as part of their financial crime investigations. 
 
Product Service Code: 7A21, IT and Telecom - Business Application Software. 
NAICS code: 541511, Custom Computer Programming Services. 
 
This procurement action is being conducted in accordance with the statutory authority of FAR Part 
6.103-1, which states that only one brand-name and no other will satisfy Embassy Bogota requirements.  
 
Any interested party that believes it can meet the requirements described herein may identify 
themselves and must provide evidence of their capability to fulfill the requirement.  
 
Responses must be submitted in writing to contact Javier F. Lopez at LopezJF@state.gov and must 
be received no later than April 4, 2026, at 16:00 hours (Bogota, Colombia) time. 
 
 
Sincerely, 
 
Chantale Breton

DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION 
OFFICE OF THE ASSISTANT SECRETARY FOR RESEARCH AND TECHNOLOGY 
VOLPE NATIONAL TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS CENTER (VOLPE CENTER) 
TECHNOLOGY, INNOVATION AND STRATEGY DIVISION (V336) 
 
SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION 
 
A. Description of Supplies/Services. The Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center), in 
collaboration with the Intelligent Transportation Systems Joint Program Office (ITS JPO) and the Office 
of the Assistant Secretary for Research and Technology (OST-R), is investigating methods for the 
federal government to partner with private industry to leverage disparate data streams to create a “real-
time” picture of freight carrier legitimacy. Current FMCSA datasets – Motor Carrier Management 
Information System (MCMIS), Safety Measurement System (SMS) -- are highly effective for rated 
carriers but offer limited visibility into the thousands of new and unrated entrants that dominate the spot 
market. While the vast majority of motor carriers without a safety rating are American trucking 
companies (especially small owner operators and new fleets), there are also gaps among Mexican-
domiciled carriers committing cabotage. To support the investigation of this problem, this project seeks 
to fuse public FMCSA data with private industry data to create a predictive actuarial model that acts as a 
surrogate for traditional safety ratings.   
 
 
The objective of this project is to develop and validate a predictive actuarial model that assigns an 
Interim Risk Rating to unrated Mexican-domiciled carriers with authorities to operate along the US-
Mexico commercial border zone or to conduct long-haul international transport. This rating will serve as 
a statistically valid proxy for FMCSA safety ratings, segmenting Mexican-domiciled carriers with these 
authorities into distinct risk pools based on their probability of safety incidents and FMCSA violations. 
 
 
 
 
B. Market Research. Market research was conducted to identify companies capable of developing and 
validating a predictive actuarial model that assigns an Interim Risk Rating to unrated Mexican-
domiciled carriers. The solution must utilize proprietary AI to aggregate non-traditional leading 
indicators of risk – such as crash scores, and “chameleon” carrier identifiers – to serve as a statistically 
valid proxy for FMCSA safety ratings. Furthermore, the solution must be able to segment carriers 
operating along the U.S.-Mexico commercial border zone and long-haul corridors into distinct risk pools 
based on their probability of cabotage and safety violations. 
 
While Bluewire’s model is built to bridge information gaps, its main competitors, such as Central 
Analysis Bureau (CAB) and SambaSafety, frequently fail to meet this specific requirement because they 
are fundamentally reactive rather than predictive. These platforms primarily function as data aggregators 
that rely on trailing indicators, meaning they require a substantial volume of existing FMCSA inspection 
and violation history to generate a meaningful score. For unrated Mexican-domiciled carriers or new 
entrants with limited U.S. road time, these systems often return an “Incomplete” or “Not Rated” status. 
This creates a data gap that makes it difficult to assign a statistically valid Interim Risk Rating, 
effectively leaving these carriers invisible to traditional risk assessment tools until a major incident or 
audit occurs. 
 
Furthermore, many traditional competitors lack the sophisticated leading-indicator logic required to 
identify freight behavior in the absence of DOT data. While Bluewire utilizes proprietary AI to conduct 
text mining on social sentiment, recruitment behaviors, and "chameleon carrier" identifiers, competitors 
typically stick to rigid, structured datasets like MCMIS or MVR records. Without these non-traditional 


Procurement Request No. V3362090 
V220T.12    (01/19) 
data points, other models cannot detect the latent risk of a carrier that may have irregular behavior or 
poor safety management but hasn't yet been inspected. This makes these other competitors insufficient 
for the objective of segmenting Mexican-domiciled carriers into risk pools, as they cannot differentiate 
between a “legitimate but unrated” carrier and a “bad acting but unrated” one. 
 
Bluewire is a small business that is not part of a GSA, NASA SEWP, or FAA SAVES contract. The 
company is only accessible via direct award. 
 
C.  Supporting Rationale.  
 
(1) Sole Source: Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency 
requirements. 
 
Bluewire satisfies the project requirements by transforming the traditional, often binary, safety rating 
system into a multidimensional GAP Score that proactively identifies “severity risk” rather than just 
historical compliance. For unrated Mexican-domiciled carriers, this is particularly valuable because 
Bluewire’s model does not rely on a completed FMCSA audit to generate a score. Instead, it aggregates 
data across nine critical vulnerability gaps, such as MCS-150 filing accuracy, driver out-of-service 
(OOS) rates, and legal exposure, to create a 0–100 weighted rating. This allows them to assign an 
Interim Risk Rating to carriers that would otherwise remain invisible in traditional safety databases, 
providing an immediate basis for risk pooling based on their likelihood of being involved in high-
severity incidents. 
 
The statistical validity of Bluewire's model is anchored in its use of proprietary AI and dynamic peer-
grouping. Unlike the FMCSA’s static Safety Measurement System (SMS), which can be slow to update 
and often penalizes smaller fleets unfairly, Bluewire’s AI analyzes more than 750,000 DOT numbers to 
create trend lines based on recent performance data. By comparing Mexican-domiciled carriers against 
similar-sized peers operating in the same cross-border corridors, the model accounts for the specific 
operational realities of international long-haul transport. This satisfies the objective for a statistically 
valid proxy, as it uses weighted variables—including crash recency, violation patterns in high- risk 
categories (like Hours of Service or Driver Fitness), and even sentiment analysis—to predict future 
safety or cabotage outcomes with high precision. 
 
Ultimately, Bluewire’s approach enables the precise segmentation of carriers into distinct risk pools by 
identifying latent vulnerabilities that traditional FMCSA ratings miss. For carriers operating in the US-
Mexico border zone, the model can flag “chameleon” behavior or deteriorating safety cultures before a 
formal intervention occurs. Bluewire’s approach effectively bridges the information gap for unrated 
carriers, allowing them to validate an interim rating that aligns with the same safety standards required 
for U.S.-based domestic fleets.

NCIA Request for Information (RFI)
1. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) is conducting market
research to identify qualified vendors and gather input on potential solutions to
support the upcoming provision of a commercial IP Transport Service between
NATO and Partner Nations. To that end, we are issuing this Request for
Information (RFI) 42603961 to solicit feedback from capable and interested
industry partners.
2. This RFI is issued for planning purposes only and is not a request for bids. It is part
of NCIA’s effort to ensure it has a clear understanding of the marketplace, available
capabilities, and potential acquisition strategies.
3. We hereby invite interested industry to provide a price estimate along with a review
and comments on our draft requirements (Annexes A and B), including
recommendations for improving performance outcomes, competition, efficiency
and identifying any risks or concerns that should be considered during planning.
4. Submission instructions and additional details can be found in the Annexes to the
RFI Instructions.
5. Only companies from a NATO member country can participate in or respond to this
RFI (https://www.nato.int/cps/en/natohq/nato_countries.htm).
6. Should you have any questions or need clarifications, please contact Stefania
Iacob at 42603961_AirC2RFI@ncia.nato.int.
7. We thank you in advance for your time and input, and we look forward to engaging
with you as we shape this potential acquisition.

Annex B – Draft Requirements 
1. Background
The NCIA requires enhanced IP transport capabilities to facilitate the exchange of 
NATO Unclassified (NU) data, including Air Situation Data Exchange (ASDE). NCIA is 
exploring commercial IP transport options to improve interoperability, resilience, and 
cost efficiency while maintaining compliance with NATO security standards.  
2. Scope
At this stage, NCIA has not yet finalized the technical design or detailed requirements 
for commercial IP transport between NATO and Partner Nations.  
Input from industry is requested to: 
a. Provide insights and recommendations to help fine -tune the design of the
proposed solution.
b. Suggest best practices, standards, and architectures that could be adopted.
c. Identify potential risks, constraints, and dependencies NCIA should consider.
d. Highlight innovative approaches or emerging technologies that may improve
resilience, scalability or cost-effectiveness.
3. General requirements
a. Site-to-Site VPN connectivity between NATO and Partner Nations (in Annex C):
Type of VPN offered (e.g., IPsec, MPLS, SSL etc.). 
Detail encryption standards and security features. 
Provide hardware, installation support, and maintenance post-warranty. 
Describe monitoring, incident response and support services. 
Define SLA guarantees including uptime, latency. 
b. VoIP services suitable for business communication:
Call quality and reliability. 
Define SLA and support options. 
c. Bandwidth:
Guarantee minimum 10 Mbps symmetric bandwidth as baseline. 
Offer scalability options - ability to scale up to higher capacities (e.g., 50 
Mbps, 100 Mbps) upon demand. 
d. Pricing:
Provide one-time setup costs. 
Detail monthly recurring charges. 
List optional services and associated costs. 
e. Transition assistance:
Upon termination or expiration, the Vendor shall provide reasonable

cooperation and technical support to ensure seamless migration of 
services to another provider.
Documentation, configuration data, and technical support must be made 
available to facilitate transition.
High level diagram
4. Performance Requirements
a. Availability & Uptime:
Minimum 99.9% service availability guaranteed under SLA.
Redundant paths and failover mechanisms to ensure continuity of 
service. 
b. Latency & Jitter:
End to end latency not exceeding 150 ms between NATO and Partner 
Nation endpoints.
Jitter maintained below 30 ms to support real time applications VoIP. 
c. Quality of Service (QoS):
Prioritization of traffic, data, VoIP. 
Mechanisms to prevent congestion and packet loss.
d. Security and Integrity:
End-to-end encryption (IPsec or equivalent).
Continuous monitoring for intrusion detection and anomaly reporting.
e. Resilience and Recovery:
Automatic rerouting in case of link failure.

BACKGROUND

The Veteran Health Administration (VHA) National Teleradiology Program (NTP) is the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in-house Teleradiology service and has been providing 24x7 Teleradiology service to VA facilities since 2010.  NTP is currently supporting over 120 sites across all Veterans Integrated Service Networks

(VISNs).  Yearly workload is approximately 1.4 million exams of which 80% are STAT interpretations.  Currently NTP has approximately 230 Picture Archive and Communication System (PACS) workstations distributed across remote users and in-house reading centers providing remote Radiology interpretations.  

NTP’s current Teleradiology PACS archive (IntelePACS) and core application servers are located in the Sacramento Data Center, and the software and hardware are well past their end of life.  Additional servers are located in regional data centers and NTP reading centers and those system are similarly past their useful life.  NTP requires an upgrade of the existing IntelePACS software to the latest commercially available release while providing ongoing service/support to the legacy system until the upgrade is approved for clinical use. 

In November 2018, VA issued the Cloud First Policy mandating that all new and existing

Information Technology (IT) solutions be assessed to determine suitability to be offered as an enterprise cloud computing service. The VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) was established by the Enterprise Cloud Solutions Office (ECSO) in 2017, to host cloud computing solutions. The upgraded system shall be deployed in the VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) and the VA shall be responsible for VAEC hosting, while the Contractor shall provide all software and licenses beyond items within the VAEC catalog.  The Contractor shall be responsible for managing all VAEC resources associated with the PACS as part of initial deployment and ongoing service and support.

BACKGROUND

The mission of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Health Administration (VHA) is to provide superior healthcare services to Veterans of the United States. As the largest integrated healthcare system in the country, VA is uniquely positioned to develop and provide advanced healthcare capabilities to over 9 million Veterans. One significant challenge facing the VA and its ability to deliver high quality and reliable patient care to our Nation’s Veterans is the increase in demand for veteran patients to be seen within the VA healthcare system. In the short window of time allocated for each patient appointment, providers have a multitude of clinical and administrative tasks to be completed. This increases risk of important information being omitted due to rushed interviews and contributes to provider burn out. The myriad of tasks expected of providers beyond caring for patients puts significant cognitive burden and increased strain on them professionally. This strain has the potential to negatively impact patient care. It can also contribute to provider attrition, causing additional impact to Veterans and clinical staff. 

One method to reduce the risk of missing vital clinical information that impacts patient care planning and reducing cognitive burden for our providers is the use of ambient scribe technology Artificial Intelligence (AI) ambient scribes utilize a microphone on a secure device. The ambient AI scribe transcribes patient encounters. We then use machine learning and natural-language processing to summarize the conversation's clinical content and produce a transcribed note documenting the visit. Such transcribed conversations between patients and providers automatically leverage AI technologies to create notes in the appropriate format (generate clinical documentation) and summarize a patient’s visit. Automating these tasks increases accuracy of information, saves the providers time, and reduces their mental strain. Visit notes that include a patient’s care plan is a critical component of treatment and care delivery. The software functions as a medical and clinical system, equipment, device, or software (MCSEDS) as defined in VA Directive 6008.

Ambient scribe technology also enables other labor-saving capabilities to include but not limited to: pre and post visit charting to summarize important information prior to visit by either completing the task with AI or integrating with provider pre-charted note, coding support, order capture, after-visit summaries, drafting care plans and other capabilities. 

The ambient scribing solution required is unique to the operational environment and specific challenges faced by the Veterans Health Administration (VHA). In January 2024, VHA undertook an AI Technical Sprint challenge to ensure that potential solutions were rigorously tested through a competitive and impartial evaluation process under H.R. 4521-Bioeconomy Research and Development Act Of 2021 [America COMPETES Act of 2022]. The goal of the competition was to identify the top AI solutions identified through the VHA AI Tech Sprint Track 1: Ambient Dictation of Clinical Encounters. 

The advanced AI-enabled tools for ambient scribing focus on enhancing clinical documentation across primary care, mental health, and specialty care settings. The solution shall meet the following requirements:

Transcription and Note Generation: Automatically extract transcripts and key details from ambient recordings of patient encounters, creating traceable, high-fidelity medical records to include capabilities to populate diversified note templates.

Interoperability and Integration: Seamlessly integrate with existing VA health system information technologies, particularly the Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems, to ensure smooth operational continuity and data consistency.

Security Compliance: Adhere to stringent VA privacy and security standards for the protection of patient data.

Advanced Functionalities: Provide continuous improvements to include record query, recommend diagnoses and referrals, inpatient discharge summaries, nursing patient management, pre-charting capabilities and maintain high performance even in challenging clinical settings.

Patient Communications: Generate patient-facing summaries (After Visit Summaries and Discharge Summaries) that include educational materials, reminders, and follow-up recommendations which adhere to clinical documentation compliance standards.

Throughout the Technical Sprint, many solutions demonstrated superior technical maturity and clinical performance. Their development was closely aligned with the urgent needs of the VHA, specifically targeting enhancements in provider burnout and clinical documentation efficiencies. IT professionals and healthcare providers assessed these solutions for their maturity and practical applicability in real-world clinical settings, ensuring that they met the highest standards for operational readiness. 

Moreover, the effectiveness and safety of these solutions were evaluated through a series of blind scoring assessments. Physicians compared the AI-generated outputs against those produced by human clinicians, establishing their accuracy and reliability without bias. Additionally, their usability and potential for seamless integration into the VHA’s existing EHR systems were critically assessed to determine their capability to enhance operational continuity and data consistency within the VA health care system. This approach ensured a thorough evaluation of potential Contractors in a manner that fostered broad competition and verified that the selected Contractors met legal, technical, and operational requirements. Evaluations concluded in May 2024.

VA personnel assigned to the Digital Health Office will coordinate with SimLEARN personnel to access the system and run a real-time test to verify outputs. The test will occur at VA’s SimLEARN facility and will be conducted by VA staff. The test will require access to the system to simulate an encounter.

2. Contract Title: Support Licensing with Services for HYCU

3. Background: The Overton Brook Veterans Affairs Medical Center located at 510 East Stone Ave, Shreveport, Louisiana 71101, is requesting HYCU Licensing and Support Services for the purpose of backup and disaster recovery capabilities for their Nutanix HCI Platform installed at Shreveport LA and Disaster Recovery Cluster installed at Jackson, MS.  HYCU Licenses and Support Services will provide Data Protection and Recovery contingencies for all Nutanix HCI Nodes.  The goal is to enhance the center's data protection, backup, and disaster recovery capabilities. The Overton Brooks VAMC currently utilizes Nutanix for our Data Storage and virtualization solutions and transitioning to a different provider would require significant redevelopment, reconfiguration, retesting of all dependent systems, and exorbitant costs, resulting in potential downtime and increased risk to operations. The contractor will provide services for one (1)12-month base year and two (2) 12-month options years.  HYCU licenses and any necessary hardware shall be delivered and installed according to the SOW. 

     

The continued use of our current cloud service provider is critical to ensure the uninterpreted operation and security of the organization’s web servers, virtual system drives, and hosted data. The provider currently hosts all production web environments, database and virtual infrastructure. 

4. Scope: The scope of this project includes the procurement, installation, and continued support of the existing HYCU software solution integrated with the current Nutanix HCI environment at the Overton Brooks VA Medical Center (OBVAMC). The contractor shall provide all required licensing for purchase and usage, along with all associated support services for the existing Nutanix HCI infrastructure located at 510 E. Stoner Avenue, Shreveport, LA 71101.

OBVAMC Biomedical Engineering recommends renewal of the HYCU software solution to sustain the Nutanix HCI platform. This renewal will generate cost savings by enabling further virtualization of resource‑intensive clinical applications and eliminating the need for additional, less effective, and more costly backup and recovery systems. It will also support increased compliance with the VA’s Virtual First policy.

OBVAMC will provide all necessary power requirements, rack space, and network infrastructure.

Procurement of 24 HYCU licenses and any necessary hardware

Comprehensive installation and configuration of the HYCU software

Providing detailed documentation and support material

Facsimile, e-mail, and scanned documents are not acceptable forms of submission for payment requests.

The VA has mandated electronic invoice submission to the Veterans Affairs Financial Services Center (VAFSC). VAFSC has partnered with Tungsten Network e-Invoicing network, for submissions of all electronic invoices to VA.  Tungsten Network electronic invoicing is free to all VA vendors.  In order to submit electronic invoices, all VA vendors must register with Tungsten Network by submitting an email to VA.Registration@Tungsten-Network.com or calling  1-877-489-6135 for Enrollment.  

Contractor shall submit an electronic invoice by the tenth (10th) of the following month services were performed to the Veterans Affairs Financial Services Center (VAFSC) e-Invoice through the website at https://portal.Tungsten-Network.com/Login.aspx.  For questions regarding the submission of VA electronic invoices, Tungsten Network customer service may be contacted at 1-877-489-6135.  

All invoices shall reference the vendor name and address, customer name, contract number, appropriate obligation/funding order number, description of services provided, quantity, unit price, and total invoice amount (any additional info).  Invoices shall also include any payment discount terms.  

VA’s Electronic Invoice Presentment and Payment System – The Veterans Affairs Financial Services Center (VAFSC) uses a third-party contractor, Tungsten Network e-Invoice, to transition vendors from paper to electronic invoice submission. Please go to this website: http://www.tungsten-network.com/customer-campaigns/veteransaffairs/ to begin submitting electronic invoices, free of charge.

As of July 1, 2020, the VA10091 form has been eliminated and the VAFSC is requiring our vendors to update and add their information in the Customer Engagement Portal (CEP) at  https://www.cep.fsc.va.gov/. This is for new vendors being added to FMS only. 

For assistance setting up e-Invoice, the below information is provided:

* Tungsten Network e-Invoice Setup Information: 1-877-489-6135 
* Tungsten Network e-Invoice email: VA.Registration@Tungsten-Network.com
* FSC e-Invoice Contact Information: 1-877-353-9791 
* FSC e-invoice email: vafsccshd@va.gov   

FACILITY REQUIREMENTS: In addition to any other requirements set forth in this Contract, the Contractor, including its employees, agents, and subcontractors (collectively “the Contractor”), shall comply with the following facility requirements. Failure to comply with these requirements shall be considered a material breach of this Contract and may be a violation of Federal law resulting in charges answerable in the United States District Court.

Contractor is responsible to follow all on site facility policies 

All VA property is considered Federal property and all Federal laws are applicable. 

It is the responsibility of the Contractor to park in the appropriate designated parking areas. Information on parking is available from the VA Police Section. The VA will not invalidate or make reimbursement for parking violations of the Contractor under any conditions.   

All VA facilities are drug free. Possession of drugs, to include Marijuana and all Marijuana bi-products are prohibited. Enclosed containers, including tool kits, shall be subject to search. Violations of VA regulations may result in citation answerable in the United States (Federal) District Court, not a local district, state, or municipal court.

All contractor personnel are required to adhere to all VA rules and regulations.

Smoking is prohibited on the entire campus, both inside and outside the VA Facility 

Possession of weapons is prohibited. Enclosed containers, including tool kits, shall be subject to search. Violations of VA regulations may result in citation answerable in the United States (Federal) District Court, not a local district, state, or municipal court.   

VHA DIRECTIVE 1192: This Veterans Health Administration (VHA) directive establishes policy and provides guidance for the prevention of seasonal influenza in VHA facilities through the vaccination or masking of health care personnel (HCP). AUTHORITY: Title 38 United States Code (U.S.C.) 7301(b), 7318(b). Contractor is responsible in ensuring that all aspects of this directive are implemented, including providing face masks and influenza vaccines for all employees working at a VA facility.

SECURITY & PRIVACY CONTROL:  

PIV Card: 

Applies to unsupervised, full-time, logical and/or physical access for more than 6 months OR more than 180 aggregate days in a one-year period.

Defined in VA Directive 0735 as: “Personal Identity Verification (PIV) Credential: An identification card that complies with FIPS 201 and related guidance that contains a photograph and stored identity information so that the claimed identity of the cardholder can be verified by another person or an automated process. PIV credentials are issued to persons requiring routine access to VA facilities or information systems.”

All contractor employees are subject to the same level of investigation as VA employees who have access to VA Sensitive Information.  The level of background investigation commensurate with the level of access needed to perform in accordance with the statement of work is: Special Agreement Check (SAC) & National Agency Check with Inquiries (NACI).  This requirement is applicable to all subcontractor personnel requiring the same access.

National MOU/ISA is in place and applies to this contract. Sensitive information exposure as part of this contract involves applicable security controls within the facility as part of the VA Information Security.  If there are any questions related to privacy, please have a member of your staff contact the VA Privacy Service at (202) 461-6309.  If there are any questions related to the information security, please have a member of your staff contact the Office of Cyber Security at (304) 262-7733.

Routine Access and Personal Identity Verification of Contractor Personnel: 

The Contractor shall comply with agency personal identity verification procedures identified in the contract that implement Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12 (HSPD-12), Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance M-05-24 and Federal Information Processing Standards Publication (FIPS PUB) Number 201.

The Contractor shall account for all forms of Government-provided identification issued to the Contractor employees in connection with performance under this contract. The Contractor shall return such identification to the issuing agency at the earliest of any of the following, unless otherwise determined by the Government:

           (1) When no longer needed for contract performance.

           (2) Upon completion of the Contractor employee’s employment.

           (3) Upon contract completion or termination.

 The Contracting Officer may delay final payment under a contract if the Contractor fails to comply with these requirements.

It shall be the responsibility of the prime Contractor to return such identification to the VA.

RECORDS MANAGEMENT OBLIGATIONS

Contractor shall comply with all applicable records management laws and regulations, as well as National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) records policies, including but not limited to the Federal Records Act (44 U.S.C. chs. 21, 29, 31, 33), NARA regulations at 36 CFR Chapter XII Subchapter B, and those policies associated with the safeguarding of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a). These policies include the preservation of all records, regardless of form or characteristics, mode of transmission, or state of completion. 

In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, all data created for Government use and delivered to, or falling under the legal control of, the Government are Federal records subject to the provisions of 44 U.S.C. chapters 21, 29, 31, and 33, the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) (5 U.S.C. 552), as amended, and the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a), as amended and must be managed and scheduled for disposition only as permitted by statute or regulation. 

In accordance with 36 CFR 1222.32, Contractor shall maintain all records created for Government use or created in the course of performing the contract and/or delivered to, or under the legal control of the Government and must be managed in accordance with Federal law. Electronic records and associated metadata must be accompanied by sufficient technical documentation to permit understanding and use of the records and data. 

[FACILITY] and its contractors are responsible for preventing the alienation or unauthorized destruction of records, including all forms of mutilation. Records may not be removed from the legal custody of [FACILITY] or destroyed except for in accordance with the provisions of the agency records schedules and with the written concurrence of the Head of the Contracting Activity. Willful and unlawful destruction, damage or alienation of Federal records is subject to the fines and penalties imposed by 18 U.S.C. 2701. 

In the event of  any unlawful or accidental removal, defacing, alteration, or destruction of records, Contractor must report to [FACILITY]. The agency must report promptly to NARA in accordance with 36 CFR 1230.

The Contractor shall immediately notify the appropriate Contracting Officer upon discovery of any inadvertent or unauthorized disclosures of information, data, documentary materials, records or equipment. Disclosure of non-public information is limited to authorized personnel with a need-to-know as described in the [contract vehicle]. Department of Veterans Affairs 

Enterprise Digital Government Enablement 

Request for Information 

Introduction

This is a Request for Information (RFI) is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation 15.101(c)(2), responses to RFIs are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. 

The purpose of this RFI is to identify qualified vendors, who are able to meet the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requirements for Office of Information and Technology (OIT), Enterprise Digital Government Enablement (EDGE). Accordingly, this RFI constitutes neither a Request for Quote (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP), nor a guarantee that one will be issued by the Government in the future; furthermore, it does not commit the Government to contract for any services described herein. Any contract/order that might be awarded based on information received or derived from this market research will be the outcome of the competitive process. The purpose of this RFI is to obtain market information on capable sources of supply, industry best practices, and input specific to the information provided. The Government is not responsible for any cost incurred by industry in furnishing this information. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the interested vendor’s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions will become Government property and will not be returned. Interested vendors are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. 

The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512.

Requirement:

VA, OIT, Digital Service Delivery, Digital Transformation Center (DTC) strives to establish VA-wide Digital Modernization initiatives which can be supported and delivered via Product Delivery and Lifecycle Management methodologies to transform VA by tapping into emerging technologies, connecting developers with VA data, and making Human Centered Design the method of how all VA products are designed.

The DTC ecosystem is a persistent collaboration of platform management, program management teams, and system integrators (SI) across the entire capability delivery lifecycle with centralized enterprise platform management with quality approval gates assuring the SI’s delivery of high-quality low code/no code (LCNC) solutions. EDGE as a SI team is focused on delivering complex, large-scale solutions within the DTC Capability Delivery Lifecycle Management. DTC success is measured and validated through the incremental and iterative delivery of business and technology capabilities driving modernization efforts. 

As part of VA’s digital modernization, Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) is a strategic application delivery model. A SaaS Product is hosted on a cloud infrastructure outside the security boundary of VA and is provided to the Cloud Service Customer (CSC) over the internet. The CSC uses the SaaS offering via a thin-client interface, such as web-browser or a program interface. The CSC subscribes to the SaaS offering and is only responsible for limited application configuration settings. The Cloud Service Provider  offering the application is responsible for management of the application, safeguarding of data stores or processed by the application, and all elements of the underlying infrastructure.

To further accelerate the adoption of VA’s Cloud First policy, VA sponsors Hybrid and Managed Solutions in addition to the SaaS application delivery model. A Hybrid Solution is comprised of both SaaS and on-premise components which shall adhere to both SaaS and VA Enterprise Cloud established policies. A Managed Solution is defined as a single-tenant product not hosted within the VA Network. The mission of the VA is to provide benefits and services to Veterans of the United States. In meeting these goals, OIT strives to provide high quality, effective, and efficient Information Technology (IT) services to those responsible for providing care to the Veterans at the point-of-care as well as throughout all the points of the Veterans’ health care in an effective, timely, and compassionate manner. VA depends on Information Management/Information Technology systems to meet mission goals. 

In support of VA systems modernization and the agency’s mandate to move to the cloud, this task order seeks to continue developing Veterans Enterprise Systems Integrator Product-as-a-Service (PaaS)/SaaS Applications to modernize VA Health and Business specific case management solutions across the enterprise. The EDGE solution will utilize a platform agnostic approach to provide VA with modern solutions to support EDGE modular LCNC solutions that enables an innovative reusable service-focused software component architecture including PaaS functions/capabilities, SaaS integrations, Application Program Interfaces, and Digital modernization and emerging technology support. EDGE architecture will make configuring and customizing DTC PaaS and SaaS solutions easier to scale and faster to create, enabling innovation and accelerating time-to-market for new features. 

In addition, as an emerging technological part of VA’s digital modernization strategy, VA is increasingly embracing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) as foundational capabilities integrated within SaaS, PaaS, and LCNC platforms to enhance productivity, decision-making, and service delivery across VA agencies. DTC enables the responsible adoption of AI technologies by embedding AI capabilities directly into the EDGE capability delivery ecosystem, ensuring alignment with VA policies, security requirements, and enterprise governance, including oversight by the VA Chief Information Officer.

RFI Response Instructions 

The capability package must be clear, concise, and complete. VA is under no obligation to provide feedback to the company, or to contact the company for clarification of any information submitted in response to this RFI.

There is a page limitation for this RFI of 10 pages. The Government will not review any information or attachments in excess of the page limit.

Provide the following information:

Company Information:

	

Company Name

CAGE/UEI Number under which the company is registered in SAM.gov

Company Address

Point of Contact name

Telephone number

Email Address

Socio-economic Data (If small business, please identify socio-economic category(ies)

For small business concerns, indicate whether at least 50 percent of the total amount paid by the Government will be paid to firms that are similarly situated.

Company Business Size and Status for NAICS (541512).

Existing contractual vehicles (GWAC, FSS, MAC, SEWP, etc.)

Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI. Reponses should be as complete and as informative as possible.

Summary describing your company’s technical approach to meeting the requirements, to include:

Describe in detail your approach to directly supporting a minimum of 75+ concurrent LCNC projects/products and 75,000 end users (new development and enhancements) across multiple customer organizations, including the peak number of concurrent projects supported, specific LCNC platforms utilized, size of your reusable asset library, the scaled staffing model (number of full-time architects, developers, integration specialists, and DevSecOps engineers), proven integration patterns and architecture that sustained surges of several million transactions per day while consistently meeting or exceeding SLAs, mechanisms for dynamic allocation of scarce specialists across the portfolio, and measured outcomes such as delivery velocity improvement, asset reuse percentage, SLA compliance rates, and peak transaction throughput achieved.

Describe in detail your approach and operational expertise with modern delivery frameworks to include concurrent linear and iterative delivery frameworks to attain high delivery confidence for a large-scale enterprise solution that encompasses independent product team priorities; LCNC products and platforms; and VA source systems with varying degrees of system maturity, stability, and SLAs.

Describe in detail your approach to implementing an enterprise-wide automation framework and continuous improvement program that reduced manual interventions by at least 60% while supporting end users of varying technical complexity. State the peak number of concurrent projects directly managed and the measured overall reduction in manual touchpoints achieved through robotic process automation, intelligent workflow orchestration, automated testing/regression suites, or AI-assisted requirement triage tools. Describe the governance model and tools that enabled rapid incorporation of changing or emerging requirements within sprint cycles.

Describe your experience in simultaneously staffing and managing multiple concurrent Scrum teams (minimum of 200 teams at once) across different task areas or product lines throughout the full lifecycle. Include specific examples of how you determined optimal Scrum team sizes (e.g., 5–9 members), composed cross-functional skillsets (Dev, QA, DevSecOps, UX, etc.), and dynamically adjusted team structures and personnel across 200+ concurrent Scrum teams to meet evolving performance requirements and delivery schedules.

The Government is seeking industry feedback to determine vendor capabilities, socio-economic categories, industry best practices, and alternative contract vehicles and models well-suited for this requirement.  The Government values candid, experienced-based input focused on concepts, approaches and lessons learned.

Identify and describe any innovative pricing models you would recommend for this requirement.  What are the strengths and limitations of such pricing models?

Identify and describe any innovative contracting methodologies you would recommend for this requirement.  

Please provide any questions or comments on the Draft PWS. The Government does not anticipate answering questions prior to the RFI closing date.  

Responses to this RFI shall be submitted electronically by 3:00 PM Eastern Daylight Time, March 25, 2026 via email the Technology Acquisition Center (TAC) points of contact:

Contract Specialist: Mario Awad at Mario.Awad@va.gov 

Contracting Officer: Kathryn Pantages at Kathryn.Pantages@va.gov

Please note EDGE RFI in the subject of your response. Mark your response as “Proprietary Information” if the information is considered business sensitive.  

All proprietary/company confidential material shall be clearly marked on every page that contains such. The file size shall not exceed 5 MB.
